To comprehensively delineate the mechanistic basis of this therapeutic effect, we conducted integrated miRNA and mRNA sequencing analyses on liver tissues obtained from exosome-treated ACLF murine models. Methods: Mice subjected to a CCl4-based acute-on-chronic liver injury regimen received saline or an MSC-derived extracellular vesicle (EV) preparation intravenously through the tail vein. Liver miRNA and mRNA profiles were examined by differential expression, GSEA, functional enrichment, exploratory LASSO feature selection and integrative network analysis. Expression measurements were complemented by senescence-associated transcript assays, a Cat 3′UTR reporter assay and CCK-8 assessment in cell models. Results: Exosome treatment significantly activated longevity-regulating pathways, mitophagy, and glutathione metabolism in ACLF mice, concurrent with characteristic remodeling of hepatic immune infiltration involving follicular helper T cells, activated NK cells, and macrophage subpopulations. Hepatic injury severity demonstrated positive correlations with mmu-let-7j and Mmp27, and negative associations with mmu-let-7f-2-3p and Tmem8b. The reconstructed miRNA-mRNA network converged on FoxO signaling-mediated regulation of oxidative stress, cellular senescence and autophagy, with FoxO/Catalase (Cat) identified as core regulators. Experimental studies confirmed that MSC-derived exosomes downregulated miR-7b-5p in hepatocytes and enhanced Cat expression, with attenuation of cellular senescence. Conclusions: Integrative transcriptomic analysis revealed that MSC-exos activate the FoxO/Cat axis through miRNA-mRNA interactome remodeling, thereby orchestrating coordinated antioxidant, pro-autophagic, and anti-senescence effects alongside immune microenvironment reprogramming in liver failure. These findings establish a pivotal theoretical framework for developing exosome-based therapeutic strategies targeting hepatic disorders.

article.title: Dentin Collagen Crosslinking for Enhanced Resin-Dentin Bond Longevity: Evidence and Clinical Perspectives.
article.authors: Ajaj RA.
article.abstract: Abstract The durability of the dentin-resin bonded interface remains a major challenge in adhesive dentistry, largely due to hydrolytic and enzymatic degradation of exposed collagen fibrils within the hybrid layer. Endogenous proteolytic enzymes, particularly matrix metalloproteinases and cysteine cathepsins, play a critical role in the progressive degradation of the exposed collagen matrix. Collagen crosslinking has emerged as a promising strategy to stabilize the dentin matrix, enhance resistance to endogenous proteases, and potentially improve the long-term durability of adhesive bonds; however, current evidence remains largely experimental, and its routine clinical application is still limited. This narrative review synthesizes current preclinical and emerging translational evidence on collagen crosslinking approaches investigated to reinforce the dentin-resin interface and the characterization techniques used to evaluate their effectiveness. Emphasis is placed on mechanisms of action, key evaluation approaches, and potential clinical relevance. While several crosslinking strategies, particularly carbodiimide-based systems and polyphenol-derived agents, demonstrate encouraging in vitro and laboratory-based outcomes, significant barriers to routine clinical translation persist. These include application time, penetration depth, esthetic concerns, biocompatibility, and integration within existing clinical adhesive workflows. Future research should prioritize clinically feasible formulations, standardized testing protocols, and long-term in vivo and clinical validation to facilitate the potential translation of collagen crosslinking strategies into clinically durable adhesive restorations.

article.title: Histone lactylation mediates the regulation of dental follicle cells' senescence driven by RUNX2 during the process of tooth eruption
article.authors: Lingli Ji; Weiwei Zhao; Jie Li; Dandan Liu; Chenying Zhang; Xiaozhe Wang; Yang Liu; Shuguo Zheng
article.abstract: Abstract Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD), an autosomal dominant disorder caused by RUNX2 mutation, is characterized by delayed or failed eruption of the permanent teeth; however, the pathogenesis of tooth impaction remains unclear. Tooth eruption is a complex developmental process in which the dental follicle plays a crucial role. Although the dental follicle is known to coordinate osteoclastogenesis and osteogenesis, the precise cellular mechanisms that initiate eruption are still not fully defined. Moreover, how dental follicles activate the signals of tooth eruption and whether the other biological alterations occur in CCD dental follicles have not been reported. Previous work from our group demonstrated that RUNX2 mutations inhibit dental follicle cell senescence in CCD patients. Cellular senescence participates in diverse physiological and pathological processes and is increasingly implicated as a dynamic regulator of morphogenesis and tissue remodeling. This study investigates whether the senescence of dental follicle cells (DFCs) critically mediates tooth eruption and elucidates its underlying regulatory mechanism. Analysis of dental follicle tissues showed a significant reduction in SA-β-gal-positive and P16 INK4a -positive cells in CCD patients compared with healthy controls. Animal studies revealed a progressive accumulation of senescent cells in the dental follicle during normal tooth eruption, whereas this accumulation was suppressed in Runx2 +/− mice, which exhibit delayed tooth eruption. Inhibition of dental follicle senescence via nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) in wild-type mice similarly delayed tooth eruption, confirming the functional necessity of DFCs senescence. Mechanistically, RUNX2 knockdown or mutation upregulated HDAC3 expression, which catalyzed histone delactylation, predominantly at H3K18. The reduced H3K18la levels could lead to transcriptional repression of PLAU. Thus, RUNX2 knockdown or mutation suppressed DFCs senescence via the HDAC3/H3K18la/PLAU axis. Collectively, our study reveals that DFCs senescence acts as an important driver of tooth eruption and identifies a novel epigenetic regulatory mechanism involving histone lactylation that regulates cellular senescence mediated by RUNX2.

article.title: SA-β-Gal stratification reveals senescence-associated heterogeneity and differential cell death susceptibility in human CD8 effector T cells
article.authors: Luis Garza-Martínez; Mark Apadeer; Nica Mariz Aquino; Paolo S. Turano; Elizabeth Akbulut; Dillon Oswald; Sukhwinder Singh; Patricia Fitzgerald-Bocarsly
article.abstract: Introduction Cellular senescence in human T cells remains incompletely defined, particularly with respect to how senescence-associated states influence susceptibility to cell death. Methods We used flow-cytometric SPiDER-based detection of senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) activity to profile human CD8+ T-cell subsets from young and old donors. We stratified effector memory (CD8 EM ) and effector memory re-expressing CD45RA (CD8 EMRA ) subsets by the lowest (bottom 25%) and highest (top 25%) quartiles of SA-β-Gal signal. Results CD8 EM and CD8 EMRA cells displayed the greatest within-subset heterogeneity in SA-β-Gal activity. The SA-β-Gal low and high populations occupied distinct regions in UMAP projections and were reproducibly enriched in different FlowSOM metaclusters, indicating that SA-β-Gal activity captures structured phenotypic states within differentiated CD8+ T-cell compartments. These states differed in senescence-associated markers, including CD27, CD28, CD57, and CX3CR1, as well as granzyme-associated programs involving Gzm A, B and K, whereas chronological age had only a limited effect once subsets were analyzed separately. Functionally, nutrient-limited conditions unmasked marked differences in cell death susceptibility between these populations. Following PMA/ionomycin stimulation, SA-β-Gal high CD8 EM and CD8 EMRA cells underwent accelerated stimulation-induced cell death, showed increased caspase-3/7 activation, and exhibited lower post-treatment γH2AX signal relative to SA-β-Gal low counterparts. In contrast, in the absence of stimulation-induced energetic demand, SA-β-Gal high cells displayed greater resistance to cell death. Discussion Together, SA-β-Gal stratification resolves structured heterogeneity within human CD8 effector T cells and supports a context-dependent model in which senescence-associated effector states become selectively vulnerable to stimulation-induced death under metabolic stress.

article.title: Cellular senescence in ovarian cancer: context-dependent effects on tumor immunity and therapy response
article.authors: Yubo Zhang; Mengqi Deng; Junyi Jiang
article.abstract: Cellular senescence is a stress-responsive state marked by sustained proliferative arrest and changes in metabolism, chromatin organization, secretion, and immune signaling. In ovarian cancer (OC), platinum therapy and PARP inhibition can generate senescence-associated states with distinct consequences. Their effects depend on treatment context, cellular compartment, stability of arrest, and the surrounding immune state. Therapy-induced senescent tumor cells may increase antigen presentation and inflammatory signaling and, in immune-competent settings, facilitate dendritic-cell and CD8+ T-cell responses. Persistent senescence can instead maintain a SASP that remodels stromal and immune compartments and may support residual disease, dissemination, or relapse. OC studies have linked altered senescence responses to cisplatin resistance, while senescence-associated states have also been reported after PARP inhibition and taxane treatment. Senescence in CAFs, mesothelial cells, adipose-associated stroma, and immune cells can further alter tumor-cell survival, invasion, immune surveillance, and treatment response. We therefore distinguish stable TIS from reversible senescence-like or dormant states and separate tumor-cell effects from stromal and immune effects. Senolysis, SASP modulation, ferroptosis, and immune-mediated clearance represent potential strategies, but most evidence remains preclinical. Overall, senescence in OC is best viewed as a context-dependent state that can either support antitumor immunity or facilitate immune escape and treatment persistence.

article.title: Plant-Derived Bioactive Compounds, Cancer Stemness and Cellular Senescence: A Narrative Review of Preclinical Evidence and Translational Relevance to Cancer Recurrence and Drug Resistance
article.authors: Sara Naseer; Wai-Yann Tan; Yin-Teng Sow; Zhi-Yin Wai; Sahana-Shri Ramanitharan; Paey-Ern Bay; Ching-Hsein Chen; Soi-Moi Chye
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer recurrence and drug resistance arise from tumour-cell plasticity and microenvironmental adaptations that may persist after treatment. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are associated with self-renewal, tumour initiation, residual disease, and treatment tolerance, whereas cellular senescence has context-dependent effects. Although therapy-induced senescence may restrict tumour-cell proliferation, persistent senescent tumour or stromal cells and their senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) can, in selected models, promote inflammatory signalling, stemness-associated phenotypes and therapeutic resistance. This narrative review critically evaluates preclinical and translational evidence concerning curcumin, resveratrol, epigallocatechin gallate, berberine, piperine and shikonin as potential adjunctive modulators of CSCs and senescence-associated processes. Methods: Relevant literature was identified through searches of the MEDLINE/PubMed database from June 2000 and July 2026, using terms related to plant-derived bioactive compounds, CSCs, cellular senescence, SASP, recurrence and drug resistance. Evidence was evaluated according to model relevance, exposure, functional validation and whether it represented direct cross-axis evidence, intermediate mechanistic evidence, or marker- and pathway-level support. Results: Most studies examined CSCs and senescence as separate processes. Direct evidence showing that the same compound, within the same cancer model, modifies a validated cancer stem-cell function and a defined senescence or SASP and subsequently reduces resistance or recurrence is limited or absent. Moreover, poor bioavailability, variable formulations, potentially unachievable experimental exposures, drug interactions, tumour heterogeneity and limited clinical evidence constrain translation. Conclusions: Future studies should incorporate pharmacologically relevant exposures, functional and longitudinal endpoints, causal validation and biomarker-guided combination designs to determine whether these compounds can safely complement standard anticancer therapies.

article.title: Therapeutic induction of Nrf2 activation to reduce senescence in COPD
article.authors: Inés Roger; Paula Montero; Cristina Estornut; Maria Anton; Carolina Ferrer-Gomez; Ángel Cogolludo; Juan Escrivá; Julio Cortijo; Javier Milara
article.abstract: Abstract Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated lung aging, characterized by oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and accumulation of senescent cells. Impaired activity of the antioxidant regulator nuclear factor erythroid 2–related factor 2 (Nrf2) contributes to redox imbalance in COPD; however, whether pharmacological activation of Nrf2 can directly modulate senescence-associated processes in COPD remains unclear. Methods We first analyzed senescence markers in lung tissue from COPD patients across GOLD stages. We then investigated the effects of pharmacological Nrf2 activation using obacunone, omaveloxolone, and the reference compound bardoxolone, with metformin as a senescence-modulating comparator, in primary human bronchial epithelial cells (HBECs) from control subjects and COPD patients exposed to cigarette smoke extract (CSE). Senescence hallmarks, including oxidative stress, DNA damage, cell-cycle arrest, and SASP mediators, were assessed. Translational relevance was further evaluated in a murine model of acute lung injury–induced senescence. Results COPD lung tissue exhibited increased DNA damage, altered senescence markers, and telomere shortening, which correlated with disease severity. In HBECs, CSE induced oxidative stress, Nrf2 activation, DNA damage, senescence markers, and SASP factor release, with more pronounced effects in COPD-derived cells. Pharmacological Nrf2 activators significantly enhanced antioxidant defenses, reduced γH2AX accumulation, attenuated senescence markers (p21, p16, SA-β-gal), and suppressed IL-1β and IL-6 secretion in both control and COPD HBECs. Obacunone showed the most consistent protective profile. These effects were recapitulated in vivo, where Nrf2 activation mitigated inflammation, tissue remodeling, and senescence-associated alterations. Conclusions This study demonstrates that pharmacological activation of Nrf2 restores senescence-associated alterations in both healthy and COPD airway epithelial cells and in an in vivo model of lung injury–induced senescence. These findings identify Nrf2 activation, particularly via obacunone, as a promising strategy to target senescence-driven lung pathology.

article.title: Drought‐induced leaf senescence and regreening upon rewatering associated with chlorophyll metabolism in Kentucky bluegrass
article.authors: Devan Gladden; Stephanie Rossi; Bingru Huang
article.abstract: Abstract Drought stress is a major factor limiting the quality and persistence of cool‐season turfgrass species by accelerating leaf senescence and reducing overall vigor. This study was conducted to examine physiological responses associated with drought‐induced leaf senescence and post‐drought regreening in Kentucky bluegrass ( Poa pratensis L.), with particular emphasis on chlorophyll metabolism. Plants of two cultivars, Baron and Bewitched, were grown under controlled environmental conditions and subjected to well‐watered control and drought stress treatments, with post‐drought rewatering. Physiological parameters such as turf quality, relative water content, chlorophyll fluorescence, and chlorophyll content were evaluated throughout drought and recovery. In addition, the activities of a chlorophyll degradation enzyme, pheophytinase (PPH), and a chlorophyll synthesis enzyme, porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), were measured in response to drought and rewatering to observe the effect of drought on chlorophyll metabolism and to determine which pathway plays a more important role. Drought stress caused leaf dehydration, chlorophyll loss, reduced photochemical efficiency, and lower turf quality in both cultivars, although these parameters recovered following rewatering. PPH activity increased significantly during prolonged drought stress, whereas PBGD activity did not change significantly under drought. During post‐drought recovery, PBGD activity increased, while PPH activity declined to non‐stress levels. The decline in chlorophyll during drought‐induced leaf senescence may be associated with enhanced chlorophyll degradation enzyme activity, whereas the regreening observed during rewatering is likely related to the resumption of chlorophyll synthesis. These findings provide insight into the physiological mechanisms controlling drought‐induced senescence and post‐stress recovery in turfgrass and may be useful for the development of drought‐tolerant cultivars.

article.title: Kanzan cherry blossom and its active compounds attenuate methylglyoxal-induced skin fibroblast senescence through RAGE/NF-κB suppression and ECM restoration
article.authors: Limin Ouyang; Huiji Zhou; Binrui Yang; Xue Zhang; Xuefei Cai; Jiawei Zhang; Bo Li; Liang Chen
article.abstract: Introduction The accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) is a key driver of skin aging, accelerating the process through oxidative stress, inflammation, and disruption of extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis. Cerasus serrulata 'Sekiyama' Kanzan cherry blossom (KCB) is rich in bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anti-glycation potential. However, its compositional variations across flowering stages and their functional relevance remain unclear. Methods This study systematically characterized the chemical profile of KCB using UPLC-QTOF-MS and monitored six major active components across four flowering stages using UPLC-MS/MS. The anti-glycation, antioxidant, tyrosinase, and collagenase activities of the identified compounds were evaluated in vitro . The protective effects of KCB extract (KCBE) and major active compounds were further investigated in a methylglyoxal (MGO)-induced human skin fibroblast senescence model. Results Thirteen compounds were identified, including one organic acid, five flavonoid glycosides, and seven phenolic acids. The half-bloom stage (KCB3) contained the highest levels of the six quantified compounds. 1- O -caffeoyl glucoside (CG) was the predominant phenolic acid (8.025 ± 0.203%), while quercetin 3- O -6 ′′ - O -malonyl-β-glucopyranoside (QMG) was the major flavonoid (1.155 ± 0.035%). QMG showed strong anti-glycation activity (IC50 = 0.41 ± 0.01 mM), whereas CG exhibited strong tyrosinase (IC 50 = 0.19 ± 0.03 mM) and collagenase inhibition (IC 50 = 2.51 ± 0.90 mM). KCBE, QMG, and CG significantly alleviated MGO-induced cellular senescence, reduced intracellular ROS, restored F-actin organization, and promoted type I collagen deposition. These effects were associated with suppression of RAGE/NF-κB signaling, normalization of the Nrf2/HO-1-mediated antioxidant response, and restoration of ECM-related gene expression. Discussion Half-bloom KCB exhibits prominent anti-glycation and anti-skin-aging activities, with CG and QMG representing major bioactive constituents. These findings indicate that KCB and its characteristic phenolic acid and flavonoid constituents may have potential as natural functional ingredients for skin health.

article.title: Environmental noise, GABA, and the auditory brain across the lifespan: A mechanistic gap analysis
article.authors: Thomas Franklin
article.abstract: Environmental noise has been associated with altered auditory physiology, impaired speech perception, and adverse developmental outcomes, yet the causal mechanisms connecting these observations remain incompletely established. This review applies the Mechanistic Gap Index (MGI), a quantitative framework for evaluating individual causal transitions, to proposed pathways involving environmental noise, cochlear synaptopathy, GABAergic inhibition, neural encoding, and auditory development. Eight relationships yielded a mean MGI of 0.75, with four critical evidentiary bottlenecks. Application of the same scoring criteria to a more established auditory-training mechanism yielded an MGI of 0.33, providing a preliminary comparison of mechanistic completeness. Beyond identifying missing causal links, we propose extending the MGI in four directions: prioritizing experiments capable of closing specific gaps; investigating long-range causal relationships between apparently disconnected biological observations; identifying overlooked intermediate mechanisms concealed within unsupported causal transitions; and iteratively refining causal pathways as new evidence emerges. Importantly, a high-gap transition may reflect not only insufficient evidence but also an incompletely specified mechanism containing unidentified intermediate processes. Decomposing such transitions could reveal experimentally supported connections and isolate the specific missing steps required for causal closure. Prospective measures of mechanistic gain, longitudinal MGI assessment, and a complementary measure of mechanistic resolution could further support this approach. Although these extensions require independent validation, the proposed advance is to transform the MGI from a descriptive assessment of evidentiary gaps into an iterative framework for experimental prioritization, mechanistic reconstruction, and causal discovery.

article.title: Maladaptive lipid partitioning in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: From depot dysfunction to metabolic phenotyping
article.authors: Si-Shang Qin; Zi-Min Wu; Bao-Shi Zheng; Cheng Luo
article.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is a heterogeneous syndrome, with obesity defining an increasingly treatable cardiometabolic phenotype. Building on recent work identifying dysfunctional adiposity as an upstream contributor, this minireview focuses on the complementary question of how failure of safe lipid storage redirects substrate across visceral, hepatic, skeletal muscle, epicardial, perivascular, and myocardial compartments, and how this depot-specific routing intersects with myocardial metabolic inflexibility. Human imaging, invasive physiology, myocardial metabolomics, and recent clinical trials support associations between ectopic adiposity, insulin resistance, inflammation, impaired vascular and atrial reserve, congestion, and exercise intolerance, although causal pathways remain incompletely established in humans. We therefore propose an adiposity-aware, hypothesis-generating framework integrating body composition, regional adipose depots, metabolic-inflammatory biomarkers, atrial and right-sided function, and exercise assessment for phenotype-enriched research and future trial design. This framework is not intended to guide current treatment selection. Established treatment should remain evidence based, including exercise, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism, decongestion, and obesity-directed incretin therapy, with attention to lean-mass preservation. Future prospective studies should investigate whether depot quality, metabolic flexibility, sex and ethnic heterogeneity, and body composition provide additional information for phenotypic characterization and risk stratification beyond conventional measures.

article.title: Combined supplementation effects of bacterial organic selenium and vitamin E on post-mortem meat quality, selenium bioaccumulation, serum lipid metabolism and selenoprotein expression in spent laying hens
article.authors: Nurafiqah Najwa Zainudin; Aliyu Ibrahim Muhammad; Nazri Nayan; Anjas Asmara Samsudin
article.abstract: Context Antioxidants from biological sources play a vital role in preventing oxidative cellular damage in livestock. The dietary inclusion of biogenic organic selenium produced by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (ADS18) represents a novel antioxidant strategy in poultry nutrition. Aim This study investigated the effects of combined dietary supplementation of diverse selenium (Se) sources and vitamin E on tissue Se deposition, systemic lipid profiles, antioxidant capacity, and postmortem muscle quality attributes in spent laying hens. Method One hundred and twenty 68-week-old Lohman Brown-Classic spent hens were randomly assigned to the following four dietary treatments for 90 days: a basal control (T1), basal diet supplemented with 250 mg/kg vitamin E and 0.3 mg/kg Se as sodium selenite (T2), selenium yeast (T3), or biogenic bacterial selenium (ADS18; T4). Key results Muscle Se deposition significantly higher in hens receiving Se sources (ADS18 and Se-yeast) than in inorganic Se and control groups. Co-supplementation of ADS18 and vitamin E significantly improved systemic lipid profile, characterised by increased high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and reduced triglyceride and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) concentrations. At the molecular level, organic Se combined with vitamin E significantly upregulated SELW1 and GPX4 mRNA expression. SELW1 expression was strongly associated with Se influx, serving as a responsive biomarker of bioavailability, whereas GPX4 remained stable across treatments. However, dietary treatments did not significantly alter postmortem physicochemical meat quality parameters, including drip loss, cooking loss, Warner–Bratzler shear force, or muscle fatty acid profiles. Conclusion Combined dietary supplementation with biogenic ADS18 selenium and vitamin E effectively enhances tissue Se accumulation, optimizes systemic lipid status, and upregulates key selenoprotein gene expression in spent laying hens, without negatively affecting or altering fundamental postmortem meat quality characteristics. Implications These findings demonstrate that biogenic selenium produced by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (ADS18), when co-supplemented with vitamin E, serves as an efficient nutritional strategy to enhance tissue selenium bioaccumulation, optimize lipid profiles, and upregulate key selenoprotein gene expression in aging spent laying hens. This provides the poultry industry with a sustainable bio-additive alternative to improve metabolic health and functional product value without compromising commercial meat quality attributes.

article.title: Insights into Composition-Induced Structural Shifts in Lipid Nanoparticles
article.authors: Rongmei Judy Wei; Shadi Fuladi; Doug J. Grzetic; Mayank Misra; Thomas F. Hughes; Dave J. Giesen; Febin Tom; Neha Chopra; Kunal Paul; Tati Reddy Vadicherla; Mee Y. Shelley; Andrea R. Browning; Naveen K. Thakral; Peter J. Skrdla; Shiva Sekharan; John C. Shelley
article.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
article.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading platform for nucleic acid delivery, yet current formulations typically suffer from rapid in vivo clearance and limited extrahepatic delivery. Recent experiments demonstrate that increasing the helper lipid content (e.g., to 40% 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine [DSPC]) can significantly improve mRNA stability, prolong circulation, and enhance transfection efficiency. In this study, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to provide mechanistic insight into the structural changes driving these improvements. Our simulations confirm that an elevated helper lipid content fundamentally alters the internal morphology of the LNP. Consistent with experimental observations, at high DSPC levels, the core transitions from a compact, disordered, predominantly lipid state to an extended structure with distinct lamellar-like elements encompassing lipid-rich and water-rich regions. This structural reorganization can be used to rationalize the enhanced stability and delivery properties reported in the experiments. These findings provide a molecular-level understanding of the composition-morphology relationship and suggest that coarse-grained modeling can inform the design of novel LNP formulations.

article.title: Decoding lipid metabolic reprogramming in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: from tumor–microenvironment crosstalk to therapeutic resistance
article.authors: Xingyu Liu; Zitong Ye; Liuyang Wang; Yubo Chi; Tongjia Chu; Ziyu Liu; Shanxiang Yu; Haocheng Yang; Xinyue Yin; Jian Zhang; Alfred Wei Chieh Kow; Huan Liu
article.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a nutrient-poor, hypoxic, and highly desmoplastic microenvironment that imposes substantial metabolic stress on malignant cells. Under these unfavorable conditions, lipid metabolism reprogramming provides cancer cells with the flexibility needed to maintain growth and survive therapeutic stress. Recent advances have uncovered new links between lipid metabolic reprogramming, the tumor microenvironment, and therapeutic resistance in PDAC, highlighting the need for an updated synthesis of this rapidly evolving field. In this review, we focus on the major tumor-intrinsic alterations in fatty acid and cholesterol–mevalonate metabolism, including changes in lipid synthesis, uptake, desaturation, storage, and oxidative utilization. These processes support membrane homeostasis, oncogenic signaling, and redox control, thereby linking lipid handling directly to tumor progression and treatment adaptation. We further review how these pathways are reshaped by the tumor microenvironment, where cancer-associated fibroblasts, immune cells, adipocytes, and neural-associated cells influence lipid availability, trafficking, and signaling. These reciprocal interactions can shape stromal plasticity, immune suppression, invasion, metastasis, and treatment response. We also evaluate current strategies targeting lipid metabolism and discuss why their clinical translation remains limited by metabolic compensation, tumor heterogeneity, drug specificity, and systemic toxicity. Overall, the available evidence suggests that lipid metabolism in PDAC is better understood as a dynamic, interconnected adaptive network rather than a set of isolated metabolic pathways. This perspective supports biomarker-guided combination strategies that target context-dependent lipid dependencies and treatment-induced metabolic adaptation, rather than relying on inhibition of a single pathway.

article.title: Hepatocyte-derived lipid droplets in MASH: macrophage sensing and inflammation
article.authors: Di Jin; Yinan Zhao
article.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) develops through interactions between hepatocyte injury and hepatic immune responses. Lipid droplets (LDs) exposed or released from damaged hepatocytes provide a potential link between lipid accumulation and macrophage-mediated inflammation. Experimental studies indicate that these structures can both promote disease-associated macrophage responses and attenuate inflammatory signaling. This mini-review examines how hepatocyte-derived LDs influence macrophage sensing, uptake, and inflammatory responses in MASH. We discuss the contribution of membrane-spanning 4-domains A7 (MS4A7) to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and disease progression, alongside evidence that LD treatment suppresses inflammatory responses in cultured macrophages. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) supports this suppression without being required for LD uptake in the tested system, while reduced MS4A7 expression contributes to the attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings distinguish LD internalization from its downstream immune effects and warrant separate consideration from the efferocytosis of intact apoptotic hepatocytes. We examine experimental conditions and macrophage states as possible explanations for differing outcomes and identify unresolved questions about LD recognition and relevance to human disease. Finally, we consider therapeutic strategies that limit pathogenic macrophage activation while preserving beneficial clearance functions. Defining the molecular basis of LD sensing and establishing its consequences in vivo will be essential for translating this form of hepatocyte–macrophage communication into immunological interventions for MASH.

article.title: Correlation between serum Vitamin D levels and lipid profile in patients with obesity undergoing metabolic bariatric surgery Correlação entre os níveis séricos de Vitamina D e o perfil lipídico em pacientes com obesidade submetidos à cirurgia bariátrica metabólica
article.authors: Flaviana Freitas Pedron; Glauco da Costa Alvarez; Luciana Dapieve Patias; Ana Cristina Machado; Cristina Machado Bragança de Moraes; Alexandre Vontobel Padoin
article.abstract: Introduction: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass demonstrates high efficacy in reversing vitamin D deficiency and improving the lipid profile in obese patients, thereby reducing cardiovascular risks. The high prevalence of dyslipidemia and cardiovascular risk associated with obesity constitute a serious public health problem, a scenario significantly exacerbated by vitamin D deficiency. Objective: To evaluate the correlation between serum vitamin D levels and the lipid profile in patients with obesity undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Methods: A retrospective study in which data were collected at baseline (0) and at 6 and 12 months postoperatively during the periods 2018–2019 and 2021–2022. All patients underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Patients were divided into Group 1 (pre-pandemic) and Group 2 (post-pandemic). Preoperatively, participants were classified according to vitamin D status as sufficient, deficient, or insufficient. Data were organized in Excel 2010, with variables described using frequencies. Longitudinal variability was assessed using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE), and Pearson's correlation was used, with a significance level of p

article.title: The Vicious Cycle of Hepatic Ferroptosis and Inflammation Drives Lipid Accumulation and Injury in Dairy Cows with Fatty Liver
article.authors: Xiaobing Li; Yan Tian; Shiyue Ma; Jiawei Jin; Caiyin Yu; Taiyu Shen; Changlin Si; Junlong Bi; Gefen Yin; Qingqing Zhou; Zhiyuan Fang
article.venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
article.abstract: Abstract In dairy cows, the complex pathophysiology of fatty liver continues to pose substantial obstacles to both prevention and treatment. Here, we identified hepatic inflammatory injury and ferroptosis in fatty liver cows and reproduced these phenotypes by exposing bovine hepatocytes to NEFA. Mechanistically, NEFA disrupted TFR1/FPN-mediated iron metabolism and impaired the SLC7A11-GPX4 axis, thereby driving uncontrolled lipid peroxidation. These molecular events were consistent with the hepatic pathological changes observed in fatty liver cows. Importantly, ferroptosis blockade reduced lipid deposition and inflammatory injury during NEFA exposure in bovine hepatocytes more effectively than NF-κB inhibition. Furthermore, TNF-α alone induced ferroptosis, lipid accumulation, and cell injury , and these effects were further exacerbated by NEFA. Consequently, our work reveals that a vicious cycle between ferroptosis and inflammation is a key pathogenic mechanism in fatty liver, thereby pinpointing ferroptosis as a novel therapeutic target with high translational potential for dairy cows.

article.title: Ultrabright Thermally Boosted Ln‐MOF X‐Ray Scintillators: A Multifunctional Platform for Upconversion Luminescence and Lipid Droplet Imaging
article.authors: Wen‐Kang Jiang; Yu‐Feng Wang; Fan Yang; Hua‐Hong Zou; Fu‐Pei Liang; Zhong‐Hong Zhu; Hai‐Ling Wang
article.abstract: ABSTRACT The sharp decline in light yield ( LY ) of X‐ray scintillators under extreme high temperatures remains a key bottleneck for their application in high‐temperature radiation imaging. Herein, 1,2,4,5‐tetra(4‐carboxyphenyl)benzene (H 4 TCPB) are employed as linkers to assemble lanthanide cluster {Eu 4 O 30 } secondary building units, affording ultrabright thermally enhanced Eu‐TCPB‐MOF based X‐ray scintillators. Specifically, the luminescence intensity of the X‐ray excited luminescence (XEL) spectrum of the Eu‑TCPB‑MOF based X‐ray scintillator in the range of 300–440 K continues to increase with increasing temperature, and the peak luminescence intensity is 1.96 times the room temperature value. It shows that the material has excellent scintillation properties under high temperature conditions. This improvement stems from reduced nonradiative energy loss caused by O–H vibration, after coordinated terminal water desorbs from the framework at high temperatures. Eu‐TCPB‐MOF also retains excellent radiation stability and high‐resolution scintillation imaging performance. Furthermore, the isostructural Eu‐TCPB‐MOFs platform integrates multiple functionalities: two‐photon upconversion luminescence and lipid droplet‐targeted live‐cell optical imaging. This work opens new avenues for designing thermally enhanced ultrabright Ln‐MOF scintillators and establishes a versatile platform for multifunctional Ln‐MOFs applications.

article.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
article.authors: Priya D Gopal Krishnan; Kah Yong Goh; Kai Hung Chen; Chi Peng; Wen Xing Lee; Elizabeth A. Mendes; Shi Chee Ong; Sze Mun Choy; Qian Gou; Kanya Moolsuwan Ng; Kenon Chua; Shu-Yi Huang; Reshma Taneja; Corinne M. Linardic; Chih-Chiang Chan; Hong-Wen Tang
article.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79206-0 Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

article.title: A Reproducible CD36-Enriched Lipid-Associated Macrophage State in Lung Adenocarcinoma and Its Spatial Relationship to Exhausted CD8+ T Cells
article.authors: Qiangping Ma; Jianqing Liang; Jintian Li; Juan Li
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: The reproducibility of lipid-associated macrophage (LAM) states in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and their spatial relationship to exhausted CD8+ T cells are unclear. Methods: Single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts (discovery, GSE131907; replication, GSE189357) were analyzed at patient level with selection-independent replication criteria. Spatial analyses used one Xenium section and one independent Visium HD specimen. Transcription-factor inference, CellChat and drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) generated hypotheses. Results: A macrophage state combining lipid-handling/lysosomal (APOE, TREM2) and resident-like (FOLR2, SELENOP) features was recovered in both cohorts and every patient (held-out signature area under the curve, 0.91). CD36 enrichment was weaker in the replication cohort, hence the name CD36-enriched LAM. Inferred NR1H3/liver X receptor α (LXRα) activity was higher, but its magnitude depended on population-defining genes. Exhausted CD8+ T cells were modestly over-represented near CD36-enriched LAM in both specimens; adjustment for transcript depth and tissue region attenuated this excess. Predicted Galectin-9 and macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) signals were not population-specific. MR found no evidence that genetically predicted CD36 expression affects LUAD risk (odds ratio 0.98; 95% confidence interval 0.95–1.01). Conclusions: CD36-enriched LAM is a reproducible LUAD macrophage state modestly associated in space with exhausted CD8+ T cells. The roles of CD36, LXRα, Galectin-9 and MIF require protein-level and functional testing.

article.title: Magnolol alleviates high-fat diet-induced steatosis, inflammation and fibrosis in obesity-associated liver injuries via MOGAT1-mediated lipid metabolism and NF-κB signaling
article.authors: Ziqing Huang; Zixia Huang; Linfei Luo; Zhengqiang Wu; Zhili Wen; Zhihua Xiao
article.abstract: Background Magnolol (MAG), a bioactive compound from Magnolia officinalis, possesses anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering properties, but its role in obesity-associated liver injury and its molecular targets remain unknown. Methods High-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice were treated with MAG (10 or 20 mg/kg) daily for 7 days. AML12 hepatocytes were challenged with PA with or without MAG pretreatment. Liver injury was evaluated by histology, serum biochemistry, qPCR and Western blot. RNA-seq and mechanistic studies were performed to identify MAG-regulated pathways and targets. Results MAG significantly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, serum transaminases, and collagen deposition in HFD-fed mice. RNA-seq identified monoacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 1 (MOGAT1) as the most significantly downregulated lipogenic gene by MAG. MOGAT1 expression correlated positively with liver triglyceride and injury markers. MAG also suppressed HFD-induced NF-κB activation (reduced P65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, lower IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings were recapitulated in PA-treated AML12 cells. Critically, MOGAT1 overexpression largely reversed MAG-mediated suppression of inflammatory and fibrotic responses, demonstrating a causal role of MOGAT1 in MAG’s protective effects. Conclusion MAG alleviates HFD-induced hepatic steatosis, inflammation and fibrogenic responses by suppressing MOGAT1-mediated triglyceride synthesis and subsequent NF-κB-driven inflammation. This study identifies MOGAT1 as a novel downstream effector and functional mediator of MAG, providing new mechanistic insight into its hepatoprotective action and supporting its therapeutic potential for obesity-associated liver injuries.

article.title: Microwave-assisted stabilization of lipid-rich melon seed powder: enzyme inactivation, oxidative stability, and quality changes during storage
article.authors: Gulcin Yildiz; Gökçen Yıldız
article.venue: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
article.abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of microwave-assisted stabilization in reducing endogenous enzyme activities, delaying lipid deterioration, and preserving the quality of lipid-rich melon seed powder (MSP). A 3 × 3 factorial design comprising three microwave power levels (100, 200, and 300 W) and three treatment durations (30, 60, and 90 s) was employed. Nine microwave treatments and an untreated control were evaluated for lipase and lipoxygenase (LOX) activities, physicochemical characteristics, antioxidant activity, and functional properties. Storage stability was assessed over 60 days by monitoring free fatty acid (FFA) content, peroxide value (PV), and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS). Among the tested conditions, MW8 (300 W × 60 s; nominal specific energy input of 360 J/g) achieved the greatest enzyme inactivation, reducing lipase and LOX activities by 78.2% and 69.0%, respectively. After 60 days of storage, MW8 exhibited substantially lower FFA content (2.45% versus 5.65%), PV (5.97 versus 12.80 meq O 2 /kg sample), and TBARS (1.02 versus 2.18 µM MDA/g sample) than the untreated control. MW8 also increased total phenolic content and DPPH radical-scavenging activity while improving water and oil absorption capacities. Extending the treatment duration to 90 s at 300 W did not provide additional enzyme inactivation or storage protection, demonstrating a non-linear response to microwave treatment severity. Overall, microwave treatment at 300 W for 60 s provided the most favorable balance between enzyme inactivation, delayed lipid deterioration, and preservation of the evaluated quality characteristics under the investigated experimental conditions.

article.title: Genotypic Differences in Triacylglycerol-Centered Lipid Metabolism at the Kernel Developing Stage in Three Representative Yunnan Macadamia Cultivars Revealed by Integrated Omics
article.authors: Yuanqi Wang; Siyuan Zhang; Yurou Wang; Mingju Hu; Hùng Tiến Lương; Tao Liu; Ran Tang; Xiaoyu Xu
article.abstract: Macadamia integrifolia is an economically important woody oil crop valued for its high monounsaturated fatty acid content and excellent kernel nutritional quality. Although it has great industrial potential, variety-related differences in lipid metabolism and kernel quality are still poorly understood. Resolving these differences will support targeted quality improvement and molecular-breeding efforts. In this study, three representative macadamia cultivars, namely DS1, GR1 and O.C., which are widely cultivated in Yunnan province of China, were employed to investigate the dynamic variations in kernel quality traits across three physiological stages. Integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic analyses were applied at the kernel development stage to characterize the metabolic differentiation. Multi-omics results revealed distinct carbon allocation and lipid accumulation patterns observed among the three cultivars. Variety-related differences in oil yield and nutrient profiles were associated with altered gene expressions and metabolite levels linked to fatty acid biosynthesis, triacylglycerol (TG) assembly and oil-body formation. Differences in lipid and carbon metabolite accumulation also contributed to these phenotypic variations. This study preliminarily identified candidate genes and pathways associated with TG-centered lipid metabolism in developing macadamia kernels at a critical developmental stage, based on samples collected from single trees per cultivar.

article.title: Lipid‐matrix‐dependent effects of ceramide enrichment on cholesterol‐containing PSM and DLPC membranes
article.authors: Eun Sub Song; Taejin Kwon
article.venue: Bulletin of the Korean Chemical Society
article.abstract: Abstract Ceramide is a bioactive sphingolipid that can reorganize cholesterol‐containing membranes, but how membrane properties change with increasing ceramide content in different lipid matrices remains unclear. Using Martini 3 coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations, we examine cholesterol‐containing PSM and DLPC membranes across a controlled palmitoyl ceramide (PCER) composition series at a single liquid‐phase temperature. Increasing PCER fraction generally decreases area per lipid and increases lipid ordering, consistent with membrane condensation. However, the responses differ between matrices. In PSM/CHOL, PCER is accommodated within an already ordered environment, producing only modest membrane stiffening. In DLPC/CHOL, PCER leads to greater changes in local packing heterogeneity and lateral organization, accompanied by a nonmonotonic mechanical response. PCER enrichment also changes the positional and orientational distributions of cholesterol in a matrix‐dependent manner. These results show that ceramide‐induced condensation does not necessarily produce monotonic membrane stiffening and highlight the importance of the host lipid matrix in determining membrane structure and mechanics.

article.title: Microfluidically fabricated self-oxygen-supplied DL-86 lipid nanoplatform for in vitro synergistic photodynamic/photothermal dual phototherapy against hypoxia-tolerant glioblastoma.
article.authors: Jun Gong; Xiaoming Pan; Shichao Wang; Yifan Liu; Guangwei Wang; Min Yu; Pu Chun Ke; Mengze Xu
article.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) bears sustained intratumoral hypoxia that blocks oxygen-dependent photodynamic therapy (PDT). Hypoxia suppresses Type II photochemical reactions and singlet oxygen (¹O₂) generation, while oxygen-free photothermal therapy (PTT) can complement PDT for synergistic tumor suppression. Copper phthalocyanine DL-86 is a single NIR dual-responsive photosensitizer capable of simultaneous ROS and heat production, yet its anti-tumor potency is limited by tumor hypoxia and poor cellular uptake. Herein, microfluidics was adopted to fabricate self-oxygenated liposomes DL-86@CAT@Lip co-loaded with DL-86 and catalase (CAT). The uniform spherical nanoparticles (114.7 nm) exhibited excellent colloidal and serum stability. Encapsulated CAT decomposed intracellular H₂O₂ to relieve hypoxia, and the nanosystem achieved a photothermal conversion efficiency of 46.15%. Under 660 nm laser irradiation, combined PDT/PTT drastically reduced hypoxic C6 glioma cell viability to ~20.3%. Hemolysis tests confirmed favorable intravenous hemocompatibility. This work first proves that the self-oxygenation liposomal platform enhances hypoxic anti-GBM dual phototherapy, supplying an in vitro concept and a blueprint for brain tumor phototherapeutic nanomedicines.

article.title: The Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Glycemic Control, Lipid Profiles, Androgen Levels, and Blood Pressure in PMOS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
article.authors: Yang Yang; Zheng Liu; Jing Zhang
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a common endocrine–metabolic disorder. Time-restricted eating (TRE) has emerged as a potential dietary intervention, but its efficacy in PMOS remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of TRE on metabolic, hormonal, and anthropometric parameters in women with PMOS. Methods: A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science databases, Embase, Cochrane Library, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform for studies published from inception to 1 July 2026. Eight studies involving 363 women with PMOS were included in the systematic review. Among these, five controlled studies (four randomised controlled trials and one randomised crossover trial), involving 264 participants, were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Results: Quantitative synthesis was conducted using five controlled studies involving 264 participants. Meta-analysis showed that TRE significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose (MD = −0.17 mmol/L, 95% CI: −0.31 to −0.03), fasting insulin (MD = −28.86 pmol/L, 95% CI: −51.98 to −5.74), and HOMA-IR (MD = −0.66, 95% CI: −0.86 to −0.45). TRE also significantly improved QUICKI (SMD = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.92) and reduced HbA1c levels (MD = −1.70%, 95% CI: −3.18 to −0.22). No statistically significant differences were observed for body weight, BMI, waist circumference, lipid profiles (LDL-C, HDL-C, TC, and TG), total testosterone, SHBG, free androgen index, or blood pressure outcomes (SBP P = 0.05; DBP P = 0.11). Subgroup analyses based on comparator type revealed no significant subgroup differences for the key outcomes. Conclusions: TRE may improve insulin sensitivity-related outcomes—including fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and QUICKI—as well as HbA1c in women with PCOS. However, current evidence does not demonstrate significant effects on anthropometric measures, lipid metabolism, androgen-related outcomes, or blood pressure. Long-term, larger trials are warranted to confirm these benefits.

article.title: Helicobacter pylori Positivity and Quantitative Breath-Test Values in Relation to Lipid and Inflammatory Phenotypes Across Multiple Observational Datasets
article.authors: Kaifeng Sun; Jingjing Xia; Jinting Wang; Le He; Weixuan Yang; Honggang Wang
article.abstract: Quantitative urea breath-test (UBT) values are routinely reported, but their systemic significance beyond Helicobacter pylori positivity remains uncertain. We analyzed 21,195 adults from two health-check cohorts, distinguishing test positivity from delta-over-baseline (DOB) variation among positive participants. We used adjusted models, cohort comparisons and false discovery rate (FDR) correction, with public serological and gastric expression datasets providing exploratory comparisons. Overall, 5484 participants tested positive. In pooled analyses, positivity was associated with higher white blood cell counts (adjusted difference, 0.302 × 109/L; 95% confidence interval, 0.249–0.355). Neutrophil counts were also higher (0.199 × 109/L; 0.164–0.234), whereas high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol was lower (−0.029 mmol/L; −0.038 to −0.019). The HDL association was not clearly replicated in Cohort 2. Associations within the positive range varied with model specification and were not consistently replicated. Additional adjustment for smoking and socioeconomic factors attenuated the leukocyte association in the serological data. Among 3670 positive adults with clinical records, ordinal associations with coded fatty liver, diabetes or hypertension were not FDR significant, and estimates remained imprecise. Gastric expression data supported local inflammation but did not establish a mechanism linking infection to circulating HDL. DOB within the positive range showed no consistent systemic gradient. Residual confounding and imprecise clinical estimates limit interpretation; nonsignificant results do not establish equivalence. These findings neither validate DOB as a measure of bacterial burden nor establish its incremental predictive value. They provide insufficient evidence to use DOB magnitude for metabolic risk assessment or treatment prioritization.

article.title: ITGB1 Contributes to Matrix Stiffness–Induced Lipid Raft Organization and Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cell Migration
article.authors: Xu Zhang; Xinyu Liu; Yan Liu; Guanbin Song
article.abstract: Matrix stiffening is a characteristic pathological feature of the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment and promotes HCC cell migration. Lipid rafts are cholesterol–enriched plasma membrane microdomains involved in cell adhesion and migration. However, whether matrix stiffness promotes lipid raft organization and whether lipid rafts contribute to stiffness–promoted HCC cell migration remain unclear. Using two HCC cell lines cultured on polyacrylamide hydrogels with distinct stiffnesses, we found that stiff matrix enhanced cell migration, increased Area-normalized GM1 fluorescence, and upregulated Caveolin-1 and Flotillin-1 protein expression, consistent with enhanced lipid raft–associated membrane organization. Cholesterol depletion with methyl-β–cyclodextrin (MβCD) reduced GM1 fluorescence and attenuated migration on the Stiff matrix. Cholesterol replenishment partially restored GM1 fluorescence and wound closure after MβCD treatment. To explore how extracellular matrix stiffness is coupled to lipid raft organization, we next examined integrin β1 (ITGB1), a major extracellular matrix mechanoreceptor. The Stiff matrix increased ITGB1 protein expression, ITGB1–GM1 colocalization, and ITGB1 levels in raft-enriched fractions. ITGB1 knockdown reduced GM1 fluorescence, decreased Caveolin-1 and Flotillin-1 levels in raft-enriched fractions, and suppressed migration under Stiff–matrix conditions. These findings support a contributory role for ITGB1 in stiffness-associated lipid raft organization and HCC cell migration.

article.title: Exploratory Untargeted Plasma Lipidomics Suggests Subtype-Associated Lipid Alterations in Hereditary Hemolytic Anemias
article.authors: Neslihan Ayhan Donmez; Yesim Oztas; Tuba Reçber; Emirhan Nemutlu; Cagri Coskun; Sule Unal
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hereditary hemolytic anemias (HHAs) are rare genetic disorders characterized by chronic hemolysis, systemic oxidative stress, and inflammation. Altered lipid homeostasis has previously been reported in HHAs; however, untargeted plasma lipidomic studies comparing HHA subtypes remain limited. This exploratory study aimed to characterize shared and subtype-specific plasma lipid alterations across five HHA subtypes. Methods: Forty-eight participants were enrolled, including 29 patients with HHA (6 with β-thalassemia, 5 with hereditary xerocytosis, 7 with hereditary spherocytosis, 5 with sickle cell disease, and 6 with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia) and 19 healthy controls. Plasma lipids were analyzed by untargeted liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry, followed by multivariate, univariate, and lipid pathway analyses. Results: A total of 375 lipid species were putatively annotated, revealing both shared and putative subtype-specific lipid alterations across the five HHA subtypes. The putatively annotated species Cer 59:7;4O and PC 46:1 remained significantly altered after false discovery rate correction, whereas species such as PC 34:4 and Cer 42:3;2O showed only nominal subtype-specific differences. Mostly nominal alterations in individual ceramide, triglyceride, and phosphatidylcholine species were observed across most hemolytic groups relative to controls. Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia exhibited the fewest nominal differences from controls. Among the 25 species with nominal Kruskal–Wallis differences, SM 37:1;2O was the only lipid species that nominally differed from controls exclusively in this subtype. Conclusions: These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that plasma lipidomics may help characterize lipid alterations accompanying chronic hemolysis. However, the candidate lipid species and predicted pathways require validation in larger, age-matched, independent cohorts.

article.title: Construction of a Dicyanomethylene-4 H -pyran− N , N ′-Diphenyl-dihydrodibenzo[ a , c ]phenazine Conjugate for the Ratiometric Imaging of Lipid Droplets
article.authors: Cheng-Jun Zhao; Hui-Qi Gan; Jin-Kai Qiu; Hai-Hao Han; Xi-Le Hu; Cheng Lian; Tony D. James; Jia Li; Xiao-Peng He
article.abstract: Abstract The aberrant accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs) is a hallmark of a variety of human diseases including the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Here, we constructed a new fluorescent probe (DCM-DPAC-OMe) based on the conjugation between dicyanomethylene-4H-pyran (DCM) and an N,N′-diphenyl-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine (DPAC) derivative as a single-molecule ratiometric imaging agent for LDs. Interestingly, the introduction of the electron-withdrawing DCM group completely reverses the dual-emission pattern of DPAC. This mechanistic reversal was studied by theoretical and fluorescence-based analyses. The probe was used for the imaging of LDs in live cells exhibiting a ratiometric red-to-blue fluorescence emission shift when dissolved by in situ generated intracellular LDs.

article.title: Fenofibrate and Lomitapide in PNPLA2-Related Neutral Lipid-Storage Disease with Myopathy: A Single-Patient In Vitro Approach
article.authors: Kajus Merkevicius; Graeme Preston; Sadie Larson; Nathalie S. Houssin; Sander Houten; Tamas Kozicz; Eva Morava
article.abstract: Neutral lipid-storage disease with myopathy (NLSD-M), caused by pathogenic PNPLA2 variants, has no established treatment. We report a single-patient in vitro study in a 32-year-old female evaluating fenofibrate and lomitapide in patient-derived fibroblasts, selected based on prior therapeutic evidence. Therapeutic endpoints included lipid-droplet (LD) burden, quantified by volumetric z-stack imaging, and bioenergetic profiling, performed by Seahorse respirometry, citrate synthase (CS) activity, cellular NADH capacity, and complex II activity. Fibroblasts were treated with fenofibrate (20 µM) and lomitapide (5 nM) for two weeks. PNPLA2-mutant fibroblasts exhibited LD burden of median 56 droplets per cell, reduced CS activity, a proxy for mitochondrial content, and a hypometabolic profile. Preserved total NADH oxidase and Complex II activities indicated unaffected intrinsic electron transport chain function. Under fenofibrate exposure, most measured bioenergetic parameters in the patient-derived line were closer to the corresponding values in treated controls, but paradoxically increased LD count 1.5–1.9-fold. Lomitapide did not reduce LD burden and further worsened bioenergetic parameters. Loss of PNPLA2-mediated lipolysis produces a dual phenotype of LD accumulation and bioenergetic impairment. Fenofibrate and lomitapide produced divergent and partially adverse effects across these two endpoints. These findings informed precautionary, patient-specific clinical management decisions. Combined LD and metabolic profiling in patient-derived fibroblasts may complement therapeutic decision-making in NLSD-M, pending validation in larger cohorts.

article.title: Mean Platelet Volume and Lipid Profile Levels In Patients With Follicular Thyroid Cancer
article.authors: Çağrı Kızıltunç; Yunus Emre Aytekin; Sinan Yılmaz; Seda Aşkın; Habib Bilen
article.abstract: Background: In this study, we studied plasma mean platelet volume (MPV) and lipid profile levels in the follicular thyroid cancer patients and the correlation in between these parameters. Methods: The levels of MPV and lipid profile tests were assessed in 52 patients with follicular thyroid cancer and 33 control subjects. Results: While serum MPV levels were low in the healthy control group, this value was significantly increased in follicular thyroid cancer patients (FTC) (p = 0.001). In addition, when serum total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels in the healthy control group were compared with FTC patients, it was found that these three values increased statistically significantly (p = 0.001) in these patients. Finally, when the healthy control group and FTC groups were compared for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels; HDL-C values were lower in the FTC groups (p=0.002) while LDL-C values were measured statistically significantly higher (p = 0.001). There was a positive correlation between serum MPV levels and total cholesterol, LDL-C and TG levels (r=0.532, p = 0.001; r=0.701, p = 0.001; r=0.724, p = 0.001, respectively). However, when serum MPV levels and HDL-C levels were compared in terms of correlation, no correlation was detected between them. Finally, a correlation was also determined between measured tumor dimensions, total cholesterol, LDL-C and TG levels (r=0.756, p = 0.001; r=0.493, p = 0.001; r=0.527, p = 0.001, respectively). No statistically significant correlation was observed between MPV and tumor size (r = 0.239, p = 0.088) Conclusions: The results of the present study demonstrated that the patients with FTC are affected to increased serum MPV and changed lipid profile values which contribute to increased risk factor of cardiovascular diseases.

article.title: First-Trimester Lipid Profile and Subsequent Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Case–Control Study
article.authors: Erinc Tekin; Askın Yıldız; Simge Tezel Yozgat
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic complication of pregnancy, and identifying women at increased risk early in gestation may facilitate closer surveillance and timely preventive strategies. This study aimed to investigate the association between first-trimester maternal lipid profile parameters and subsequent GDM and to evaluate their discriminatory performance for GDM. Methods: This retrospective case–control study included singleton pregnancies followed at İzmir Kâtip Çelebi University Atatürk Training and Research Hospital between January 2015 and December 2019. Serum lipid parameters obtained between 11 + 0 and 13 + 6 weeks of gestation were retrospectively retrieved and compared between women who subsequently developed GDM and those who did not. Associations with GDM were evaluated using binary logistic regression, and discriminatory performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Of 367 women assessed for eligibility, 336 were included in the final analysis (201 with GDM and 135 controls). Women who developed GDM had higher triglyceride levels (median: 138 vs. 103 mg/dL; p 125 mg/dL yielded 62.69% sensitivity and 74.81% specificity. Conclusions: First-trimester maternal lipid alterations, particularly higher triglyceride levels, were associated with subsequent GDM. However, triglycerides demonstrated only modest discriminatory performance and should not be considered a stand-alone predictor. Routinely available lipid parameters may provide additional information for early GDM risk stratification.

article.title: Structural basis for inhibition of the lipid flippase MurJ by phage lysis protein SglPP7 suggests convergent evolution with other Sgl peptides
article.authors: Kaito Hosoda; Hidetaka Kohga; Sixian Wu; Hiroyuki Tanaka; Hideki Shigematsu; Ryoji Miyazaki; Min Fey Chek; Tomoya Tsukazaki
article.abstract: Some bacteriophages encode lysis proteins that inhibit essential bacterial processes, and elucidating their mechanisms is valuable for developing antibacterial strategies against drug-resistant pathogens. We determined the cryo-EM structure of the complex between the essential Escherichia coli lipid II flippase MurJ and the phage lysis protein Sgl PP7 . Structural, mutational, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation analyses revealed that Sgl PP7 binds along the intramembrane cleft of MurJ and inserts its C-terminal tail into the internal cavity, stabilizing MurJ in an outward-facing conformation. Structural comparison with Lys M (Sgl M ) and Sgl CJ3 showed that these sequence-divergent Sgl proteins stabilize MurJ in the outward-facing conformation through distinct binding modes, consistent with the possibility of convergent evolution toward MurJ inhibition.

article.title: The Influence of Microbial Fermentation on Growth Performance, Protein Solubility, and Lipid Modulation in the Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) Larvae
article.authors: Hafiza Mehwish Malik; Khurshied Ahmed Khan; Khurram Yousaf; Shehzad Abid Khan; Imran Tarique; Saadia Andleeb; Hussnain Ahmed Janjua
article.abstract: Organic waste is being generated at an increasing pace across the globe, creating an urgent need for sustainable approaches to convert organic residues into value-added bioproducts. Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL, Hermetia illucens) represent an effective biotechnological solution for waste valorization due to their ability to transform organic waste into nutrient-rich biomass. This study evaluated the impacts of microbial fermentation of fruit–vegetable and kitchen waste on BSFL growth performance and nutritional composition. Substrates were fermented using protease- and cellulase-producing bacterial strains, including Bacillus subtilis (S1), Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (KSM12) previously reported from our lab, and Lactobacillus rhamnosus (FM9), and Lactobacillus fermentum (FM16) from Microbiology Research Group collection. Sixteen treatments were formulated using specific and mixed bacterial inoculations to evaluate their individual and combined effects on larval development and nutrient assimilation. The findings indicated that substrate fermentation extensively enhanced larval mass, length, survival rate, bioconversion efficiency, efficiency of conversion of ingested feed, conversion ratio, and waste reduction index compared with unfermented substrates. The nutritional value of BSFL was also increased, with increased crude protein and lipid content. Protein fraction analysis demonstrated higher levels of soluble proteins (albumins and globulins) and reduced prolamin and glutelin fractions, indicating enhanced protein digestibility. Lipid profiling by GC–MS analysis of selected groups exhibited improved medium-chain fatty acids, particularly lauric (C12:0) and palmitic (C16:0) acids. Overall, microbial fermentation of BSFL substrates boosts organic waste utilization and validates sustainable waste valorization within a circular bioeconomy, providing nutrient-rich feed components for poultry and aquaculture sectors.

article.title: Lipid Nanoparticles Enhance the Antichlamydial Efficacy of Ciprofloxacin and Sulfamethoxazole–Trimethoprim
article.authors: József Nyári; Valéria Endrész; Katalin Burián; Dezső Virok; Maryana Salamah; Gábor Katona; Anita Bogdanov
article.abstract: Background/Objectives:Chlamydia trachomatis (C. trachomatis) infections represent a major global public health concern, with over 100 million new cases annually. Although commonly used antibiotics like azithromycin and doxycycline are generally effective, increasing antibiotic resistance and therapeutic failures highlight the need for alternative treatments and innovative delivery systems. Methods: The efficacy of alternative antimicrobial agents, including ciprofloxacin and the combination of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, was evaluated in both free and nano-formulated states. Drug encapsulation was achieved using liposomes as well as niosomal and aspasomal delivery systems. In vitro experiments were conducted on HeLa cells infected with C. trachomatis serovar D. Host cell viability and cytotoxicity were assessed using the MTT assay, while bacterial genomic load was quantified by qPCR. Results: Encapsulation significantly enhanced antimicrobial activity, with certain antibiotic-loaded lipid nanoparticles demonstrating 2–4 times greater effectiveness compared to their free counterparts. The prepared formulations exhibited no cytotoxic effects and did not interfere with PCR-based detection, confirming that observed outcomes reflect true antimicrobial activity. Conclusions: Nanocarrier-based drug delivery, particularly using lipid nanoparticles, represents a promising strategy for improving the therapeutic management of C. trachomatis infections. These findings highlight the potential of delivery platforms to enhance antibiotic performance and support the development of more effective and innovative antimicrobial therapies.

article.title: Profiling Temperature-Dependent Lipid Remodeling in Yersinia pestis Using Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry and Ozonolysis
article.authors: Dylan H. Ross; Joshua R. Hansen; Meagan C. Burnet; Josie G. Eder; Brooke L. Deatherage Kaiser; Xueyun Zheng
article.venue: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry
article.abstract: Abstract Yersinia pestisundergoes dramatic physiological changes as it transitions from its flea vector (∼20–30 °C) to mammalian hosts (37 °C), including remodeling of its cell envelope lipids to evade innate immunity and enhance virulence. While various temperature-dependent changes in this organism have been previously documented, the broader lipidome remains poorly characterized. We applied liquid chromatography coupled with ion mobility spectrometry and tandem mass spectrometry (LC-IMS-MS/MS), in addition to ozone-induced dissociation (OzID), to comprehensively profile lipids in three attenuated Y. pestis strains (A1122, KIM D27, and KIM D1) grown at 30 and 37 °C. Untargeted lipidomic analysis identified 97 lipids across multiple classes, with principal component analysis revealing temperature-dependent clustering patterns distinct from strain-specific variations. Comparison of lipid profiles between temperatures revealed many significantly differentially expressed lipids per strain, with most strain-specific responses rather than shared across all strains. OzID fragmentation successfully identified double-bond positions for common unsaturated fatty acids and lysophospholipids, also enabling structural discrimination between monounsaturated and cyclopropyl fatty acid isomers. Notably, lipids containing cyclopropyl fatty acids were significantly upregulated at 37 °C across all three strains, suggesting a conserved temperature-responsive mechanism for enhancing membrane stability during mammalian host infection. Our study demonstrates that comprehensive, high-detailed, structurally resolved lipidomics reveals temperature-dependent lipid remodeling characteristics in Y. pestis that may support host transition and virulence, with potential applications for identifying lipid biomarkers.

article.title: A Liposome-Reconstitution Assay Reveals Lipid-Dependent Modulation of EGFR Kinase Activity
article.authors: Ronald Arlet Villaber; Mahboubeh Ghahremani; Benedicta Quainoo; Adam W. Smith
article.abstract: Abstract The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a receptor tyrosine kinase whose activity is regulated by ligand binding and dimerization but also by its membrane environment. Although anionic lipids such as phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) have been implicated in modulating EGFR activation, direct biochemical evidence for lipid-dependent effects on EGFR catalytic function has not yet been reported. Here, we reconstitute the catalytically active intracellular domain (ICD) of EGFR (residues 669–1210) on synthetic liposomes to probe the influence of lipid composition on kinase activity. We find that both PIP2 and PS suppress the apparent catalytic output of membrane-tethered EGFR-ICD and produce distinct changes in ATP-dependent kinetic parameters. PIP2 produced stronger suppression than PS under matched assay conditions, consistent with electrostatic modulation of EGFR-ICD catalytic output. These results show that defined anionic lipid compositions can modulate EGFR-ICD catalytic activity and establish a platform for quantifying membrane-dependent regulation of receptor kinase activity.

article.title: Microfluidic fabrication of lipid-coated PLGA nanoparticles co-delivering CuS and curcumin for combined chemo-photothermal therapy
article.authors: Alhasan Mohammed; Yu Xia; Hemin Roghzai; Bo Zhang; Xiubo Zhao
article.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, with chemotherapy serving as a primary treatment modality. However, its clinical efficacy is often compromised by systemic toxicity, poor drug solubility, and non-specific targeting. To address these limitations, we report the fabrication of lipid-coated poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) co-delivering curcumin (Cur) and copper sulfide (CuS) for combined chemo-photothermal therapy using a microfluidic swirl mixer. The microfluidic platform enables controlled, reproducible preparation of the NPs with low polydispersity (PDI) and high co-encapsulation efficiency of both compounds. The primary innovation of this work lies in integrating a PLGA -lipid hybrid architecture with simultaneous encapsulation of a model anticancer drug Cur and an NIR-responsive photothermal agent, CuS into a single formulation. Optimization of the flow rate ratio (FRR) and total flow rate (TFR) enabled precise tuning of particle size and physicochemical properties. CuS/Cur@PLGA@Lipid NPs the sustained drug release from the PLGA core with the improved colloidal stability and cellular uptake provided by the lipid shell. In vitro evaluations demonstrated pH-sensitive release, with accelerated Cur liberation under acidic microenvironments relative to physiological conditions. Furthermore, the NPs exhibited pronounced cytotoxicity against cervical cancer cells (HeLa), which was significantly enhanced under NIR laser irradiation via CuS-driven photothermal ablation. Quantitative fluorescence and flow-cytometry analyses confirmed superior cellular uptake and intracellular retention compared to free Cur, while multicellular tumor spheroid models demonstrated enhanced three-dimensional antitumor efficacy. Overall, this study provides an in vitro proof-of-concept for the high-throughput potential for the production of lipid-coated PLGA NPs with dual chemo-photothermal therapeutic potential.

article.title: Targeting ALOX15 with a ROS‐Responsive Lipid Nanoparticle for the Treatment of Allergic Conjunctivitis and Its Comorbidity Dry Eye Disease
article.authors: Zhi Wang; Huimin Shan; Rui Yao; Jingchen Li; Xiaohua Yu; Xiaomei Tang; Xibo Ma; Ming Wang; Yong Tao; Xiaojun Wang
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Allergic conjunctivitis (AC) and its frequent comorbidity, dry eye disease (DED), represent prevalent ocular surface inflammatory disorders, significantly impairing patients’ visual quality. Arachidonic acid 15‐lipoxygenase (ALOX15) emerges as a common pathogenic factor, mediating inflammatory responses and lipid peroxidation in both conditions. Here, a therapeutic strategy is designed based on reactive oxygen species‐responsive lipid nanoparticles loaded with siALOX15‐5 (rLNP@siALOX15‐5). This strategy enhances ocular penetration and sustains silencing of ALOX15, alleviating the symptoms of AC by executing a dual mechanism. It simultaneously suppresses multiple signaling pathways involved in the inflammatory response, particularly cytokine‐cytokine receptor interaction and chemokine signaling pathway, while potently inhibiting lipid peroxidation and enhancing antioxidant defenses. In an autoimmune‐related DED mice model, rLNP@siALOX15‐5 alleviates clinical symptoms and restores ocular surface homeostasis. Moreover, in the AC and DED comorbid model, it outperforms cyclosporine A and TobraDex monotherapies, achieving effects comparable to their combination. These studies not only validate the value of ALOX15 as a common therapeutic target for both AC and DED but also establish rLNP@siALOX15‐5 as an effective strategy for treating these two associated ocular surface diseases through its dual‐regulatory mechanism.

article.title: Trimester-Specific Associations Between Maternal Fatty Acid Ratios and Cognitive and Executive Functioning in 4-Year-Old Children
article.authors: Xiruo Kou; Josefa Canals; Victoria Arija
article.abstract: Purpose: Early prenatal fatty acid balance is vital for brain development, yet trimester-specific effects on long-term neurodevelopment remain unclear. This study examined associations between maternal omega-6/omega-3 (n-6/n-3) ratios in the first and third trimesters and child neurodevelopment at age four. Methods: In the ECLIPSES cohort (n = 223), maternal serum n-3 and n-6 fatty acids were measured at 12 and 36 gestational weeks. At age four, children’s cognitive and executive function were assessed using the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence (WPPSI), and the Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF)—Preschool Version, respectively. Multivariable regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. Results: A higher n-6/n-3 ratio in the first trimester was significantly associated with poorer executive functioning, as reflected by higher BRIEF scores indicating greater difficulties in inhibition (b = 2.45, p = 0.002), working memory (b = 1.87, p = 0.030), planning/organization (b = 2.20, p = 0.004), and the Global Executive Composite (b = 1.96, p = 0.006). Higher first-trimester ratios were also associated with lower WPPSI working memory performance (b = −2.14, p = 0.013), while general cognitive abilities were largely unaffected. Conclusions: An elevated maternal n-6/n-3 ratio in early pregnancy is associated with poorer executive function in preschool children, whereas evidence linking these ratios to general cognition remains limited. These findings indicate that associations between fatty acid balance and executive function were mainly observed during the first trimester.

article.title: Long-Term Palmitoleic Acid-Enriched Marine Oil Ingestion Attenuates Adiposity and Glucose Intolerance in Cafeteria Diet-Fed Mice
