article.title: Beyond reproduction: the emerging role of FSH in postmenopausal aging.
article.authors: Vallejo MS, Paradas A, Neira H.
article.venue: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
article.abstract: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

article.title: Biomimetic Nanomedicine for Aging‐Impaired Bone Regeneration: From Microenvironmental Dysfunction to Precision Therapeutics
article.authors: Zeyu Wang; He Zhang; Simo Liu; Rui Wang; Yiran Wei; Kailu Zheng; Yanming Guo; Min Li; Dian Yuan; Yuxin Liu; Lifang Feng; Yongping Ma; Yan Liu
article.abstract: Aging‐impaired bone regeneration represents a major clinical challenge due to diminished regenerative capacity and a progressively deteriorated microenvironment. This dysfunction arises from the interplay of cellular senescence, chronic inflammation driven by the senescence‐associated secretory phenotype (SASP), vascular insufficiency, and disrupted neuroregulation, collectively limiting effective bone repair. Conventional therapies, largely relying on single‐target interventions or passive delivery, remain insufficient to address these multifactorial barriers. Biomimetic nanomedicine offers a promising strategy by integrating biologically inspired designs with therapeutic cargos. Based on the principal biological feature emulated, these systems can be organized into four operational categories: cell‐derived, extracellular vesicle‐inspired, biomolecule‐inspired, and microenvironment‐inspired platforms. Biomimetic features dictate biological recognition, localization, retention, and stimulus responsiveness, whereas therapeutic cargos or active materials mediate downstream regenerative effects. To bridge this design‐based taxonomy with the biology of aging‐impaired bone repair, this review organizes current evidence within a pathology–design–outcome framework centered on four major pathological barriers: cellular dysfunction, osteoimmune dysregulation, vascular impairment, and disrupted neural regulation. This framework links age‐related pathological deficits with biomimetic design principles and regenerative outcomes, while highlighting key priorities for more precise and clinically translatable bone regeneration.

article.title: Beyond Sun Protection Factor: Astaxanthin Is a Multifunctional Marine-Derived Compound for Antioxidant and Anti-Aging Skin Protection
article.authors: Levent Alparslan; Tunay Doğan; Gülşah Torkay-Çay; Ayça Bal-Öztürk; Tuğba Sağır; Emília Sousa; Anake Kijjoa
article.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced oxidative stress is a major cause of skin photoaging, prompting interest in multifunctional antioxidants of marine origin for topical photoprotection. Astaxanthin, a xanthophyll carotenoid predominantly obtained from the microalga Haematococcus pluvialis, exhibits antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and matrix-metalloproteinase (MMP)-modulating activities relevant to skin protection. This study aimed to formulate and systematically characterize oil-in-water (O/W) sunscreen emulsions containing 1%, 2.5%, and 5% (w/w) natural astaxanthin-containing extract (AstaReal® P4AF), in combination with an inorganic titanium dioxide (TiO2) UV filter, and to evaluate the influence of astaxanthin concentration on formulation performance and biological tolerability. Formulations were characterized in terms of viscosity, antioxidant activity using the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) assay, mechanical and adhesive performance using back-extrusion and adhesion tests, in vitro sun protection factor (SPF), UVA protection, water resistance (WR), and local tissue tolerability using the in ovo chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model. Viscosity increased with AstaReal® P4AF concentration at both temperatures (from 3801.9 to 5704.6 mPa·s at 25 °C, and from 1931.8 to 5118.9 mPa s at 36 °C), with the 5% AstaReal® P4AF formulation showing the greatest thermal stability. DPPH radical scavenging activity increased markedly with AstaReal® P4AF concentration up to 2.5% (33.15% at 1% and 63.04% at 2.5%) and remained comparable at 5% (62.62%), versus 22.05% for the placebo formulation. Back-extrusion analysis revealed a non-linear, concentration-dependent effect on consistency and firmness, peaking at 2.5% AstaReal® P4AF, while adhesion parameters remained statistically unaffected across concentrations. SPF and UVA protection factor decreased with increasing AstaReal® P4AF concentration (74.37 to 35.02 and 37.62 to 19.78, respectively), whereas WR was improved at the highest concentration. CAM histopathological scoring indicated that AstaReal® P4AF incorporation did not increase tissue injury relative to the formulation base. These findings indicate that AstaReal® P4AF concentration critically influences the physicochemical and photoprotective balance of sunscreen emulsions, supporting further optimization toward a multifunctional, marine-derived ingredient.

article.title: Gender affirmation concerns of aging transgender women: findings from qualitative listening sessions
article.authors: Megan Lau; Naya Velazco; Jamie Arangure; Maile Young Karris; Jill Blumenthal
article.abstract: Abstract Older transgender persons are a specific minoritized population with unique health and care concerns. The needs and priorities of older transgender adults are poorly understood, likely due to implicit biases surrounding age, sexuality, and gender. Four listening sessions were conducted with transgender women, ages 55 years old and above, in the San Diego and Palm Springs area between August and November 2023. Two sessions were held in-person in English, one was held virtually in English, and one was held in-person in Spanish. Individuals were recruited through local clinics, community-based organizations, and social media. All sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed, translated as needed, and analyzed using a rapid thematic analysis approach. Nineteen individuals participated (median age 62 years, range 55–87). Of the 16 who completed the demographics questionnaire, all identified as transgender female and/or female. Four identified as Hispanic/Latinx, 7 as White, 1 as Black/African American, 1 as American Indian/Alaska Native, and 3 as mixed race. Six were living with HIV and taking anti-retroviral therapy. Participants expressed concerns about aging, including companionship, financial security, access to routine healthcare maintenance screenings, and safe housing. These concerns were balanced by future aging goals like living authentically and mentoring younger generations. 75% were using gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT), and most shared frustrations with inconsistent provider guidance on GAHT duration, dosing, method of administration, and long-term risks. Many viewed GAHT as essential, despite potential risks. While all participants reported positive and negative healthcare experiences, many emphasized a desire for providers to address mental and sexual health more openly and to be better informed about community resources. Older transgender adults represent a heterogenous population with distinct medical, psychological, and social needs. Identifying their key concerns is essential to advancing patient-centered, transgender-informed research and improving care for this historically underserved population.

article.title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis.
article.authors: Stein SN, Braid LR.
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age‐associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age‐associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis‐based model in which MSCs translate age‐associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell‐supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine‐directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC‐derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue‐resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

article.title: Sociodemographic patterns of psychological distress, non-communicable diseases, and disability among south Africans 60 years and older: a generalized structural equation modelling approach
article.authors: Sbonelo Chamane; Simangaliso Mnyandu; Lehlogonolo Makola; Musawenkosi Mabaso; Zaynab Essack; Ronel Sewpaul; Sean Jooste; Sizulu Moyo; Nompumelelo Zungu; Khangelani Zuma
article.abstract: Background South Africa is experiencing a steady increase in ageing population alongside a growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs), disability and mental health challenges. However, the interplay between these conditions in later life remains underexplored. Methods The study draws data from the sixth South African National HIV Prevalence, Incidence and Behaviour Survey which used a multi-stage, stratified, cluster random sampling design. The analysis estimated the prevalence of self-reported psychological distress, NCDs and disability among adults aged 60 years and older. Sociodemographic factors associated with these outcomes were examined using a Generalized Structural Equation Model. Results Among adults aged 60 years and older, the prevalence of psychological distress was 3.1%, NCDs 59.7%, and disability 64.1%. Having at least one NCD significantly increased the likelihood of psychological distress, while having a disability increased the likelihood of having an NCD. Women and those aged 70–79 years had higher odds of both NCDs, and disability compared to men and those aged 60–69 years, respectively. Compared to Black Africans, participants from other racial groups had lower odds of distress but higher odds of NCDs. Relative to primary education, secondary education lowered the odds of distress and disability but increased the odds of NCD, while tertiary education was only protective against disability. Unemployment was associated with higher odds of NCDs, while residing in rural informal areas and never being married was associated with lower odds of NCDs only, compared to those who were employed, living in urban areas and ever married, respectively. Conclusion The findings highlight strong interconnections between chronic disease, disability and mental health in later life, shaped by age, sex, education, marital status and place of residence. Interventions that integrate social, physical and psychological care are essential to improving healthy ageing outcomes in South Africa.

article.title: Mechanisms governing calendar aging in three-electrode lithium-ion cells with layered oxide cathode and milled silicon anode
article.authors: Hrishikesh Tupkar; Pavan Badami; Ankit Verma; Avi Gargye; Marco-Tulio F. Rodrigues; Andrew Colclasure; Matthew A. Gebbie; Ilya Shkrob; Daniel P. Abraham
article.abstract: Calendar aging is a major degradation pathway for silicon-containing lithium-ion batteries because parasitic reactions continue during open-circuit storage, consuming cyclable lithium and altering electrode behavior. Here, we investigate the calendar aging of three-electrode cells, with LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) and silicon (Si) electrodes, over an 11-month period to identify electrode-specific degradation mechanisms. Capacity measurements, voltage-relaxation analysis, impedance evaluation and post-test characterization were used to monitor evolution of the individual electrodes. The Si anode dominates full-cell voltage relaxation and discharge impedance throughout aging, while progressive loss of lithium inventory continuously shifts operating windows of both electrodes, forcing the NMC811 cathode to increasingly higher states of delithiation. Voltage-relaxation analysis reveals two kinetically distinct equilibration processes, with the longer-timescale process evolving systematically within each month-long storage interval and partially resetting following the reference performance test (RPT) cycling indicating a strong dependence on the electrochemical history of the Si electrode. Although the harvested NMC811 and Si electrodes exhibit only minor capacity loss, the increase in anode impedance demonstrates evolution of the SEI and the Si interfacial environment. These results indicate that calendar-aging-induced capacity loss is governed primarily by interfacial reactions and associated loss of lithium inventory rather than extensive loss of active material. More broadly, the results demonstrate the utility of voltage-relaxation analysis as a non-destructive diagnostic for resolving electrode-specific degradation mechanisms in Si-containing lithium-ion cells.

article.title: Rosa rugosa Root Extract as a Functional Food Ingredient, Mitigating UVB ‐Induced Skin Aging Through MAPK / AP ‐1 and AGE ‐ RAGE Pathway Modulation
article.authors: Min Ji Gu; Guijae Yoo; Sang‐Hoon Lee; Ho‐Young Park; Yoonsook Kim; Donghwan Kim; Sang Keun Ha
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Rosa rugosa root extract (RR‐r) has been used in East Asian medicine to treat metabolic disorders, including diabetes and alcohol‐induced liver toxicity. Although RR‐r has been demonstrated to exhibit anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant properties, further research is required to elucidate its protective effects against ultraviolet B (UVB)‐induced skin photoaging. In this study, high‐performance liquid chromatography was used to identify rutin as the major indicator compound of RR‐r. The photoprotective activity of RR‐r was evaluated using a mouse model of UVB‐induced skin damage. Mice were orally administered RR‐r (100 or 200 mg/kg) for 8 weeks during UVB irradiation. RR‐r significantly alleviated UVB‐induced wrinkle formation, epidermal thickening, and collagen fiber degradation. The assessment of skin morphology and hydration was conducted through the use of histological staining (H&E and Masson's trichrome), wrinkle and moisture analysis, and enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay quantification of hyaluronic acid. Western blotting revealed that RR‐r increased pro‐collagen type I, tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 1, hyaluronan, collagen‐1 while reducing the matrix metalloproteinase family, hyaluronidase 1 and hyaluronidase 2. A further mechanistic analysis revealed that RR‐r inhibited UVB‐induced phosphorylation of mitogen‐activated protein kinase pathway components and downstream activator protein‐1 factors. Furthermore, RR‐r significantly suppressed UVB‐induced accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and expression of their receptor, RAGE. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that oral RR‐r effectively protects against UVB‐induced photoaging by regulating wrinkle‐related proteins, enhancing skin hydration, and modulating MAPK/AP‐1 and AGE‐RAGE signaling. Thus, RR‐r may represent a promising natural candidate for skin anti‐aging interventions.

article.title: Lived Experiences and Perceptions of Aging and Quality of Life Among Elderly People in the City of Buta: A Qualitative Study Expériences Vécues, Perceptions du Vieillissement et Qualité de Vie des Personnes Âgées dans la Ville de Buta : Une Étude Qualitative
article.authors: Masikini Ewale Faustin; Bertine Mbongopasi Ekeni; Musenga Tshibangu John; Emmanuel Kitete Mulongo; Ngbolua Koto-Te- Nyiwa; Jacques Lofandjola Masumbuko; Mukandu Basua Leyka
article.abstract: ABSTRACTIntroduction. Aging presents a significant public health challenge in low-income regions like the Democratic Republic of the Congo, particularly in Buta, where older adults face socioeconomic vulnerabilities and social marginalization. This study investigates the lived experiences of older adults, focusing on their perceptions of aging and quality of life. Methodology. Utilizing a qualitative phenomenological approach, 20 participants aged 60 and above were interviewed to explore themes such as perceptions of aging, living conditions, family dynamics, and care access. Results. The analysis identified three primary themes: economic precariousness linked to a lack of pensions, social isolation resulting from younger generations' migration, and challenges in accessing care due to costs and staff shortages. Despite these adversities, some participants demonstrated resilience through spirituality, community support, and acceptance of aging, which contributed to their well-being. Conclusion. The findings indicate that social, economic, and institutional factors significantly affect the experiences of older adults in Buta and suggest the necessity for active aging programs, age-appropriate care services, and enhanced community support in local health policies to improve their quality of life and reduce vulnerabilities.RÉSUMÉ Introduction. Le vieillissement représente un défi majeur de santé publique dans les régions à faibles revenus comme la République Démocratique du Congo, en particulier à Buta, où les personnes âgées font face à des vulnérabilités socio-économiques et à une marginalisation sociale. Cette étude examine l'expérience vécue par les personnes âgées, en se concentrant sur leurs perceptions du vieillissement et leur qualité de vie. Méthodologie. Selon une approche phénoménologique qualitative, 20 participants âgés de 60 ans et plus ont été interrogés pour explorer des thèmes tels que les perceptions du vieillissement, les conditions de vie, la dynamique familiale et l'accès aux soins. Résultats. L'analyse a identifié trois thèmes principaux : la précarité économique liée au manque de pensions, l'isolement social résultant de la migration des jeunes générations, et les difficultés d'accès aux soins dues aux coûts et au manque de personnel. Malgré ces adversités, certains participants ont fait preuve de résilience à travers la spiritualité, le soutien communautaire et l'acceptation du vieillissement, ce qui a contribué à leur bien-être. Conclusion. Les résultats indiquent que les facteurs sociaux, économiques et institutionnels affectent de manière significative l'expérience des personnes âgées à Buta et suggèrent la nécessité de programmes de vieillissement actif, de services de soins adaptés à l'âge et d'un soutien communautaire renforcé dans les politiques de santé locales pour améliorer leur qualité de vie et réduire leurs vulnérabilités

article.title: Enhancing Thermal Longevity and Transdermal Delivery of High-Dose Vitamin C: The Role of Particle-Reinforced Thixotropic Networks in Anhydrous Matrices
article.authors: Hyungjoon Jeon; Jiwon Choi; Jong Gu Won; Sungho Cha; Sojung Lee; Woonghee Cho; Sang-Wook Park; Moonju Kim; Nam Seo Son
article.abstract: Background: Topical delivery of high-dose L-ascorbic acid (AA) is limited by rapid oxidative degradation in water and physical particle aggregation in lipophilic vehicles. Here, we engineered an anhydrous delivery system combining a structured wax–oil matrix with high-shear roll-milling process to stabilize up to 40% AA. Methods: Dispersion morphology and 3D ultrastructure were evaluated via optical microscopy and Cryo-SEM. Rheological flow profiles and thixotropic recovery were measured using a rotational rheometer. Accelerated chemical stability was monitored at 0–50 °C for 4 weeks via RP-HPLC. Percutaneous delivery kinetics were investigated across synthetic biomimetic membranes (Strat-M®) using a sequential toner-application regimen. Biological efficacy was clinically assessed in 15 human volunteers over 4 weeks using 3D optical skin analysis (ANTERA 3D®). Results: The high-shear roll-milling process homogenized AA aggregates into micro-dispersions, establishing an apparent yield-stress network with an ultra-high zero-shear plateau (105 P) and shear-thinning thixotropy. The milled formulation retained highly stable chemical potency (93.99%) at 50 °C for 4 weeks. Sequential application with an aqueous toner facilitated in situ active dissolution at the barrier interface, increasing the absolute delivered payload from the 20% system by >10.5-fold relative to the 5% formulation. A 4-week clinical evaluation confirmed measurable improvements in skin brightness (∆L* = 1.66%), and reductions in hyper-pigmentation (25.65%), wrinkle area (31.17%), and pore area (26.00%). Conclusions: The milling-integrated anhydrous matrix provides a robust formulation framework that resolves physical sedimentation and oxidative instability while enabling the stable delivery of high-dose payloads via enhanced thermodynamic concentration gradients for enhanced dermatological rejuvenation.

article.title: BL-DVDMS-mediated photodynamic therapy induces oxidative response associated with cellular senescence via p53/GADD45A signaling in lung cancer
article.authors: Xing Li; Minghai Ma; Yibo Mei; Pan Zhang; Xiao Liang; Rou Huang; Yuanquan Zhang; Dalin He; Lei Wang
article.abstract: Current chemotherapy options for lung cancer (LC) are limited by poor tumor selectivity, systemic toxicity, and acquired resistance. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers a promising minimally invasive modality as a potential conservative or complementary approach, yet its clinical adoption has been constrained by suboptimal photosensitizers and unclear mechanisms. This study investigated a novel PDT regimen combining a 450 nm blue laser with the photosensitizer sinoporphyrin sodium (DVDMS) to address these limitations in LC. Our findings demonstrate that BL-DVDMS treatment selectively inhibits lung cancer cell proliferation while sparing normal bronchial epithelial cells. Low-dose PDT induces a moderate oxidative stress response, leading to DNA damage and G2/M cell cycle arrest. Importantly, this treatment triggers a senescence-associated phenotype, evidenced by increased SA-β-Gal activity and elevated secretion of SASP factors (IL-6, IL-8), accompanied by altered p53/GADD45 A signaling. These effects are abrogated by ROS scavenging or p53 inhibition, indicating that the oxidative response plays a central role in the observed antitumor activity. In the subcutaneous xenograft model, this regimen significantly suppresses tumor growth with no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work identifies BL-DVDMS-mediated PDT as a mechanistically defined, senescence-associated therapeutic strategy. This study provides a potential complementary treatment option for inoperable LC patients, particularly for managing residual disease and enhancing existing therapies.

article.title: hiPSC Extract Attenuates Senescence-Associated Phenotypes in AB-MSCs In Vitro
article.authors: Yuanyuan Pan; Lumiao Zhang; Rongyuan Zhu; Fangfang Sun; Guofeng Wu
article.abstract: Background: Bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells (BMSCs) are widely used as seed cells in bone tissue engineering. However, sufficient cell quantities for effective engineering typically require prolonged in vitro expansion of BMSCs, which can lead to cellular senescence after excessive subculturing. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the effects of human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) extract on replicative senescence, clonogenic ability, proliferation-associated characteristics, and osteogenic differentiation capacity of human alveolar bone-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (AB-MSCs). Methods: AB-MSCs were isolated from alveolar bone fragments discarded during dental implant surgery. Cells were divided into three experimental groups: P3 AB-MSCs (Young), P10 AB-MSCs (senescence-associated, YRS), and P10 AB-MSCs treated with hiPSC extract (YRSiE). Senescence markers, clonogenic ability, proliferation-associated characteristics, osteogenic potential, mRNA sequencing and pathway-related expression changes were compared among groups. Small RNA sequencing on hiPSCs and AB-MSCs with qRT-PCR validation were performed to identify candidate miRNAs in hiPSC extract that were differentially expressed in this setting. Results: In the presence of hiPSC extract, senescent AB-MSCs showed altered morphology, a lower proportion of β-galactosidase-positive cells, higher Ki67 expression, and lower expression of the senescence-associated genes and proteins P16 and P21. Treated senescent AB-MSCs also showed higher proliferation-associated metabolic activity, clonogenicity, and osteogenic differentiation than untreated senescent cells. Pluripotency-related genes (NANOG, OCT-4) and osteogenic markers (ALP, RUNX2, OCN) were higher in the treated group. qRT-PCR validation of small RNA sequencing data showed that miR-514a-3p, miR-582-5p and miR-520c-3p were upregulated in senescent AB-MSCs after hiPSC extract treatment. Concurrently, pathway enrichment and pathway-related expression changes were consistent with an association with the NF-κB pathway. Conclusion: In this in vitro study, hiPSC extract attenuates senescence-associated phenotypes in AB-MSCs, and the observed transcriptional and pathway-related expression changes were consistent with NF-κB pathway enrichment, with the identified miRNAs upregulated in treated cells and previously reported to target NF-κB pathway components. However, these mechanisms require further validation.

article.title: SenescenceBioKG reveals full-text-supported biomaterial design, mechanisms, and regeneration patterns in senescence-oriented tissue engineering
article.authors: Shengyue Li; Xinxin Jing; Jin Tan; Qiang Zhang
article.abstract: Background Senescence-oriented biomaterial studies provide evidence regarding material design, responsive behavior, cellular targets, mechanisms, regeneration, and validation across different full-text sections. However, publication-level labels cannot reliably answer questions that require several of these relations to occur in the same study. Methods We constructed SenescenceBioKG based on 283 original experimental or translational full-text studies. Candidate relations were generated under a typed ontology, adjudicated against same-record evidence, linked to unique evidence identifiers, and canonicalized into a queryable graph. Fifteen competency questions were evaluated using graph traversal and an independently implemented dataframe method. A local read-only R Shiny Explorer was developed for evidence inspection. Results The frozen graph contained 654 canonical nodes, 1,868 supported edges, and 1,868 linked evidence records. Within the curated corpus, strict material responsiveness comprised 64 RESPONDS TO edges from 55 studies and 55 material platforms, led by acidic pH and reactive oxygen species. Same-study analyses recovered responsive-design modules and 35 complete target-cell–mechanism–regeneration modules. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells, senescent cells, and macrophage or innate immune populations were recurrent targets, whereas oxidative-stress control, mitochondrial homeostasis, and NF-κB/Senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) signaling frequently accompanied bone, wound/skin, cartilage, and disc endpoints. Validation was concentrated in Cell and Small-Animal studies; Organoid/chip and Large-Animal evidence was sparse, and no Clinical edge was supported. All 15 queries achieved exact-set agreement between the two implementations, with macro precision, recall, and F1 values of 1.00. Conclusion SenescenceBioKG provides a full-text-supported structure for examining smart and responsive biomaterial design, fabrication, cellular evidence, regenerative outcomes, and validation gaps. Its provenance model separates co-supported evidence from causal inference and supports reproducible, material-centered retrieval.

article.title: Effects of chiglitazar on glycemic, lipid, and hepatic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
article.authors: Abdulaziz Altamimi; Yousef H Albegamy; Jehan Al Al Omar; Mohammed M Alkehili; Bader Abdullah M Alshajry; Musab H Alruwaili; Remas Mohammed Alqahtani; Farah K Alruqi; Majed F Alosemy; Talal Mohammed Alotaibi; Mohammed Abdullah Alkhulayfi; Afnan D Alhejaili; Mansuor A Alanazi
article.venue: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
article.abstract: PURPOSE: Chiglitazar is a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pan-agonist with potential metabolic benefits. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed its efficacy and safety versus placebo or active comparators in adults with metabolic disorders. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to August 2026 for studies assessing chiglitazar in adults with metabolic disorders. Outcomes were pooled via random-effects meta-analysis with 95% confidence intervals, alongside heterogeneity, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Five studies involving 1,457 participants were included. Chiglitazar reduced fasting glucose at 24 weeks (MD - 0.99 mmol/L, 95% CI - 1.75 to - 0.24). HbA1c decreased at 12 weeks (MD - 0.52% points, 95% CI - 0.68 to - 0.37), but its 24-week reduction was not statistically significant. Fasting insulin decreased at 12 weeks (SMD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.39 to - 0.11), and HOMA-IR decreased at 12 and 24 weeks. Triglyceride levels decreased and HDL-C increased at both time points; total and LDL cholesterol increased at 12 weeks. At 12 weeks, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) decreased (MD - 4.44 U/L, 95% CI - 6.09 to - 2.79; and - 1.23 U/L, 95% CI - 2.28 to - 0.19, respectively). AST decreased at 24 weeks (MD - 3.03 U/L, 95% CI - 5.85 to - 0.21), whereas ALT did not significantly decrease (MD - 4.52 U/L, 95% CI - 9.34 to 0.30). No significant differences in overall or serious adverse events were detected; edema was increased (RR 8.77, 95% CI 1.60-47.97). CONCLUSION: Chiglitazar may improve short-term glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, selected lipid measures, and aminotransferase levels in adults with metabolic disorders. Increased edema risk, heterogeneity, and limited follow-up warrant cautious interpretation; long-term clinical benefits remain unproven. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02119-8.

article.title: Decoding Ferroptosis: Mechanistic Insights and Future Directions in the Precision Analysis of Lipid Hydroperoxides
article.authors: Junya Ito
article.abstract: Abstract Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation of polyunsaturated phospholipids. While its core regulatory axis involving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and glutathione has been extensively studied, emerging evidence highlights the presence of multiple parallel defense systems. In addition, recent findings identify peroxiredoxin 6 as a critical regulator of intracellular selenium utilization, linking selenium metabolism to GPX4 biosynthesis and ferroptosis sensitivity. Despite these advances, a comprehensive understanding of ferroptosis mechanisms requires precise characterization of lipid hydroperoxides, the primary executioners of this cell death pathway. Here, we review the molecular basis of ferroptosis and its multilayered defense networks, with a particular focus on analytical challenges in lipid peroxidation research. We highlight recent progress in mass spectrometry–based approaches, including alkali metal adduction strategies, which enable positional isomer–resolved analysis of lipid hydroperoxides.

article.title: LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS): A Standardized Representation Language for Lipid Membrane Systems
article.authors: Pratima Khadka; Shikha Nangia
article.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
article.abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations of lipid membranes lack a standardized, machine-readable representation, creating significant barriers to reproducibility, data sharing, and AI-driven analyses. Current membrane descriptions are fragmented across software-specific input files, making it difficult to reconstruct published systems or compare results among studies. Here, we introduce LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS), a line notation not a simulation tool or membrane-building program, for lipid membrane simulations that extend SMILES, BigSMILES, and CG-BigSMILES to membrane systems. LiMBS version 1.0 uses a dual-block architecture that separates a system-level descriptor block from a chemical structure block, enabling the independent specification of membrane geometry, composition, environmental conditions, and molecular identity. The framework supports planar bilayers, vesicles, and bacterial outer membranes in atomistic, coarse-grained, and supercoarse-grained resolutions within a unified syntax. We provide a reference tool that reads, checks, and standardizes LiMBS strings, and we show that its output can be handed off to existing membrane-building software for system construction. LiMBS1.0 is human-readable, machine-readable, tool-independent, and compatible with FAIR data principles, providing a standardized description layer for membrane simulations that supports reproducible reporting, interoperable databases, and AI-enabled membrane biophysics.

article.title: Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases in female reproductive diseases: isoform-specific regulation of lipid metabolism, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling
article.authors: Shanyuan Jin; Lin Guo; Zishuo Wu; Zirong Wang; Runyuan Liu; Ying Kong; Hongshuo Zhang
article.abstract: Female reproductive diseases (FRDs) substantially affect women’s health and fertility, with lipid metabolic reprogramming emerging as a shared pathological feature. Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases (ACSLs) activate long-chain fatty acids and direct lipid flux toward β-oxidation, lipid synthesis, and phospholipid remodeling, thereby influencing oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling. Unlike previous reviews centered on broad ACSL biology, selected isoforms, or pathway-based ferroptosis mechanisms, this review adopts a disease-spanning, isoform-specific framework. We compare ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL4, ACSL5, and ACSL6 across cervical, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, and preeclampsia. By integrating isoform-specific substrate preference, subcellular localization, and lipid-channeling functions, we examine how individual ACSLs differentially regulate fatty acid oxidation, lipid synthesis and phospholipid remodeling, ferroptosis sensitivity, and inflammatory signaling across reproductive disease contexts. We further distinguish disease-specific experimental evidence from bioinformatic associations and mechanistic extrapolations from other disease models. Current evidence most consistently supports a disease-relevant role for ACSL4 in ferroptosis regulation, whereas ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL5, and ACSL6 show greater context dependence. This integrated framework identifies shared metabolic mechanisms, disease-specific differences, and priorities for cell-resolved validation and future isoform-selective therapeutic development.

article.title: Photoacoustic phase and intensity dual-modality imaging for characterization of plaque viscoelasticity and lipid composition: a feasibility study.
article.authors: Yuxuan Liang; Yiting Tan; Ao Jiang; Heng Zhang; Pingping Wang
article.abstract: SIGNIFICANCE: Rupture of atherosclerotic plaque is the most important cause of sudden death in acute myocardial infarction. Plaque stability is closely related to mechanical characters and histological composition. A dual-modality technique, combining photoacoustic phase imaging (PPI) and intensity imaging (PAI), was developed providing viscoelasticity and lipid component of plaques simultaneously. AIM: We aimed to investigate the feasibility of PPI to identify thin-cap fibrous plaques by detecting viscosity-elasticity ratio (VER), to further examine the correlation between VER and the major components of plaque, and ultimately to verify the accuracy of PPI-PAI in assessing plaque types. APPROACH: PPI-PAI experiments were performed on the aortas of 18 Apolipoprotein E-knockout (ApoE) mice fed with high-fat/high-cholesterol diet. After each experiment, the plaques at the target sites were stained with Oil Red O, Masson, and F4/80 staining to verify the accuracy of the imaging and to further investigate the correlations between VER and lipid core area, fibrous cap thickness, and macrophage content. Finally, conventional statistical methods, such as linear analysis, were used to summarize the experimental data and draw general conclusions. RESULTS: PPI enables quantitative VER detection of plaques, with thin-cap fibrous plaques exhibiting the highest VER ( 3.77 × 10 - 5 ∼ 4.68 × 10 - 5 s ). There is a high positive correlation between VER and lipid cross-section area ( R 2 = 0.81 , p < 0.0001 ) and macrophage content ( R 2 = 0.75 , p < 0.0001 ) in lipid plaque lesions. Likewise, in fibrous plaques, a strong negative correlation ( R 2 = 0.71 , p < 0.0001 ) is demonstrated between VER and fibrous cap thickness; and a high positive correlation ( R 2 = 0.12 , p = 0.02 ) between VER and macrophage content. As lipid plaques and thick-cap fibrous plaques may have the same VER values, the combination of PPI and PAI can effectively identify plaque types. CONCLUSIONS: PPI facilitates the characterization of thin-cap fibrous plaques by VER measurements, and further combination with PAI can improve the detection rate of distinct plaque types.

article.title: Incomplete Recovery of Cutaneous Lipid Homeostasis during Psoriasis Remission Links Mast Cell Activation to Relapse: A Mechanistic Study
article.authors: Li Zhang; Ce Shuai; Han Cao; Lihong Chen; Jianglu Zhou; Feng Xue; Youcong Wang; Haoying Chen; Xia Li; Jie Zheng
article.venue: International Journal of Dermatology and Venereology
article.abstract: Objective: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by relapse. Mast cells have been implicated in early relapse, but the mechanisms driving their activation remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to identify key regulatory factors associated with mast cell activation in psoriasis relapse. Methods: In this mechanistic study, longitudinal skin samples were collected from patients with psoriasis receiving IL-17A inhibitor therapy at Ruijin Hospital, between 2018 and 2020. Skin transcriptomes of psoriasis patients on IL-17A inhibitor therapy were compared at baseline, remission, and relapse between those with (n=6) or without (n=8) mast cell activation features. Mechanistic findings were validated in an imiquimod-induced psoriasiform mouse model using histopathology, transcriptomics, and metabolomic analyses. In addition, in vitro assays were performed to assess the effects of candidate mechanisms on mast cell function. Results: Bulk RNA-seq identified 102 differentially expressed genes during remission, including 93 downregulated genes predominantly enriched in lipid metabolism-related pathways. Compared with healthy controls, psoriasis-associated lipid metabolism genes remained incompletely restored during remission in patients with mast cell activation but normalized in patients without mast cell activation. Enrichment scores for lipid metabolism pathways were inversely correlated with mast cell activation signatures. In the murine model, restoration of skin lipid metabolism reduced mast cell retention including IL-17A + mast cells (8.33 ± 1.22 vs. 16.33 ± 1.15 per visual field, P = 0.008), and alleviated psoriasiform inflammation upon imiquimod re-challenge (51.82 ± 1.72 vs. 94.62 ± 5.59 μm, P vs. 16.56 ± 0.33%, P = 0.02) and reduced both IL-17A uptake (2.79 ± 0.40% vs 22.57 ± 0.20%, P vs. 720.6 ± 55.4 pg/mL, P = 0.02). Conclusion: Incomplete recovery of cutaneous lipid homeostasis during remission may sustain mast cell activation and contribute to psoriasis relapse. Restoration of skin barrier-associated lipid homeostasis, particularly ceramide metabolism, may represent a translational strategy to stabilize mast cells and delay disease recurrence.

article.title: Food Contaminant Deoxynivalenol Causes Muscle Damage by Inducing Lipid Peroxidation and Ferroptosis
article.authors: Bingxuan Jia; Huikang Lin; Yingzhu Tan; Aibo Wu
article.venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
article.abstract: Abstract Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a prevalent food contaminant that has been proposed to exert myotoxicity, but direct experimental validation remains insufficient. In this study, we used pig models and cell lines to investigate DON-induced muscle toxicity. In vivo, DON exposure leads to pathological muscle injury, disrupts energy metabolism, alters fatty acid metabolism, promotes the generation of lipid peroxides, and elevates Fe2+ levels. Cellular assays further confirmed that exposure to DON increases intracellular Fe2+ levels, inhibits the glutathione antioxidant pathway, and promotes lipid remodeling, ultimately facilitating lipid peroxidation and triggering ferroptosis. Cellular supplementation with complex lipids and free fatty acids improved C2C12 cell viability, which may be achieved by maintaining membrane lipid homeostasis. Collectively, this study demonstrates that DON induces muscle damage associated with lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, which may offer a promising direction for the development of protective intervention strategies.

article.title: Atorvastatin-Curcuminoids Co-Treatment Suppresses ApoB Secretion and Alters Lipid and Glucose Homeostasis in HuH-7 Cells
article.authors: Ahmed Bakillah; Haidar A. Alsahoud; Abeer Al Otaibi; Sindiyan Al Mubarak; Fatimah M. Al Sayafi; Muwadah Al Said; Yara Al Mihmadi; Badr Al Subei; Abdulrahman D. Mostafa; Hala B. Khalil; Abutaleb Asiri
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Although statins are still the main treatment for dyslipidemia, differences in patient responses, residual cardiovascular risk, and treatment side effects highlight the need for additional methods. Curcumin has attracted considerable interest because of its reported cardioprotective and lipid- and glucose-modulating effects, as well as its ability to influence cellular stress and survival pathways, highlighting its potential relevance to cardiovascular and metabolic disease. This study investigated the effects of atorvastatin (ATO), curcuminoid extract (CUR), and their combination on lipid and glucose metabolism and cell fate in hepatocellular carcinoma-derived cell lines. Methods: Huh-7 cells were treated for 48 h with ATO (10 μM), CUR (20 μM), or their combination (MIX). MTT assays characterized concentration-dependent cytotoxicity and informed concentration selection, and CellTiter-Glo assessed cell viability. ApoB expression and secretion were evaluated by Western blot and ELISA. Lipid accumulation was assessed by Oil Red O microscopy and quantitative analysis. Glucose uptake was measured before and after insulin challenge. Additionally, expression of relevant genes regulating cholesterol, lipoprotein, and glucose metabolism was assessed by qPCR, and apoptosis was examined by Annexin V/PI flow cytometry and Western blotting for apoptotic markers. article.title: pH‐Responsive Nanoplatform‐Mediated Lipid Hijacking and Metabolic Collapse for Synergistic Starvation‐Immunotherapy
article.authors: Xianlong Zong; Haochen Yao; Danyang Shen; Furu Gong; Zixuan Wang; Haoyang Qin; Yang Yang; Ruirui Qiao; Yongjuan Li; Rui Li
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor starvation therapy is a promising metabolism‐targeting intervention, yet its efficacy is largely counteracted by lipid droplet (LD)‐driven compensatory metabolism in malignant cells. Existing LDs‐targeted approaches are further hampered by off‐target systemic metabolic disturbances and inherent immunosuppressive adverse effects. Here, we construct a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8)‐based nanomedicine loaded with 2‐deoxy‐D‐glucose (2‐DG) and surface‐decorated with copper‐tannic acid (Cu‐TA, ZIF‐8/2‐DG@Cu‐TA). This nanosystem reroutes intracellular LDs from tumor cells to adjacent cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) to realize synergistic tumor starvation and immunotherapy. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the degradable Cu‐TA coating activates connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannels on CAFs. After internalization by tumor cells, ZIF‐8/2‐DG releases 2‐DG to suppress glycolysis, while dissociated zinc ions disrupt mitochondrial bioenergetics and further trigger Cx43 hemichannels activation on tumor cells. Fully assembled Cx43 gap junctions mediate directional LDs trafficking from tumor cells to CAFs, restricting intracellular lipid energy pools sustaining malignant metabolic demands. Simultaneous blockade of glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism induces profound tumor‐cell metabolic collapse. The resulting metabolic stress strongly amplifies antitumor immunity and markedly suppresses both subcutaneous and orthotopic MOC1 tumors. Overall, this study establishes a gap‐junction‐driven triple metabolic starvation paradigm and offers mechanistic insights for next‐generation metabolic immunotherapies.
