article.title: Nutritional Assessment, Lipid Profile, Antioxidant Capacity, and Preliminary Toxicity Assessment of the Leaf Blade and Petiole of Xanthosoma sagittifolium (Taioba) from a Cultivar in Southeastern Brazil
article.authors: Daniela Gomes de Moura; Ailton Junior Antunes da Costa; Dhionne Correia Gomes; Samuel Beiral Alves Pessoa; Rachel Oliveira Castilho; Renata Adriana Labanca; Marinalva Woods Pedrosa; Julio Onesio-Ferreira Melo; Raquel Linhares Bello de Araújo
article.abstract: Non–conventional food plants (NCFPs) have gained attention as sustainable sources of nutrients and bioactive compounds, while their underutilized edible parts may contribute to food diversification and waste reduction. This study performed a descriptive comparative analysis of the nutritional, mineral, lipid, phenolic, antioxidant, oxalate, and acute toxicity profiles of Xanthosoma sagittifolium (Taioba) cultivated in Brazil. Samples were evaluated for proximate composition; minerals by ICP–OES; Folin–Ciocalteu reducing capacity; antioxidant capacity by ABTS, DPPH, and FRAP; fatty acid profile by GC–FID; oxalic acid content; and toxicity using the Artemia salina bioassay. The leaf blade showed substantially higher protein, total phenolic equivalents, FRAP capacity, and concentrations of several fatty acids, including α–linolenic and linoleic acids, as well as higher levels of most analyzed minerals. Conversely, the petiole exhibited markedly higher moisture, carbohydrates, and potassium. Both fractions demonstrated high dietary fiber content, a predominance of polyunsaturated fatty acids, and low atherogenicity and thrombogenicity indices. Although both fractions contained oxalates—with the leaf blade presenting nearly twice the concentration of the petiole—aqueous extracts of both parts showed no detectable acute lethality in the Artemia salina screening. Overall, the results highlight that Taioba represents a highly valuable nutritional resource. Furthermore, the integral utilization of both the leaf blade and the underutilized petiole offers a complementary, sustainable, zero–waste strategy for dietary diversification, provided that appropriate thermal processing is applied to mitigate oxalate concerns.

article.title: Time Course of Lipid Peroxidation, Antioxidant Markers and C-Reactive Protein Following Simulated Soccer Match-Play: A 72-h Study in Semi-Professional Players
article.authors: Mustapha Bouchiba; Mouna Turki; Safaa M. Elkholi; Omar Trabelsi; Mohamed Amine Grati; Mohamed Amine Bouzid
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Soccer match-play triggers muscle damage and a marked increase in reactive oxygen species production, but early and late lipid peroxidation products have rarely been tracked together with non-enzymatic antioxidants and C-reactive protein in the same players over a full 72-h window. This study characterized the recovery kinetics of oxidative damage markers (conjugated dienes, malondialdehyde) and antioxidant/defense markers (uric acid, bilirubin, reduced glutathione, gamma-glutamyl transferase), together with C-reactive protein, and explored the relationships between these markers’ recovery responses. Methods: Twelve semi-professional male soccer players completed the Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). Venous blood samples were collected at Baseline, 0 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h post-LIST. Repeated-measures ANOVA or the Friedman test was applied depending on normality, with Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons against Baseline and exploratory Spearman correlations. Results: Uric acid and reduced glutathione peaked at 0 h and no longer differed significantly from baseline from 24 h and 48 h onward, respectively. CRP increased significantly at 24 h, whereas bilirubin showed only a non-significant 24-h peak. Conjugated dienes remained significantly elevated at every time point up to 72 h, whereas malondialdehyde differed significantly from baseline only at 0 h. In exploratory analyses not corrected for multiple testing, uric acid correlated with bilirubin and, on an area-under-the-curve basis, with C-reactive protein, and conjugated dienes correlated with malondialdehyde. Conclusions: The uric acid and reduced glutathione responses and the C-reactive protein response resolved within 24 to 48 h, whereas conjugated dienes remained elevated up to 72 h. These findings indicate prolonged alterations in selected circulating biomarkers rather than direct evidence of persistent muscle oxidative damage or incomplete functional recovery, and their relevance to congested fixture scheduling warrants investigation alongside performance outcomes.

article.title: Lipid Composition Modulates Organ-Specific Reactogenicity of Lipid Nanoparticles After Two Administrations
article.authors: Mikhail Bespalov; Lilia Shirokova; Elena Mazunina; Sofia Kozlova; Evgeniia Bykonia; Olga Vasileva; Sophia Konovalova; Yulia Venediktova; Maria Vorontsova; Vladimir Gushchin; Denis Logunov; Roman Ivanov; Vasiliy Reshetnikov; Darya Telegina
article.abstract: Background: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) can activate innate immunity, but the factors shaping repeat-dose reactogenicity remain unclear. We compared systemic, local, and organ-specific reactions after intramuscular administrations of empty LNPs containing ionizable lipids used in mRNA vaccines. Methods: Female BALB/c mice received two intramuscular injections, 2 weeks apart, of LNP-4 (four components, ALC-0315 as the sole ionizable lipid; 59 nm) or LNP-5 (five components, equimolar ALC-0315/SM-102 at the same total ionizable lipid content; 86 nm). Body weight was monitored for 15 days. Blood biochemical parameters, injection-site histology, and morphological and molecular markers in the hypothalamus, liver, lungs, and spleen were assessed 24 h after the second injection by histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence (IF), Western blotting, and quantitative PCR (qPCR). Results: Both LNPs were followed by transient body-weight loss, moderate biochemical changes, and local reactogenicity. The strongest organ-specific responses occurred in the liver and hypothalamus. Both LNPs induced hepatic sinusoidal dilation and leukocyte infiltration, but LNP-4 was associated with more myeloid cell numbers and higher inflammatory marker expression. In the hypothalamus, LNP-4 produced broader changes in inflammatory and myeloid marker expression than LNP-5. No marked structural damage was observed in the examined organs. Conclusions: Repeated LNP administration was followed by systemic and local reactogenicity, and organ-specific changes differed between the formulations, possibly reflecting lipid composition, particle size, and lipid dose. Carrier composition should be considered in the design and safety evaluation of LNP-based vaccine delivery systems.

article.title: Biomarcadores en el hipotiroidismo subclínico y su relación con el metabolismo lipídico y el riesgo cardiometabólico. Revisión sistemática Biomarkers in subclinical hypothyroidism and their relationship to lipid metabolism and cardiometabolic risk. A systematic review
article.authors: Diego Mauricio Tene Salcán; Franklin Vicente Ramos Flor
article.abstract: El hipotiroidismo subclínico (HSC) constituye una alteración endocrina caracterizada por concentraciones elevadas de hormona estimulante de la tiroides (TSH) y valores normales de tiroxina libre (FT4), asociada con posibles alteraciones metabólicas y cardiovasculares. El objetivo fue analizar la evidencia científica sobre los biomarcadores asociados al HSC, su relación con el metabolismo lipídico y su potencial utilidad en la identificación del riesgo cardiometabólico. Se realizó una revisión sistemática conforme a PRISMA 2020, mediante búsquedas en PubMed, Scopus y Cochrane Library de publicaciones comprendidas entre 2020 y 2026. Se incluyeron 24 estudios que evaluaron biomarcadores tiroideos, lipídicos, inflamatorios, autoinmunes y metabólicos. Los resultados evidenciaron asociaciones entre el HSC y alteraciones del perfil lipídico, principalmente concentraciones elevadas de colesterol total y LDL-C, así como modificaciones de triglicéridos y HDL-C en determinadas poblaciones. Asimismo, se identificaron relaciones con resistencia a la insulina, inflamación de bajo grado e indicadores complementarios, como el índice aterogénico plasmático, la proteína C reactiva ultrasensible y los anticuerpos antiperoxidasa tiroidea. Los biomarcadores emergentes, incluidos el LDL oxidado, la homocisteína, las proteínas ANGPTL y las adipocinas, aportaron información sobre posibles mecanismos metabólicos, aunque su utilidad predictiva permaneció insuficientemente establecida. Se concluyó que el HSC se relacionó con alteraciones lipídicas y cardiometabólicas heterogéneas, mientras que los biomarcadores convencionales presentaron mayor aplicabilidad clínica y los emergentes requirieron evidencia adicional para determinar su utilidad en la estratificación del riesgo.

article.title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARα/UCP2 Signaling Network
article.authors: Abhipsha Saikia; Semim Akhtar Ahmed; Kangkon Saikia; Pranamika Sarma; Devi Basumatary; Ashis K. Mukherjee; Jagat Chandra Borah; Asis Bala
article.abstract: Abstract Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside’s effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

article.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis reveals ApoLp ‐ III ‐mediated BmNPV suppression via host energy and lipid reprogramming
article.authors: Quadsia Jabeen; Xinhao Jiao; Zi Liang; Na Zhang; Shengyan Xiao; Wenwen Jiang; Shuyi Liu; Aniqa Shakoor Butt; Ping Wu
article.abstract: Abstract In global sericulture, the most economically important and primary causative pathogen is Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV), but the host immune metabolism that restricts the viral replication is not completely defined. A recently identified insect multifunctional apolipoprotein (apolipophorin‐III [ApoLp‐III]) was shown to suppress BmNPV proliferation by enhancing ceramide accumulation. However, it is unknown how this antiviral action is mediated through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic changes. In this study, we dissect the ApoLp‐III‐mediated antiviral mechanism by constructing an ApoLp‐III‐overexpressing BmN cell line and integrating RNA‐seq data with a previously published metabolomic profile. A total of 1067 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with significantly opposing expression trends were identified. These DEGs were prominent in DNA replication, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and amino sugar nucleotide sugar metabolism. Genes associated with amino acid metabolism were down‐regulated, while genes linked with DNA replication and OXPHOS were up‐regulated. Bidirectional regulation of sphingolipids was also confirmed by quantitative real‐time PCR (qRT‐PCR) and transcriptomic data. Ceramide accumulation resulted from the down‐regulation of alkaline ceramidase ( ACER ) and up‐regulation of regulatory subunit of the rate‐limiting ceramide synthesis enzyme, SPTssA . Integrated multi‐omics correlation analysis further showed that ceramide species positively correlated with OXPHOS and negatively correlated with amino sugar metabolism. Meanwhile, down‐regulated triglycerides showed negative correlation with DNA replication and OXPHOS genes. In addition, we identified ApoLp‐III interacting proteins, that is, the integrin‐associated cytoskeletal regulator, Talin‐1 and lepidopteran‐specific immune receptor Haemolin, using Flag‐based co‐immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry. Our results show that ApoLp‐III suppresses BmNPV replication by the coordinated reprogramming of host cellular energy (OXPHOS) and lipid (sphingolipid) metabolism. Thus, ApoLp‐III acts as an important immunometabolic hub in the antiviral defence of lepidopterans, and our research also offers a theoretical foundation for controlling silkworm diseases by targeting sphingolipid‐energy pathway.

article.title: Integrating tissue proteomics and bioactive lipid analysis of ovine tissue samples identifies functional relations of bioactive lipids
article.authors: Gerhard Hagn; Florien Jenner; Andrea Bileck; Sinan Gültekin; Mats Hamberg; Thomas Mohr; Christopher Gerner; Iris Gerner
article.abstract: Bioactive lipids are potent effector molecules that may help to reveal specific information about biological processes. However, analytical challenges and incomplete functional annotations remain as obstacles. We hypothesized that the functional annotation of these lipids may be improved by projecting enriched Gene Ontology (GO) terms derived from proteomics to correlating bioactive lipids. To that aim, thirteen organs and tissues from sheep ( Ovis aries ) were analyzed using mass spectrometry-based untargeted proteomics and bioactive lipid analysis. In total, 4717 proteins and 168 bioactive lipids, including fatty acids and their conjugates, oxylipins (octadecanoids, eicosanoids, and docosanoids), lyso-phosphatidylcholines (LPCs) and lyso-phosphatidylethanolamines (LPEs), endocannabinoids and related fatty amides, and bile acids and related sterol lipids were determined. Thereof, the correct identification of 114 lipids was confirmed using commercially available analytical standards, whereas the identity of the previously uncharacterized oxylipin 4-hydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (4-HETE) was verified through in-house chemical synthesis. Co-expression and clustering analyses are consistent with our hypothesis via independently corroborating known bioactive lipid functions and suggested novel functional relations. Amongst other observations, 18-HETE and 19-HETE were related to mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, 11,12-dihydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (DiHETE), 15-deoxy-prostaglandin J2 and 5(6)-epoxy-eicosatrienoic acid (EET) were related to chemical synaptic transmission, arachidonoyl ethanolamide phosphate was related to muscle contraction and numerous LPCs and LPEs were related to exosome formation. Tissue levels of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), pro-resolving mediators and the newly characterized 4-HETE were related to the cellular protein synthesis and folding machinery. The latter finding suggested that PUFAs and their derivatives support protein synthesis fidelity in addition to efferocytosis, both essential contributors for the effective resolution of inflammation.

article.title: A Curcumin‐Loaded Iron‐Porphyrin Covalent Organic Framework Alleviates Atherosclerosis by Modulating Oxidative Stress and Lipid Metabolism
article.authors: Chengpeng Niu; Yujie Xia; Zhiquan Chen; Shanshan Yu; Haojie Yu; Feiqi Wang; Xinzheng Jiang; Yong'ai Liu; Shuyong Zhang
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Atherosclerosis (AS) requires multi‐target therapies addressing lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and inflammation, yet lipid‐lowering alone insufficiently mitigates residual cardiovascular risk. Curcumin (Cur), a natural polyphenol with well‐established anti‐atherosclerotic activities, is severely hampered by extremely low oral bioavailability and rapid metabolic clearance. To overcome these limitations, an iron porphyrin‐based covalent organic framework (COF), FeTAPP‐Dha, was prepared by condensing 5,10,15,20‐tetrakis‐(4‐aminophenyl)‐porphyrin‐Fe‐(III) chloride with 2,5‐dihydroxyterephthalaldehyde. Cur was then incorporated into the hydrophobic channels of FeTAPP‐Dha through hydrogen‐bond‐mediated size matching, producing FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur with a loading efficiency of 12.5%. The incorporated iron porphyrin units provide reactive oxygen species scavenging capability, enabling sustained H 2 O 2 decomposition and intercepting oxidative stress at its source. Moreover, the acidic microenvironment characteristic of atherosclerotic plaques impairs hydrogen‐bonding interactions, facilitating on‐demand Cur release at lesion sites while minimizing systemic exposure. In ApoE −/− mice, FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur effectively inhibited foam cell formation and significantly reduced aortic plaque burden. These effects were accompanied by activation of the AMP‐activated protein kinase–acetyl‐CoA carboxylase signaling axis and suppression of inflammation. Collectively, FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur achieved superior therapeutic outcomes compared with free Cur or empty carrier. This work establishes a COF‐based synergistic platform that integrates carrier‐mediated microenvironment regulation with stimuli‐responsive drug delivery, offering a promising paradigm for multi‐target AS therapy.

article.title: Short‐Term Effects of Golden Rice Cookies Enriched With Piper crocatum Extract on Lipid Profiles in Adults With Diabetes: A Quasi‐Experimental Study
article.authors: Altje Suwardi Abram; Andina Setyawati; Andi Masyitha Irwan
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) commonly coexists with dyslipidemia and elevated cardiovascular risk. Food‐based interventions containing antioxidants and polyphenols may support lipid metabolism. This study evaluated the short‐term effects of Golden Rice cookies enriched with active Piper crocatum extract on lipid profiles in adults with DM. Methods This quasi‐experimental pretest–posttest control group study included 102 adults with DM assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received Golden Rice cookies enriched with P. crocatum extract, while the control group received similar cookies without the extract for 28 days. Total cholesterol, low‐density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL‐C), high‐density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL‐C), and triglycerides were measured before and after the intervention. Bivariate analyses were performed in the full sample, whereas analysis of covariance was performed among non‐statin participants, adjusting for baseline lipid values, age, body mass index, diabetes duration, carbohydrate intake, and protein intake. Results In the unadjusted analysis, total cholesterol and LDL‐C increased significantly in the intervention group, whereas total cholesterol decreased significantly in the control group. Between‐group analysis showed a significant difference only in total cholesterol. Among non‐statin participants, an exploratory adjusted analysis showed a significant between‐group difference in total cholesterol ( p = 0.016; adjusted mean difference = −12.55 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI] = −22.74 to −2.36). No significant adjusted differences were observed for LDL‐C, HDL‐C, or triglycerides. Conclusion A 28‐day intervention with Golden Rice cookies enriched with active P. crocatum extract was associated with a limited exploratory adjusted between‐group difference in total cholesterol among non‐statin adults with DM. These preliminary findings require confirmation in longer randomized controlled trials with stronger dietary control and mechanistic biomarker assessment. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT07268781

article.title: Salicylic Acid as a Food-Derived Bioactive Constituent of Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction: A Potential Functional Food Ingredient to Restoring Gut Barrier Function in Constipation-Predominant IBS.
article.authors: Min Duan; Lixia Huang; Yingyue Xu; Ya Huang; Xiaojun Yang
article.abstract: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) is a chronic gut disorder with limited dietary management options. Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction (TQDZD), composed of medicine-food homologous plant materials traditionally consumed for digestive comfort, represents a dietary strategy with functional food potential, yet its systemically bioavailable constituents and nutritional mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the orally bioavailable polyphenol profile of TQDZD and elucidate its barrier-protective mechanisms within a functional food framework. Using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) serum metabolite profiling, we characterized TQDZD's polyphenol composition and identified orally bioavailable constituents in rat circulation after dietary administration. Untargeted serum metabolomics coupled with orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) was performed to map metabolic network perturbations in an IBS-C rat model, and dietary bioactive pathways were predicted by comparing intervention-induced metabolic trajectories. IBS-C was induced in rats by ice-water enema, and an in vitro inflammatory model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated Caco-2 monolayers. Barrier function was assessed by fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-dextran flux; tight junction proteins, cytokines, and signaling pathways were evaluated by Western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and qPCR. To explore the mechanistic basis of the observed barrier-protective effects, Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) signaling involvement was assessed using siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-mediated overexpression as complementary pharmacological tools. A total of 1962 non-redundant compounds were identified in TQDZD aqueous extract, with phenolic acids and flavonoids as the predominant chemical classes. These polyphenol-rich profiles are characteristic of functional foods with gut-protective potential. In dosed rat serum, 257 systemically bioavailable components were detected, of which 150 (58.4%) were prototype constituents. Multi-criteria screening (treatment/control peak area ratio ≥ 2, top-20 abundance rank in the formula, coefficient of variation < 30%, and Level 1 identification confidence) yielded four core prototypes: salicylic acid, N-acetyl-L-phenylalanine, L-valyl-L-phenylalanine, and L-phenylalanyl-L-hydroxyproline. Among these, salicylic acid-a naturally occurring phenolic acid widely distributed in plant-based foods-was prioritized for functional validation. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that IBS-C rats exhibited profound dysregulation of a lipid-inflammatory network, characterized by disturbances in glycerophospholipid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, and sphingolipid signaling. TQDZD intervention remodeled this network in a dose-dependent manner; notably, the metabolic trajectory of the high-dose TQDZD group converged strikingly with that of the BTK modulator orelabrutinib. In vivo, TQDZD significantly reduced intestinal permeability (p < 0.001), restored colonic expression of tight junction proteins zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), Occludin, and Claudin-1 (p < 0.001), and suppressed mucosal and serum levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), IL-1β, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) (p < 0.001). Mechanistic studies demonstrated that Tiaoqi Daozhi Decoction (TQDZD) inhibited the BTK-spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK)- phospholipase C gamma 2 (PLCγ2)-protein kinase B (AKT) axis, thereby blocking IκBα phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation. BTK knockdown potentiated, whereas BTK overexpression abrogated, the barrier-protective and anti-inflammatory effects of TQDZD. Salicylic acid alone fully reproduced TQDZD's phenotype in vitro and in vivo, and its effects were strictly BTK-dependent. TQDZD exerts its therapeutic effect on constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) via its core systemically bioavailable constituent salicylic acid. The biological activity of salicylic acid relies on the BTK signaling pathway, which blocks the non-canonical nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway, thereby restoring the intestinal epithelial barrier and suppressing low-grade inflammation. Given salicylic acid's abundance in edible plants and its long history of safe dietary exposure, these findings provide a mechanistic rationale for developing phenolic-acid-rich botanical blends as supportive dietary strategies for IBS-C and related barrier-centric gastrointestinal disorders.

article.title: Exercise-induced lactylation in WDR41 initiates autophagy and improves fatty liver diseases.
article.authors: Ouyang Q, Liang P, Zhang H, Zhang Q, Liao H, Nie C, Kuramoto K, Zhang C, Ji D, Ren F, He C, Liu R.
article.abstract: Excess lipid accumulation and a sedentary lifestyle are associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but the causal mechanisms and preventive methods are not fully understood. Macroautophagy/autophagy is a lysosomal degradation pathway robustly induced by exercise and plays a key role in lipid metabolism. Understanding the mechanisms by which exercise activates autophagy and elicits metabolic benefits in the liver will provide important insights into the pathogenesis of MAFLD. Here, we discovered negative correlations between expression and lactylation of WDR41 (WD repeat domain 41) and pathogenesis of a series of human hepatic metabolic diseases. We found that WDR41 was a pro-autophagy protein that underwent lactylation in response to autophagy-inducing conditions, such as exercise. WDR41 was lactylated at lysine 319 (K319), a modification facilitated by LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) upon autophagy induction, and delactylated by SIRT2 (sirtuin 2). Lactylated WDR41 promoted autophagy initiation by directly interacting with the autophagy proteins ATG13 (autophagy related 13) and RB1CC1/FIP200 (RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1) and driving the ULK1 (unc-51 like autophagy activating kinase 1) complex assembly. Physiologically, WDR41 and WDR41 K319 lactylation, were important for exercise-induced improvements in insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism against excess lipid accumulation in the liver. Thus, we demonstrated that WDR41 lactylation at K319 is an important regulatory mechanism by which exercise regulates autophagy and hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism.

article.title: Cholesterol Biomimetic Fluorescent Probe for the High Signal‐to‐Noise Ratio and Selectivity Imaging of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver
article.authors: Kunyi Wang; Guoyang Zhang; Xuefan Guo; Zixuan Zhang; Nan Xiao; Junya Lei; Yulong Jin; Zhuo Wang
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) lacks sensitive and non‐invasive imaging tools. Conventional fluorescent probes label lipid droplets through non‐specific hydrophobic interactions, failing to distinguish pathological lipid overload from normal lipid storage. Here, we propose an “uptake‐targeted” strategy based on cholesterol biomimicry. TPAS‐PyCHO+ was synthesized as a fluorescent probe that structurally mimics cholesterol to hijack the clathrin‐mediated endocytosis pathway—a process hyperactive in steatotic hepatocytes. In lipid‐laden cells, the probes were actively internalized and accumulated in lipid droplets. TPAS‐PyCHO+ activated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) to produce strong fluorescence. In contrast, normal hepatocytes show minimal uptake. TPAS‐PyCHO+ achieves high‐contrast imaging of NAFLD in cell and mouse models, with a signal‐to‐noise ratio superior to conventional lipid‐droplet dyes. Moreover, TPAS‐PyCHO+ successfully monitored disease recovery by dietary intervention. This work introduces a biomimetic “uptake‐targeted” design paradigm for metabolic disease imaging by active hijacking of the pathological endocytic pathway.

article.title: Randomized comparative blood glucose, lipids, malondialdehyde, liver enzymes, and C-reactive protein responses to laser acupuncture versus interscapular wet cupping in fatty liver
article.authors: Ali Ismail; Yousef M. Alshehre; Ahmed Mohamed Abdelhalim Elfahl; Ahmed Bayuomy Abo Elatta; Ahmed M. Elfahl; Sami Kamal Mohamed Elgendy
article.abstract: Background: Wide appreciation of the use of complementary therapies is reported by patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Objectives: This study aimed to compare the effect of interscapular wet cupping (IWC) versus laser acupuncture (LA) on systolic and diastolic blood pressure, aspartate transaminase, pulse rate, alanine transaminase, serum malondialdehyde, fasting blood glucose, serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and blood lipids (total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein) in NAFLD patients. This was a randomized comparative study. Materials and methods: Sixty fatty liver participants were recruited from the Internal Diseases Outpatient Clinic, Specialized Clinics, Badr City, Egypt. Patients were randomly assigned to the IWC or LA group. For 3 months, the TWC group received 2 cupping sessions per month (on days 0 and 14). The selected acupoints received 3 LA sessions per week for 3 months. We assessed the above measurements before and after the 3-month complementaryinterventional study period. Results: Significant improvements were reported in the IWC and LA groups (except for serum hs-CRP in the IWC group). Conclusion: LA or IWC may help in controlling blood pressure, blood glucose, lipids, inflammatory markers, liver enzymes, and oxidative stress markers in patients with fatty liver.

article.title: Fluorinated Fatty Acids: Origin, Synthesis and Activity
article.authors: Valery M. Dembitsky; Alexander O. Terent’ev
article.abstract: Fluorinated fatty acids occupy a distinctive position at the intersection of natural-product chemistry, lipid metabolism, and synthetic organofluorine chemistry. This mini-review examines their natural occurrence, structural characterization, proposed biosynthetic origins, selected synthetic approaches, and biological effects, with particular emphasis on plant-derived ω-fluorinated fatty acids. Fluorinated constituents of Dichapetalum toxicarium seed oil illustrate variation in chain length and unsaturation, while historical assignments highlight the importance of analytical confirmation. A biosynthetic model involving fluoroacetyl-CoA as a starter unit offers an explanation for terminal fluorination, although precursor transport, enzyme specificity, and individual transformations require distinction between direct evidence and inference. Biological consequences are considered in relation to compound structure and metabolic fate, including experimental evidence for conversion of a terminally fluorinated fatty acid to fluorocitrate. Selected synthetic examples encompass terminal radiofluorination, fluorinated coriolic-acid analogues, and 22-[18F]fluorodocosahexaenoic acid, a tracer evaluated preclinically for brain fatty-acid uptake. Nonradioactive analogues and radioactive tracers are discussed separately, and activities of parent lipids are distinguished from those demonstrated for fluorinated derivatives. The available evidence supports compound-specific interpretation rather than universal claims concerning toxicity, metabolic stability, or therapeutic potential. Priorities include verification of historical structures, characterization of plant biosynthetic pathways, quantitative comparative bioassays, and identification of metabolic products.

article.title: Childhood Adiposity and Bisphenol Exposure Are Linked to Gut Dysbiosis, Altered Short-Chain Fatty Acid and Complex Carbohydrate-Degrading Profiles
article.authors: Pilar Ortiz; Esther Palacios; Ana Moreno-Blanco; Alicia Ruiz-Rodríguez; Margarita Aguilera
article.abstract: Background: Dietary exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals is increasingly associated with pediatric adiposity and gut dysbiosis. Although short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are traditionally known for being involved in metabolic homeostasis, their contribution to energy harvesting remains controversial and under continuous debate. Methods: We conducted an integrative study of 100 children (aged 3–12 years) stratified by BMI and total body fat percentage, with bisphenol exposure assessed via nail matrix biomonitoring. Gut microbiota was profiled via amplicon gene sequencing, fecal SCFAs were quantified by GC-MS, and the genomic capacity for complex carbohydrate degradation was predicted using functional profiling tools. Results: Children with high body fat percentage exhibited higher fecal concentrations of acetate, butyrate, and propionate. High bisphenol levels were also positively associated with both increased adiposity and elevated fecal SCFA profiles. Integrative analyses identified a distinct microbiota-metabolic signature: obesity and high bisphenol exposure were linked to an expansion of specific taxa such as Blautia, Collinsella, and Catenibacterium, contrasting with a reduction in potential protective markers including Oscillospiraceae, Bacteroides plebeius, and Christensenellaceae R-7. Notably, key functional and gene-enzymatic profiling revealed an enriched carbohydrate-degrading potential within the adiposity and BPA-associated microbiota, consistent with enhanced fiber degradation, increased SCFA production, and greater predicted energy-extracting potential. Conclusions: The co-occurrence of host metabolic and environmental factors together with the altered microbiome features, points towards a shift in microbial energy harvesting. The findings outline a correlative ‘chemical obesogen–microbiome–adiposity’ interplay, linking environmental xenobiotic exposure to specific microbial alterations and metabolic changes associated with pediatric fat accumulation.

article.title: Morphology, Molecular Data, and Fatty Acid Composition of Some Monoraphid Diatoms from the South China Sea, with Description of Two New Species of Astartiella
article.authors: Natalia Tseplik; Elena Kezlya; Anton Glushchenko; Zinaida Krivova; Yevhen Maltsev; Sergei Genkal; Hai Doan-Nhu; Maxim Kulikovskiy
article.abstract: We examined 13 strains of marine monoraphid diatoms belonging to the genera Schizostauron, Astartiella, and Achnanthes, isolated from the South China Sea near Viet Nam, with the use of light, fluorescent and electron microscopy, and molecular methods. Based on our investigation, two new species of Astartiella are described: Astartiella triundulata and Astartiella zinaidae. A morphological comparison with close species is provided, and the results of molecular analysis are discussed. Schizostauron strains were identified as S. trachyderma: the cryptic diversity and genetic variability within this genus are examined. Data on geographical distribution of these taxa are presented. A total fatty acid profile was obtained for both Schizostauron and Astartiella strains, and the results are discussed as well.

article.title: Synergistic Anti-Zika Activity of Repurposed Statin and Clofibrate Combinations: Evidence from Oleic Acid-Mediated Metabolic Complementation
article.authors: Chung-Do Lee; Sang-Ik Park; Gun Lee; Hyeon Jeong Moon; Jaewoo Choi; Jun Bong Lee; Luis Martinez-Sobrido; Fernando Almazán; Eun-Hye Ryu; Yeong-Bin Baek; Jun-Gyu Park
article.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) substantially relies on host lipid metabolism, presenting a prime target for host-directed antivirals. To identify host-directed antiviral interventions while circumventing interferon-mediated transcriptomic masking, we curated a dual-virus (dengue and ZIKV) gene signature to query the Connectivity Map. Top lipid-lowering candidates were validated using a reporter virus (rZIKV-Venus) and an authentic wild-type (WT) ZIKV in Vero E6 cells—a model deliberately selected for its interferon deficiency to isolate pure metabolic responses. Dose–response screening of 67 prioritized compounds identified atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, and clofibrate as potent ZIKV inhibitors. Statin–clofibrate combinations exhibited strong synergy, with fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) values of 0.203 (atorvastatin–clofibrate) and 0.117 (rosuvastatin–clofibrate) for the 4:1 clofibrate-to-statin ratio and an optimized selectivity index. Mechanistically, exogenous oleic acid supplementation induced significant metabolic complementation, significantly restoring both host lipid droplet (LD) abundance and ZIKV replication readouts suppressed by the dual treatment. article.title: Extraction of unsaturated fatty acids from Aurantiochytrium sp. using amino acid-based deep eutectic solvents.
article.authors: Eri Tanaka; Shogo Suzuki; Shogo Torii; Toyonobu Usuki
article.abstract: This study used an amino acid-based deep eutectic solvent (DES) to extract unsaturated fatty acids, including docosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid, from the microalga Aurantiochytrium sp. Microalgae represent valuable biological resources with diverse applications in fields such as biofuels, nutritional supplements, and cosmetics. Efficient methods for extracting unsaturated fatty acids from microalgae are thus desired. To address this need, DESs, which have attracted attention as environmentally benign solvents, were evaluated as extraction media. By combining various hydrogen bond acceptors and hydrogen bond donors to form DESs, proline/1,3-butylene glycol (ProBG) was found to provide the highest extraction yield. When the effect of the HBA:HBD molar ratio in ProBG was examined, a 1:3 molar ratio resulted in a further increase in extraction yield. To elucidate the factors underlying the differences in extraction yield, the polarity and viscosity of the solvents were measured and analysed.

article.title: Securing Long‐Chain Omega‐3 Fatty Acid Supply for Sustainable Aquaculture Development and Human Nutrition
article.authors: Sadasivam Kaushik; Douglas R. Tocher
article.abstract: ABSTRACT There is increasing awareness of combatting lifestyle diseases through improved nutrition and the important role that adequate intake of omega‐3 long‐chain PUFA has in promoting human health and development. Given the role and strategic importance of aquaculture in overall seafood production and in the supply of omega‐3 long‐chain PUFA to human consumers, this article reviews the possible differences between terrestrial and aquatic systems at different trophic levels in terms of long‐chain PUFA, and the importance of dietary fats and essential fatty acids, particularly omega‐3 long‐chain PUFA, in aquaculture nutrition and as human food. Given that most farmed fish and shrimp depend on dietary sources of PUFA for optimal growth and physiological well‐being, a synthetic and systematic review of available data on dietary EFA requirements in different groups of fish is made. Besides growth, dietary PUFA have physiological and metabolic roles for ensuring membrane integrity, reproduction, immunity and health. Additionally, omega‐3 long‐chain PUFA are critical for ensuring the nutritional value of aquatic foods for consumers. Thus, the review also addresses current challenges associated with the reduced use of fish oil in aquafeeds and explores strategies to maintain the nutritional value of farmed fish. These include finishing diets, selective breeding for enhanced biosynthesis and optimised feed formulations capable of supporting both aquaculture productivity and human nutritional needs. Compared to terrestrial food webs, aquatic ecosystems are unique in providing EPA and DHA through microalgae from low marine trophic levels. Exploitation of these in a judicious manner addresses the challenges of sustainability of aquaculture.

article.title: Comparative evaluation of macronutrient compositions and fatty acid profiles in aquatic and terrestrial edible insects consumed in Arunachal Pradesh, Northeast India
article.authors: Salomi Jugli; Bompu Bagra; Minam Moyong; Karsing Megu; Sandipan Ray; Mousumi Poddar Sarkar; Jharna Chakravorty
article.venue: Journal of Insects as Food and Feed
article.abstract: Abstract Insects, one of the oldest dietary resources, are gaining attention as sustainable sources of protein and fibre. Among ethnic communities of Arunachal Pradesh, NE India, entomophagy remains a rooted cultural practice. This study evaluated and compared the macronutrient and fatty acid profiles of selected aquatic insects ( Lethocerus indicus , Laccotrephes ruber , Gestroiella insignis , Cybister tripunctatus , assorted dragonfly larvae) and terrestrial insects ( Lepidiota sp., Mimela sp., Heliocopris bucephalus , Arcte coerula , Pericyma cruegeri ). The macronutrient analysis revealed that aquatic species exhibited higher fat content (13.45%) and calorific value (378.49 kcal/100 g DM) compared to terrestrial species (9.83% fat; 289.99 kcal/100 g DM), while terrestrial insects showed higher protein (55.26%) and fibre (20.33%) levels. The fatty acid composition shows obvious differences between the two groups: aquatic insects possessed higher proportions of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), particularly eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; C20:5 n-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; C22:6 n-3), whereas terrestrial insects were dominated by monounsaturated and saturated fatty acids. Interestingly, Gestroiella insignis and dragonfly larvae contained docosadienoic acid (DDA, C22:2 n-6), advocating a habitat-specific diversion in lipid metabolism. Indices related to cardiovascular health, together with Atherogenic Index (AI 2), point toward favourable lipid quality, particularly in aquatic species. Variation in macronutrient and fatty acid profiles reflects the influence of habitat, trophic ecology and developmental stage on insect lipid composition. The study highlights the nutraceutical potential of the examined insect species, whose macronutrient and fatty acid profiles support their use as sustainable functional foods and feeds.

article.title: Phase 1 Study of Safety and PK With A Combination of Omeprazole and Trimetazidine for Fatty Acid Oxidation Inhibition in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors
article.authors: Wonyoung Choi; Jung W. Chun; Sung H. Sim; Sung‐Sik Han; Woo J. Lee; Joon H. Kang; Hyun Chul Kim; SeungHwan Lee; Jun H. Lee; Hyun J. Yoo; Soo‐Youl Kim; Sang M. Woo
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a metabolic vulnerability in cancer cells, making pharmacologic FAO inhibition a promising therapeutic strategy. This Phase I, open‐label, 3 + 3 dose‐escalation study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of two oral FAO inhibitors—omeprazole (KN510), a carnitine–acylcarnitine translocase inhibitor, and trimetazidine (KN713), an acetyl‐CoA acyltransferase inhibitor—given once daily in combination to patients with advanced solid tumors. Twelve patients were enrolled across four dose cohorts (omeprazole and trimetazidine, each 60–120 mg/day). The maximum tolerated dose was not reached; the recommended Phase 2 dose was set at 120 mg once daily for each agent. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with most adverse events Grade 1–2; the most common were flu‐like symptoms (25.0%), constipation (16.7%), nausea (16.7%), and dizziness (16.7%). Omeprazole showed time‐dependent pharmacokinetics consistent with auto‐inhibition of its own metabolism, whereas trimetazidine showed dose‐proportional pharmacokinetics across the studied range. The best response was stable disease in five patients (disease control rate 41.7%). Median progression‐free survival was 1.66 months (95% CI, 1.18–3.55) and median overall survival was 9.13 months (95% CI, 3.29–not reached). Dual pharmacologic FAO inhibition with oral omeprazole and trimetazidine was feasible and well tolerated, supporting the mechanistic rationale for combination dosing. Disease stabilization observed in this heavily pretreated population warrants further clinical evaluation, particularly in combination with standard chemotherapy regimens. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov , NCT06012708; registered August 25, 2023

article.title: Hepatoprotective Effect of Nicotinamide Mononucleotide on High‐Fat Diet‐Induced Non‐Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Mice
article.authors: Yiwen Zhang; Yafei Wu; Yanhong Wei; Xuan Liu; Xiaocan Lei; Hua Huang; Meixiang Li
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a significant global public health issue characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a crucial cofactor in cellular metabolism across mammalian organs. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), an important intermediate in NAD+ salvage synthesis, may influence high‐fat diet (HFD)‐induced hepatic steatosis. An HFD‐induced NAFLD mouse model was established in C57BL/6 mice, followed by NMN administration for 8 weeks. HepG2 cells were treated with palmitic acid and co‐incubated with NMN to establish an in vitro lipid accumulation model. Network pharmacology analysis and transcriptomic profiling were performed to identify potential molecular targets and pathways involved in the protective effects of NMN against NAFLD. Lipid accumulation was evaluated by H&E staining and Oil Red O staining. Serum lipid metabolism parameters were measured using assay kits. Quantitative RT‐PCR and Western blotting were used to examine the expression of pathway‐related genes and proteins to investigate the potential mechanism by which NMN alleviates hepatic steatosis. Compared with the HFD model group, NMN intervention significantly reduced body weight and alleviated hepatic steatosis. It also lowered levels of low‐density lipoprotein (LDL), triglycerides, total cholesterol, and fasting blood glucose, while increasing high‐density lipoprotein (HDL) levels. Liver PPAR‐γ levels decreased, while HNF4α and SHBG levels increased. These findings suggest that the protective effects of NMN on HFD‐induced hepatic steatosis are associated with decreased hepatic PPAR‐γ expression and increased HNF4α and SHBG expression. NMN showed protective effects against HFD‐induced NAFLD, which were associated with improvements in hepatic lipid metabolism. By integrating network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, and experimental validation, this study provides initial evidence regarding molecular changes associated with the effects of NMN in NAFLD.

article.title: Ellagic acid alleviates paraquat-induced oxidative stress and metabolic disturbances in the muscle of piglets
article.authors: Yuankun Deng; Nan Wang; Yuxin Xiao; Jing Wang; Xiyuan Bao
article.abstract: Oxidative stress disrupts nutrient metabolism and may impair muscle development in piglets. This study investigated whether dietary ellagic acid (EA) supplementation alleviates paraquat (PQ)-induced oxidative stress and metabolic disturbances in the longissimus dorsi muscle of piglets. Piglets were assigned to a control group, a PQ-challenged group, and a PQ-challenged group supplemented with 0.01% EA. PQ challenge did not significantly affect final body weight or average daily gain but impaired antioxidant status, as evidenced by decreased serum total antioxidant capacity and glutathione peroxidase activity and reduced superoxide dismutase and glutathione levels in the longissimus dorsi muscle. EA supplementation significantly increased these four antioxidant indices relative to PQ alone. PQ also decreased the expression of several muscle development-related genes, including MYOD, MYOG, DESMIN, and CAV3 , whereas EA significantly increased CAV3, FOXO1, P21 , and MCP-1 expression relative to PQ alone without significantly altering MYOD, MYOG , or DESMIN . Furthermore, PQ markedly altered the amino acid profile of the longissimus dorsi muscle and reduced the expression of amino acid transporters, including SLC1A1 and SLC6A6 . EA supplementation increased muscle Tau, Glu, Ile, Leu, Phe, and Pro concentrations, increased SLC1A1 and SLC6A6 expression, and decreased PRODH, OAT , and ODC expression relative to PQ alone. PQ challenge also disrupted the long-chain fatty acid profile and suppressed genes involved in fatty acid handling, whereas EA increased FABP3, CD36, and PLIN3 expression and increased C18:3N-3 and C22:1N-9 relative to PQ alone. Overall, these findings suggest that EA may alleviate selected PQ-associated biochemical and metabolic disturbances by improving antioxidant status and modulating muscle amino acid and lipid metabolism.

article.title: Milk, Cheese, and Fatty Acid Characterization in Latin America: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Methodological Gaps, and Emerging Analytical Approaches (2010–2025)
article.authors: Luisa F. Diaz-Bernal; Diana Chito-Trujillo; Maite Rada-Mendoza; José Luis Arciniegas Herrera; Nancy Janneth Molano-Tobar; Rubén Andrés Ortega-Bonilla
article.abstract: Milk and cheese research in Latin America includes nutritional composition, processing, and fatty acids (FAs) characterization, but a well-founded structure and the analytical tools employed have not been mapped. This bibliometric review gathers the structure, thematic evolution, collaboration networks, and analytical capacity of research on milk, cheese, and FA characterization in the region. Scopus records (2010–2025) with at least one of the authors affiliated with a Latin American institution were screened following PRISMA 2020, yielding 651 documents, analyzed with Bibliometrix (v4.3.3) and VOSviewer (v1.6.20). Brazil contributed 66% of the output, and 20.43% of the documents involved international co-authorship, mainly with Spain and the United States. Cheese, whey, and lactic acid bacteria were prominent topics, while gas chromatography and conjugated linoleic acid were the main analytical and FA terms; terms linked to high-resolution techniques and chemometrics were rare or recent. These patterns suggest a consolidated thematic base, with opportunities to integrate advanced analytical and multivariate approaches and to strengthen interinstitutional collaboration.

article.title: Maternal inheritance accelerates sex chromosome degeneration and mitonuclear coevolution in a brood parasitic bird.
article.authors: Sorenson MD, Osipova E, Spottiswoode CN, Jamie GA, Dixit T, DaCosta JM, Sackton TB, Warren WC, Balakrishnan CN.
article.abstract: The coevolution of interacting mitochondrial and nuclear genes is increasingly recognized as a critical component of organismal fitness and a potential source of genetic incompatibilities that promote speciation. In species with 'ZW' sex chromosomes, however, selection on maternally inherited traits may impact mitonuclear coevolution owing to the effective linkage of the W chromosome and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Here we show that in brood parasitic cuckoo finches (Anomalospiza imberbis), enhanced ecological selection on a maternally inherited trait (mimetic egg colouration) subjects both the W chromosome and mtDNA to increased accumulation of slightly deleterious mutations via genetic hitchhiking, accelerating W chromosome pseudogenization and gene loss, as well as mitonuclear coevolution. Remarkably, as other W-linked genes were lost, two egg colour genes, representing likely targets of selection during cuckoo finch-host coevolution, were recruited to the W chromosome. Using structural models of the respiratory complexes and mitoribosome, we also show that the rate of amino acid substitution in nuclear-encoded residues is a function of their proximity to mtDNA-encoded residues, providing evidence of compensatory mitonuclear coevolution. Our results link species-level coevolution to both sex chromosome degeneration and mitonuclear coevolution. More generally, they highlight the genomic consequences of adaptation without recombination.

article.title: MiR-204-5p signalling modulates apoptosis and mitophagy-related changes after intracerebral hemorrhage in adult rats
article.authors: Li D, Wen X, Song w, Ouyang Y, Luo Q, Yin M, Zhong Y, Qin Z, Bao B, Cao X, Wu M, Chen Z, Yin X.
article.abstract: Abstract Background The survival of neurons around the hematoma is crucial for the recovery of neurological function after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Neuronal apoptosis and mitochondrial quality control disturbances are important factors for secondary brain injury after ICH, but their molecular mechanisms have not been fully elucidated. This study investigated the role of miR-204-5p in ICH and analyzed its association with apoptotic and mitophagy-related signalling. Methods A collagenase-induced ICH model was established in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. miR-204-5p expression was assessed in perihaematoma brain tissue and in serum from patients with ICH. Neurological deficits, brain water content and blood-brain barrier permeability were evaluated after intracerebroventricular administration of a miR-204-5p agomir. Apoptosis-associated markers and mitophagy-related proteins were assessed by western blotting, TUNEL staining, immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy. Target prediction, luciferase reporter assays and gene knockdown experiments were used to investigate TAOK1 and CAMK1. GATA3 promoter activity and the effects of donepezil pretreatment were also examined. Results miR-204-5p was reduced in perihaematoma brain tissue and in serum from patients with ICH, and lower serum levels were associated with higher NIHSS and mRS scores in the available clinical samples. miR-204-5p overexpression improved neurological deficits and reduced apoptosis-associated changes and mitophagy-related molecular and ultrastructural changes after ICH. TAOK1 and CAMK1 were identified as direct post-transcriptional targets of miR-204-5p by bioinformatic prediction, expression analysis and dual-luciferase assays. TAOK1 knockdown reduced TUNEL-positive signals, whereas CAMK1 knockdown attenuated mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. GATA3 increased miR-204-5p promoter activity, and its expression was reduced after ICH. Donepezil pretreatment increased GATA3 expression and was associated with reduced apoptosis-associated and mitophagy-related changes. Conclusions Together, these findings suggest that the GATA3–miR-204-5p–CAMK1/TAOK1 axis may contribute to neuronal injury after ICH. Mitophagic flux and the causal relationships among these components remain to be established. The clinical association and donepezil findings are preliminary and require further validation.

article.title: Multi-scale effects of single-dose psilocybin in the macaque brain
article.authors: Wang J, Chen J, Sun W, Yang Z, Luo C, Yang F, Zhu Y, Wang H, Zhang X, Masthay J, Baek S, Li J, Zhuo Y, Wang X, Wu Y, Ma Y, Sun Q, Ji W, Chang S, Wang X, Zhu X, Hu J, Chen Y, Yuan T.
article.abstract: Abstract Psilocybin holds strong therapeutic promise for treating major depressive disorder. However, the cellular and molecular substrates underlying its action have not been fully elucidated, especially in the primate brain. We combined multimodal MRI, magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomics and metabolomics, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to map the multiscale temporospatial dynamics induced by a single dose of psilocybin in cynomolgus macaques. Psilocybin increased the integration of the frontoparietal network (FPN) with the default-mode and limbic networks, transiently reduced integration of the FPN with the somatomotor network, and induced global network segregation. Several regions in the cortex, striatum, and thalamus as well as certain of the frontoparietal white matter pathways showed persistent enhancement lasting 1 week. Notably, these changes were accompanied by a CSF multi-omics shift from acute prostaglandin-dominated inflammation to a sustained enrichment of an omega-3 fatty acid-associated anti-inflammatory state together with a bidirectional reorganization of extracellular matrix (ECM)-related signatures, characterized by increased CD44 and decreased fibulin-family proteins. In addition, we found lasting upregulation of TCA-cycle and NAD(P)-dependent redox enzymes. This was further supported by sustained elevations of glutamate/glutamine and total creatine in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), which was found using in vivo MRS. At the cellular level, psilocybin promoted HTR2A selective upregulation in deep-layer excitatory neurons along with a widespread enhancement of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation centered on the complex I subunit ND3 across diverse excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Glial-state remodeling, including a shift of astrocytes toward ECM remodeling states and microglia toward an anti-inflammatory state, also occurred. Collectively, these findings provide evidence in the primate brain that psilocybin induces functional integration and segregation of brain networks, enhances energy metabolism and synaptic plasticity, and modulates neuroimmune signaling. All the data will be shared as an integrated resource for primate psilocybin research.

article.title: Respiration-deficient cells require pyruvate carboxylase to suppress asparagine auxotrophy.
article.authors: Cui R, Ryu KW, Fu Y, Bakouny Z, Li D, Kavlashvili T, Sfeir A, Thompson CB.
article.abstract: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) impair ETC activity and oxidative phosphorylation, but their phenotypic consequences vary with heteroplasmy levels. Whether increasing mtDNA heteroplasmy creates metabolic dependencies not present in respiratory-competent cells remains unknown. Here, we show that low pyruvate carboxylase (PC) expression creates an asparagine dependency in high-mtDNA-heteroplasmy, respiration-compromised cells. In isogenic cells carrying similar mtDNA deletions, respiration declines linearly with increasing heteroplasmy, whereas redox imbalance emerges only above 50% heteroplasmy. Above 70% heteroplasmy, integrated stress-response-associated translational defects emerge, which can be reversed by either exogenous asparagine or PC overexpression. Asparagine dependence inversely correlates with PC expression across respiration-deficient cells. Consistent with this pattern, patient-derived thyroid tumour cells harbouring a high-heteroplasmy complex I mutation and low PC levels exhibit asparagine auxotrophy and sensitivity to L-asparaginase. Together, these findings demonstrate a role for mitochondrial PC in cellular asparagine synthesis under conditions of compromised respiratory activity.

article.title: Therapeutic Potential of [(AP) 2 M]: A Rationally Designed Polyherbal Formulation for Antidiabetic and Antihyperlipidemic Effects in Alloxan-Induced Diabetic Mice.
article.authors: Ahmed MS, Hasan MT, Bismillah M, Rahman MM, Hossain MI, Khan MH, Islam MA.
article.abstract: Medicinal plants are widely used in diabetes management due to their multi-targeted bioactive constituents. Phyllanthus emblica , Piper nigrum , Aegle marmelos , Moringa oleifera , and Azadirachta indica possess well-documented antidiabetic properties, providing a scientific basis for developing a rationally designed polyherbal formulation. This study evaluated the basic phytochemical characterization, antioxidant, antidiabetic, antihyperlipidemic, and preliminary toxicity profiles of a polyherbal formulation (designated as [(AP) 2 M]) in an alloxan-induced type 1 diabetic mouse model. Polyphenolic (phenolic and flavonoid) contents, antioxidant activity (DPPH & metal-chelating assays), and α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities were determined. Acute oral toxicity was assessed according to OECD Guideline 423, with LD 50 estimation to establish the preliminary toxicity profile and effective dosing. Diabetic mice received the formulation [(AP) 2 M] (30-120 mg/kg) orally for 3 weeks, after which blood glucose, the lipid profile, SGPT, SGOT, and histopathological changes in the liver, kidneys, and pancreas were evaluated. The formulation exhibited substantial phenolic (111.52 ± 0.444 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (211.30 ± 5.129 mg CAE/g) contents together with strong antioxidant and antidiabetic enzyme inhibitory activity. Acute oral toxicity assessment estimated an LD 50 of 900 mg/kg (GHS Category 4). At 120 mg/kg, it reduced blood glucose to a level comparable with glibenclamide and significantly improved lipid profile, SGPT, and SGOT levels ( p < 0.001). Histopathological examination demonstrated improvement in pancreatic, hepatic, and renal tissues. Since the formulation demonstrated promising antioxidant, antihyperglycemic, and antihyperlipidemic activities in a diabetic mouse model, it could be a potential alternative for further investigation as a complementary therapeutic approach for diabetes management.

article.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline.
article.authors: Li J, Wang ZH, Pan JX, Jiang ZL, Li R, Gao XF, Sheng G, Wang ZH, Ma YQ, Wang ZL, Wang T, Huan R, Zeng LT, Zhang W, Dai DP, Cui J, Zhou XY, Zhang LQ, Su W, Chen HB, Hu GX, Qi RM, Cai JP.
article.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)-a major product of NTP oxidation-not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

article.title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
article.authors: Calista Diehl; H. Robert Horvitz
article.abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O 2 ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

article.title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
article.authors: Chun Zhang; Xiuxing Liu; Nanwei Xu; Hui Chen; Yuehan Gao; Chenyang Gu; Xinyue Shen; Junying Wu; Xuejing Lu; Pei Zhang; Yuxuan He; Zhuping Xu; Wenru Su
article.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T H 17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4 + T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

article.title: The Major Iron Transporter DMT1 Promotes Renal Fibrosis by Activating Ferroptosis and Enforcing TGF-β1 Signaling in Renal Tubular Cells.
article.authors: Ying Pan; Meiqi Liu; Jiawei Qiu; Liqin Jia; Mingyang Li; Xiaohui Gong; Hongfei Cao; Hongru Cao
article.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Renal fibrosis is a common pathological feature of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but effective therapies are still lacking. Ferroptosis has been increasingly associated with CKD; however, the iron-handling proteins that link ferroptotic stress to fibrotic signaling remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1) as a previously unrecognized regulatory factor that integrates iron metabolism, ferroptotic stress, and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling in tubular epithelial cells (TECs). RESULTS: DMT1 expression was elevated in TECs from folic acid injection- or unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced mouse CKD models and in isolated primary TECs exposed to TGF-β1 or palmitic acid, accompanied by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of DMT1 in TECs significantly attenuated renal fibrosis, with reduced renal fibrosis area, decreased expression of profibrotic genes and markers, lower mtROS production, and restored fatty acid oxidation. DMT1 deficiency also attenuated lipid peroxidation, with reduced 4-HNE levels and lipid droplet deposition in mouse CKD models. Additionally, DMT1 deletion reduced tissue iron content, reversed ferroptosis-associated morphological changes in TECs, and restored tissue glutathione peroxidase-4 expression. Notably, DMT1 deletion reduced both total Smad2 and phosphorylated Smad2 induced by TGF-β1, consistent with suppression of the TGF-β1-Smad axis. INNOVATION AND CONCLUSIONS: These findings support a model in which tubular DMT1 integrates iron overload, ferroptotic stress, and TGF-β1-Smad signaling during fibrotic progression in CKD. DMT1 functions as a signaling hub contributing to TGF-β1-Smad axis activation, although a direct causal chain from iron influx to transforming growth factor beta receptor 1 induction remains to be fully delineated. DMT1 inhibition may offer a tubular-selective therapeutic strategy for CKD. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

article.title: Multifaceted Physiological Roles of Lipoproteins and Understanding Atherosclerosis: Crosstalk Between Lipoproteins and Bioactive Lipids.
article.authors: Makoto Kurano
article.abstract: Traditional management of atherosclerosis focuses primarily on cholesterol and triglycerides; however, lipoproteins also transport bioactive lipids that critically regulate systemic inflammation and metabolic health. This review highlights the diverse physiological and clinical roles of apolipoproteins and bioactive lipids beyond classical lipid accumulation. First, we discuss how hepatic transporters NPC1L1 and ABCG5/8 modulate glucose metabolism and handle non-cholesterol lipids, including phytosterols. Second, we emphasize the apolipoprotein M (ApoM) and sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) axis. ApoM protects S1P from degradation and directly mediates the pleiotropic benefits of high-density lipoprotein (HDL), including anti-apoptotic, antithrombotic, and renoprotective effects. Third, reverse translational research utilizing genome-wide association studies identifies apolipoprotein D (ApoD) as a key anti-inflammatory modulator. Finally, clinical lipidomics underscores the importance of "minor" lysophospholipids, such as lysophosphatidylinositol and lysophosphatidylserine, alongside lysophosphatidic acid in the pathogenesis of acute coronary syndrome. Understanding the dynamic crosstalk between lipid transporters, apolipoproteins, and bioactive lipids provides novel mechanistic insights into cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, paving the way for innovative biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies.

article.title: Nanoarchitectonics via emulsion interfacial in situ polymerization for enhanced cross-presentation and antitumor immunity.
article.authors: Fang Y, Zhang J, Ma Y, Xiang L, Wang Y, Li S, Cheng Y, Li Y, Ma L, Zhang H, Shi Y, Zhao G.
article.venue: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
article.abstract: Emulsion adjuvants enhance vaccine responses by forming antigen reservoirs and maintaining local immune stimulation, but their dynamic oil-water interfaces have limitations in regulating intracellular transport and cross-presentation. Here, we developed a mild in situ emulsion interface polymerization (EIIP) strategy, utilizing the oil-water interface as a confined reaction zone to generate functional polymer shells around the antigen-containing droplets. By constructing particles with consistent components, the same antigen is confined to the aqueous core or on the shell surface respectively, thereby evaluating the contribution of antigen location to immunity. Internal compartmentalization enhanced dendritic-cell maturation and MHC-I cross presentation. It retained antigen within the pH-responsive shell during intracellular trafficking, which triggered mitochondrial perturbation, cytosolic mitochondrial DNA accumulation and increased 2'3'-cGAMP. In vivo, internal antigen compartmentalization strengthened antigen-specific CD8 + T cell responses and antitumour efficacy. EIIP retains the squalene emulsion, which prolonged antigen retention at the injection site and promoted delivery to draining lymph nodes. The distinct contributions of squalene in prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models further indicate that prolonged antigen exposure and antigen localization are non-equivalent determinants of vaccine activity. EIIP turns the emulsion interface into a reaction zone, thereby alters its cross-presentation and antigen-specific CD8 + T cell response.

article.title: Insights into CD36/P-gp involvement in dietary lipid-driven PAH transport across the blood-brain barrier.
article.authors: Xiaofang Liu; Jie Zhu; Li Liang; Jixian Zhang; Chaoting Wen; Youdong Li; Guoyan Liu; Xin Xu
article.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), as widespread environmental contaminants, exhibit neurotoxicity. Because PAHs often co-occur with dietary lipids in foods, those lipids might serve as vehicles that alter PAH biotransport and accumulation in the brain. In this work, we systematically investigated how three common dietary fatty acids-oleic acid, linoleic acid (LA), and linolenic acid-differently influence the transport steps (including cellular uptake, efflux, and clearance) of benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) and benzo[b]fluoranthene (BbF) across the blood-brain barrier, using a bEnd.3 cell-based model, and explored the potential underlying molecular mechanisms. Results revealed that dietary lipids, acting as carriers, significantly enhanced cellular uptake of PAHs, with LA increasing the uptake of BaP and BbF by 20.36% and 17.90%, respectively, and accelerated transmembrane transport dynamics. Simultaneously, distinct lipids differentially affected PAH clearance and efflux. Notably, LA delayed the clearance of PAHs, prolonging the elimination half-life of BaP from 10.117 h to 17.696 h and that of BbF from 7.418 h to 14.964 h, thereby increasing overall brain exposure. Mechanistically, LA was observed to upregulate the fatty acid transporter CD36, and functional inhibition studies suggested that P-glycoprotein and CD36 may jointly contribute to lipid-modulated effects. This study suggests that dietary lipids influence brain exposure to PAHs through a multi-level network, highlighting a factor that warrants consideration when assessing their neurotoxicity risks.

article.title: P2X7 receptor-mediated inflammatory and ionic remodeling promotes atrial fibrillation in diabetes.
article.authors: Fu Y, Ke Y, Cao Z, Chen Y, Long X, Li Y, Guo K, Luo Y, Hu K, Zhao Q.
article.abstract: Aims Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the mechanisms by which diabetic metabolic stress promotes atrial arrhythmogenesis remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence suggests that purinergic signaling-driven sterile inflammation plays an important role in cardiac remodeling. This study aimed to investigate the role of the ATP-gated purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) in DM-associated AF and to explore its underlying mechanisms. Methods and results Rats were randomly assigned to four groups: control (Con), diabetes mellitus (DM), P2X7R overexpression in controls (Con+P2X7), and P2X7R knockdown in diabetic rats (DM + P2X7 KD), with gene manipulation achieved using AAV9-cTnT vectors. AF susceptibility, atrial structural and electrical remodeling were systematically evaluated using electrophysiological studies, optical mapping, patch-clamp recordings, and molecular analyses. DM markedly increased AF inducibility and duration, accompanied by enhanced sympathetic nerve activity and activation of P2X7R-related inflammatory signaling. Compared with controls, DM atria exhibited pronounced interstitial fibrosis, connexin remodeling, delayed atrial activation, slowed conduction velocity, and increased conduction heterogeneity. Atrial P2X7R overexpression in control rats recapitulated key arrhythmogenic features, whereas P2X7R KD in diabetic rats significantly attenuated atrial remodeling and reduced AF susceptibility, without altering the diabetes-induced increase in sympathetic activity. At the cellular level, P2X7R selectively modulated I Na , I Ca,L , and I Kur while relatively preserving I to , and was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and disturbed Ca 2+ homeostasis, characterized by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, increased cytosolic Ca 2+ signals, and reduced mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake. Conclusion P2X7R-mediated inflammatory and mitochondrial signaling contribute to diabetic atrial remodeling and AF susceptibility. Targeting P2X7R may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing AF in diabetes.

article.title: Alginate Oligosaccharide Alleviates Age-Related Hearing Loss via TFEB-Associated Autophagy Restoration to Attenuate Oxidative Stress and Inflammation.
article.authors: Su S, Zhang X, Li M, Zhang P, Ya B, Wang W, Wang L, Li S, Li H, Li X, Chen J, Yin H.
article.venue: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
article.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is a highly prevalent sensory disorder characterized by progressive cochlear degeneration. To date, no effective pharmacological treatment is clinically available. In this study, we investigated the otoprotective efficacy and underlying mechanisms of alginate oligosaccharide (AOS) against D-galactose (D-gal)-induced senescence in vitro and age-associated cochlear dysfunction in C57BL/6J mice. Multi-omics analyses identified oxidative stress, inflammation, cellular senescence, and autophagy, as core targeted pathways associated with AOS treatment. In D-gal-treated HEI-OC1 cells and cochlear explants, AOS treatment markedly reduced senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity and downregulated senescence markers P16 and P21. These anti-senescent effects were accompanied by ameliorated oxidative and pro-inflammatory stress, as reflected by decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS), preserved mitochondrial function, and suppressed nuclear factor-κB/NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NF-κB/NLRP3) signaling. AOS also promoted transcription factor EB (TFEB) nuclear translocation and attenuated D-gal-induced autophagy-related dysregulation. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy and TFEB nuclear entry effectively blunted these cytoprotective, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory benefits of AOS, supporting the involvement of TFEB-associated autophagic signaling in AOS-mediated protection. In C57BL/6J mice, long-term AOS administration significantly lowered auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds, attenuated the age-related degeneration of hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons, and reduced cochlear senescence markers. Furthermore, AOS suppressed MDA accumulation, elevated SOD activity, inhibited NF-κB/NLRP3 activation, and restored TFEB-associated autophagic homeostasis in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that AOS protects against age-associated cochlear dysfunction and senescence, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and inflammation and improved autophagy-related homeostasis. TFEB-associated signaling may contribute to these protective effects, supporting further investigation of AOS for the prevention or delay of cochlear aging.

article.title: Cross-kingdom metabolic regulation by a symbiotic virus: Transient viral microRNAs coordinate host metabolism and immune responses.
article.authors: Yu-Chun Lin; Yao-Kuang Tseng; Ping Chen; Chia-Yang Lin; Cheng-Kang Tang; Yueh-Lung Wu
article.abstract: Symbiotic microorganisms and endogenous viruses play fundamental roles in shaping host physiology, yet the non-coding RNA-mediated mechanisms underlying viral-driven metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate a novel mechanism of cross-kingdom metabolic manipulation mediated by symbiotic viral microRNAs. Using the tobacco cutworm Spodoptera litura, its endoparasitoid wasp Snellenius manilae, and the wasp-associated bracovirus SmBV as a model system, we identified two virus-derived microRNAs, SmBV-miR-2733 and SmBV-miR-3772, that target the host lipogenic genes encoding AGPAT and lipin, leading to the suppression of glycerolipid biosynthesis and reduced lipid accumulation.
