Functional analyses revealed that these symbiotic viral miRNAs concurrently attenuate host innate immune signaling pathways (Toll and JAK/STAT) and cellular encapsulation, establishing a mechanistic link between viral metabolic coercion and host immunomodulation. Crucially, this viral microRNA-mediated regulation is transient and highly dynamic; miRNA expression declines during later stages of infection, coinciding with an intermediate recovery of host lipogenic gene expression and lipid reserves, which may help sustain the developing parasitoids. Prolonged experimental maintenance of viral miRNAs disrupted host energetic homeostasis and compromised symbiotic success, underscoring the evolutionary necessity of temporally coordinated metabolic regulation. Comparative genomic analysis identified miR-2733- and miR-3772-like candidate loci with miRNA-precursor-like structures that are unevenly distributed across related bracovirus lineages. Together, our findings provide significant mechanistic insights into how symbiotic viral effectors post-transcriptionally rewire host metabolic and immune networks, offering a broader conceptual framework for understanding homeostasis in diverse host-microbe symbioses.

article.title: Lipid remodeling during phosphate starvation in plants: from metabolism to inter-organelle lipid transport.
article.authors: Siqi Yan; Samia AlSayyad; Morgane Michaud
article.abstract: Phosphate (Pi) starvation triggers extensive membrane lipid remodeling in plants, in which phospholipids are degraded and replaced by phosphorus-free glycolipids to recycle Pi while preserving membrane integrity. Although the metabolic pathways underlying this process have been extensively studied, the mechanisms coordinating lipid trafficking between organelles remain poorly understood. In this review, we summarize current knowledge of lipid metabolism during Pi starvation, including glycolipid synthesis, phospholipid and sphingolipid degradation, and triacylglycerol accumulation. We then discuss recent advances highlighting the emerging role of lipid transport in membrane remodeling. Finally, we highlight the major unanswered questions regarding the spatial organization of lipid remodeling and the molecular mechanisms linking lipid degradation, synthesis, and inter-organelle transport. Understanding these processes will be essential for building an integrated view of plant adaptation to phosphate limitation and for improving phosphorus-use efficiency in crops.

article.title: Influence of hemin on biophysical properties of membranes.
article.authors: Laspa Z, Jarnot N, Andronico L, Sych T, Rohlfing AK, Gone N, Castor T, Pillaiyar T, Laufer S, Sezgin E, Gawaz MP.
article.abstract: Hemin released from erythrocytes activates platelets through both receptor-dependent and receptor-independent mechanisms. While lower hemin concentrations predominantly activate the immune receptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAM) signaling via glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2), higher concentrations induce pronounced receptor-independent cellular alterations, including loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid peroxidation, and plasma membrane fragmentation. However, the mechanism of receptor-independent effect of hemin is still unclear. To test whether hemin can directly interact with and remodel membranes, we employed giant unilamellar vesicles composed of different lipid compositions as model membrane systems and treated them with unlabeled and fluorescently-labeled hemin. We analyzed how hemin treatment alters membrane biophysical properties using fluorescence microscopy, spectral imaging, fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS), and flow cytometry. We found that fluorophore-labeled hemin can be directly visualized in lipid bilayers. Furthermore, high concentrations of hemin increased membrane order in all lipid compositions tested. The strongest effect was observed in more fluid membranes, whereas highly ordered membranes were less affected. Interestingly, in cholesterol-containing membranes, even the lowest hemin concentration produced changes comparable to those induced by the highest concentration, suggesting that cholesterol enhances the influence of hemin on lipid bilayers. Finally, we observed strong increase in permeability of membranes upon hemin treatment. Overall, our findings demonstrate that hemin can directly accumulate in lipid membranes, increase membrane order, reduce membrane fluidity and alter membrane integrity, resulting in enhanced membrane permeability.

article.title: A case for DNA-membrane interactions in the responses to DNA damage.
article.authors: Moriel-Carretero M.
article.abstract: Eukaryotic cells harbour two genomes, the nuclear and the mitochondrial ones. Both are subjected to spontaneous and induced DNA damage that threatens biological function. In the nucleus, damage in the DNA is detected, signalled and taken care of by a dedicated, complex network of proteins termed the DNA Damage Response (DDR). In the mitochondria, this first-front DNA damage detection network is less characterized, despite that effective, downstream mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) repair is documented. Also, given that mtDNA exists as multiple copies inside a single mitochondrion, the cell can selectively get rid of unhealthy mtDNA molecules. This later process suggests the existence of an additional quality control mechanism operating within mitochondria. Careful analysis of the literature suggests that damaged DNA can cause alterations in surrounding membrane structure / composition that could be integrated as an output to appropriately respond to such DNA damage. In this review, I discuss the evidence for membranes' involvement in the response to mtDNA damage. Finally, I discuss similarities and differences between mitochondrial and nuclear membranes and further extend the hypothesis to the possibility that membranes may play roles in signalling DNA damage that arise in the nuclear genome.

article.title: Gramine limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
article.authors: Zhang Y, Su L, Cheng H, Wei W, Xu W, Bao X, Lu C.
article.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis-related damage. NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1), together with its regulatory GTPase Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1 (RAC1), forms a regulatory module that governs redox signaling. Yet small molecules that engage NOX1 and suppress these coupled injury programs remain insufficiently defined. Here, we identified gramine as a candidate NOX1-engaging compound and delineated its protective mechanism in ethanol-associated hepatocellular injury. Alcohol challenge induced a hepatic NOX1/RAC1 response, recapitulated in ethanol-injured hepatocytes. Silencing Nox1 or Rac1 blunted ethanol-driven injury phenotypes, limiting injury-associated enzyme release, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential disturbance, mitochondrial network disruption, and DNA fragmentation while partially preserving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Molecular docking predicted a gramine-NOX1 interaction, a cellular thermal shift assay supported target engagement, and cycloheximide chase analysis showed gramine accelerated NOX1 protein turnover. In ethanol-exposed hepatocytes, gramine conferred concentration-associated protection, improving cell viability, and reducing injury-associated enzyme release, lipid droplet signals, and DNA fragmentation. Post-ethanol gramine treatment reduced injury-associated enzyme release. NOX1 overexpression undermined gramine-mediated protection and reinstated ferrous iron accumulation, glutathione redox imbalance, reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial dysfunction, and damage-associated signaling. Erastin weakened gramine-mediated protection, implicating inhibition of ferroptotic responses in the protective mechanism. In alcohol-gavaged mice, gramine reduced hepatic NOX1 abundance, serum injury markers, Fe 2+ levels, lipid accumulation, and lipid peroxidation-associated changes, while preserving GPX4 abundance and limiting histopathological injury. These findings support gramine as a NOX1-engaging small molecule that limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.

article.title: Withaferin A induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells via ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 axis.
article.authors: Liu Y, Tang Y, Xie D, Zhang Q, Hu Z, Bai L, Feng S.
article.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide with a high mortality rate, and conventional chemotherapy faces significant limitations due to drug resistance and severe adverse effects. Natural products represent promising alternative therapeutic agents. In this study, withaferin A (WA), a major bioactive compound derived from Withania somnifera, was investigated for its anticancer activity in GC. We found that WA inhibited the growth and migration of GC cells while inducing both apoptosis and ferroptosis. WA dose-dependently suppressed GC cell proliferation and colony formation. Mechanistically, WA induced apoptosis through ROS accumulation, resulting in mitochondrial depolarization, increased expression of BAX/BAD, and decreased expression of Bcl-2. Meanwhile, WA triggered ferroptosis by promoting ubiquitin-dependent degradation of GPX4, depleting GSH, increasing lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, and activating the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling axis to elevate Fe 2 ⁺ accumulation. Western blotting and transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that WA regulated apoptosis- and ferroptosis-related proteins and activated the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway. In vivo, WA significantly suppressed tumor growth in a xenograft model without causing apparent systemic toxicity, indicating its therapeutic potential for GC treatment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that withaferin A is a potent and promising natural compound that induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells through ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling pathway, respectively, highlighting its potential as a candidate therapeutic agent for cancer treatment.

article.title: A protein modification of TIGAR Fuels HCC Growth by Boosting Tumor Glucose Metabolism.
article.authors: Claudia M Rejano-Gordillo; Carolina Conter; Patricia Peña-Sanfélix; Laura Mosca; Miguel Ángel Merlos-Rodrigo; Joaquín Tamargo-Azpilicueta; Carlos Díaz-Cuevas; Sofía Lachiondo-Ortega; L Estefanía Zapata-Pavas; Nerea Ferreiro; Eleonora Davoli; Naiara Gutiez; Juan Anguita; Marco Piva; Pietro Guerra; Irene González-Recio; Naroa Goikoetxea-Usandizaga; Marc Beltrà; Mikel Azkargorta; Félix Elortza; Natalia Herman Sánchez; Patrizia Pontisso; Jesús M Banales; Rubén Nogueiras; José J G Marín; Maite G Fernandez-Barrena; Matías A Ávila; Antonio Zorzano; Raúl M Luque; Zbynek Heger; Manuel D Gahete; Erica Villa; Miguel Lafarga; Irene Díaz-Moreno; María Luz Martínez-Chantar
article.abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver malignancy and is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming. TIGAR (TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator) regulates glucose metabolism and redox balance by redirecting glucose flux toward the pentose phosphate pathway. Although TIGAR is frequently upregulated in HCC, the mechanisms controlling its activity remain poorly understood. We investigated whether SUMOylation regulates TIGAR function and HCC progression. METHODS: TIGAR SUMOylation was evaluated in two independent HCC patient cohorts (n=86 and n=19), HCC cell lines and mouse models. Seahorse assays, metabolomic profiling, 13C-glucose tracing, mitochondrial analyses and in vivo tumor models were used to investigate its effects on glucose metabolism, oxidative stress and tumor growth. RESULTS: TIGAR was found to be SUMOylated in HCC tissues, cultured cells and murine tumor models. SUMOylation enhanced the pro-tumorigenic activity of TIGAR by promoting its interaction with glycolytic enzymes, including PFKFB3 and HK2, resulting in increased glycolytic activity and pentose phosphate pathway flux. Conversely, SUMOylation-deficient K82R cells exhibited increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and reduced proliferation and invasion compared with WT TIGAR. In the orthotopic liver model (n=4 per group), K82R expression was associated with reduced tumor growth. In the CAM assay, SUMOylation-deficient K82R clones showed significantly reduced tumor weight (n=8 per group, p < 0.0001) and volume (n=4 per group, p < 0.05) compared with WT TIGAR cells. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies Lys82 SUMOylation as a novel mechanism regulating TIGAR-mediated metabolic reprogramming and HCC progression. Targeting TIGAR SUMOylation may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for HCC. IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: This study identifies TIGAR SUMOylation as a new mechanism driving metabolic adaptation in hepatocellular carcinoma. SUMOylated TIGAR promotes glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway activity and mitochondrial function. Loss of TIGAR SUMOylation increases oxidative stress and reduces tumor growth and invasion. These findings highlight TIGAR SUMOylation as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in liver cancer. Overall, our data support targeting this pathway to improve therapeutic strategies for hepatocellular carcinoma.

article.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation and its role in aging of rats: Behavioral and pathological evidence.
article.authors: Ahangari A, Tukmechi A, Hadian M, Mahmoudi S, Babaei-Balderlou F.
article.abstract: Aging is associated with progressive oxidative stress, chronic inflammation and functional deterioration across multiple organs. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in regulating aging through the gut-brain axis and systemic immune interactions. The present study investigated the therapeutic potential of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in a D-galactose-induced rat model of accelerated aging. Male rats were allocated into four experimental groups: Healthy control, D-galactose-induced aging, aging treated with FMT and aging treated with antibiotics prior to FMT. Accelerated aging was induced by intraperitoneal administration of D-galactose (150 mg/kg/day). FMT was performed using fecal microbiota obtained from healthy donor rats. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Morris Water Maze (MWM), and histopathological alterations were evaluated in the heart, hippocampus and colon using hematoxylin and eosin staining. D-galactose administration significantly impaired spatial learning and memory and induced marked pathological alterations, including myocardial edema and hemorrhage, neuronal degeneration and vacuolation in the hippocampus, and crypt disruption with inflammatory cell infiltration in the colon. FMT markedly improved behavioral performance and substantially attenuated tissue damage in all examined organs. In contrast, antibiotic pretreatment was associated with less pronounced improvement following FMT, suggesting that the recipient intestinal environment may influence the response to transplantation. These findings provide behavioral and histopathological evidence consistent with beneficial effects of FMT on several features of accelerated aging; however, direct changes in microbial composition, microbial function, and donor engraftment were not assessed.

article.title: Tumorigenic microenvironment alters N-terminal membrane protein topology via a mechanism consistent with the Charge Balance Rule.
article.authors: Savenkova D, Bulatova L, Kozlova A, Akberova N, Skripova V, Firsova D, Vlasenkova R, Bogdanova N, Kiyamova R, Bogdanov M.
article.venue: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
article.abstract: The molecular mechanism of changing and varied antigenicity of membrane proteins during cancerogenesis, where changes in membrane lipid composition and abiotic tumor microenvironment occur regularly, is unknown. By challenging ovarian cancer cells to tumorigenic hypoxia and acidosis, we observed unexpected surface exposure of the Na + -dependent phosphate transporter (NaPi2b) N-termini (NT) previously hidden on the cytoplasmic side of "resting" cancer cells in the accordance with its predicted orientation, violating the Positive Inside Rule. Consistently with the Charge Balance Rule of membrane protein assembly, the reorientation of NaPi2b NT coincides with loss of asymmetry and surface exposure of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), while the coincident exposure of PE and NT of NaPi2b is prevented by knockdown of phospholipid scramblase 1 (PLSCR1). These dynamic topological events can lead to unmasking of previously hidden extramembrane domains (epitopes), which can be potentially used as a novel target for targeted anti-tumor immunotherapy.

article.title: A cascade-targeted nanoplatform for in situ remodeling of the atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment through bidirectional cholesterol regulation and ROS/NO rebalancing.
article.authors: Guan Q, Li Z, Qiao G, Du J, Liu M, Zhang L, He L, Yang Q, Liu L, Shen M, Li Y.
article.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is driven by intertwined dysregulation of cholesterol homeostasis, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, limiting the efficacy of single-target therapies. Here, we developed a hierarchically engineered pH/ROS-responsive nanoplatform, TSCA@OL, for plaque targeting and coordinated microenvironment remodeling. CD44-mediated accumulation enhances plaque localization, while simvastatin (SV) and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) jointly suppress cholesterol synthesis and promote cholesterol efflux. In parallel, suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) and L-arginine (L-Arg) restore ROS/NO balance, promote endothelial repair, and attenuate inflammatory activation. In ApoE ⁻/⁻ mice, TSCA@OL markedly increased plaque ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression, improved serum lipid profiles, and reduced aortic plaque burden by 62.97% relative to the high-fat diet group. Treatment also suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization and improved plaque stability. Collectively, TSCA@OL integrates cholesterol regulation with oxidative-inflammatory correction, providing a coordinated biomaterials strategy for reducing plaque burden and remodeling the atherosclerotic microenvironment. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Atherosclerosis is driven by intertwined lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, endothelial injury, and inflammation, yet most therapies address only one process. This study introduces TSCA@OL, a hierarchically engineered nanoplatform that links biomaterial structure with coordinated biological function. A hyaluronic acid-based outer layer recognizes plaque-associated cells through CD44 and responds to acidic conditions, while a reactive oxygen species-sensitive inner module enables local release. The platform combines simvastatin-mediated suppression of cholesterol synthesis with β-cyclodextrin-mediated cholesterol removal, antioxidant regulation, and nitric oxide support. In atherosclerotic mice, TSCA@OL reduced plaque burden, improved lipid profiles, enhanced markers of cholesterol efflux, and promoted features associated with plaque stabilization. This work provides a biomaterials strategy for remodeling complex disease microenvironments through spatially coordinated, multi-pathway intervention.

article.title: Associations of early measured low-density lipoprotein cholesterol with 12-month stroke recurrence and 90-day functional outcome after moderate-to-severe ischemic stroke.
article.authors: Min Chen; Yue Zhu; Hexian Li; Dezhi Liu; Renliang Zhang; Mingchao Shi; Qingwen Jin
article.venue: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
article.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Current secondary prevention guidelines generally target low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) <1.8 mmol/L after ischemic stroke, but the prognostic relevance of an early level <1.4 mmol/L remains unclear. We examined associations of LDL-C measured within 15 days with 12-month recurrent ischemic stroke and 90-day functional outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: This retrospective day-15 landmark cohort included 1,800 adults with admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale scores of 6-20. All were alive and recurrence-free at day 15. The last fasting LDL-C within 15 days defined groups of 1.8 mmol/L. Cox and Fine-Gray models assessed recurrence. A partial proportional odds model assessed the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 213 patients (11.8%). Recurrence proportions were 6.7%, 9.9%, and 14.2% across groups (global P=0.014). Compared with >1.8 mmol/L, <1.4 mmol/L was associated with a lower recurrence hazard (adjusted hazard ratio 0.49, 95% confidence interval 0.28-0.83). Among 1,677 patients with mRS data, the pairwise common odds ratio (OR) was 1.38 (1.04-1.83), while the overall three-group P value was 0.056. Further adjustment for treatment and measurement day yielded a common OR of 1.37 (0.97-1.93). The day-121 analysis showed no clear association with later recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: Lower early LDL-C was associated with a lower subsequent recurrence hazard among patients meeting the day-15 landmark criteria. Functional findings remained exploratory.

article.title: Deletion of TRPV4 in the POMC neurons exacerbates diet-induced obesity via Ca 2+ -dependent PGAM5-mediated mitophagy.
article.authors: Xi P, Li X, Zhang Y, Song X, Li S, Wen J, Yuan N, Yu C, Qi Z, Shen Y.
article.venue: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
article.abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge driven by profound metabolic dysregulation. Hypothalamic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons are indispensable for whole-body metabolic homeostasis, and transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) channels have emerged as regulators of metabolic control. However, the cell-type-specific function of TRPV4 in POMC neurons remains poorly defined. Herein, we demonstrate a vital role of TRPV4 in regulating POMC neuronal activity. We found that hypothalamic TRPV4 was selectively upregulated in diet-induced obese mice, but remained unchanged in genetically obese mice. TRPV4 expression levels were influenced by nutritional status and exhibited co-localization with POMC. Mice lacking TRPV4 specifically in POMC neurons showed no alterations in systemic energy metabolism under chow diet conditions. However, under high-fat diet feeding, these mice exhibited exacerbated obesity and hyperphagia. In vitro assays revealed that TRPV4 activation impaired POMC neurons by promoting mitophagy. In contrast, TRPV4 inhibition restored POMC neuronal function. Mechanistically, TRPV4 compromised POMC neuronal activity by triggering Ca 2+ -dependent PGAM5 activation and enhancing PINK1/PARKIN-mediated mitophagy. These findings provide comprehensive insights into TRPV4 as a critical regulator of hypothalamic energy balance circuits and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for metabolic disorders.

article.title: mtdsRNA‑driven endoplasmic reticulum stress contributes to trichloroethylene‑induced immune kidney injury.
article.authors: Li R, Jiang R, Chen J, Qin Z, Zhou D, Lian P, Zhu Z, Chen G, Chen M, Zhang J, Zhu Q, Xie H.
article.abstract: Exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE) can cause occupational medicamentose-like dermatitis and severe immune-related kidney damage. Existing treatments focusing on TNF-α and complement pathways show limited effectiveness against TCE-induced kidney injury, with unclear molecular mechanisms. This study explores the involvement of mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mt-dsRNA) in TCE-related kidney damage and its regulatory pathways. Patients with occupational medicamentose-like dermatitis due to TCE (OMDT) showed higher serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels, especially in severe cases. Both in vivo and in vitro studies indicated that LPS reduced PNPT1 expression, leading to mt-dsRNA release, triggering the PKR/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP pathway, causing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and apoptosis. By boosting PNPT1 or inhibiting mitochondrial RNA polymerase with inhibitor of mitochondrial transcription 1(IMT1) decreased mt-dsRNA production and reduced cell damage. These findings suggest that TCE exposure increases systemic LPS, which suppresses PNPT1, causing pathological mt-dsRNA buildup. This activates PKR-dependent ER stress, leading to tubular injury.

article.title: Jinfeng Pills Ameliorate Levonorgestrel-Induced Ovarian Injury by Modulating ApoA1-Associated Cholesterol Homeostasis and PI3K/Akt Signaling.
article.authors: Yingyi Hu; Guoting Li; Qicheng Ni; Ruihua Zhong; Jieyun Zhou; Xiangjie Guo; Wenjie Yang; Huijuan Shi; Yan Zhu
article.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jinfeng Pills (JFP, NMPA approval No. Z20064400) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used to regulate menstruation and support ovulation. It consists of nine medicinal materials: Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. (Yinyanghuo), Cervus elaphus Linnaeus (Lurong), Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. (Renshen), Equus asinus (EJiao), Ligustrum lucidum W.T.Aiton (Nvzhenzi), Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke (Heshouwu), Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. (Xianmao), Cinnamomum cassia (L.) J.Presl (Rougui) and Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Yimucao). Previous studies have demonstrated the protective effects of JFP against ovarian dysfunction. However, the potential protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic exposure to levonorgestrel (LNG), a progestin commonly used in emergency contraception, and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic LNG exposure and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A rat model of chronic LNG exposure was established, and the efficacy of JFP was evaluated based on estrous cycles, serum hormone levels and ovarian morphology. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis and cholesterol-related biochemical assays were performed to investigate the alterations in ovarian cholesterol homeostasis. The role of apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA1) was further examined by using ApoA1 silencing in primary rat ovarian theca cells and intrabursal administration of ApoA1 in vivo. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were subsequently used to validate the key molecular changes and assess the effects of JFP on ApoA1expression, cholesterol homeostasis and the associated signaling pathways. RESULTS: JFP significantly ameliorated LNG-induced ovarian injury, as evidenced by increased serum levels of FSH, LH and AMH, and decreased estradiol levels and the LH/FSH ratio, reduced cystic follicle formation, and attenuated follicular depletion. Transcriptomic analysis in ovarian tissues, together with cholesterol assays, RT-qPCR and Western blotting, revealed that LNG exposure disrupted ovarian cholesterol homeostasis, with alterations in cholesterol transport and increased ovarian ApoA1 abundance. Intrabursal administration of ApoA1 induced ovarian pathological changes and activated PI3K/Akt signaling in vivo, whereas ApoA1 silencing attenuated PI3K/Akt activation and inhibited the viability of primary ovarian theca cells. JFP markedly reduced ovarian ApoA1 accumulation, improved cholesterol homeostasis, and suppressed PI3K/Akt/NF-κB signaling. CONCLUSION: JFP effectively ameliorated ovarian injury induced by long-term LNG exposure in rats, and its protective effects were likely associated with modulation of ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and suppression of PI3K/Akt signaling.

article.title: Dihydrocaffeic acid alleviates APOE4-associated astrocyte dysfunction and cognitive impairment via LRP1/p38 MAPK signaling.
article.authors: Jiahui Shang; Yiwei Wang; Wei Wang; Fangkai Dai; Junwu Liu; Xi Li; Xinmei Xie; Xiaobin Pang
article.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Dihydrocaffeic acid (DHCA) is a phenolic acid produced through the microbial metabolism of plant-derived caffeoylquinic acids. DHCA has been detected in human plasma following oral administration of a standardized aqueous extract of Centella asiatica (L.) Urb., a medicinal plant traditionally used to improve memory and cognitive function. However, whether DHCA exerts neuroprotective effects against APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease-like pathology remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether DHCA ameliorates APOE4-associated cognitive deficits and neuropathological abnormalities and to assess the role of astrocytic LRP1/p38 MAPK signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twelve-month-old APOE4 mice were administered DHCA once daily for 21 days, with age-matched APOE3 mice and vehicle-treated APOE4 mice serving as controls. Cognitive function, Alzheimer's disease-related neuropathology, neuronal and synaptic integrity, astrocyte phenotypes, and lipid metabolism were evaluated. Mechanistic studies were performed in APOE4-overexpressing U251 cells using siRNA-mediated LRP1 knockdown and pharmacological activation of p38 MAPK. RESULTS: DHCA improved object recognition and spatial learning and memory, reduced amyloid deposition and tau phosphorylation, restored neuronal and synaptic markers, shifted astrocyte-reactivity markers toward a neuroprotective profile, and restored proteins involved in lipid metabolism. DHCA also increased LRP1 expression and reduced p38 MAPK phosphorylation. LRP1 knockdown or p38 MAPK activation partially reversed these cellular effects. CONCLUSIONS: DHCA ameliorated APOE4-associated cognitive deficits and neuropathological alterations, at least partly through modulation of LRP1/p38 MAPK-related signaling in the APOE4-overexpressing U251 model, astrocyte reactivity, and lipid metabolism. These findings identify DHCA as a potential neuroprotective metabolite derived from plant polyphenols.

article.title: Effect of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on growth, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome in a hybrid fish (Megalobrama amblycephala♀ × Culter alburnus♂).
article.authors: Liu Y, Chen S, Ma Y, Zhu W, Xi H, Yuan Y, Zhou Z, Li Y, Shen Z, Wang C, Li W.
article.abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on the growth performance, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome of a hybrid fish (Megalobrama amblycephala♀ × Culter alburnus♂). Experimental fish were diet supplemented with C. butyricum at 0 (control group [CG]), 4.02 × 10 8 (L), 1.66 × 10 9 CFU/kg (T), respectively, for 8 weeks feeding. The results showed that the growth performance of fish followed the trend of T > L > CG. Compared to group CG, the microbial community structure in group T shifted significantly. The relative abundance of Fusobacteriota and Cetobacterium was higher while that of Pseudomonadota, Bacillota and Plesiomonas was lower. The predicted functional abundances of biotin metabolism, D-alanine metabolism and propanoate metabolism in the intestinal microbiota were higher in group T than in group CG. Besides, 131 DEMs were identified and mainly enriched in glycerophospholipid metabolism and beta-alanine metabolism. In addition, transcriptome analysis showed 1479 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and mainly enriched in pentose and glucuronate interconversions, peroxisome and protein digestion and absorption. Correlation analysis showed that the dominant bacterium Cetobacterium was positively associated with fish growth performance and glycerophospholipid metabolites. These findings suggested that dietary supplementation with C. butyricum reshaped intestinal microbiota structure and influenced lipid, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, as well as the expression of genes related to carbohydrates and lipids, which may provide insights into the microbiota-host interactions that regulate growth in hybrid fish.

article.title: Systematic Review of the Literature on Associations Between Symptoms, Stress, Resilience, and Epigenetic Aging in Patients With Cancer.
article.authors: Lisa M Morse; Sandra Weiss; Christine S Ritchie; Melisa L Wong; Carolyn Harris; Peggy Thair; Christine Miaskowski
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer and its treatments can have long-term adverse effects that may accelerate aging and worsen symptom burden. The cognitive and behavioral strategies that patients utilize to adapt to their environment and respond to stress may influence inter-individual variability in aging and symptom burden. This systematic review summarizes the relationships between symptoms, stress, resilience, and epigenetic aging in oncology patients and identifies knowledge gaps. METHODS: A search of relevant databases was done from January 2000 to May 2026. Studies were included that examined DNA methylation patterns to predict biological age using algorithms known as epigenetic clocks in adults with cancer. A qualitative synthesis of the quantitative studies is reported. RESULTS: Of the 10 studies included in this review, a total of nine different methods were used to predict epigenetic age. The most common methods were the Levine, Horvath, and Hannum clocks. Nine studies reported on associations between symptoms and epigenetic age acceleration; one study reported on an association between stress and epigenetic age acceleration; and one study reported on an association between resilience and epigenetic age acceleration. CONCLUSION: More longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and investigate variations by epigenetic age estimate, timing of assessment, cancer type, and stage of disease. Studies are needed to evaluate the role of stress and resilience in mediating/moderating the relationships between epigenetic age acceleration and symptoms in patients with cancer. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: A subset of patients with cancer who develop more severe fatigue, pain, sleep disturbance, peripheral motor neuropathy, cognitive, depressive, and/or anxiety symptoms may experience epigenetic age acceleration. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: This systematic review was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42024545895).

article.title: Mechanistic insights into cholesterol-mediated MASH pathogenesis: Glycation, lipoxidation, and RAGE pathway.
article.authors: Beatriz Peres de Araujo; Raquel Rangel Silvares; Evelyn Nunes Goulart da Silva Pereira; Karine Lino Rodrigues; Marjo P H Van de Waarenburg; Jean L J M Scheijen; Caroline Fernandes-Santos; Kristiaan Wouters; Casper G Schalkwijk; Anissa Daliry
article.abstract: The pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is multifactorial, with evidence suggesting a pathogenic role for the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis. Although cholesterol and the AGE/ALE axis have been linked, evidence of their association in MASH remains limited. In this study, we investigated the role of the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis in cholesterol-driven MASH progression. Male C57BL/6 mice were fed either a short- or long-term high-fat, high-carbohydrate, high-cholesterol diet to induce MASH. In a subgroup of mice with MASH, the pharmacological RAGE inhibitor FPS-ZM1 (1 mg/kg/day) was administered. Mechanistic insights were further explored in vitro using HepG2 cells exposed to free fatty acids (FFAs) and oxidized LDL (oxLDL) to mimetize diet-induced MASH. Body and liver weights, adipose tissue distribution, blood glucose, liver histology, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, and AGE/ALE signaling were assessed. In HepG2 cells, inflammation, dicarbonyl stress, and AGE formation were evaluated. Cholesterol supplementation exacerbated MASH progression, increasing steatosis, inflammation, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, accompanied by activation of the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis, redox imbalance, and inflammation. RAGE blockade improved hepatic lipid accumulation, steatosis, inflammation, hepatocellular ballooning, AGE levels, and restored antioxidant capacity. In vitro, oxLDL induced the inflammatory response and promoted dicarbonyl stress. Collectively, these findings identify dietary cholesterol as a key modulator of MASH. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of RAGE with FPS-ZM1 effectively reversed key pathological features, supporting a functional contribution of RAGE signaling to cholesterol-associated disease severity.

article.title: Biomolecular condensates orchestrate small RNA pathways and transgenerational inheritance.
article.authors: Chen L, Wang K.
article.venue: Biochemistry and cell biology = Biochimie et biologie cellulaire
article.abstract: Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules are biomolecular condensates composed of RNAs and RNA-binding proteins that help organize gene expression, small RNA pathways, and genome surveillance. Recent studies have shown that germline RNP granules in Caenorhabditis elegans are not uniform structures; instead, they comprise multiple functionally specialized yet spatially coordinated subcompartments. Growing evidence indicates that this higher-order organization is crucial for RNA-mediated gene silencing and the transgenerational inheritance of epigenetic information. Here, we summarize recent advances in the composition, spatial organization, and functional specialization of C. elegans germline RNP granules, with an emphasis on how compartmentalization coordinates small RNA pathways and supports the maintenance and inheritance of gene silencing. We also highlight unresolved questions and emerging challenges in the field to provide an updated framework for understanding how membraneless organelles regulate RNA metabolism and epigenetic inheritance.

article.title: The Epidemiological Transition of Neurodegenerative Diseases in China: A Multi-Layered Deconstruction Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
article.authors: Zhaoyi Jing; Shuhong Liu; Qingyu Song; Shengda Tian; Qingbo Zhou
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), including Alzheimer's disease and other dementias (ADOD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and motor neuron disease (MND), represent a mounting public health challenge in China amid rapid population aging. A systematic deconstruction of their epidemiological transition using the most recent data remains lacking. METHODS: Data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 were utilized to examine temporal trends (1990-2023) for ADOD, PD, and MND in China. Age-standardized rates of incidence (ASIR), prevalence (ASPR), mortality (ASMR), and disability-adjusted life-years (ASDR) were analyzed. Joinpoint regression was used to identify significant inflection points. Decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population aging, population growth, and epidemiological change. And bayesian age-period-cohort models projected trends to 2035. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, the ASIR for ADOD (EAPC 0.41; 95% CI 0.33 to 0.49) and PD (EAPC 0.84; 95% CI 0.76 to 0.92) rose significantly. Between 2019 and 2023, multiple indicators across the three diseases demonstrated a consistently synchronous upward trend. This acceleration coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic. Decomposition demonstrated that population aging was the dominant driver. Sex-specific disparities were pronounced. Females bore a higher ADOD burden, whereas males predominated in PD. ASIR and ASPR are expected to rise, while ASMR and ASDR are projected to decline for ADOD and PD. For MND, only the ASPR indicated a brief, peaked rise in the predicted trends. CONCLUSIONS: In the field of neurodegenerative diseases, China is projected to undergo an epidemiological transition characterized by chronicization. This trend calls for systematic adjustments in healthcare services, long-term care systems, and social support structures. Sex and gender differences further underscore the need for gender-sensitive prevention, clinical management, and care strategies to prevent the further widening of inequalities. Population aging remains a critical factor that cannot be overlooked. Therefore, there is an urgent need to establish a proactive, gender-sensitive framework for system-wide restructuring that incorporates long-term monitoring and oversight.

article.title: Keratinocyte-derived CHI3L2 reprograms phospholipid metabolism to promote skin inflammation in psoriasis.
article.authors: Fei Li; Wentao Zhang; Wenxian Ma; Yanglong Guan; Yu Wang; Yuanyuan Cheng; Dongxia Liang; Yudan Wang; Xiangyu Xu; Leyao Feng; Bo Wang; Jing Xu; Lingfei Mo; Jingyuan Wang; Dan Han; Kuanhou Mou; Yan Zhou; Shemin Lu; Rikard Holmdahl; Liesu Meng; Wenhua Zhu
article.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

article.title: A Mixed‑Valence Cu/Mn Bimetallic Coordination Polymer Nano‑Assembly Co‑Loaded With Taurine and Lenvatinib for Synergistic Tumor Chemo-Metalloimmunotherapy.
article.authors: Luo Y, Sun Y, Zhang W, Shi X, Shen T, Gu M, Shen J, Yuan WE, Yang G, Yang H.
article.abstract: Despite considerable progress in cancer immunotherapy, the therapeutic efficacy of current cancer therapy continues to be hampered by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (ITME), which is characterized by acidification, hypoxia, elevated H 2 O 2 levels, and aberrant angiogenesis. While transition metal-based nanomaterials hold great promise for modulating the ITME, their effectiveness is often constrained by insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, low immunogenicity, poor immune cell infiltration, and T-cell exhaustion. To address these issues, we developed a bimetallic Cu/Mn-doped nanoplatform, CMPTL, which further integrates acid-dissociable taurine and the angiogenesis inhibitor lenvatinib for malignant solid tumor therapy. This nanoplatform simultaneously triggers violent ROS and cuproptosis, leading to mitochondrial damage and the release of mitochondrial DNA. The subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, synergistically enhanced by Mn 2+ , initiates robust immune responses. Additionally, taurine helps alleviate T-cell exhaustion, while lenvatinib promotes tumor vessel normalization, leading to comprehensive remodeling of the TIME. Together, these multimodal mechanisms endow CMPTL with potent antitumor activity, positioning it as a promising candidate for cancer therapy.

article.title: First-principles analysis of the metal-free H 2 dissociation mechanism by semiquinone radicals in mitochondrial Complex I and III.
article.authors: Ishibashi T, Harunari E.
article.abstract: Although ameliorative effects of molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) have been reported in a wide range of pathological conditions, an unresolved issue is the molecular mechanism by which H 2 is activated in animal cells, which lack the metal hydrogenases that dissociate the exceptionally strong nonpolar H-H bond. Using first-principles calculations (geometries optimized with spin-unrestricted B3LYP-D3BJ/def2-SVP/CPCM and energies evaluated with ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPP) with the active-site clusters of the Q-chamber of mitochondrial respiratory-chain Complex I (PDB 7QSK) and the Q o site of Complex III (PDB 1PP9), this study examined whether semiquinone could directly dissociate H 2 in the low-dielectric environment buried within the enzyme and examined what changes when a conserved residue is added as a second hydrogen atom acceptor. At both sites, the anionic semiquinone Q˙ - had no reaction pathway for cleaving H-H, and only the neutral QH˙, protonated by nearby residues, opened a homolytic hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) pathway with a well-defined transition state and a bound product. The continuous shift in the spin density on the transferring hydrogen from nearly 0 in the reactant to +0.99 for free H˙ confirmed, at the electronic level, that this is a true homolytic HAT and neither a proton transfer nor a hydride transfer. The reaction energies (+21 to +26 kcal mol -1 ) agree with an estimate based on the difference between the bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of the O-H bond of ubiquinol QH 2 and the H-H bond that is broken. The same BDFE comparison also makes QH˙ a spin-allowed hydrogen-atom abstractor superior to superoxide by about 30 kcal mol -1 . For HAT with a single hydrogen atom acceptor, the reaction energy of QH˙ + H 2 → QH 2 + H˙ is +28.3 kcal mol -1 , and the barrier cannot fall below this value. In the Q-chamber, the conserved Tyr108 residue can act as a second acceptor, and for hydrogen atom transfer with H 2 held between QH˙ and TyrO˙, the barrier falls to +27.0 kcal mol -1 . However, this reactive QH˙ arises only under hyper-reductive pressure, where quinone-pool overreduction and high membrane potential coincide, upon occupation and protonation at the buried semiquinone reaction site. Therefore, H 2 dissociation itself is established only when the semiquinone reaction-site environment under hyper-reductive pressure is present as a necessary condition. Because H 2 possesses one of the strongest σ bonds, the barrier is high and sharp, and quantum tunnelling makes a substantial contribution to crossing it at body temperature. At the one-dimensional Eckart level, this contribution does not exceed thermal activation, and it is obtained as a lower bound. The crossover temperatures, set by the imaginary frequency at the saddle, are 293.9 K for Complex I and 264.7 K for Complex III. The buried semiquinone reaction site makes a barrier against one of the strongest known σ bonds, which is thin enough to bring the crossover temperature to within 16 K of body temperature, and is itself a quantitative result of the study. The Marcus inverted region (bell-shaped kinetics) that we observed in solution in the previous work shows that H 2 can be activated under metal-free conditions, but in that case, it is the electron that tunnels, moving along a coordinate distinct from the hydrogen nucleus analysed here. For the in-enzyme mechanism, the moderate primary isotope effect predicted at the same level ( k H / k D ≈ 4) could be tested by detecting dissociated deuterium using D 2 as a tracer. Taken together, the above results shift the mechanistic account of H 2 medicine from classical antioxidant scavenging to redox regulation as a quantum-tunnelling-assisted conditional hydrogenase activity conditioned by reductive pressure and position it as a field of quantum biology.

article.title: PHGDH-Mediated Serine Metabolism in Nucleus Pulposus Cells Is a Potential Therapeutic Target for Intervertebral Disc Degeneration.
article.authors: Xu HW, Chang SJ, Liu XW, Zhang SB, Wang YJ, Wang SJ.
article.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine-serine-threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. In vivo, AAV mediated PHGDH overexpression alleviates puncture induced IVDD, while a serine deficient diet exacerbates degeneration. Collectively, we uncover a PHGDH/Rap1b/mTORC1/autophagy cascade linking serine deprivation to NPC senescence, and propose that restoring PHGDH or serine availability may be a viable strategy to combat age related disc degeneration.

article.title: Noninvasive Detection and Subtyping of Esophageal Cancer by Circulating Cell-Free mtDNA Fragmentomics: A Multi-Center Validation Study.
article.authors: Liu Y, Yang W, Li Y, Wang S, Li X, Peng F, Dang M, Zhang H, Jiao H, Yang Y, Su Z, Ma X, Gong Z, Lu R, Xing J, Liu Y.
article.abstract: Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non-invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. In this large multi-center study enrolling 1,260 participants spanning healthy control (HC), benign esophageal diseases (BED), precancerous lesions and EC patients, we developed two machine learning models based on plasma ccf-mtDNA fragmentomic profiles: an EC detection (ED) model and a pathological subtyping prediction (PSP) model. The ED model achieved an AUC of 0.9706 (EC vs. non-EC) in the training cohort, with high performance in internal (0.9762), external (0.9748), and Chinese minority (0.9668, Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts. At the optimal cut-off, it yielded 92.16% sensitivity for stage I EC in the combined validation cohort and correctly identified 93.10% of early EC cases missed by preoperative biopsy. It also discriminated high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia from non-EC with an AUC of 0.9597. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. In summary, ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics provides a robust, non-invasive platform for early EC detection, precancerous risk stratification, and histological subtyping, demonstrating strong potential to transform clinical management.

article.title: 4'-Hydroxywogonin Attenuates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Suppressing Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT Signaling.
article.authors: Chen CY, Chen CC, Yeh CT, Chan CW, Chu YD, Leu YL, Satange RB, Chou LF, Chuang WY, Hsueh C, Shieh TM, Wang TH.
article.abstract: 4'-Hydroxywogonin, a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanism in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-tumor effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin and its regulatory role in Gas6/Axl-associated signaling. Human HCC cells were used to evaluate proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, senescence, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, molecular docking, and thermal shift analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanism, and antitumor efficacy and safety were further examined in a mouse xenograft model. 4'-Hydroxywogonin significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing G1-phase arrest, apoptosis, and senescence. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses identified Axl as a key affected target. 4'-Hydroxywogonin reduced Gas6 and Axl expression, suppressed PI3K/AKT activation, and downregulated cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between 4'-hydroxywogonin and Axl, which was supported by thermal shift analysis. Axl overexpression partially rescued the inhibitory effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin, suggesting involvement of Axl-dependent and additional pathways. In vivo, 4'-hydroxywogonin markedly reduced tumor growth with efficacy comparable to sorafenib and without evident hepatotoxicity. These findings indicate that 4'-hydroxywogonin suppresses HCC progression, at least in part, through inhibition of the Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, supporting its further development as a natural therapeutic candidate.

article.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Triggered by T-2 Toxin-Induced Thioredoxin Reductase 2 (TXNRD2) Depletion and Its Molecular Mechanism.
article.authors: Changyu Cao; Yu Wang; Weifeng Ni; Yihao He; Yang Liu; Nan Li; Xinran Li
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: The T-2 toxin is a prevalent trichothecene mycotoxin that threatens food safety and animal health, yet its direct mitochondrial targets remain poorly defined. Using network toxicology and in vitro validation in porcine renal PK15 cells, thioredoxin reductase 2 (TXNRD2) was identified as the most significantly downregulated mitochondrial selenoprotein upon T-2 toxin exposure. Molecular docking and enzymatic assays demonstrated that T-2 binds to and inhibits TXNRD2 by occupying its FAD/NADPH-binding pocket. Notably, SeMet restored TXNRD2 expression and partially rescued mitochondrial injury, whereas direct TXNRD2 overexpression independently conferred comparable protection, confirming TXNRD2 as the key downstream effector. These interventions attenuated the abnormal elevation of intracellular ATP content and reduced ROS overproduction by approximately 39%. Conversely, TXNRD2 knockdown attenuated SeMet's efficacy to establish TXNRD2 as a direct mitochondrial target of the T-2 toxin. Supplementation with SeMet protected cells by restoring both the expression and enzymatic activity of TXNRD2 and preventing T-2 toxin-induced cytotoxicity.

article.title: Multilevel Engineering of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for Scalable Production of Ergosterol as a Vitamin D2 Precursor.
article.authors: Wenqian Wei; Qihang Chen; Chen Sang; Song Gao; Qian He; Sha Xu; Weizhu Zeng; Jingwen Zhou
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: Ergosterol, a nutritionally relevant fungal sterol and vitamin D2 precursor, is valuable for food and feed applications, but its overproduction in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is constrained by stringent sterol homeostasis, limited organelle capacity, and the coordination of gene-dense pathways. A multilevel engineering framework was established by relieving inhibitory regulation, enhancing acetyl-CoA supply, strengthening rate-limiting steps, expanding endoplasmic reticulum capacity, and rewiring ethanol assimilation. A bidirectional-terminator-based integration toolkit enabled programmable chromosomal integration, modular pathway refactoring, and tunable expression partitioning. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy provided label-free visualization of intracellular ergosterol distribution and storage at single-cell resolution, supporting sterol homeostasis optimization. Robustness-oriented engineering of central carbon metabolism, mitochondrial function, and epigenetic regulation enhanced cellular fitness and fermentation performance. The resulting strain produced 0.983 g/L ergosterol in shake-flask cultures and 4.39 g/L in a 5-L bioreactor, corresponding to 51.7 mg/g dry cell weight (DCW), demonstrating the potential for scalable ergosterol biomanufacturing.

article.title: PPARγ Is Critical for Lycopene Antagonizing Zearalenone-Induced Ferroptosis by Promoting Autophagy-Mediated TFRC Degradation in Swine Testicular Cells.
article.authors: Xin-Yue Mao; Zi-Yan Hu; Xin Yao; Ming Lou; Yue Cheng; Yi-Feng Huang; Hong-Li Si; Ming-Shan Chen; Jia-Xin Wang; Fu-Wei Jiang; Zhuo-Yu Liu; Xiao-Wei Li; Jin-Long Li; Yi Zhao
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: Mycotoxins are common contaminants in agricultural products and feed, which pose a serious threat to public health. Zearalenone (ZEA) is a well-known environmental endocrine disruptor that causes reproductive disorders. Lycopene (LYC) is a possible therapeutic and preventive agent for male diseases. Here, we aim to explore the mechanism of ZEA-induced swine testicular (ST) cell injury and antagonism of lycopene. ST cells were treated with lycopene and/or ZEA for mechanistic validation. In this study, ZEA caused pronounced mitochondrial structural damage, whereas lycopene restored mitochondrial integrity. Lycopene also reduced ZEA-induced lipid peroxidation and ferrous ion levels, eventually inhibiting ferroptosis. Mechanistically, lycopene recovered PPARγ expression and regulated AMPK/mTOR signaling, thereby facilitating TFRC turnover. Of note, PPARγ knockdown weakened the effects of lycopene on ferroptosis, whereas TFRC overexpression diminished the protection afforded by autophagy activation. These findings indicate that lycopene mitigates ZEA-induced ferroptosis by regulating the PPARγ-AMPK-mTOR pathway and thus promoting autophagy-mediated TFRC degradation.

article.title: PPARγ/P21 Signaling Mediates Butyrate-Driven Protection against Aging-Related Endothelial Dysfunction: A Novel Effect of Soybean Polysaccharide via the Gut-Vascular Axis.
article.authors: Qile Zhang; Zhengming Zhou; Hoi Wa Yeung; Yiu Ming Cheung; Yuen Lam Wong; Chufeng He; Shouhe Huang; Lu Jiang; Xiao Yu Tian; Zhen-Yu Chen; Wing Tak Wong
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: Aging-induced endothelial dysfunction is a core driver of age-related cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In 20-month-old naturally aged mice, 12-week soybean polysaccharide (SP) supplementation restored endothelium-dependent relaxation, reduced aortic reactive oxygen species and VCAM-1 in the aortic endothelium, and attenuated colon senescence, improved gut barrier integrity, and reduced systemic inflammation, as shown by decreased serum LPS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and fecal and serum TMA/TMAO levels. SP enriched butyrate-producing gut bacteria, including Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group, and increased gut and serum butyrate, consistent with enhanced microbial short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis capacity predicted by PICRUSt2. Direct butyrate supplementation reproduced these vascular and colonic benefits. It activated PPARγ signaling and downregulated p21, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, and p16, whereas PPARα and PPARδ remained unchanged. These findings support a gut microbiota-butyrate-PPARγ/p21 axis through which SP protects against aging-related endothelial dysfunction, providing a nutritional basis for targeting the gut-vascular axis in cardiovascular aging.

article.title: Clostridium butyricum Alleviates Meat Quality Deterioration in Eimeria-Infected Lambs Alongside Recovery of Thiamine Diphosphate-Dependent Glucose Metabolism.
article.authors: Manyu Liu; Lizhen Guo; Meiqi Lin; Juanfeng Li; Aoning Zhen; Junqiang Li; Longxian Zhang; Senyang Li; Shucheng Huang; Fuchun Jian
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: Eimeria spp. infection impairs lamb performance and meat quality, but the associated muscle metabolic basis and potential nutritional mitigation remains unclear. Twenty-four lambs were assigned to control (CON), Eimeria-infected (IF), and Eimeria-infected supplemented with Clostridium butyricum (CB; CB-IF) groups. Infection increased drip loss, and reduced cooking yield, whereas CB supplementation improved these traits. Metabolomics analysis revealed reduce thiamine diphosphate (TDP) and 4-methyl-5-hydroxyethylthiazole phosphate (HET-P) after infection, with partial recovery following CB supplementation. Integrated transcriptomic and WGCNA analysis identified coordinated associations among thiamine-related metabolites, glucose- and mitochondrial-metabolism-related gene signatures, and meat-quality traits. RT-qPCR supported the expression patterns of selected transcriptomic candidates. Collectively, CB supplementation alleviated selected meat-quality alterations and was associated with coordinated recovery of thiamine-related and glucose/mitochondrial metabolic signatures during Eimeria spp. infection.

article.title: BzAM terpolymer series with stepwise systematic change in hydrophobicity provides a nuanced platform for GPCRs functional studies in native‑like nanodiscs.
article.authors: Gestél C Kuyler; Rebecca J Murray; Farhaan Napier-Khwaja; Joseph Gunner; Ellie Thacker; Bert Klumperman; David R Poyner; Hoor Ayub; Mark Wheatley
article.abstract: Detergent-free extraction of membrane proteins using polymers directly into nanodiscs from the cell membrane has been used widely in recent years. Since the first use of poly(styrene-co-maleic acid) (SMA), numerous related polymers have been developed that differ in chemical architecture and nanodisc characteristics, each capable of influencing the structural and functional properties of the encapsulated membrane protein and its surrounding lipids. Identifying an optimal solubilising polymer, therefore, requires consideration not only of extraction efficiency but also compatibility with downstream applications and analyses. Polymer series in which a single parameter is systematically varied provide a valuable, nuanced tool for optimising nanodisc utility in downstream applications. This study utilises a chemically defined series of poly(styrene-co-maleic acid-co-(N-benzyl)maleimide) (BzAM) terpolymers that exhibit a stepwise, systematic increase in hydrophobicity. Using the human calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor as an exemplar class B1 G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), the ability of each BzAM terpolymer to solubilise the receptor from mammalian cell membranes was assessed. All members of the series successfully solubilised CGRP receptor, with solubilisation efficiency correlating positively with increasing hydrophobicity. Importantly, the receptor retained its characteristic high-affinity ligand-binding capability when encapsulated within the BzAM nanodisc, demonstrating that functional integrity is preserved following BzAM-mediated extraction and enrichment (Ni-NTA). These findings establish the BzAM terpolymer series as a systematic, tuneable, well-defined tool for the detergent-free solubilisation and functional investigation of GPCRs, and other membrane proteins, in near-native lipid environments.

article.title: Clinical and computational exploration of IRS1 and Pancreastatin genetic variants in metabolic response to metformin-sulfonylurea therapy.
article.authors: Aliya Abbas Rizvi; Mohammad Abbas; Tabrez Faruqui; Asma Imran Ansari; Zeba Siddiqi; Sushma Verma; Farzana Mahdi
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) show variable responses to metformin-sulfonylurea therapy. Genetic variation in insulin signaling and metabolic regulation, particularly in insulin receptor substrate-1 (IRS1) and pancreastatin (PST), may contribute to this variability. This study assessed the influence of IRS1 (rs1801278) and PST (rs9658664) polymorphisms on baseline metabolic profiles and response to combination therapy. METHODS: We enrolled 202 diabetic individuals receiving metformin-sulfonylurea therapy. Clinical and biochemical parameters were measured at baseline and follow-up. Genotyping for IRS1 (rs1801278) and PST (rs9658664) was performed using PCR-RFLP and statistically analyzed by SPSS (v.27). Exploratory molecular docking analyses were performed to examine mutation-dependent differences in PST interactions with insulin-signaling proteins. RESULTS: Renal complications were more prevalent among non-responders (p = 0.029). IRS1 and PST genotypes were not associated with therapeutic response. Individuals with IRS1 TT genotype exhibited higher baseline cholesterol, triglyceride, and LDL levels (p = 0.05). Docking analyses suggested mutation-dependent differences in PST interactions with insulin receptor, IRS1, and GRP78. Metformin showed slightly stronger predicted binding to insulin receptor and IRS1 than sulfonylurea. CONCLUSION: Although IRS1 and PST polymorphisms did not show association with treatment response, genotype-based metabolic variability and in silico analyses suggest functional effects on insulin-signaling pathways, highlighting the potential of personalized medicine approaches for optimizing antidiabetic therapy.

article.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C 4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
article.authors: Lunn D, Park K, Deshavath NN, Dong J, Swaminathan K, Guest J, Leakey ADB, Butler NM, Schwender J, Singh V, Shanklin J, Altpeter F, Cahoon EB.
article.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C 4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C 4 feedstocks: saccharum (Saccharum spp. hybrids), sorghum (Sorghum bicolor), and miscanthus (Miscanthus × giganteus). Through iterative DBTL cycles, CABBI has produced transgenic saccharum and sorghum lines with substantially elevated levels of vegetative TAG, with multi-location field trials having confirmed stable trait heritability and lipid yields. We have also leveraged our integration to develop a dual system biorefinery that co-recovers vegetative lipids with fermentable sugars at levels sufficient to achieve industrial ethanol titres. Importantly, this fully integrated cross-disciplinary data integration model has highlighted the key constraints currently preventing TAG-rich vegetative oil from achieving commercial viability as: (i) active lipid turnover, (ii) photosynthetic trade-offs, (iii) spatial misexpression, and (iv) bioprocessing challenges. CABBI uses emerging technologies, including biofoundry-enabled construct screening, precision genome editing, and machine-learning-assisted regulatory design, to further accelerate DBTL cycles. More broadly, this work illustrates how integrative centre-scale research that unites diverse expertise can accelerate discovery and translation, positioning these systems to expand agricultural markets and contribute to a more secure and resilient bioeconomy.

article.title: Collagen VI-derived endotrophin impairs adipocyte function and insulin action in human obesity.
article.authors: Dimitrios M Karadedos; Alaa Alhomsi; Isla Koiso-Kanttila; Maria K Svensson; Magnus Sundbom; Giovanni Fanni; Jan W Eriksson; Maria J Pereira
article.venue: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
article.abstract: CONTEXT: Obesity-associated adipose tissue dysfunction is characterized by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and fibrosis, where collagen VI and its bioactive cleavage peptide endotrophin have been implicated as key mediators. OBJECTIVE: Characterize collagen VI alpha-3 (COL6A3) depot-specific expression in obesity and determine whether endotrophin impairs adipocyte metabolism and insulin responsiveness. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: COL6A3 expression was examined in paired subcutaneous (SAT) and omental adipose tissue (OAT) from 60 individuals spanning a broad Body-Mass-Index (BMI) range. Plasma endotrophin was measured in a subset of the cohort (n=42). Endotrophin effects were assessed in adipose explants, primary human and SGBS adipocytes. MAIN OUTCOME ME: asures. Depot-specific COL6A3 expression relative to BMI and endotrophin's effects on adipose tissue gene expression, GLUT4 levels, and adipocyte glucose uptake rate. RESULTS: COL6A3 expression was associated with adiposity only in SAT. BMI remained an independent predictor after adjustment for age, sex, and metabolic covariates. COL6A3 co-expression patterns were positively associated with ECM remodeling and inflammation genes in both depots, while inverse associations with lipid metabolism and insulin signaling genes were specific to SAT. Circulating endotrophin levels were associated with fat mass percentage and triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio, but not with adipose tissue COL6A3 expression. Endotrophin treatment reduced expression of PPARγ, SLC2A4 (GLUT4), and NR3C1, decreased GLUT4 protein, and impaired adipocyte insulin-stimulated glucose uptake rate without affecting AKT phosphorylation. Endotrophin reduced PPARγ, DGAT2, and SLC2A4 expression in differentiating SGBS adipocytes. Glucocorticoids upregulated COL6A3 in both depots. CONCLUSIONS: These findings implicate COL6A3-associated ECM remodelling and endotrophin in adipose dysfunction and impaired adipocyte insulin responsiveness in obesity.

article.title: Impact of material type and acidic oral environment on physical properties and protein adsorption of subtractively and additively manufactured resin-ceramics for definitive crowns.
article.authors: Mustafa Borga Dönmez; Ye-Hyeon Jo; Hyung-In Yoon; Burak Yilmaz
article.venue: Journal of prosthodontics : official journal of the American College of Prosthodontists
article.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore how material type and simulated acidic oral environment can affect the physical properties and protein adsorption of subtractively manufactured (SM) and additively manufactured (AM) resin-ceramic materials for definitive crowns. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Disk-shaped specimens (Ø10 × 5 mm) were fabricated from an SM (Vita Enamic, VE) and an AM (Permanent Crown, PC) resin-ceramic material indicated for definitive crowns. Each specimen surface was finely polished. Twenty-five specimens from each material were immersed in acidic artificial saliva (pH 5.0 ± 0.2) at 37°C for 7 days to simulate aging in an acidic oral environment. The non-aged specimens (n = 25 per material) served as controls. Surface roughness (Ra, Sa), microhardness (HV), and protein adsorption (OD) were evaluated. Ra and Sa were analyzed using two-way aligned rank transform analysis of variance (ANOVA) tests, HV using a two-way ANOVA, and OD using a factorial linear model with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Post hoc comparisons were performed using estimated marginal means with Sidak or Tukey adjustments, with the significance level set at α = 0.05. RESULTS: Aging significantly increased the Ra and Sa, whereas it decreased the HV for both materials (p ≤ 0.013). VE had higher HV than PC (p < 0.001). Although the OD of tested materials did not differ under non-aged condition and aging did not affect the OD (p ≥ 0.091), PC demonstrated greater OD than VE when aged in acidic saliva (p = 0.039). CONCLUSIONS: Although the roughness of tested materials remained below clinical thresholds, acidic aging increased surface irregularities and reduced the hardness. VE may be more resistant to wear and protein accumulation-related complications than PC with acidic oral challenges.

article.title: Hepatocyte Pparg knockout and restored Bhmt expression reduce liver steatosis in male mice with diet-induced MASH.
article.authors: Izabela Hawro; Samuel M Lee; Marta Sierra-Cruz; Jose Cordoba-Chacon
article.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by the accumulation of triglycerides in hepatocytes and can progress to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with inflammation, hepatocyte ballooning, and fibrosis. MASLD is associated with increased plasma homocysteine levels. Homocysteine is an amino acid generated by the S-adenosylmethionine-dependent transmethylation pathway of the methionine cycle, and it is remethylated to methionine by the betaine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase (BHMT) in hepatocytes. Mice fed a high-fat, cholesterol, and fructose (HFCF) diet develop MASLD and MASH associated with increased peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ, Pparg) expression and homocysteine levels, and decreased hepatic Bhmt expression. Here, we sought to determine whether the hepatocyte-specific knockout of Pparg (PpargΛHep) or restoration of Bhmt expression in hepatocytes (BhmtHep) in mice with HFCF-induced MASH reduce MASLD progression. To this end, adult male Pparg-floxed mice were fed an HFCF diet for 20 weeks to induce MASH. Then, we generated PpargΛHep and/or BhmtHep mice using an adeno-associated virus encoding Cre recombinase or Bhmt in hepatocytes, respectively. HFCF diet-induced MASH increased hepatic Pparg expression and reduced Bhmt expression. 8 weeks after the induction of PpargΛHep, hepatic Bhmt expression was increased, and both MASH severity and homocysteine levels decreased. The restoration of hepatocyte BHMT in BhmtHep (Pparg-intact) mice reduced hepatic triglyceride and homocysteine levels, which were associated with reduced expression of the steatogenic genes Cidea and Cidec. Overall, our results indicate a protective role for BHMT in hepatocytes of mice with MASH, even in mice expressing Pparg in hepatocytes.

article.title: Synergistic induction of apoptosis in human prostate cancer PC3 cells by silver-coated cerium oxide nanoparticles: unveiling the role of ROS-mediated p53-associated apoptotic signaling and antioxidant system depletion.
article.authors: Al-Awassi H, AlAbdulhadi SAS, Aslam A, AlMoshary M, Alrefaei GI, Al-Qahtani SA, Barnawi J.
article.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) represents a formidable clinical challenge due to intrinsic defects in apoptotic execution, elevated baseline antioxidant capacity, and rapid resistance to standard chemotherapy. Herein, we report the rational design, template-directed synthesis, and antineoplastic evaluation of silver-coated cerium oxide core-shell nanoparticles (Ag@CeO2 NPs) derived from a cerium-based metal-organic framework (Ce-UiO-66) for targeted intervention in androgen-independent prostate carcinoma. Uniform Ce-UiO-66 MOF nanoparticles were thermally converted via controlled calcination (550 °C, 3 h) into porous cubic fluorite nanoceria (CeO₂) cores, followed by in situ surface nucleation and reduction of a metallic silver (Ag⁰) nanoshell stabilized by polyvinylpyrrolidone. The physicochemical properties were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, FESEM, EDX mapping, DLS, and Zeta potential analysis. In vitro anticancer efficacy was evaluated in human androgen-independent PC-3 prostate cancer cells and normal human fibroblasts (HFF-1). Cellular viability, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) enzymatic kinetics, apoptosis-related transcriptomics (p53, Bax, Bcl-2 via qRT-PCR), and p53 protein levels (ELISA) were systematically quantified. PXRD and Scherrer analysis confirmed the formation of pure, face-centered cubic fluorite CeO₂ (Cerianite-(Ce), Fm3̄m, *a* = 5.4110 Å) with an average primary crystallite size of 7.27 ± 0.36 nm (7.44 nm for the (111) reflection), alongside characteristic reflections of metallic Ag. FESEM, DLS, and electrophoretic measurements revealed spherical, cauliflower-like hierarchical clusters with a hydrodynamic diameter (Z-average) of 111.68 nm, narrow polydispersity (PDI = 0.2860), and stable negative surface charge (ζ = - 14.96 mV). The Ag@CeO2 NPs displayed pronounced, tumor-selective cytotoxicity, yielding an IC₅₀ of 32.14 µg/mL against PC-3 cells while sparing normal HFF-1 fibroblasts (IC₅₀ = 171.6 µg/mL, > 5.3-fold selectivity window). Mechanistically, the nanocomposite triggered a severe, concentration-dependent intracellular ROS burst (*p* < 0.0001 at 30 µM) accompanied by the functional collapse of the cellular antioxidant barrier through profound suppression of SOD (*p* < 0.01) and CAT (*p* < 0.0001) activities. This unmitigated oxidative crisis was associated with increased TP53 transcript levels and increased p53-associated protein signals as measured by ELISA (*p* < 0.0001), which coincided with upregulated Bax, downregulated Bcl-2, and elevated the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio (*p* < 0.001), consistent with activation of mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. Ag@CeO2 NPs function as a potent, tumor-selective pro-oxidant nanotherapeutic platform capable of overriding endogenous antioxidant defenses, enhancing p53-associated apoptotic signaling and promoting mitochondrial apoptotic responses, suggesting that Ag@CeO2 NPs may serve as a potential candidate for further investigation in prostate cancer nanomedicine.

article.title: Cascade-Catalytic MnO2 Nanoreactor Amplifies Oxidative Stress and Activates cGAS-STING Pathway To Remodel the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
article.authors: Shiman Li; Shuchang Yao; Jingwen Yang; Wenqi Wang; Wenjing Li; Xinzhu Wang; Ke Zhang; Sha Xie; Xiaoyu Peng; Jian Ni; Xiaoxv Dong
article.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which severely limits the therapeutic efficacy of current immunotherapies. To address this challenge, we developed a hyaluronic acid-modified tumor-targeted MnO2 nanoreactor (HMGR@HA) for the codelivery of GOx and 20(S)-ginsenoside Rg3 (Rg3), thereby integrating metabolic interference with cascade catalytic therapy and endogenous immune activation. In this system, GOx continuously catalyzed the oxidation of glucose to generate H2O2, which was subsequently converted by MnO2 into highly cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) while simultaneously producing oxygen. This process established a self-reinforcing catalytic cycle that effectively circumvented the intrinsic limitation of insufficient endogenous H2O2 within the tumor microenvironment. The resulting amplified oxidative stress, in synergy with the chemotherapeutic effect of Rg3, induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction and triggered the cytosolic release of mtDNA.
