As a potent endogenous danger signal, cytosolic mtDNA robustly activated the cGAS-STING signaling axis, thereby converting localized oxidative damage into strong innate immune activation. In addition, HMGR@HA induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoted dendritic cells (DCs) maturation, enhanced infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells, and significantly depleted regulatory T cells (Tregs), collectively leading to extensive remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Ultimately, this self-amplifying catalytic platform effectively drives the transition from localized tumor eradication to systemic antitumor immunity, offering a highly efficient therapeutic strategy for TNBC immunotherapy.

article.title: Quadruple Boronic Acid-Functionalized Lanthanide MOFs Enable Deep and Unbiased Spatial Proteomics from Ultra-Trace Laser-Captured Microtissues.
article.authors: Yuankang Zhu; Jiahui Wu; Qi Luo; Shuang Zhang; Qingwen Wang; Lai Jiang; Junli Duan; Alex F Chen; Xianting Ding
article.abstract: Spatial proteomics of laser capture microdissection (LCM) specimens is fundamentally constrained by protein loss during processing of ultra-trace samples, limiting proteomic depth and biological insight. Here, we report the integration of a quadruple metal-organic framework (qMOF)-enhanced surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (MSOP) workflow for deep proteomic profiling of micro-scale tissues. The qMOF composite, featuring high-density boronic acid functionalities, acts as a potent protein capture vehicle, drastically minimizing surface adsorption losses. Applied to LCM-isolated mouse myocardial sections as small as 100 × 100 μm (∼20 cells), the MSOP workflow approximately doubled the number of confidently identified proteins, compared to the conventional surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (SOP) method (mean of 2238 vs. 1116), while exhibiting lower quantification variance and preserving unbiased coverage of the proteome's physicochemical landscape. We further demonstrate the workflow's utility by resolving spatially distinct proteomic signatures in perivascular regions of aged cardiac tissue, identifying molecular hallmarks of aging characterized by impaired cytoskeletal stability and dysregulated mitochondrial functions. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified Rack1 as a potential key node in cardiac aging, which was further validated by immunohistochemistry. This MSOP-assisted platform provides a robust, cost-effective, and highly sensitive chemical strategy to significantly enhance the depth of discovery-driven spatial proteomics.

article.title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling.
article.authors: Chen Li; Li Zhao; Zhaofeng Zhang; Yiran Du; Jiaojiao Yu; Xiaomeng Yue; Shao-Kai Sun; Ruxia Liu; Chunxiao Wan
article.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)-Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs-Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs-Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·-, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs-Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs-Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs-Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs-Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

article.title: High-Throughput Screening of a Lipid Nanoparticle (LNP) Library Identifies Lead Formulations for CRISPR-Cas9 Ribonucleoprotein Delivery and Gene Editing.
article.authors: Yu Wang; Amin Haghighat Naeini; Nishant Kumar; Ming Zhao
article.abstract: Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) using synthetic materials can bypass the host translational machinery and limit the duration of genomic exposure, minimizing the risk of off-target mutations. Despite their advantages, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery that achieve highly efficient editing at low doses remain limited. In the present study, we developed a library of ionizable lipids (ILs) and corresponding LNPs to enhance the delivery and editing efficiencies of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complexes. Following comprehensive in vitro screening and formulation optimization, an optimal LNP candidate containing the C12A9 IL (denoted as LNPC12A9) was identified that achieved ∼90% EGFP disruption in HEK293T-EGFP cells at an RNP concentration of 30 nM and ∼60% at 15 nM. The editing performance was consistently observed at an RNP concentration of 15 nM when editing the Gcgr and HPRT1 genes across multiple hepatic cell lines. Moreover, coencapsulation of RNP and a single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (ssODN) template for homology-directed repair (HDR) within LNPC12A9 induced an HDR rate of 37.8%. Systemic administration of LNPC12A9 into C57BL/6J mice led to liver tropism and a total hepatic Pcsk9 gene disruption rate of 1.39%. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the construction of an LNP platform to improve the delivery efficiency of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP, thereby facilitating the development of LNPs for safe, precise, and tissue-specific Cas9 RNP-based genome editing therapies.

article.title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids as Endogenous Inhibitors of DPP-IV Enzyme: Implications in GLP-1 Stability and Metabolic Health.
article.authors: Paul Dias; Ravindran Mugesh; Ajmal Rahim; Amit Chakrabortty; Manoj Kumar Joshi
article.venue: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
article.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV/CD26) is a circulating serine protease that rapidly degrades incretin hormones, including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), limiting incretin activity and glucose homeostasis. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), major gut microbiota-derived metabolites, influence metabolic health through multiple mechanisms; whether they directly inhibit DPP-IV remains unknown. Here, we investigated the inhibitory activity and mechanism of acetate, propionate, and butyrate against recombinant human DPP-IV. All three SCFAs inhibited DPP-IV concentration-dependently, with an average IC50 of 0.62 ± 0.13 mM. Michaelis-Menten, Lineweaver-Burk, Dixon, and Cornish-Bowden analyses demonstrated reversible mixed-mode inhibition, whereas sitagliptin exhibited competitive inhibition (Ki = 2.6 nM). SCFAs protected GLP-1 from DPP-IV mediated degradation and preserved GLP-1-induced calcium signaling in INS-1 cells. Molecular docking indicated preferential SCFA interactions within the DPP-IV β-propeller domain. These findings identify SCFAs as direct, reversible DPP-IV modulators, providing a molecular link between gut microbial metabolites and incretin regulation.

article.title: Splenic macrophage polarization and plasma lipid remodeling in cardiac allograft rejection.
article.authors: Yanxia Zhan; Lili Ji; Peng Zhang; Zheng Li; Jian Wang; Qiancheng DU; Wei Cai; Yunfeng Cheng; Jie Cheng; Hao Chen
article.abstract: Cardiac transplantation is the final therapeutic option for end-stage heart disease. Immune rejection is one of the major sources of morbidity and mortality. Macrophages play important roles in host defense and immune regulation, yet they remain poorly studied in heart transplant rejection. This study investigated macrophage polarization and associated lipid alterations in a well-established rat model of heart transplant. Splenic macrophage phenotypes, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and lipid peroxide were examined using flow cytometry. Plasma lipids were analyzed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Next-generation sequencing of mRNA (RNA-seq) was used to analyze the expression of splenic CD11b+ cells genes. Allogeneic heart transplant was associated with systemic innate immune alterations and splenic macrophage M1 polarization. ROS and lipid peroxide levels in splenic CD11b+ cells tended to be higher in allografts than in isografts, although these differences were not statistically significant. Splenic CD11b+ cells showed up-regulation of Nos2, Cxcl10, Cd68, Il1r1, Cenpf, and Cyp27a1 mRNA in allografts compared with isografts, while Insig1 was down-regulated. Plasma CE, LPC, LPE, PC, and SM were decreased in allografts. Splenic macrophage polarization toward the M1 phenotype and plasma lipid remodeling were both observed in allograft rejection, but a causal relationship was not established.

article.title: Isolation of Ventricular Cardiomyocytes from the Annual Killifish Nothobranchius furzeri for Whole-Cell Patch Clamp Recordings.
article.authors: Shamshura AV, Dzhumaniiazova I.
article.abstract: Isolated working cardiomyocytes remain the standard approach for studying cardiac electrophysiology. Single-cell preparations allow for direct investigation and precise measurement of ionic currents and action potentials without the structural complexity of intact cardiac tissue. Nothobranchius furzeri (African turquoise killifish) has rapidly emerged as a prominent model organism for gerontological research due to its exceptionally short lifespan and similarities in aging mechanisms with mammals, including humans. This species combines practical advantages such as small size, inexpensive husbandry, and a rapid life cycle with translational relevance. N. furzeri exhibits age-dependent declines in locomotor activity, cognition, and organ function, accumulation of molecular hallmarks of aging, and sensitivity to pharmacological treatments that modulate lifespan and healthspan. However, investigating the functional decline of the aging heart requires a reliable method to obtain high-quality, viable cells suitable for demanding single-cell techniques. This study optimized a previously described protocol for the isolation of Danio rerio cardiomyocytes to ensure consistent recovery of healthy working myocytes from both young and senescent N. furzeri. This protocol describes the isolation of ventricular cardiomyocytes from N. furzeri specifically optimized for the whole-cell patch clamp technique. The article demonstrates how to efficiently excise the heart, perform enzymatic dissociation of the myocardium by retrograde perfusion, and store the isolated cardiomyocytes. We discuss the selection of enzymes required to digest the extracellular matrix and intercellular junctions without compromising ion channel structure. Freshly isolated cardiomyocytes are suitable for high-resolution electrophysiological assays, including action potential recordings and measurements of major inward and outward ionic currents across age groups. The article also addresses the features of cardiomyocyte isolation in fish that differ from standard mammalian isolation procedures.

article.title: Design and Evaluation of Ethylene Glycol Monopiperate as a Novel Antihyperlipidemic Prodrug: Synthesis, Antihyperlipidemic Activity, and Pharmacokinetics.
article.authors: Guirong Borijihan; Mimi Liu; Mingming Bao; Zhengkun Sun; Meng He; Youxin Li
article.venue: Journal of analytical methods in chemistry
article.abstract: Piperine, a major active component isolated from the traditional Mongolian medicine Piper longum L., exhibits antihyperlipidemic activity but also demonstrates inherent toxicity. In this study, ethylene glycol monopiperate (EGM), a piperine derivative, was synthesized via concentrated H2SO4-catalyzed esterification. Its structure was systematically characterized by FTIR, MS, 13C NMR, and 1H NMR, with a yield of 60% and a purity of 99.2%. Subsequently, the in vitro cytotoxicity of EGM on HepG2 cells was evaluated, and the results indicated that over 90% cell viability was observed at concentrations up to 150 μg/mL. It was also investigated in male Wistar rats, and a sensitive, rapid, and accurate solid-phase extraction (SPE)-UPLC method was developed and validated for the quantification of EGM in rat plasma. The novel method showed good linearity over the concentration range of 1-16 µg/mL, a limit of detection (LOD) of 1 μg/mL, and high accuracy and precision (relative error [RE%] < 15%, relative standard deviation [RSD%] < 10%). In terms of antihyperlipidemic efficacy, EGM demonstrated excellent performance in reducing total cholesterol (TC), glucose (GLU), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), as well as elevating high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C); these effects were notably better than the conventional control drug simvastatin. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that the plasma concentration-time profile of EGM followed a first-order open one-compartment model. Calculations using WINNONLIN software (ver. 5.2) showed a half-life (t 1/2) of 1.46 ± 0.67 h and an area under the curve (AUC0-∞) of 7,15,530 ± 522.4 ng h/mL. EGM was stable in plasma over 24 h at room temperature and one month at -20°C, after three freeze-thaw cycles. These results verified that EGM may serve as a promising candidate for an antihyperlipidemic prodrug.

article.title: Positioning Creation of Cell Communication Channels via Chinese Microneedle.
article.authors: Xu Y, Fang M, Chen Z, Liu H, Xue Y, Li Z, Lin Y, Wang K, Lin F, Zhang N.
article.abstract: The core dilemma of senescence mitigation lies in the disrupted and even detrimental communication between senescent cells and local immune cells. Existing delivery methods cannot precisely establish protective intercellular communication channels across cell types within the enclosed lesion cavity. In this study, we utilize Chinese microneedle technology for precise, minimally invasive localization of aged lesions, and to release spatially targeted and temporally sustained dual-field to create intercellular communication channels between macrophages and senescent cells. The unique physical properties of this Chinese microneedle system confine the current path to specific spatiotemporal windows, releasing an electro-field while simultaneously activating dynamic van der Waals forces that release functionalized hydrogel microparticles, thereby superimposing a vita-field. Within the dual-field active zone, the electro-field not only attenuates cellular senescence but also forms a communication channel from senescent cells to macrophages, driving macrophages into a hyperactivated state. Meanwhile, the vita-field stabilizes the macrophage membrane, enabling long-term, stable communication between hyperactivated macrophages and senescent cells. Ultimately, the intercellular communication channels established by this Chinese microneedle system alleviate cellular senescence and apoptosis, supporting the repair of aged lesions.

article.title: Understanding natural variation in milk lipids: why parity and lactation stage matter for nutritional value.
article.authors: Rodrigo Muiño Otero; Elena Niceas Martínez Díez; Patricia Regal; Joaquín Hernández; Cristina Castillo; Jose Luis Benedito; Jose María Viana
article.venue: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bovine milk is a major dietary source of lipids whose fatty acid (FA) profile shapes its nutritional and technological quality, yet its natural variation is commonly described using fixed days-in-milk windows that ignore individual peak-yield timing and parity-specific metabolism. We used routine milk-recording data and Fourier transform mid-infrared spectroscopy (FT-MIR) to characterize parity- and stage-dependent dynamics in milk composition, defining lactation stages relative to each cow's model-based peak yield. RESULTS: A total of 10 209 test-day records from 677 Holstein cows (160 primiparous; 517 multiparous) from a commercial herd in Galicia (Spain) were analyzed for milk components, FA groups and individual FAs, β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) and udder-health traits using linear mixed models. Multiparous cows had higher milk fat, BHB and somatic cell count and higher concentrations of most FA fractions, whereas primiparous cows had higher lactose, protein and urea (P < 0.05); peak-referenced stage effects were larger and more coherent in multiparous cows. Disaggregating multiparous cows by lactation number revealed consistent gradients with advancing parity (declining de novo synthesized FAs and rising BHB and somatic cell count) superimposed on, but not overturning, the primiparous-multiparous contrast. CONCLUSION: Parity structure and peak-referenced lactation staging are practical, FT-MIR-measurable determinants of raw-milk fat quality; accounting for them supports more precise milk characterization and stage- and parity-informed standardization of dairy products for human nutrition. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.

article.title: USP25 promotes ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy by deubiquitinating p53 and suppressing the GPX4/SLC7A11 axis.
article.authors: Yanjun Gao; Wenjing Zhao; Qiannan Chai; Cunxi Ye
article.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore the expression of the deubiquitinase (DUB) USP25 in diabetic retinopathy (DR) and its mechanistic role in regulating ferroptosis. METHODS: Bioinformatics was used to screen for DR-related DUB candidate genes. USP25 expression was validated in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse model and high glucose (HG)-treated ARPE-19 cells. Loss- and gain-of-function approaches for USP25 were employed to assess retinal structural damage, tight junction proteins, cell viability, and TUNEL positivity. Ferroptosis-related changes were evaluated by measuring iron content, Fe2+ fluorescent signals, lipid peroxidation levels, and antioxidant enzyme activities. The molecular mechanism underlying USP25-mediated ferroptosis was elucidated through bioinformatics prediction, co-immunoprecipitation, and protein stability assays, followed by rescue experiments with p53 knockdown. RESULTS: USP25 was upregulated in the retinas of diabetic mice. USP25 knockdown ameliorated retinal structural damage and restored the expression of tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and occludin) in DR mice. USP25 exacerbated HG-induced cellular injury and ferroptosis by promoting iron accumulation, enhancing lipid peroxidation, suppressing the antioxidant defense system, and downregulating the ferroptosis suppressors GPX4 and SLC7A11. Mechanistically, USP25 stabilized p53 protein by reducing its ubiquitination. Rescue experiments further demonstrated that p53 knockdown significantly reversed ferroptosis-related alterations in the context of USP25 overexpression, mitigating ferroptosis-related damage in ARPE-19 cells and retinal tissues of diabetic mice. CONCLUSION: USP25 is aberrantly upregulated in DR and promotes ferroptosis by deubiquitinating and stabilizing p53, thereby exacerbating retinal damage. The USP25-p53-ferroptosis axis may represent a potential therapeutic target for DR intervention.

article.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
article.authors: Gordon I Smith; Max C Petersen; Sean M Hartig; Samuel Klein
article.abstract: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

article.title: Cartilage-binding coacervate with therapeutic payload delivery and biomimetic lubrication alleviates osteoarthritis by reducing joint friction and inflammation.
article.authors: Sirong Chen; Tianshen Jiang; Xiaorou Qiu; Ruitong Luo; Haiyang Yao; Ruinan Wang; Zhuo Li; Pengchao Zhao; Liming Bian
article.abstract: Healthy articular cartilage maintains ultralow friction through the lipid/hyaluronic acid/lubricin complex lubrication layer, in which the zwitterionic lipids mediate lubrication and the hyaluronic acid and lubricin anchor to cartilage matrix. However, in osteoarthritis this lubrication system is progressively degraded, leading to increased cartilage wear and joint dysfunction. Therefore, early and lubrication-based intervention is urgently needed. Here we present biomimetic polyzwitterionic coacervates (pZCOs) that recapitulate both the lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities of the natural boundary lubrication layer. pZCOs exhibit strong binding affinity to fibronectin, establish a stable and ultralow-friction lubrication layer on the cartilage surface, facilitate the sustained release of anti-inflammatory drugs, and preserve the viability and anti-inflammatory paracrine secretion of encapsulated mesenchymal stem cells. In both rat and mini-pig models of osteoarthritis, intra-articular administration of drug/MSC-laden pZCOs effectively reduces cartilage degradation, suppresses inflammation and promotes cartilage integrity, outperforming clinical hyaluronic acid lubricants in lubrication performance, in vivo retention and therapeutic efficacy. These findings highlight the translational potential of engineered biomimetic coacervates as next-generation joint lubricants for integrated management of osteoarthritis.

article.title: Effect of food deprivation on physiological parameters and muscle quality of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
article.authors: Qifeng Lu; Huai Zhang; Junhui Liu; Liqi Jiang; Han Zhang; Li Lin; Qingqing Li
article.abstract: Food deprivation is a pre-harvest management practice that can alter body composition and muscle quality in cultured fish. This study compared growth performance, physiological indices, histological characteristics, muscle texture, proximate, fatty acid and amino acid content between food-deprived and normally fed Oreochromis niloticus over a 30-day period. Food deprivation significantly reduced specific growth rate (SGR), and liver somatic index (LSI) after 15 days and body weight (BW), weight gain rate (WGR), SGR, viscerosomatic index (VSI) and LSI after 30 days (p < 0.05), whereas condition factor (CF) and visceral fat index (VAI) did not differ significantly between treatments. There were no significant changes in activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) after food deprivation. Muscle hardness was significantly greater in food-deprived O. niloticus than in normally fed O. niloticus after 15 days (p < 0.05). Micrographs from food-deprived O. niloticus showed liver cells to be slightly irregular in shape, with some showing signs of dispersion and vacuolization; in addition, the intestine showed substantially more pronounced vacuolation, enlarged intercellular spaces and shortened villi compared with normally fed fish. Muscle crude protein content was significantly higher in food-deprived O. niloticus than in normally fed O. niloticus (p < 0.05); however, this increase may partly reflect a relative concentration effect associated with lipid depletion rather than an increase in absolute protein deposition. Serine and tyrosine concentrations were significantly higher after 15 days of food deprivation than in normally fed fish; the reverse was seen for total lipid content (p < 0.05). After 30 days of food deprivation, muscle n-3 PUFA content was significantly lower, whereas the n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio was significantly higher, than in normally fed fish (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that a 30-day food deprivation period reduced growth performance and altered muscle composition and texture, while producing only limited changes in the physiological indicators examined.

article.title: Survey of the human proteostasis network: translation, protein folding, and organelle-specific systems.
article.authors: Powers ET, Elsasser S, Stoeger T, Cao K, Collier M, Rainbolt TK, Pokhrel S, Taguwa S, Sui X, Kurtzbard RD, Martínez-Botía P, Richardson RAK, Chou CC, Aviner R, Barbosa N, Masto VB, Morales-Polanco F, Lima L, Rodriguez Gama A, Mockler E, Garza D, Kelly JW, Finley D, Clerico EM, Prado MA, Gestwicki JE, Elia LP, Finkbeiner S, Frydman J, Morimoto RI.
article.abstract: The condition of having a healthy, functional proteome is known as protein homeostasis, or proteostasis. Maintaining proteostasis is the province of the proteostasis network, which consists of the cellular components that regulate protein synthesis, folding, localization, and degradation. The proteostasis network is a fundamental functional unit in biology with relevance to many diseases. Despite its importance, the human proteostasis network has until now lacked a precise definition, limiting our ability to interrogate proteostasis, integrate multiomic datasets, compare results across studies, or model proteostasis dysfunction in disease. To address this limitation, we have operationally defined the human proteostasis network by providing a comprehensive, annotated, and manually curated list of its components classified into nine Branches based on their function and localization - cytonuclear proteostasis, ER proteostasis, mitochondrial proteostasis, nuclear proteostasis, proteostasis network regulation, translation, extracellular proteostasis, the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and the ubiquitin-proteasome system - which we present in a series of three manuscripts of which this is the first. Overall, the proteostasis network annotation encompasses 3,151 components described by 4,043 annotations. Here, we present the 1,190 components that make up the first seven of these Branches, which comprise the compartment-based proteostasis network (cytonuclear, ER, mitochondrial, nuclear, and extracellular proteostasis), proteostasis network regulation, and translation. These Branches include chaperones, folding enzymes, systems for trafficking proteins, organelle-specific degradation systems, and the cell's translation machinery. This work provides a framework that will facilitate insights into how proteostasis is preserved in health, lost in aging and disease, and how it could be restored through pharmacological intervention.

article.title: Organization of neuropeptide signaling: cross-species insights from small model organisms.
article.authors: Zandawala M, Filosa A, Beets I.
article.abstract: Neuropeptides are ancient signaling molecules that modulate neural circuit function and behavior across the animal kingdom. Model organisms such as Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, and zebrafish serve as powerful in vivo models for deciphering the organization of neuropeptidergic signaling, owing to their smaller nervous systems, genetic tractability, and the growing availability of neural connectomes. In this article, we review how these organisms have advanced current understanding of neuropeptidergic transmission across three interconnected themes: (i) the roles of peptides in sensory-motor transformations, (ii) the conservation and divergence of peptidergic expression and network architecture across species, and (iii) the diversity of neurotransmission strategies employed by single neurons. Finally, we highlight recent technological innovations as well as open questions that could shape this field in the coming years.

article.title: Fluorescence signatures for interleaflet coupling - missing link in monolayer-bilayer correspondence.
article.authors: Pinchu Xavier; Emilia Krok; Hanna Orlikowska-Rzeznik; Lukasz Piatkowski
article.venue: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
article.abstract: Model membrane systems, including Langmuir monolayers, supported lipid bilayers (SLBs), and vesicles, are widely used to investigate the structure and dynamics of biological membranes and membrane-associated processes. It is widely assumed that lipid monolayers compressed to approximately 30 mN/m provide a physicochemical environment comparable to that of lipid bilayers. However, the validity of this correspondence remains debated. Here, we systematically test monolayer-bilayer equivalence using the fluorescence spectral responses of three molecular probes, DOPE-Atto633, Laurdan, and NR12S. Their spectra were recorded in DOPC and DPPC monolayers over a broad range of surface pressures, with and without cholesterol, and compared with corresponding bilayer systems formed as SLBs and small unilamellar vesicles (SUVs). Our results reveal pronounced differences between monolayer and bilayer environments depending on the lipid composition, cholesterol content, and the molecular probe used. For pure DOPC and DPPC, Laurdan revealed close monolayer-bilayer correspondence at approximately 30 mN/m, whereas NR12S required substantially higher surface pressures to reproduce bilayer-like spectral responses. Cholesterol further altered this correspondence, and for some compositions full spectral correspondence was not reached even at the highest surface pressures investigated. These findings challenge the general applicability of the established monolayer-bilayer correspondence and demonstrate that a single surface-pressure criterion cannot reliably reproduce the physicochemical properties of bilayer membranes across different lipid systems. They also underpin the importance of second leaflet and interleaflet coupling in shaping membrane structure and packing. More broadly, our findings emphasise the need to critically consider appropriate model systems when investigating biological membranes and their functions.

article.title: Exposure to polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics elicits renal injury with limited compensation and associated intestinal alterations: A time-resolved multi-omics study.
article.authors: Cui M, Wang X, Li T, Ma H, Li S, Sang R, Zhang X.
article.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) are emerging contaminants of toxicological concern. However, the temporal progression of PET-NPs-induced renal injury during repeated oral exposure remains poorly understood. Male C57BL/6 J mice received PET-NPs at 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 14, 28, or 56 days to characterize time-dependent nephrotoxicity and intestinal alterations. Fluorescence imaging detected gastrointestinal signals at all time points and a time-dependent increase in renal fluorescence following administration of Nile red-labeled PET-NPs. PET-NPs exposure was associated with impaired intestinal barrier integrity and altered gut microbial composition. Renal assessments revealed functional impairment, tubular injury, inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, and lipid peroxidation. Integrated renal transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified alterations in inflammatory signaling, redox homeostasis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid metabolism. Mean TUNEL positivity was numerically highest at 28 days and remained elevated relative to controls at 56 days. At 56 days, tubular injury, renal dysfunction, and inflammation persisted alongside increased Ki-67 positivity. Although the renal Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant axis was activated, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and renal injury indicated insufficient antioxidant compensation. Repeated oral PET-NPs exposure elicited time-dependent nephrotoxicity characterized by inflammatory-redox-lipid metabolic remodeling and constrained antioxidant compensation. These findings provide a time-resolved multi-omics framework for assessing PET-NPs-associated renal hazards following repeated oral exposure.

article.title: Divergent aging patterns of polylactic acid (PLA) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) plastic sheets and their differential associations with soil carbon stability.
article.authors: Zhang Y, Li C, Wang Y, Yan S, Zhang X, Xu J, Ren K, Liu J.
article.abstract: Plastic pollution is a growing concern. Plastic particles undergo aging that changes their properties and ecological impacts, yet how different polymers age in natural settings and relate to soil carbon cycling remains unclear. We conducted a nine-month in situ experiment to compare the aging of biodegradable PLA (polylactic acid) and conventional PVC (polyvinyl chloride) sheets and to assess their associations with soil microbial communities, enzymes, and organic carbon fractions. PLA surfaces developed hydrolysis‑induced cracks and fragmentation, whereas PVC showed oxidative roughening. These aging patterns were associated with divergent functional potential of plastisphere microbial communities. PLA‑associated soils had higher β-glucosidase and peroxidase activities, together with a trend toward higher labile carbon (FPOC) indicators than PVC‑associated soils. Mineral‑associated organic carbon (MAOC) did not differ between treatments, but MAOC proportion was negatively correlated with bulk density only under PLA. Because our study lacked an unamended control, our conclusions are limited to PLA-PVC comparisons. Our findings show that the two polymers differ in aging pathways, microbial associations, and associations with labile carbon turnover that vary with soil physical properties, suggesting that the environmental implications of biodegradable plastics cannot be assumed from their label alone.

article.title: Redistribution of Corneal Endothelial Cells After Descemet Stripping Only Combined With Cataract Surgery for Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy.
article.authors: Tasha Miller; Stephan Ong Tone
article.abstract: PURPOSE: Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) is characterized by progressive corneal endothelial cell (CEC) loss and guttae formation. FECD pathology preferentially affects the central corneal endothelium (CE) before peripheral. Descemet stripping only (DSO) surgically removes diseased central CE and Descemet membrane, enabling rejuvenation through peripheral CEC migration. This study characterized central and peripheral CEC redistribution after DSO combined with cataract surgery. METHODS: Retrospective analysis identified patients with FECD who underwent combined DSO and cataract surgery by a single surgeon between 2021 and 2025. Central and peripheral endothelial cell density (ECD), coefficient of variation, and percentage hexagonality were measured using specular microscopy (Konan CellChek 20 Plus) preoperatively and at 1 to 3, 3 to 6, 6 to 12, and ≥12 months postoperatively. RESULTS: Sixteen eyes from 11 patients were included (mean age 71.2 ± 9.0 years; 81.8% female). Mean descemetorhexis diameter was 4.2 ± 0.3 mm (range 4-5 mm). Peripheral ECD declined significantly at 1 to 3 months postoperatively compared with preoperative values (1904.3 ± 524.3-987.3 ± 452.6 cells/mm2; P < 0.001) and remained reduced throughout follow-up (all P < 0.001). Central ECD increased progressively from 452.5 ± 696.9 cells/mm2 preoperatively, exceeding baseline by 6 to 12 months (1138.6 ± 200.7; P < 0.001) and remaining elevated beyond 12 months (1142.8 ± 124.4; P < 0.001). Over 12 months, visual acuity improved significantly (P = 0.003), accompanied by a reduction in central corneal thickness (P = 0.03). CONCLUSIONS: After DSO combined with cataract surgery, early peripheral CEC depletion was accompanied by progressive central ECD recovery over 12 months, supporting peripheral redistribution as a primary mechanism of central CE rejuvenation.

article.title: PIrates of the vacuole: phosphoinositide hijacking by T4SS intracellular pathogens.
article.authors: Bonazzi M.
article.abstract: Intracellular bacteria equipped with a Type IV Secretion Systems (T4SS), including Legionella pneumophila, Coxiella burnetii, Brucella abortus , and Anaplasma/Ehrlichia species, evolved a convergent strategy of exploiting host cell lipids at every stage of infection, from cholesterol-rich raft-mediated entry to the establishment of replicative vacuoles that evade lysosomal destruction. Indeed, these pathogens actively remodel host cell membranes by deploying T4SS effectors that bind, generate, or deplete specific lipid species, in particular phosphoinositides and cholesterol, to dictate the identity and trafficking fate of their containing vacuole. A remarkable diversity of effectors with lipid-binding or lipid-modifying activities has now been characterized across these pathogens: from the PI4P-centric Dot/Icm effector cascade of Legionella to the cooperating CvpB, CvpE, and Vice triad of Coxiella , and the phosphoinositide-binding immune evasion effector BtpA of Brucella . These pathogens also tap into host lipid droplets for energy and membrane precursors, modulate bioactive lipid mediators such as prostaglandins to curb immune clearance, and present atypical surface lipids to minimize pattern recognition. Advances in lipidomics, including a landmark systematic identification of novel α-helical PI-binding effector folds conserved across Legionella and Coxiella , have shed new light on these processes with unprecedented resolution. This review examines the shared and divergent lipid-subversion strategies of T4SS-bearing intracellular pathogens from an integrated molecular, cellular, and lipidomic perspective, and highlights emerging opportunities for host-directed therapeutic intervention.

article.title: They grow up so fast - the birth and development of membrane contact site research.
article.authors: Tim P Levine; Christopher J R Loewen; William A Prinz
article.abstract: Over the past 15 years, the field of 'membrane contact sites' and research into direct communication between organelles has taken off. In this Perspective, we look back at how the field has developed. Rather than cover every forward step, we focus on conceptual advances in the study of interorganelle communication - particularly advances that were not obvious at the start of this journey. Among these advances is the demonstration that different functions located at the same membrane contact site interact with each other. Another is that a wide range of molecules are transferred between organelles at contact sites, well beyond the two best-known cargos, Ca2+ and lipids. By looking at the history of the field, we explain how our understanding of Ca2+ flux and lipid transfer have grown at different rates. Finally, we suggest that the field has been liable to several types of error, from concrete thinking about the significance of contact to misusing terms such as 'tether'. Nevertheless, the application of new cutting-edge techniques to the future of contact site research presents many exciting opportunities.

article.title: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase mediates atherosclerosis progression by regulating copper metabolism via PHOX2A.
article.authors: Qingquan Xue; Guilin Feng; Jiqiong Hu; Fangkuan Li; Shusen Tang
article.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a major cardiovascular disease whose underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigates the role of dopamine beta-hydroxylase (DBH) in AS pathogenesis and its regulation of copper metabolism via the transcription factor PHOX2A. Through transcriptomic profiling of aortic tissues from ApoE⁻/⁻ mice fed a high-fat diet, we identified 2891 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between AS and control mice, with DBH being significantly upregulated. DBH expression was also elevated in the serum of AS patients and in ox-LDL-treated human vascular smooth muscle cells (HVSMCs). Mechanistically, we demonstrate that PHOX2A directly activates the DBH promoter, and that DBH knockdown attenuates ox‑LDL‑induced apoptosis and lipid accumulation in HVSMCs while PHOX2A overexpression exacerbates these effects. Importantly, DBH knockdown in ApoE⁻/⁻ mice not only reduced atherosclerotic plaque burden and improved serum lipid profiles but also restored serum copper concentrations and altered the expression of cuproptosis‑related proteins (FDX1, LIAS, DLAT). These findings identify DBH as a key mediator of AS progression linked to PHOX2A‑dependent regulation of copper metabolism and cuproptosis, suggesting that targeting the DBH/PHOX2A axis may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for AS.

article.title: Remnant cholesterol predicts progression from prehypertension to incident hypertension: Evidence from a prospective cohort study and Mendelian randomization analysis.
article.authors: Mengmeng Qi; Mengmeng Wang; Yonghao Li; Xiaoxiao Cai
article.abstract: ObjectiveRemnant cholesterol (RC), a marker of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnants, has emerged as an important contributor to residual cardiometabolic risk. However, whether RC contributes to the transition from prehypertension to clinical hypertension remains unclear. We investigated the association between RC and incident hypertension among adults with prehypertension and further assessed genetic evidence using Mendelian randomization (MR).MethodsThis prospective cohort study included 2,858 adults with prehypertension from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, followed from 2011 to 2015. RC was calculated as total cholesterol minus low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. Two-sample MR, including inverse-variance weighted and Bayesian weighted MR methods, was used to evaluate the genetic association between RC and hypertension-related traits.ResultsDuring 4 years of follow-up, 891 participants developed incident hypertension. Higher RC was independently associated with increased odds of incident hypertension. In the fully adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL increase in RC was associated with a 2% higher odds of hypertension. Compared with participants in the lowest RC quartile, those in the highest quartile had 67% higher odds of incident hypertension, corresponding to an absolute increase of 11.86% in cumulative hypertension incidence during follow-up. Compared with the lowest RC quartile, the highest quartile showed a significantly higher risk of incident hypertension. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a linear dose-response association, with no evidence of nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses suggested stronger associations among older adults, non-smokers, individuals with normal body weight, and participants without depressive symptoms. MR analyses further supported a positive genetic association between elevated RC and hypertension-related traits.ConclusionsAmong adults with prehypertension, elevated RC was independently and linearly associated with higher risk of progression to incident hypertension. Genetic evidence further supported a potential role of RC in hypertension-related traits. These findings suggest that RC, which can be readily calculated from routine lipid profiles, may complement existing approaches for hypertension risk assessment and targeted blood pressure monitoring among individuals with prehypertension.

article.title: Neural precursor cell expressed developmentally downregulated 4-mediated phosphatase and tensin homolog ubiquitination alleviates senescence and apoptosis of nucleus pulposus cells under interleukin-1 beta conditions.
article.authors: Yang Lin; Cheng Li; Xuehui Chang; Ye Wang; Shiying Jia
article.venue: The Journal of international medical research
article.abstract: ObjectiveIncreasing evidence indicates that aging and apoptosis of nucleus pulposus cells are closely associated with the pathogenesis of intervertebral disc degeneration. This study investigated the role of E3 ubiquitin ligase neural precursor cell expressed developmentally downregulated gene 4 (NEDD4) in the interleukin-1 beta-induced aging and apoptosis of human nucleus pulposus cells and evaluated whether NEDD4 mediates these effects by promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN).MethodsTwo commercially available immortalized human nucleus pulposus cells were used for in vitro experiments, without involving human participants or collecting human tissues. The cells were treated with interleukin-1 beta (10 ng/mL for 24 h) to establish an inflammatory model of intervertebral disc degeneration. Transfection of overexpressed NEDD4 and/or PTEN was performed in the model cells. Cell viability, apoptosis, senescence, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediators, and extracellular matrix-related proteins were assessed. The interactions between NEDD4 and PTEN and the stability of the PTEN protein were investigated using co-immunoprecipitation, actinomycin D tracking, MG132 treatment, and intracellular ubiquitination experiments.ResultsInterleukin-1 beta treatment downregulated NEDD4 expression in nucleus pulposus cells to 2.3-fold of the baseline level (p < 0.001) while simultaneously upregulated PTEN protein expression to 1.8-fold of the baseline level (p < 0.01). Overexpression of NEDD4 shortened the half-life of PTEN protein from 8 h to 3 h through the ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation pathway (p < 0.001). In addition, overexpression of NEDD4 reduced the level of reactive oxygen species, inhibited cell apoptosis, decreased the expression levels of p21 and p16, and restored the expression levels of type II collagen and aggrecan (p < 0.05). NEDD4 interacted with PTEN and enhanced its ubiquitination. Functional rescue experiments indicated that overexpression of PTEN weakened the protective effects of NEDD4.ConclusionsThis study preliminarily demonstrated that the overexpression of NEDD4 can alleviate the interleukin-1 beta-induced apoptosis and senescence phenomena of nucleus pulposus cells. This effect may be partially mediated by promoting the ubiquitination of PTEN and the proteasome degradation pathway. However, further functional deficiency experiments and in vivo validations are warranted to establish the causal relationship and therapeutic relevance.

article.title: P. aeruginosa disrupts ARP-2/3 mediated apical F-actin organization to induce intestinal deformation in C. elegans
article.authors: Divyashree, A.; Sinha, T.; Padmanabhan, A.
article.abstract: Apico-basal polarity is essential for maintaining cytoskeletal organization and regulating transport and secretory functions in the intestinal epithelium. The opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa exploits the interactions between cell polarity and cytoskeletal networks to promote infection. However, most mechanistic insights into these processes have come from in-vitro epithelial monolayers, which do not fully capture the complexity of multicellular tissues. Here, we show that heat-labile factor/s secreted by P. aeruginosa disrupt apical polarity in Caenorhabditis elegans enterocytes through a PI3K-AKT-dependent mechanism. This disruption is accompanied by apical enrichment of PI(3,4,5)P3, fragmentation of ARP-2/3 organization, localized disruption of apical F-actin, release of F-actin-rich vesicles into the intestinal lumen, and pronounced deformation of the apical surface. Perturbing CDC-42-ARP-2/3-dependent actin assembly, PI3K-AKT signalling, or the endotube regulators, IFB-2 and IFO-1 suppressed intestinal deformation and significantly extend host survival following P. aeruginosa exposure. Notably, these changes occured without detectable loss of epithelial tissue integrity. Together, our findings identify epithelial polarity disruption as a mechanism through which extracellular P. aeruginosa remodels the host cytoskeleton and alters tissue mechanics during infection.

article.title: Nine-Year Changes in Work Satisfaction in Midlife – the Role of Age and Flexible Goal Adjustment
article.authors: Henning G, Kelle N, Infurna FJ.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: As the work force is ageing and many countries raise or abolish retirement ages, it becomes more and more important to understand how work satisfaction develops over the lifespan, particularly in midlife and older age. Although many studies report positive associations of age and work satisfaction, there are only few longitudinal studies with large samples investigating within-person change over longer time spans. To overcome these limitations, we used data from the German Ageing Survey to investigate changes in work satisfaction among n = 2,588 individuals aged 40 – 59 at four measurement occasions between 2008 and 2017. As our study was informed by life span approaches to self-regulation at work, we were also interested in the role of age and flexible goal adjustment, which is the ability to adjust one’s goals according to restrictions in the environment. Results showed that work satisfaction was characterized by stability in midlife, but workers in their 60’s experienced increases in work satisfaction. Nevertheless, these effects may partly show selection effects due to dissatisfied older workers retiring over time and / or dropping out of the survey. Flexible goal adjustment was related to higher work satisfaction, but not to changes in work satisfaction. Our results demonstrate that work satisfaction can increase in older age and that flexible goal adjustment may play a role in shaping the course of work satisfaction in midlife and older age. More research is needed to understand which coping mechanisms help aging workers to stay satisfied at work.

article.title: The senescence-linked factor Chi3L1 contributes to mesenchymal stromal cells dysfunction promoting joint aging and osteoarthritis progression
article.authors: Maroun G, Bonnefont A, Silva R, Terreza C, Pradenas C, Asencio C, Robert B, De Seny D, De CEUNINCK F, Pastoureau P, Jorgensen C, Djouad F, Pers Y, Brondello J.
article.abstract: Abstract Ageing progressively disrupts joint homeostasis and increases susceptibility to osteoarthritis (OA), yet why repair fails in the altered joint remains poorly understood. Cellular senescence accumulates with age and is prominent in osteoarthritic joints, contributing to a persistent catabolic, inflammatory and tissue-remodelling microenvironment through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Such signals can alter the function of endogenous reparative cells including mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), which are important to tissue repair and immunomodulation. Nonetheless, little is known on which senescence associated stromal factors within this altered niche could compromise MSCs competence. In this study, we are interested by chitinase-3-like 1 (CHI3L1), a SASP glycoprotein whose levels are elevated in both ageing and OA. We revealed that CHI3L1 accumulates in OA joints in correlation with senescence and the disease features, where it in vitro chronic exposure converts MSC toward a dysfunctional age-like state characterized by impaired potencies, disrupted tri-lineage commitment, reduced mobility, altered metabolomic profiling, loss of immunomodulatory activity together with an acquisition of a pro-inflammatory secretome. Consequently, CHI3L1 preconditioning abolishes the homeostatic function of healthy MSCs in an inflammatory OA model. Conversely, in spontaneous age-related OA model, MSC transplantation combined to CHI3L1 transient neutralization restores joint dynamics by enhancing cartilage repair, reducing synovial inflammation, preventing bone remodeling, improving maximal speed locomotor and shifting selective circulated factors related to stromal, skeletal, and hematopoietic homeostasis toward a more youthful pattern. Collectively, our findings establish CHI3L1 as a novel senescence-associated contributor in the decline of MSC fitness and regenerative niche competence during joint ageing. Furthermore, it provides a rationale for combining microenvironment-targeted interventions with stem cell therapy to maximize their potentials for tissue regeneration in age-related diseases.

article.title: Eye See Your Intentions: Age-Related Differences in Gaze Perception and Trustworthiness Attributions
article.authors: Shoenfelt A, Chadwick RE, Lin T, Park S, Barres TA, Ebner NC.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: Successful social interactions depend on regulating approach-avoidance tendencies as well as accurately understanding those motivations in others. Direct gaze signals approach intentions, whereas averted gaze signals avoidance intentions. Older relative to younger adults display a stronger direct gaze bias (i.e., are more likely to perceive eye gaze as direct vs. averted). This bias in motivational cue perception likely impacts social trait attributions. This study, for the first time, leveraged a lifespan sample across a wide age range (18 – 88 years; N = 307) to investigate adult lifespan differences in gaze perception using a novel set of gaze-modified face stimuli with varying expressions and tested whether perception of gaze aversion affected attributions of facial trustworthiness. Participants were recruited and the study conducted online via Prolific. Faces with more averted gaze were perceived as more direct-looking with age. This bias was relatively weaker for fearful faces compared to all other facial expressions. Further, greater perception of direct gaze was associated with greater facial trustworthiness attributions, and especially with age. Combined, these findings confirm a direct gaze bias in aging and support its impact on social trait attributions. These adult lifespan differences in approach-avoidance motivational cue perception may reflect shifts in sensitivity, capacity, and/or motivation and are discussed as a possible mechanism in greater trust and susceptibility to deception with age. This work also adds substantially to the widely used FACES Lifespan Database corpus by making the newly gaze-modified faces, and their norm ratings, publicly available for research on motivational and cognitive aging.

article.title: Age-of-acquisition Effects across the Adult Lifespan: Evidence from Eye Movements in Compound Word Reading
article.authors: Elsherif MM, li w, Tompson M, Paterson K.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: The Age of Acquisition (AoA) effect is where words acquired during childhood are recognised more quickly than those acquired during adulthood. However, the influence of AoA on compound words and its stability across the adult lifespan remain under-investigated. We conducted two eye-tracking experiments to clarify how the AoA effect is moderated by ageing and spacing. Ninety British English adults participated across two eye-tracking experiments: 60 young adults (30 reading unspaced compounds in Experiment 1 and 30 reading spaced compounds in Experiment 2) and 30 older adults (who read both unspaced and spaced compounds across experiments). Using Bayesian linear mixed-effects models, we observed a robust AoA effect in both spaced and unspaced compound words in young adults. However, in older adults, we only observed an AoA effect in unspaced compound words. The AoA effect declined with increasing age, whereas the slope of AoA effect was shallower in spaced than unspaced compound words. These findings suggest that the functional influence of AoA is contingent upon orthographic structure and reading experience: while whole-word AoA influences processing across visual formats in younger readers, older readers shift away from whole-word lexical properties toward constituent-level strategies when orthographic structure is disrupted by spacing.

article.title: Biological State-Space and Adaptive Reserve Across Scales: An Entropy-Symmetry Framework for Ageing and Cancer
article.authors: Peacock EJ.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: Biological function depends on constrained transitions between physiological states, yet a biomarker sampled at a single time point describes only an occupied state, not the pathways accessible from it; capacity to respond, recover or tolerate further challenge is inferred accordingly. To address this distinction, a framework drawing on concepts of entropy and symmetry is postulated, in which molecular, structural, energetic, immune, and temporal constraints shape the integrity of the occupied state and access to a repertoire of viable states.A symmetry-integrity function, Φ(t), serves as a latent descriptor of a currently occupied multiscale state. Adaptive reserve describes the breadth, connectivity, traversability and recoverability of viable state-space; resilience defines its effective deployment during perturbation. Ordinary physiological capacity is distinguished from failsafe responses, through which unresolved burden may be contained or damaged components eliminated while higher-order function is sustained. Such compensation can preserve current output despite restricted transitions, maintenance expenditures and reduced capacity to absorb subsequent challenges. Physiological and failsafe responses may draw on pre-existing capacity and challenge-induced mechanisms.In this context, ageing is hypothesised to alter state accessibility through loss of viable states, altered transition barriers, slower restoration, increased stochastic dispersion in state-space or pathological trapping. Cancer presents a nested-scale problem in which malignant reserve can be preserved while constraints that sustain host function deteriorate. Quiescence, reproductive transitions and comparative longevity illustrate the distinction between contemporaneous activity, integrity of the occupied state and retained response capacity.An operational schema is developed using spatially specified measurements, graded perturbations, recovery dynamics and repeated challenges. Membrane organisation, multivariate molecular profiles and spatial tumour states afford candidate descriptions of occupied states, with measured states distinguished from inferred trajectories. Testable predictions concern compensated function, activation thresholds, response ceilings and whether niche context adds predictive information. The framework is a testable synthesis whose explanatory and predictive value lies in its assessment against simpler models based on baseline state, damage burden and recovery. It gives a basis for subsequent evaluation of therapeutic strategies.

article.title: PIN1-p53 bifurcation dictates opposite cell fate decisions in Alzheimer’s disease and glioblastoma via distinct energy landscape topologies
article.authors: Lyu J.
article.abstract: Abstract Although Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and glioblastoma (GBM) share common aging-related risk factors, they lead to opposite cellular fates—neurodegeneration versus uncontrolled proliferation. The system-level mechanisms driving this striking divergence remain elusive. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic data from AD (84 donors) and GBM (18 samples) to comparatively map the energy landscape of cell fate decisions in these two diseases. By computing a PIN1-p53 Bifurcation Index and CellEnergy landscape, we reveal that AD and GBM diverge at a critical Bifurcation Point. AD cells descend from a Health Peak into a deep AD Valley, characterized by a senescent profile with PIN1 downregulation and p53 activation. In contrast, GBM cells settle on a flat, low-energy GBM Plateau, exhibiting a proliferative profile driven by PIN1 overexpression and p53 suppression. We further identified pioneer gene candidates at the Bifurcation Point, with MDM2 and PIN1 upregulated in AD, and BBC3 in GBM. Interpreted within the Hyper Solution Landscape (HSL) framework, these findings provide a biological explanation for the path-dependent nature of cell fate decisions and provide a mechanistic framework linking the PIN1-p53 axis to the inverse comorbidity between AD and cancer, suggesting that the PIN1-p53 axis acts as a critical decision node.

article.title: Nasal Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Respiratory and Allergic Biomarkers in Mexican American Young Adults
article.authors: Perez-Garcia, J.; Gunier, R. B.; Eskenazi, B.; Balmes, J.; Kogut, K.; Guo, W.; Rifas-Shiman, S. L.; Hivert, M.-F.; Oken, E.; Gold, D. R.; Holm, S.; Holland, N.; Cardenas, A.
article.abstract: Background: Mexican Americans have low asthma prevalence, but they experience a disproportionate clinical asthma burden. Nasal DNA methylation (DNAm) is a biomarker of airway diseases, but its relevance in young adult Mexican Americans and links to air pollution are underexplored. Objective: To identify nasal DNAm markers associated with asthma, allergic sensitization, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and lung function and evaluate associations with air pollution. Methods: We tested associations between nasal DNAm at 804,220 CpGs (EPICv2) and respiratory outcomes in 354 young adults from CHAMACOS (age 22) and evaluated replication in 540 adolescents from Project Viva (age 13). Epigenome-wide association studies were adjusted for confounders, and significance was declared at a false discovery rate (FDR)<0.05. Significant CpGs were evaluated for association with prenatal and past-year PM2.5 and O3 exposures, and with gene expression and genetic variation (in silico). We examined differentially methylated regions (DMRs), gene-set enrichments, and epigenetic aging. Results: We identified 49 CpGs associated with FeNO and 557 DMRs across multiple respiratory outcomes (FDR<0.05). Twenty-six CpGs and 103 DMRs associated with FeNO, asthma, and FEV1/FVC were replicated (e.g., LRRFIP1, PCSK6, EPX, IL13). Ten FeNO-related CpGs were associated with PM2.5 and/or O3 exposures (p<0.05) and 15 CpGs with nasal epithelial expression. We found enrichment for associations with respiratory/allergic biomarkers, obesity, smoking, longevity, asthma-related pathways (PI3K-AKT, TNF-, IL-2), inflammatory transcription factors, and candidate asthma drugs. FeNO was associated with greater epigenetic aging acceleration ({beta}=0.3, p=0.008). Conclusions: We identified nasal DNAm markers implicated in airway epithelial integrity and immune response predominantly associated with FeNO.

article.title: Nrf2 Activation Induces Fibroblast Senescence and Promotes Melanosome Accumulation in a Fibroblast-Keratinocyte Co-Culture Model.
article.authors: Yoon JH, Kil IS, Cho S, Park S, Kim HS, Kim JH, Cho JY.
article.abstract: Solar lentigo (SL) is an age-associated hyperpigmented skin disorder linked to oxidative stress, impaired autophagy, and cellular senescence. However, experimental systems that recapitulate the senescence-associated skin microenvironment remain limited. In this study, we investigated the role of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) in fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses using transcriptomic analyses and a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture model. Public transcriptomic datasets revealed increased NFE2L2 expression together with altered autophagy-related and senescence-associated signatures in hyperpigmented skin lesions. In dermal fibroblasts, Nrf2 overexpression induced senescence-associated phenotypes, including increased SA-β-gal activity and elevated expression of SASP-related genes. In a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture system, Nrf2-activated fibroblasts promoted melanosome accumulation in keratinocytes, suggesting that senescence-associated dermal-epidermal interactions contribute to pigmentation-related alterations. SENOMUNE, a formulation with autophagy-modulating activity, enhanced LC3 puncta formation in keratinocytes and attenuated melanosome accumulation in the senescence-associated co-culture system. Collectively, these findings suggest that sustained Nrf2 activation contributes to fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses and provide a useful co-culture platform for evaluating senescence-associated pigmentation modulators.

article.title: Association of dietary protein intake with accelerated biological aging markers and all-cause mortality in adults
article.authors: Reyes Barrera, J.; Bello-Chavolla, O. Y.; Fermin-Martinez, C. A.; Kammar Garcia, A.; Sanchez-Ortiz, N. A.; Reyes Reyes, R.; Garcia Arroyo, F. E.; Antonio Villa, N. E.
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aging processes could be influenced by diet. However, the extent to which dietary protein intake is associated with biological aging (BA) markers remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVES: Here, we evaluated the association between dietary protein intake and BA markers and explored the extent to which BA markers mediate the association between protein intake and all-cause mortality. METHODS: We analyzed data from NHANES cycles 1999-2000 and 2001-2002. Dietary protein intake was expressed in g/kg/day. BA was estimated with TL, AnthropoAge, PhenoAge, and the Klemera-Doubal Method (KDM). Accelerated aging was defined as TL 1.40 g/kg/day) had a lower adjusted likelihood of having accelerated aging by TL (OR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.22-0.73), PhenoAge (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.32-0.92), and KDM (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.32-0.87), compared with those in the lowest quintile (<=0.62 g/kg/day). Higher dietary protein intake was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality, and BA metrics partially mediated these associations. CONCLUSIONS: Higher dietary protein intake was associated with a lower likelihood of accelerated aging and reduced mortality, with the latter association partially mediated by BA markers. Our findings suggest that dietary protein intake could influence healthy aging. Keywords: Protein, Aging, Accelerated aging

article.title: Proteomic clocks reveal organ-specific signatures of aging in mice
article.authors: Lim, S.; Pickering, A. M.
article.abstract: Aging alters protein abundance throughout the body, but whether proteomic aging signatures are shared across organs, and how they are represented in RNA, remains unclear. Plasma proteomics does not measure protein abundance directly within individual organs. Here, we developed organ-specific proteomic aging clocks for eight mouse organs. The clocks retained age associations across independent cohorts but transferred poorly between organs of the same mice, indicating predominantly organ-specific aging signatures. This organ specificity extended to RNA. Applied to the transcriptomes of the genes encoding each clock's protein features, with protein-derived weights unchanged, the scores retained age associations in independent transcriptomic cohorts, with stronger associations in the corresponding organs. The strength of age associations across molecular layers also differed by organ: in paired analysis, protein scores tracked age more strongly than RNA scores in brain and skeletal muscle, with no statistically detectable difference in kidney, liver or lung, suggesting a greater post-transcriptional contribution to proteomic aging in brain and muscle. In spatial transcriptomes, protein-derived RNA scores rose with age within tissue niches, usually without detectable changes in relative niche abundance. In the brain, white matter and glia-enriched microdomains showed elevated proteomic scores compared to other regions since young age. Together, these findings support organ-specific regulation of proteomic aging and identify molecular remodeling within persistent tissue compartments.

article.title: ATPIF1-driven metabolic remodeling in osteoclasts promotes age-related cortical bone loss
article.authors: Kim H, Adam G, Chalke A, Warren A, Richardson K, Marques-Carvalho A, Carter M, Fan H, Zhou Y, Thostenson J, Alturkmani F, Stronach B, Stambough J, Ambrogini E, Jun S, Almeida M.
article.abstract: Abstract Age-related cortical bone loss is driven in part by increased osteoclast activity, but the mechanisms that sustain osteoclast function during skeletal aging remain poorly defined. Here, we show that aging remodels osteoclast metabolism, increasing glycolytic ATP production and reshaping metabolites linked to early tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle metabolism. Metabolomic profiling identified a glycolysis-coupled TCA node marked by increased isocitrate and -ketoglutarate in aged osteoclasts. These cells also exhibited prolonged survival and reduced activation of regulated cell-death pathways; in mice, this was accompanied by increased bone resorption, while human osteoclasts from aged donors similarly showed prolonged persistence. Mechanistically, ATPase inhibitory factor 1 (ATPIF1) was required for this aging-associated metabolic state. Osteoclast-lineage deletion of Atpif1 reduced IDH3A expression, -ketoglutarate accumulation, glycolytic ATP production, and resorptive function ex vivo, while attenuating age-related cortical bone loss and porosity in vivo. Pharmacologic perturbation of IDH3-linked metabolism similarly suppressed glycolytic ATP production and osteoclast activity and increased cortical bone mass in aged mice. Together, these findings identify glycolysis-centered metabolic rewiring as a mechanism that sustains osteoclast survival and resorption during skeletal aging and implicate an ATPIF1–IDH3A metabolic axis as a potential therapeutic target for age-associated osteoporosis.

article.title: The Aging Brain Matrix: Cross-Species Evidence Linking FREM3 to Brain and Cognitive Aging
article.authors: Clifford KP, Prevot TD, Sumitomo A, Das S, Bansal Y, Marcotte M, Zhou R, Yeung J, Ding M, Felsky D, Nieman BJ, Banasr M, Sibille E, Tomoda T, Nikolova YS.
article.abstract: Abstract The human extracellular-matrix-related FREM3 gene is strongly age-dependent, enriched in age-sensitive excitatory long-range-projecting neurons, and implicated in neurodegenerative diseases. To establish the first translationally relevant causal evidence for the gene’s roles in brain structure and cognition, we developed an excitatory-neuron-specific Frem3 conditional knockout mouse model ( Frem3 -cKO) and computed genetically regulated expression of FREM3 ( FREM3 -GReX) in humans, enabling convergent neurostructural and cognitive characterizations. Frem3 -cKO mice showed widespread lower global and regional brain volume in middle age vs young adulthood, consistent with drastic age-dependent volume loss absent in wildtype mice. These effects were strongest in cognitively relevant cortical regions and paralleled by lower cognitive performance. In humans, lower FREM3- GReX was associated with lower total surface area, which further mediated an indirect link to lower cognitive performance across multiple age-sensitive domains. We provide the first translationally relevant cross-species evidence supporting a key role for FREM3/Frem3 in maintaining brain and cognitive health across aging.

article.title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
article.authors: Zhang W, Zhang X, Zhang C, Shi X, Deng Y, Gao Y, Bi K, Wang Z, Chen G, Ye Z, An Z, Fu W.
article.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machine learning algorithms were applied to identify hub ageing-related genes (ARGs), with SHAP analysis interpreting feature importance. A nomogram model was constructed and validated across multiple cohorts. Immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics were used for mechanistic exploration. Three key ARGs (SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4) were identified and used to develop a diagnostic model with high accuracy (AUCs: 0.726-0.905). SOX4 promoted immune evasion, PRNP exhibited context-dependent duality, and FOXO4 functioned as a tumor suppressor. Spatial and single-cell analyses revealed cell-type-specific expression and fibroblast-epithelial communication via MIF, LRP1, and FZD1. Drug sensitivity profiling identified abiraterone and docetaxel as potential therapeutics for high- and low-risk patients, respectively. In conclusion, SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 are key biomarkers linking PCa, T2DM, and ageing, and the diagnostic model shows robust performance and clinical utility, providing insights into microenvironment-driven mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies for PCa patients with T2DM.

article.title: Mitochondrial genome editing reveals the impact of complex I heteroplasmic variants on human neurogenesis
article.authors: Tolle, I.; Fiorini, C.; Dobner, J.; Zink, A.; Pasti, A. P.; Balmaceda, V.; Tschuschke, F.; Herebian, D.; Mayatepek, E.; Bottani, E.; Lisowski, P.; Carelli, V.; Rossi, A.; Prigione, A.
article.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variants, whether maternally inherited or acquired somatically during aging, can be particularly detrimental to cells that rely on mitochondrial metabolism such as neurons. The functional consequences of mtDNA variants are thought to depend on their heteroplasmy, defined as the proportion of mtDNA molecules carrying that variant. However, investigating the specific effects of heteroplasmic mtDNA variants on human neuronal function has been challenging. Studies using patient-derived cells cannot conclusively attribute observed phenotypes to a single mtDNA variant, while conventional genome editing approaches are not applicable to mtDNA. Here, we use DddA-derived cytosine base editor (DdCBE) to introduce pathogenic heteroplasmic mtDNA variants into Neurogenin 2 (NGN2)-inducible human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). We focus on two variants in the genes MT-ND1 and MT-ND5 belonging to complex I (CI), the largest component of the mitochondrial respiratory chain and a frequent contributor to human disease, including the incurable neurodevelopmental disorder Leigh syndrome. mtDNA-edited iPSC lines exhibit low off-target editing and maintain similar heteroplasmy following subclonal isolation and differentiation into NGN2-induced neurons (iNs). Although the CI variants do not substantially affect mitochondrial energy metabolism in undifferentiated iPSCs, they reduce mitochondrial membrane potential in iNs where they drive a transcriptional reprogramming indicative of impaired neuronal commitment. These findings suggest that heteroplasmic CI variants are sufficient to disrupt neural fate specification even at relatively low heteroplasmy. More broadly, mtDNA editing in human iPSCs provides a powerful platform to investigate how mitochondrial fitness and heteroplasmy influence development and disease.

article.title: Novelty Processing in Aging: Absence of an Association with Episodic Memory Abilities
article.authors: Servais A, Bastin C.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: Conceptually, novelty processing and episodic memory are closely linked. Yet it remains unclear whether they rely on common or partly independent mechanisms. We investigated whether their relationship depends on the type of novelty and representational content in healthy older adults. Seventy-eight adults aged 61–84 years completed eye-tracking tasks assessing Absolute novelty (unknown stimuli) and Associative novelty (novel configurations of familiar elements) for objects and scenes, as well as a pupillometry task assessing responses to novel objects. Novelty-processing indices were correlated with performance across various episodic memory tasks using preregistered Bayesian correlations. Older adults showed reliable gaze preferences for both Absolute and Associative novelty in object and scene tasks. Contrary to our predictions, however, Absolute novelty preference was generally unrelated to performance on familiarity-based recognition and perceptual discrimination measures hypothesized to rely on the perirhinal cortex. Associative novelty preference was likewise largely unrelated to episodic memory performance, although a small number of unexpected associations with verbal recall emerged for object novelty. Novelty-related pupil responses also showed little evidence of associations with memory performance. Exploratory comparisons with data from younger adults aged 18-30 years (from Servais & Bastin, 2026) indicated largely comparable gaze-based novelty preferences across age groups, although novelty-related peak pupil dilation was reduced in older adults. Overall, these findings suggest that individual differences in novelty processing, when assessed in paradigms with no memory confound, are largely independent of episodic memory performance in healthy older adults and that gaze-based novelty processing may remain preserved with age for both novelty types.

article.title: Energetic metabolism in bipolar disorder: from markers to precision therapeutics.
article.authors: Magda Malewska-Kasprzak; Monika Dmitrzak-Weglarz; Filip Rybakowski
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder (BD) is marked by recurrent mood episodes and functional impairment. Growing evidence implicates mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic disturbances as important to its pathophysiology, affecting neuronal signalling, synaptic plasticity, and inflammatory pathways. AIMS: This review synthesises current evidence linking energetic metabolism to BD, integrates neuroimaging and peripheral biomarker findings, and discusses emerging therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial and metabolic dysfunction. METHODS: A systematic search following PRISMA guidelines was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane Library using 'bipolar disorder', 'energetic metabolism', and 'mitochondria'. Inclusion criteria comprised peer-reviewed human studies, original research, and meta-analyses; paediatric, non-English, dietary, genetic, or comorbidity-focused studies were excluded. Additional manual searches targeted biomarker-specific studies. RESULTS: Evidence consistently shows impaired oxidative phosphorylation, reduced ATP and phosphocreatine, altered NAD+/NADH ratios, and increased oxidative and inflammatory markers in BD. Neuroimaging demonstrates reduced PCr/ATP ratios, elevated lactate, and decreased TCA cycle intermediates, indicating cerebral energy deficits.
