article.authors: Ryoken Aoki; Nobuo Izumo; Megumi Furukawa; Rena Ikeda; Chisato Takiya; Ayaka Ito; Hideo Matsuzaki
article.abstract: Background/Objectives: Maternal nutritional status during pregnancy and lactation can influence metabolic and neurobehavioral development in offspring. However, the contribution of specific lipid alterations to these effects remains unclear. This study investigated whether maternal exposure to different high-fat diets produces distinct metabolic and neurobehavioral outcomes in offspring. Methods: Pregnant ICR mice were fed a control diet, a conventional high-fat diet (HFD), or a 50% choline-deficient, amino acid-defined high-fat diet (50% CDAHFD) from embryonic day 12 until weaning. Male offspring were assessed at 4–6 weeks of age for body weight, plasma lipid levels, behavioral phenotypes, prefrontal neurotransmitter release, and expression of genes related to serotonergic and dopaminergic signaling. A total of 31 dams and 196 offspring were used in the experiments and allocated to each experimental group. Results: Offspring in both HFD and 50% CDAHFD groups exhibited increased body weight and total cholesterol levels compared to controls, whereas plasma triglycerides were elevated a tendency in the 50% CDAHFD group. HFD offspring showed reduced spontaneous locomotor activity, and increased prefrontal serotonin release with altered serotonergic gene expression. Conversely, 50% CDAHFD offspring displayed increased exploratory behavior in the open field test alongside altered dopamine neuron-related genes, without locomotor or social deficits. Conclusions: Exposure of mothers to different high-fat diets has been suggested to cause specific changes in their offspring’s lipid profiles, which in turn modulate the serotonin and dopamine systems differently, leading to specific behavioral changes.

article.title: Palmitoylation Depth Determines Lipid-Phase Preference in Claudins
article.authors: Xuyang Qin; Shikha Nangia
article.abstract: Abstract S-palmitoylation is a reversible lipid modification that regulates membrane protein organization and function, but its molecular consequences remain incompletely understood. Claudins, the primary functional proteins of tight junctions, contain conserved palmitoylation sites on the cytosolic leaflet that influence tight junction assembly and barrier function. Using MARTINI coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we investigated how palmitoylation affects claudin-lipid interactions and membrane phase partitioning in four claudins (CLD3, CLD4, CLD9, and CLD14) in phase-separated bilayers. Palmitoylation enhances claudins’ affinity for ordered phases, promotes local cholesterol enrichment, and reduces disordered-lipid contacts. We find that the membrane-embedded depth of the palmitoyl chain is a key determinant of this preference: sites closer to the membrane interface stabilize claudins within ordered domains, while deeper sites favor disordered environments. This depth dependence arises from differential palmitoyl chain tilting, with upright packing at shallow sites and forced lateral tilting at deeper sites. These results identify palmitoylation depth as a structural determinant of claudin-lipid interactions and provide insight into how this reversible modification governs tight junction protein localization within heterogeneous membranes.

article.title: The lipid raft marker flotillin FloA drives relocalization of the plasma membrane H+-ATPase PmaA as a protective response to calcium stress
article.authors: Moemi Kawashima; Thomas Krüger; Maira Rosin; Sophie Tröger-Görler; Thorsten Heinekamp; Axel A. Brakhage
article.abstract: Biological membranes are laterally heterogeneous and contain specialized microdomains called lipid rafts. Lipid rafts serve as organizational platforms that cluster signaling molecules or modulate membrane protein conformation through their unique lipid environment. There are specific lipid raft marker proteins whose functions remain obscure. One of these proteins is flotillin which has been linked to endocytosis. Here, we investigated the regulation and function of FloA, the sole flotillin homolog in the model fungus Aspergillus nidulans . FloA expression is specifically upregulated in response to calcium stress, which is a regulatory pattern also conserved in Aspergillus fumigatus . BioID proximity labeling revealed that A. nidulans FloA physically interacts with proteins in the endocytic pathway as well as another lipid raft marker, the plasma membrane H + -ATPase PmaA. Under calcium stress, PmaA undergoes internalization from the cytoplasmic membrane. However, when floA is deleted, PmaA internalization is prevented, resulting in cell death. This phenotype of the Δ floA strain could be mimicked by treating the cells with an endocytosis inhibitor during calcium stress. Together, we demonstrate that FloA is essential for the internalization of PmaA during calcium stress, a process that prevents intracellular calcium overload and promotes cell viability. Our results also provide further evidence for flotillin-assisted endocytosis.

article.title: Comparison of 3 guideline lipid emulsion regimens for local anesthetic systemic toxicity: an in silico study of bolus duration, total dose, and treatment delay in intravenous bupivacaine overdose.
article.authors: Sunho Lim; Sooyoung Cho; Eunbi Cho
article.abstract: PURPOSE: Lipid emulsion is the only specific antidote for local anesthetic systemic toxicity, but no dose-finding study has been conducted. We compared 3 published regimens and alternative schedules that deliver the same dose in different ways using a human model of intravenous bupivacaine overdose. METHODS: A 14-compartment human bupivacaine model was independently reimplemented without fitted parameters, replacing first-order lipid elimination with a saturable term. Toxicity was modeled as 112.5 mg administered intravenously over 3 minutes. Benefit was defined as the predicted maximum decrease in myocardial bupivacaine within 30 minutes, and harm as the predicted relative lipid load, indexed by peak plasma triglyceride concentration. Neither measure is a validated surrogate. RESULTS: The 3 guidelines specify the same doses but different bolus durations: 1 minute versus 2-3 minutes. At a matched dose of 12 mL/kg, myocardial bupivacaine decreased by 30.5% with the 1-minute bolus and 24.9% with the 2.5-minute bolus, with the same lipid load. The completed American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine regimen (7.64 mL/kg) achieved a 24.6% decrease versus 24.9% with 12 mL/kg; thus, complete regimens differ in schedule as well as dose. Repeating the 1-minute bolus twice, for a total of 4.5 mL/kg, achieved a 31.9% decrease with 62% less emulsion. Start time had the greatest effect: the best regimen achieved a 41.8% decrease when started at the end of the injection, but only 9.6% when started at 10 minutes. CONCLUSION: In this bupivacaine model, bolus duration distinguished the regimens more than dose did, and delay had a greater effect than either, eliminating most of the benefit without changing the lipid load. Treatment should begin at the first signs of toxicity, and 20% lipid emulsion should be immediately available wherever local anesthetics are used.

article.title: Effect of Atorvastatin and Rosuvastatin on Lipid Parameters and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
article.authors: Aruba Sohail; Maman Khurshid; Aiman Khurshid; Muddassir Khalid; Areeba Raza; Mir Umer Farooq Alam Shah; Hira Khan
article.abstract: Statins produce marked reductions in total and LDL cholesterol, C-reactive protein (CRP), and help prevent stroke, re-infarction, and subsequent risk of death. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the role of atorvastatin in comparison with rosuvastatin in lowering levels of inflammatory biomarkers and lipid parameters in patients with ACS. Online databases were searched, and results from random-effects meta-analysis are presented as weighted mean differences (WMDs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. The outcomes were assessed at the short-term (≤1 month) and long-term (>3 months) follow-up. A total of 15 studies (13 RCTs and 2 observational studies) were included. The level of erythrocyte sedimentation rate ( P = 0.13), oxidized LDL ( P = 0.94), and long-term HDL-C ( P = 0.28) showed no significant difference between the two statin groups. No significant differences were observed between atorvastatin and rosuvastatin in total cholesterol and LDL-C at short-term or long-term follow-up. A significant decrease in CRP levels (WMD 4.08; 95% CI 1.53–6.63; P = 0.002; I 2 = 98%) and a significant rise in HDL-C (WMD −1.15; 95% CI −1.99 to −0.32; P = 0.007; I 2 = 39%) was reported in the rosuvastatin group compared to the atorvastatin group in the short-term. Atorvastatin was associated with a significant reduction in triglycerides at short-term follow-up (WMD −8.69; 95% CI −14.97 to −2.40; P = 0.007; I 2 = 35%), while the overall long-term comparison was borderline and did not reach conventional statistical significance. Our findings suggest that rosuvastatin may provide greater short-term reductions in CRP and modest increases in HDL-C compared with atorvastatin; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity and the absence of significant differences at longer follow-up.

article.title: Total salvianolic acids protect APP/PS1 mice from Alzheimer's disease by attenuating neuroinflammation through hippocampal lipid regulation
article.authors: Peihua Hu; Mingming Zhang; Xuemeng Wei; Shiyu Xiao; Bin Li; Kun Liu; Guo Su; Bing Han; Xiaoqian Shi; Congzhen Wei; Jingna Sun; Zheng Zhang; Zhengang Han; Li Shen
article.abstract: Background Total salvianolic acids (TSA) have been shown to exert neuroprotective effects in cognition-associated behavioral tests in APP/PS1 mice in our previous research; however, research on TSA-mediated modulation of hippocampal lipid metabolism remains limited. Objective This study elucidated the therapeutic mechanisms underlying prophylactic TSA administration by integrating lipidomic profiling and demonstrating TSA-induced neuroprotection through suppression of hippocampal neuroinflammation in APP/PS1 mice. Methods Ten 3.5-month-old APP/PS1 mice and ten age-matched wild-type mice received intraperitoneal saline injections as the disease model and healthy control groups. Another twenty APP/PS1 mice were allocated to two TSA treatment groups (30 mg/kg/day and 60 mg/kg/day). After fifteen weeks of intervention, memory performance was assessed using the Y-maze test. Hippocampal Aβ, IBA1, and GFAP protein expression levels were quantified by western blotting. Targeted UHPLC-MS/MS was used for quantitative detection of hippocampal lipid biomarkers. Results The 60 mg/kg TSA group exhibited improved memory in Y-maze tests, with elevated spontaneous alternation rate ( p p p p p p Conclusions This study reveals TSA's preventive potential against Alzheimer's disease by modulating inflammation-associated lipid metabolism in APP/PS1 mice.

article.title: Single-domain antibody-conjugated lipid nanoparticles for selective mRNA delivery to CD4⁺ T cells and Brec1-mediated excision of HIV-1 proviral DNA
article.authors: Melanie Wittner; Philip Hartjen; Oliver Keil; Volker Fehring; Leonidas Gkionis; Charlotte Maeve Dunne; Philipp D. Kaiser; Ulrich Rothbauer; Joachim Hauber; Jan Chemnitz; Niklas Beschorner; Julian Schulze zur Wiesch
article.abstract: Abstract Approaches to curing HIV infection aim to eliminate the latent viral reservoir — long-lived, resting CD4⁺ T cells harboring integrated but transcriptionally silent proviral DNA — which persists despite effective antiretroviral therapy. The HIV-1 LTR-specific designer-recombinase Brec1 can precisely excise integrated proviral DNA from infected cells. However, targeted delivery of therapeutic payloads to HIV reservoir-bearing CD4⁺ T cells remains a major challenge. Here, we present a proof-of-concept study of a modular platform combining CD4-specific single-domain antibody (sdAb)-conjugated lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with Brec1 mRNA for targeted delivery to CD4⁺ T cells. In primary human PBMCs, sdAb-LNPs achieved 44% transfection efficiency in CD4⁺ T cells with pronounced specificity over CD8⁺ T cells (4:1 ratio) and B cells (9:1 ratio), without compromising cell viability. Brec1 recombinase activity was validated across three reporter cell systems of increasing complexity, confirming efficient translation of delivered Brec1 mRNA into a functional recombinase capable of precise, error-free loxBTR-mediated proviral excision. These findings provide proof of concept for sdAb-LNP-mediated Brec1 mRNA delivery as a candidate strategy for HIV reservoir reduction, with the modular platform design enabling flexible adaptation to other cell-specific therapeutic applications.

article.title: Matrix Stiffness Controls Lipid Homeostasis in Human Corneal Endothelial Cells via a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ Mechanotransduction Axis
article.authors: Mingyue Zhong; Tingjun Fan; Jun Zhao
article.abstract: Abstract Substrate stiffness is a critical mechanical cue that regulates cellular behaviors, yet its role in governing lipid homeostasis of human corneal endothelial cells (HCECs) remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a polyacrylamide hydrogel platform with tunable stiffnesses (25, 50, and 100 kPa) covering the pathophysiological range of Descemet’s membrane to investigate stiffness-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming in HCECs. All hydrogels exhibited excellent transparency (>95%) and good biocompatibility. We found that soft substrates (25 kPa) promoted substantial accumulation of neutral lipids and free cholesterol in HCECs. Mechanistically, soft substrates upregulated SREBP1 and its target genes to enhance fatty acid synthesis while suppressing CPT1-mediated fatty acid oxidation, and simultaneously upregulated LDLR and SREBP2 to promote cholesterol uptake and synthesis while downregulating the LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis to impair cholesterol efflux. Notably, PPARγ emerged as a key regulator of stiffness-dependent lipid homeostasis; its expression was positively correlated with substrate stiffness, and pharmacological activation of PPARγ reversed soft substrate-induced lipid accumulation. Furthermore, the Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR signaling axis was identified as an upstream mechanotransduction pathway mediating stiffness-regulated PPARγ expression. Analysis of transcriptomic datasets from Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) patients revealed dysregulation of lipid metabolism genes consistent with our findings. Together, these results demonstrate that substrate stiffness governs HCEC lipid homeostasis through a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ mechanotransduction cascade, and that matrix softening promotes abnormal lipid accumulation by reprogramming fatty acid and cholesterol metabolic networks. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between the mechanical microenvironment and lipid metabolism in corneal endothelial cells, providing insights into FECD pathogenesis and a theoretical framework for designing stiffness-tuned biomaterials for corneal endothelial regeneration.

article.title: Purpurin Alleviates Chemotherapy‐Induced Thrombocytopenia Through Estrogen Receptor α Dependent Phosphoinositide 3‐Kinase/Protein Kinase B Signalling
article.authors: Xiaolin Gan; Xinle Wang; Lu Hao; Xiaoqin Tang; Zhixuan Liu; Long Wang; Xiang Xie; Xiang Li; Chunling Zhao; Yan Li; Xinwu Huang; Yuanzhi Liu; Jianming Wu
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemotherapy‐induced thrombocytopenia (CIT) increases bleeding risk and compromises chemotherapy delivery. Purpurin, a hydroxyanthraquinone found in Rubia cordifolia L., has not been examined as a regulator of megakaryopoiesis. We investigated whether purpurin restores platelet production after cyclophosphamide (CTX) exposure and examined the involvement of estrogen receptor α (ESR1)–phosphoinositide 3‐kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signalling. Purpurin was evaluated in K562 and Meg‐01 megakaryocytic differentiation models, Tg(itga2b:eGFP) zebrafish, and CTX‐induced thrombocytopenic mice. Megakaryocyte (MK) differentiation, DNA ploidy, cytoskeletal remodelling, platelet recovery, and haemostatic function were assessed. Computational target prediction was used for hypothesis generation, followed by drug affinity responsive target stability analysis and pharmacological inhibition of ESR1 and PI3K. At concentrations that did not cause detectable cytotoxicity (2.5–10 μM), purpurin increased CD41 + CD42b + cells, MK ploidy, F‐actin remodelling, and expression of NF‐E2, GATA1, RUNX1, and FOSB. Purpurin increased thrombocyte abundance in zebrafish and restored platelet counts, MK maturation, and haemostatic function in CTX‐treated mice. Purpurin increased the resistance of ESR1 to proteolysis in the drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assay. Pharmacological inhibition of ESR1 or PI3K attenuated purpurin‐induced differentiation and PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. These findings support the involvement of ESR1‐associated PI3K/AKT signalling through which purpurin promotes megakaryopoiesis and platelet recovery. Purpurin warrants further evaluation as a natural‐product lead for CIT, including genetic target validation, pharmacokinetic characterization, and assessment in tumour‐bearing models.

article.title: In-vitro exposure to mercury chloride, with and without n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, on the Th17-associated immune response in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from systemic lupus erythematosus patients.
article.authors: Cealan O Henry; Emeir M McSorley; David J Armstrong; J J Strain; Philip J Allsopp
article.abstract: TH17 cytokines are implicated in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. Mercury is an environmental factor associated with the exacerbation of SLE pathology, potentially by regulating the ThH17 pathway. Humans are primarily exposed to mercury from dental amalgams and fish consumption. Fish are also a rich source of the n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and have been shown to reduce SLE disease symptoms. This pilot in-vitro investigation isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from SLE patients (N = 15) and healthy controls (HC, N = 15). The cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and exposed to 200 nM of mercury (II) chloride (HgCl) for 24 hr, with or without pre-exposure (24 hr) to either EPA or DHA at 100 μM each. The TH17-associated cytokines were quantified in the PBMC supernatants. Pre-exposure to EPA resulted in significantly lower concentrations of IL-27 in supernatants of LPS-HgCl treated PBMC from SLE patients (29.58 [± 22.62] pg/mL) compared to HCs (51.63 [± 42.96] pg/mL) (p = 0.04). While DHA-LPS-HgCl had significantly lower IL-27 concentrations compared in LPS-HgCl in PBMC from SLE patients and HCs, there was no significant difference between groups. IL-27 exhibits pro/anti-inflammatory effects on the immune system. We suggest that the observed reductions in IL-27 concentrations following EPA-LPS-HgCl treatment support the protective role of n-3 PUFA in autoimmune responses.

article.title: Efficient Extraction and Recovery of Astaxanthin from Bacterial Sources Using Fatty Acids
article.authors: Vittoria Sapone; Mina Soleimani Hassanabadi; Eryka Mrotek; Marco Bravi
article.abstract: Abstract Natural astaxanthin is heavily preferred over synthetic alternatives for both food and pharmaceutical applications due to its superior bioactivity. However, conventional recovery methods rely on toxic volatile organic solvents (VOCs) and energy-intensive thermal distillation. This study presents an integrated, nonthermal biorefining strategy for Paracoccus carotinifaciens using short- and medium-chain food-grade fatty acids. The proposed “one-pot” process utilizes the pH-controlled dissociation of these solvents to simultaneously extract and recover the ketocarotenoids in a single vessel. Propanoic acid achieved the highest relative initial extraction efficiency (∼100%), outperforming acetic (88%) and butanoic (83%) acids. Subsequent alkaline phase-shifting triggered a thermodynamic “dissolution-to-precipitation” switch, yielding quantitative recovery (>98%) of carotenoids from propanoic, butanoic, and hexanoic acid solutions. High-performance liquid chromatography suggested the preliminary structural preservation of a highly enriched fraction of astaxanthin, adonirubin, and canthaxanthin relative to the starting bacterial biomass. Furthermore, a conceptual proof of principle of solvent recovery was demonstrated with hexanoic acid, achieving 80% bulk solvent recovery strictly via phase separation. This methodology completely eliminates VOCs and inherently bypasses thermal degradation, offering a highly sustainable, scalable route for industrial microbial pigment production.

article.title: Structural Determinants Underlying the Interplay Between Fatty Acid Binding and S-Nitrosylation of Human Serum Albumin
article.authors: Anastasia A. Batalova; Kamila V. Samodurova; Mikhail A. Vovk; Daria A. Belinskaia; Richard O. Jenkins; Nikolay V. Goncharov
article.abstract: Human serum albumin (HSA) is a multifunctional protein whose biological properties are determined not only by its amino acid sequence but also by a complex interplay of functional sites, post-translational modifications, and endogenous ligands. However, the structural mechanisms by which these regulatory factors influence the functional state of HSA remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the structural basis of the interplay between HSA functional regions, using Cys34 S-nitrosylation and fatty acid (FA) binding as model regulatory processes. For this purpose, the structural features and conformational dynamics of FA-free and FA-loaded native and nitrosylated HSA, as well as their interactions with glutathione (GSH) and S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO), were studied using molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Changes in the overall structure of HSA after incubation with GSNO were assessed by 1H NMR spectroscopy. MD analysis revealed that FA binding alters the conformational dynamics of HSA and affects the structural environment of Cys34 and other functionally significant regions. These FA-induced effects were further modulated by S-nitrosylation, which influenced the conformational landscape of albumin in a manner dependent on its fatty acid-bound state. The similarity of the one-dimensional 1H NMR spectra of HSA before and after incubation with GSNO suggests the absence of pronounced changes in the overall protein structure upon interaction with the nitrosylating agent. The obtained data provide insights into how FA binding and S-nitrosylation shape the conformational properties of HSA through modulation of the structural environment of Cys34 and other functionally significant regions. The results highlight the importance of considering post-translational modifications and endogenous ligands as key determinants of HSA structure–function relationships.

article.title: Omega-3 fatty acids in aromatase inhibitor-associated dyslipidemia: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and future perspectives
article.authors: Ruiqi Chen; Minghao Xiong; Shengchao Huang
article.abstract: Aromatase inhibitors (AIs), including anastrozole, letrozole, and exemestane, are widely used as adjuvant endocrine therapy for postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. However, prolonged estrogen deprivation induced by AI therapy may adversely affect lipid homeostasis and has been associated with alterations in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), potentially contributing to long-term cardiovascular risk. The mechanisms underlying these abnormalities appear to involve estrogen-dependent regulation of hepatic lipoprotein metabolism, together with endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), have established effects on lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health. Their metabolic actions include activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-α (PPAR-α), suppression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein-1c (SREBP-1c), modulation of hepatic very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) production, enhancement of fatty acid oxidation, and regulation of lipoprotein clearance. However, the effects of EPA and DHA on LDL-C, TC, and HDL-C are less consistent than their triglyceride-lowering effects and may differ according to formulation and dose. In this review, we critically examine the biological mechanisms underlying AI-associated dyslipidemia, compare the lipid effects of individual AIs with tamoxifen, and evaluate the potential mechanisms through which EPA and DHA may modulate cholesterol and lipoprotein metabolism. We further summarize clinical evidence from general dyslipidemia and breast cancer populations and assess its applicability to patients receiving AI therapy. Current evidence supports a strong biological rationale for omega-3 fatty acid supplementation but remains insufficient to establish its efficacy specifically for AI-associated dyslipidemia. Future randomized controlled trials should directly evaluate lipid and cardiovascular outcomes, compare EPA- and DHA-containing formulations, account for differences among individual AIs, and identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit from omega-3-based interventions.

article.title: Roasting‐Induced Changes in the Chemical Composition, Fatty Acid Profile, and Bioactive Properties of Kaluteh Date Pits
article.authors: Sedighe Moghbeli; Fatemeh Heidari‐Dalfard; Elham Assadpour; Mohammad Mahdi Shojaa‐Fard; Seid Mahdi Jafari
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Date pits (DPs), accounting for approximately 10% of the total fruit weight, are a major by‐product of the date processing industry and are generated in large quantities as waste. By containing valuable nutritional and bioactive compounds, DPs have considerable potential for utilization as functional ingredients in food applications. The present study aimed to investigate the chemical composition, fatty acid (FA) profile, and total phenolic content (TPC) of Kaluteh DPs, as well as to evaluate the effects of roasting and extraction conditions on their bioactive properties. Raw DPs contained approximately 74.92% carbohydrates, 9.30% fat, 8.45% moisture, and 6.21% protein. FA analysis revealed that lauric acid was the predominant saturated FA, whereas oleic acid was the major unsaturated FA. Response surface methodology indicated that increasing extraction temperature, extraction time, and solvent‐to‐solid ratio (SS R ) enhanced both TPC and antioxidant activity. The optimum conditions for maximizing TPC were 63°C, 2.03 h, and a SS R = 0.017 g/mL, whereas the highest antioxidant activity was achieved at 51°C, 3 h, and a SS R = 0.016 g/mL. Under these optimized conditions, roasted DP extracts had a TPC = 14.8 mg GAE/g and a DPPH radical scavenging of 98.53%. Roasting also reduced moisture content to 4.05% and induced changes in FA composition, with oleic and lauric acids remaining the predominant FAs in roasted samples. Overall, roasting and extraction optimization significantly improved the bioactive characteristics and nutritional value of Kaluteh DPs, highlighting their potential as a natural source of antioxidants and functional ingredients for food applications.

article.title: Fatty Acid Variation in Macadamia Kernels: Association of Palmitoleic Acid with Fruit Traits and Selection of Multi-Attribute Germplasm
article.authors: Yang Li; Fan Yang; Nanhua Zi; Tingyu Li; Jing Ma; Lidan Gong; Ziqiang Li; Chao Wu; Jianjian Geng; Qingyi Long; Liang Tao
article.abstract: Palmitoleic acid (C16:1) is rare among woody oil crops yet accumulates to high levels in macadamia kernels, where its inter-accession variation and relationship with fruit traits remain poorly characterized. We profiled 22 fatty acids by GC-MS, quantified crude fat, crude protein and total soluble sugar by NIRS, and measured nine fruit traits in 139 accessions. The major fatty acids ranked as C18:1 > C16:1 > C16:0. C16:1 varied widely among accessions (mean 10.66%, CV = 27.7%, range 2.78–19.05%), about 12-fold the analytical RSD, whereas C18:1 was stable (CV = 5.3%). C16:1 was strongly negatively correlated with C18:1 (r = −0.921, p

article.title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids as Modulators of the Gut–Immune Axis in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Linking Metabolism, Immune Regulation, and Epithelial Barrier Function
article.authors: Dominika Piątek; Aneta Sokal-Dembowska; Małgorzata Strycharz-Dudziak; Sara Jarmakiewicz-Czaja
article.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), which include Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), are chronic conditions associated with abnormalities in the immune response, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and disruption of the intestinal barrier homeostasis. A growing body of evidence suggests that the gut–immune axis plays a key role in the pathogenesis of IBD, and that metabolites of microbial origin influence the regulation of the immune response and the maintenance of intestinal barrier integrity. Particular importance is attributed to short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), such as acetate, propionate, and butyrate. The aim of this review is to present the current knowledge regarding the role of SCFAs as modulators of the gut–immune axis in IBD, with particular emphasis on their mechanisms of action and therapeutic potential. Physiologically, SCFAs are produced through the fermentation of dietary fiber by the gut microbiota. However, in IBD, the composition of the gut microbiota is often disrupted. SCFAs influence the expression of inflammatory genes and regulate the function of immune cells. Furthermore, butyrate in particular strengthens the integrity of the intestinal barrier by improving the function of tight junctions (TJs), increasing mucus production, and supporting epithelial regeneration. SCFAs represent an important link between diet, the gut microbiota, and immunity. Strategies to increase their availability may represent a promising approach to supporting IBD treatment, but they require further evaluation in well-designed clinical trials involving humans.

article.title: Electrochemical Features and Mechanism of Steel Corrosion Inhibition by Inhibitors Derived from Beef Tallow Fatty Acids
article.authors: Oleksandr Romanchuk; Petro Topilnytskyy; Viktoria Romanchuk
article.abstract: Ensuring the long-term operation of structural materials in heterophase oil and gas environments requires the development of effective, environmentally safe methods of anti-corrosion protection. The work aims to study the anti-corrosion efficiency and electrochemical behavior of new modified inhibitors based on higher distilled fatty acids derived from beef fat (MSEA, DSEA, DHEA) under conditions of iron acid corrosion. The objectives of the study included determining the kinetic parameters of the corrosion process and establishing the mechanism of the synthesized compounds' action at a concentration of 50 ppm using the potentiodynamic polarization method. Electrochemical measurements were performed in triplicate in a model corrosive environment of 0.1M HCl + butan-1-ol with subsequent calculation of standard deviations for the obtained values. The results of polarization studies showed a significant decrease in the corrosion current density for all modifications. The highest protective ability was observed for the DHEA compound. The positive direction of the potential shift and the nature of the change in the Tafel slopes indicate that within the general mixed mechanism of adsorption of compounds, there is a predominant kinetic inhibition of the anodic dissolution of the metal. The results obtained are consistent with previous gravimetric data and confirm the promising application of the synthesized alkanolamides for the protection of equipment in acidic environments.

article.title: Phenazine-1-Carboxylic Acid Inhibits Ferroptosis by Stabilizing EHMT2.
article.authors: Xue Sun; Yang Chen; Chaoyi Xia; Chong Wei; Junyi Shao; Dingyao Wang; Zixuan Fan; Jingshu Min; Caiyun Fu; Xi Wang
article.venue: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
article.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron‐dependent lipid peroxidation and implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases. Identifying ferroptosis inhibitors may therefore provide therapeutic opportunities for these disorders. Here, we identified phenazine‐1‐carboxylic acid (PCA) as a potent ferroptosis inhibitor through high‐throughput screening. Mechanistically, PCA reduced the accumulation of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid ROS in part by stabilizing the protein level of euchromatic histone‐lysine N‐methyltransferase 2 (EHMT2). PCA also markedly alleviated cisplatin‐induced acute kidney injury (AKI) in mice. These findings identify a previously unrecognized ferroptosis‐suppressive function of PCA and support its further evaluation as a lead compound for ferroptosis‐associated diseases.

article.title: Physicochemical and fatty acid composition of spring canola seeds after treatment with biostimulants
article.authors: Silviya Ivanova; Iliyana Petrova; Milena Pavlova; Svetlana Stoyanova; Ralitsa Mincheva
article.abstract: This study evaluates the effects of foliar application of newly developed natural biostimulants on the physicochemical composition and fatty acid profile of seeds of spring oilseed rape (Brassica napus oleifera annua), hybrid “Lakritz”, grown under organic cultivation. During 2 consecutive harvest years, in precise field trials conducted accordingly randomized block design at the Institute of Agriculture and Seed Science “Obraztsov Chiflik” – Ruse, the influence of 3 biostimulants with different characteristics applied in 2 doses was tested. Biostimulants were developed at the Institute of Cryobiology and Food Technologies – Sofia, based on vermicompost extract (HA), chitosan (Cs) and a humic complex containing a naturally identical growth regulator of auxin-type (HAR). It has been established that the application of biostimulants in critical phenological phases leads to an increase in the content of crude proteins and crude fibers in the seeds. Treatment with Cs reduces the content of crude fats compared to the control group, while the influence of the humic extract and the humic complex was less pronounced in the first year. Crude fats increase in the second year of treatment when using the preparations HA 600, HAR 300 and HAR 600. The studied biostimulants improved the fatty acid composition of rapeseed seeds by reducing the total content of undesirable saturated fatty acids (Cs 300, Cs 600, HAR 300, and HAR 600) and erucic acid (Cs 600 and HAR 600), while increasing desirable polyunsaturated fatty acids, thereby enhancing the health properties of rapeseed oil.

article.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered short-chain fatty acid biosynthetic pathways in Chinese children with obesity and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
article.authors: Xin Yuan; Ying Zhang; Xiangquan Lin; Ruimin Chen
article.abstract: Background Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), recently reclassified as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), is the most prevalent chronic liver disease in children, affecting 13% of the general pediatric population and up to 47% of children with obesity worldwide. Gut microbiota dysbiosis contributes to NAFLD pathogenesis through the gut-liver axis, yet the interplay between microbial communities and host metabolic regulators, particularly angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4), remains incompletely characterized. Methods Eighty-nine Chinese children aged 5–15 years were enrolled, including 29 healthy controls (Con), 39 with simple obesity (OB), and 21 with obesity and NAFLD. Gut microbiota was profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3–V4 region) and analyzed using QIIME2 and MicrobiomeAnalyst. Functional prediction employed PICRUSt2 referencing MetaCyc pathways. Serum ANGPTL4, leptin, adiponectin, and interleukin-6 were measured. Results Chao1 species richness differed significantly among groups (F = 4.98, p = 0.009), while Shannon diversity did not (F = 2.22, p = 0.115). Beta diversity (PERMANOVA, F = 2.87, R 2 = 0.063, p = 0.002) differed significantly among groups, although PERMDISP indicated heterogeneous dispersion (F = 6.62, p = 0.002). LEfSe analysis identified enrichment of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing genera (Bacteroides, Alistipes, Oscillospira, Parabacteroides) in healthy controls, while Megamonas, Blautia, Coprococcus, and Dorea characterized the NAFLD group. ANCOM-BC2 identified significant enrichment of Megamonas in the NAFLD group (q = 0.005 vs Con). PICRUSt2 predicted lower abundance of nine SCFA-related pathways in the obesity groups compared with controls. After FDR correction, Bacteroides-ANGPTL4 was the most significant correlation (r = 0.460, q < 0.001), and four additional associations survived correction. In hierarchical regression, Bacteroides remained independently associated with ANGPTL4 after adjustment for age, BMI, sex, and Tanner stage (β = 0.254, p = 0.016, ΔR 2 = 0.057), although this association was attenuated after additional adjustment for group status (β = 0.204, p = 0.058). Conclusion Chinese children with obesity and NAFLD exhibit gut microbial dysbiosis characterized by reduced species richness, depletion of SCFA-producing genera, and lower predicted abundance of SCFA-related pathways. The independent association between Bacteroides and ANGPTL4 suggests a potential microbiota-host metabolic link that may be associated with hepatic lipid metabolism.

article.title: Calorie restriction uncouples mutation rate from lifespan
article.authors: Björn Schumacher
article.abstract: In this issue of Cell, Grońska-Pęski et al. examine how calorie restriction (CR) affects DNA mutation rates. While CR lowers the accumulation of mutations, this effect does not scale with the degree of lifespan extension. Their work raises important new questions about how CR impacts the causal mechanisms of aging.

article.title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling
article.authors: sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Ariel L Raybuck); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Chloe Park); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Christopher D Scharer); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Denis Mogilenko); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Jeffrey C Rathmell); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Jennie Hamilton); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Jingxin Li); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (John Karijolich); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Juyeon Lim); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Karel Kalecky); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Kaylor Meyer); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Mark R Boothby); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Sakeenah L Hicks); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Shawna K Brookens); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Sung Hoon Cho); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Teodoro H Bottiglieri); sung.hoon.cho@emory.edu (Yeeun Paik)
article.abstract: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis – a major metabolic use of this amino acid – was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Gls , the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into mouse B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired. Otherwise, it was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, that is, the conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival, involved supporting progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

article.title: Hormonal and metabolic adaptations in Omega-3-supplemented rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle.
article.authors: Alda Quattrone; Nour Elhouda Fehri; Olimpia Barbato; Giovanni Ricci; Daniele Vigo; Luigj Turmalaj; Majlind Sulçe; Marta Castrica; Maria Laura Marongiu; Alessandro Dal Bosco; Bayrem Jemmali; Gerald Muça; Gabriele Brecchia; Giulio Curone; Laura Menchetti
article.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) supplementation on endocrine and metabolic profiles of forty-five nulliparous rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle. Animals were randomly assigned to one of three diets: control (CNT), 5% extruded linseed (L), and 5% extruded linseed plus 0.2% Padina pavonica extract (LPP). Blood was sampled at baseline, artificial insemination, parturition, mid-lactation, and weaning, to determine the concentrations of cortisol, insulin, leptin, thyroid hormones (T3, T4), glucose, and non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA). Reproductive stage significantly influenced endocrine and metabolic dynamics, with cortisol and NEFA peaking at parturition (p < 0.001). Supplemented groups, particularly LPP, showed higher T3 concentrations (p < 0.05) and T3/T4 ratios (p < 0.01). The L diet maintained higher insulin during lactation (p < 0.05), while LPP lowered leptin at parturition (p < 0.01) and NEFA at insemination (p < 0.01), indicating an early decrease in lipid mobilization. Multivariate analysis suggested that n-3 PUFA supplementation promoted an endocrine profile characterized by enhanced thyroid activity and reduced lipid mobilization, consistent with a potentially favorable metabolic shift. In conclusion, enriching diets with n-3 PUFA, especially linseed combined with Padina pavonica extract, represents a promising nutritional strategy to support rabbit does during the highly demanding phases of their first reproductive cycle.

article.title: ω-3 PUFAs inhibited necroptosis of mesangial cells in a mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus.
article.authors: Yu Liu; Tingting Jiang; Yiming Yuan; Lingying Niu; Genhong Yao; Lingyun Sun
article.abstract: In this study, we aimed to investigate the effects of ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFAs) on necroptosis of mesangial cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). 16-week-old female MRL/lpr mice were used as an animal model of SLE and were randomly divided into three groups: control group, necroptosis inhibitor treatment group, and ω-3 PUFAs treatment group. The mice were administered ω-3 PUFAs or the same volume of normal saline by oral gavage every other day for 4 weeks. Mice in the necroptosis inhibitor treatment group were administered Nec-1 (a necroptosis inhibitor) via intraperitoneal injection once daily for 3 weeks. After treatment, spleens and perirenal lymph nodes were harvested and weighed. Serum anti-dsDNA levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and urinary protein levels were quantified. Renal pathology was evaluated using H&E and PAS staining. Renal IgG and C3 deposition was detected by immunofluorescence staining. Necroptosis-associated proteins were determined by immunofluorescence and Western blotting. Mesangial cells were treated with TNF-α, SM164, and Z-VAD-FMK to induce necroptosis and then supplemented with ω-3 PUFAs or Nec-1, respectively. The necroptosis of mesangial cells was assessed by Western blot, immunofluorescence staining, and flow cytometry. The inflammatory cytokines of mesangial cells were measured by RT-qPCR. ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids significantly ameliorated SLE-like symptoms in MRL/lpr mice, including attenuating splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy, alleviating renal pathology and lymphocyte infiltration, and decreasing renal immune complex deposition. Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and urinary protein levels were significantly down-regulated. Furthermore, ω-3 PUFAs treatment decreased inflammatory cytokines and inhibited necroptosis of mesangial cells in the kidneys of MRL/lpr mice. In vitro experiments demonstrated that ω-3 PUFAs inhibited necroptosis and reduced the release of inflammatory cytokines in mesangial cells. The results demonstrated that ω-3 PUFAs ameliorated the symptoms and attenuated necroptosis in renal mesangial cells in SLE mice. These findings suggest that ω-3 PUFAs might represent a novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of SLE.

article.title: A symbiogenic merger enabled by oxygen initiated the evolution of eukaryotes.
article.authors: Dave Speijer
article.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
article.abstract: Recently, extensive genetic information about archaeal hosts at the basis of eukaryogenesis has come to light. Characterization of these first eukaryotic common ancestor (FECA) related organisms allows improved understanding of the enigmatic FECA to last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) transition. However, these gene-centered discoveries have the unfortunate side effect of entrenching erroneous ideas about early eukaryotic evolution. This is apparent in the two-Domain vision of life, with eukaryotes seen as specialized Asgard archaea, while underestimating the contribution of the endosymbiont to eukaryogenesis. Establishment of the alpha-proteobacterium as the future mitochondrion is treated as one of many such endosymbiotic occurrences, ignoring its unique evolutionary position. I will marshal evidence for symbiogenic mechanisms involved in the FECA to LECA transition, with a key role for the endosymbiont's electron transport chain and its acceptor molecular oxygen, especially in the incarnation of reactive oxygen species occurring in the host cytoplasm. We should overcome overestimating gene determinism, while not sufficiently allowing for effects of biological hierarchies, emergent properties, and chance. Many eukaryotic properties are best understood by envisaging the crucial uptake of the future mitochondrion as a merger instead of an acquisition. This merger is characterized by a new kind of elaborate cellular entity emerging as a result of rapid coevolution, replacing a scenario in which already complex pre-eukaryotes acquired endosymbionts, accompanied by important, but limited, changes. Successful mergers are rare because they are intrinsically more difficult, but synergistically open up completely new areas of possibilities, as illustrated by incredible eukaryotic success.

article.title: Liver Viscosity Dominates Liver Stiffness in MASLD: A Multiparametric Ultrasound Study With IPTW Adjustment and Explainable Machine Learning.
article.authors: Si-Rui Wang; Wan-Wan Wen; Zhao-Sen Meng; Rui-Fang Guo; Jun-Feng Zhao; Xiang-Dong Hu
article.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Liver stiffness measured by shear wave elastography (SWE) is widely used as a noninvasive surrogate for fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, stiffness may be influenced by multiple biomechanical factors beyond fibrosis, and the relative contributions of inflammation-related viscosity, steatosis, and metabolic parameters remain unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 573 adults with MASLD underwent multiparametric ultrasound, including SWE, viscosity plane-wave ultrasound (ViPLUS), and attenuation (ATT). Participants were stratified into lower-body mass index (BMI) (BMI < 24 kg/m²) and higher-BMI (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²) groups. Covariate balance was achieved using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Multivariable linear regression, subgroup analyses, and interaction testing were performed to identify independent determinants of liver stiffness. Machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting [XGBoost]) with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for exploratory feature attribution to identify key determinants of liver stiffness rather than to develop a standalone clinical diagnostic or prediction tool. RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, prespecified clinical covariates were well balanced between BMI groups. Hepatic viscosity (ViPLUS) was the strongest independent determinant of liver stiffness (β = 5.80, 95% confidence interval: 5.33-6.27; p < 0.001), corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE per 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS. The association remained dominant in both BMI groups and was greater in the higher-BMI group (approximately 0.63 vs. 0.51 kPa per 0.1 Pa·s). The contribution of viscosity was consistently dominant across lower-BMI and higher-BMI subgroups and appeared stronger in the higher-BMI group. SHAP-based feature attribution identified ViPLUS as the most influential model-derived feature associated with SWE, consistent with the regression findings. Nonlinear associations were observed for aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, while triglycerides and glucose showed no significant nonlinear relationships. Notably, a subset of lower-BMI individuals exhibited high-risk hepatic phenotypes despite lower BMI. CONCLUSION: Hepatic viscosity is the dominant determinant of liver stiffness in MASLD, with even a 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE. These findings suggest that liver stiffness reflects viscosity-related viscoelastic alterations rather than fibrosis alone. Multiparametric ultrasound, particularly the integration of viscosity and stiffness, may provide incremental value for identifying high-risk individuals, including those with lower BMI.

article.title: Maternal age modulates progeny social behavior via a small RNA-neuropeptide axis.
article.authors: Hyeonjeong Hwang; YongJin Cheon; Seung Hee Oh; Sujin Jo; Taehyun A Kim; Eujeong Oh; Semin Hwangbo; Jinkwang Kim; Sejoo Jeong; Abdul Rouf Dar; Rebecca Butcher; Jong-Chan Lee; Kyuhyung Kim
article.abstract: Parental age influences offspring traits across species, yet the molecular pathways by which maternal state modulates progeny neural function remain poorly defined. Here we demonstrate that maternal age in Caenorhabditis elegans regulates progeny avoidance of the social pheromone by modulating the activity of a defined sensory circuit. Progeny of young mothers exhibit stronger activity of the pheromone-sensing ADL neurons and enhanced pheromone avoidance, whereas progeny of older mothers display reduced neuronal responses and weaker repulsion. We identified an ERI-1-microRNA-neuropeptide signaling axis operating in peptidergic AVH interneurons that modulates ADL circuit responsiveness. ERI-1 promotes expression of the neuropeptide gene flp-26 by repressing mir-8207, and signaling from AVH to ADL establishes pheromone sensitivity. Maternal aging is associated with reduced ERI-1 expression in progeny AVH neurons and dampening this signaling pathway. Consequently, progeny of young mothers, though developmentally less robust, disperse more readily from crowded, pheromone-rich environments, offsetting their early-life disadvantages. Our findings reveal a molecular and circuit-level mechanism by which maternal physiology adaptively configures offspring neural computation and behavioral strategy across generations.

article.title: Hepatospora eriocheir infection affects the fitness of adult Chinese mitten crabs in their non-native range.
article.authors: Heleen Keirsebelik; Christine Ewers; April Grace Opinion; Magdalena Stachnik; Monika Normant-Saremba; Giulia Poma; Stijn Bosschaerts; Gudrun De Boeck; Jonas Schoelynck
article.abstract: For many invasive crustaceans, including the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis), the prevalence and impact of parasites in their introduced range remain largely unexplored. The microsporidium Hepatospora eriocheir was recently detected in mitten crabs across Europe, yet little is known about its physiological effects on its host. In this study, the influence of H. eriocheir infection on physiological biomarkers in adult mitten crabs collected from rivers in Germany and Belgium was experimentally investigated. We assessed metabolic rates (routine and maximum metabolic rate, aerobic scope), haemolymph glucose and lactate levels, and lipid content in the hepatopancreas. Infection prevalence reached 27% in adult mitten crabs from the Belgian population and 38% in individuals from the German population. Infected individuals showed a significantly reduced maximum metabolic rate and aerobic scope, while the routine metabolic rate remained unaffected. Glucose levels were lower in infected crabs both at rest and post-exercise, which indicates that energy reserves have dropped, whereas lactate levels showed no significant difference. The lipid content in the hepatopancreas was reduced, likely due to direct exploitation of host resources by the parasite and damage to hepatopancreatic tissue. Together, these patterns indicate an impaired energy metabolism, which may hamper energetically demanding activities such as migration and reproduction. The Chinese mitten crab is a catadromous species, and as the examined crabs were at the life stage when they commence a long-distance migration for their single reproductive event, infection by H. eriocheir may compromise their ability to complete this migration and successfully reproduce.

article.title: Integrated UPLC-Q-TOF and serum pharmacological analysis: Yinchenhao decoction alleviates alcoholic steatohepatitis via inhibition of COX-2/PI3K/Akt and suppression of M1 macrophage polarization.
article.authors: Jinjie Wen; Qiuxiang Zeng; Yuhua Wang; Tianjian Chen; Shuwen Xie; Shanshan Kuang; Kaili Deng; Min Li; Hechen Shi; Shuni Chen; Ke Li; Sha Huang; Wen Zhang; Zhiping Lv; Chuying Zhou
article.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yinchenhao decoction (YCHD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has been widely used for the treatment of liver disorders. However, its therapeutic efficacy in alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: To systematically evaluate the protective effects of YCHD and its bioactive compounds against ASH and elucidate the potential mechanisms through an integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF analysis and network pharmacology, with particular emphasis on the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and macrophage polarization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The therapeutic effects of YCHD on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation were comprehensively evaluated using multiple experimental models. The chemical composition and material basis of YCHD were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF analysis. Network pharmacology was subsequently employed to predict potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with the anti-ASH effects of YCHD. The regulatory effects of YCHD on macrophage polarization and the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway were further investigated through COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib and COX-2 siRNA. Finally, the major active compounds were screened and experimentally validated in zebrafish, AML12 cells, and RAW264.7 cells. RESULTS: YCHD exerted protective effects across multiple experimental models by improving lipid metabolic disorders, reducing hepatic lipid accumulation, and alleviating inflammatory responses. Phytochemical profiling identified 1,740 compounds in YCHD, including 195 blood-absorbed components. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that the PI3K/Akt pathway represents a critical target underlying the therapeutic effects of YCHD. Further validation demonstrated that YCHD reduced the expression of macrophage M1 polarization markers CD80/CD86 and decreased the production of inflammatory cytokines in ASH mice. Consistently, YCHD serum exerted comparable protective effects in LPS-stimulated polarized RAW264.7 cells by suppressing the activation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Pharmacological screening further identified acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin as potential key compounds. CONCLUSIONS: YCHD effectively ameliorates ASH by restoring lipid homeostasis, mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressing M1 macrophage polarization through modulation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt pathway. Acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin may represent important bioactive constituents contributing to the therapeutic effects of YCHD. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the pharmacological basis of YCHD in ASH treatment and establish a foundation for further identification and isolation of its active compounds.

article.title: Laser-responsive chitosan-coated solid lipid nanoparticles co-encapsulating CaO2 nanoparticles and IR780 for on-demand and enhanced photodynamic therapy of cancers.
article.authors: Mobina Amiri; Esmaeil Heydari; Mohammadreza Esmaeili; Hossein Zare-Behtash; Mohammad Moeini
article.abstract: The photodynamic therapy (PDT) efficacy is limited by tumor hypoxia and inefficient intracellular accumulation of photosensitizers (PSs). This study reports chitosan-coated solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) co-encapsulating the near-infrared photosensitizer IR780 and oxygen-generating CaO2 nanoparticles (NPs) for on-demand and enhanced PDT. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, the resulting IRCa@SLN-CH nanoplatform undergoes phase change due to IR780 photothermal effects, triggering the release of IR780 and CaO2. The released CaO2 subsequently hydrolyzes to generate oxygen in situ, boosting singlet oxygen production by IR780. Successful chitosan coating was confirmed by FTIR spectroscopy and a zeta potential shift from -36.2 ± 3.6 mV (uncoated IRCa@SLN) to + 35.3 ± 6.6 mV (IRCa@SLN-CH). IRCa@SLN-CH exhibited an average particle size of 51.5 ± 19.3 nm by TEM and 77.6 ± 7.0 nm by DLS, with IR780 and CaO2 loadings of 4.23 ± 0.23% and 65 ± 7%, respectively. Dissolved oxygen (DO) and ROS measurements showed that chitosan coating improved payload protection, resulting in a more controlled, on-off activation profile in response to laser irradiation. In vitro tests using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells demonstrated that chitosan coating enhanced cellular uptake, increased on-demand intracellular ROS generation, and improved laser-responsive cytotoxicity, while maintaining low ROS generation and toxicity before laser activation. Cell viability remained high before irradiation (99 ± 1%) but reduced to 51 ± 3% following laser exposure. Overall, the IRCa@SLN-CH nanoplatform shows potential for on-demand and enhanced PDT.

article.title: TMEM63B as a dual-function mechanosensitive channel and lipid scramblase: structural insights, physiological roles, and pharmacological potential.
article.authors: Zihan Chang; Zhirong Wang; Jiayi Tong; Yakun Yu; Jieyu Qi; Renjie Chai; Yanfeng Wang
article.abstract: TMEM63B, a member of the transmembrane channel/scramblase (TCS) superfamily, functions as both a mechanosensitive and osmosensitive ion channel and a lipid scramblase. Recent structural and functional studies have begun to reveal the molecular basis underlying these dual functions. In this review, we summarize the current understanding of TMEM63B, focusing on its structural architecture, channel and scramblase conformations, activation mechanisms, physiological roles and therapeutic potential. Importantly, the broad tissue distribution and disease-associated mutations of TMEM63B-linked to developmental epileptic encephalopathy, hemolytic anemia, placental dysfunction, pulmonary insufficiency, and intestinal barrier defects-underscore its emerging pharmacological relevance. We discuss the therapeutic opportunities and challenges in targeting TMEM63B, including allosteric modulation of its mechanosensitive gating, isoform- and tissue-selective strategies to mitigate on-target off-tissue toxicity, and the potential of biologics such as the agonistic antibody YN9303-24 for loss-of-function disorders. These insights provide a framework for understanding the mechanistic diversity of TCS proteins, their physiological significance, and their translational potential as a new class of druggable mechanosensitive targets.

article.title: Acquisition of Therapeutic Resistance and Structured Tissue Differentiation via Activation of the Life Cycle of Polyploid Giant Cancer Cells.
article.authors: Zhiqian Zhang; Xiaoran Li; Xinxin Tian; Limin Deng; Jin-Tang Dong; Jinsong Liu
article.abstract: To elucidate the mechanisms underlying therapy-induced resistance, we investigated the temporal dynamics of the polyploid giant cancer cell (PGCC) life cycle following treatment with the microtubule-destabilizing agent vincristine (VCR). Longitudinal live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that VCR-induced mitotic suppression activated a distinct PGCC life cycle characterized by nuclear amplification and progressive cellular reprogramming. At the cellular level, PGCCs entered a senescence-like state accompanied by an enhanced senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), increased epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), acquisition of early embryonic-like features, and multilineage differentiation potential into ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. PGCC-derived progeny exhibited dose- and time-dependent changes in proliferative behavior, aggressive phenotypes in vitro, along with time-dependent tumorigenic potential in vivo. Remarkably, at the tissue level, PGCCs also underwent spatial nuclear reorganization and self-organization into morphologically defined glandular epithelial structures exhibiting varying degrees of tissue maturation, reminiscent of early embryonic development. Silencing IL1β, IL6, or IL8, or pharmacologically inhibiting their receptors, suppressed PGCC formation, budding, EMT, and embryonic-like reprogramming associated with tissue morphogenesis. Furthermore, NAMPT emerged as a key regulator of embryonic-like stemness, glandular morphogenesis, and structural expansion. Together, these findings reveal that therapeutic stress activates a PGCC life cycle capable of generating two divergent outcomes: resistant tumor regeneration through clonal selection of undifferentiated tumor cells and organized tissue differentiation through spatial nuclear reprogramming. Our study establishes a conceptual framework linking therapy-induced polyploidization, developmental plasticity, and resistance generation at both cellular and tissue levels.

article.title: Curcumin mitigates palmitic acid-induced senescence in MIN6 β cells through NOX4/ROS regulation.
article.authors: Zhanhong Guo; Huan Zhang; Ming Shi; Yinghong Kong
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic β cell senescence is a key driver of type 2 diabetes (T2D) progression, and oxidative stress plays a critical role in this process. This study explored the therapeutic potential of curcumin against palmitic acid (PA)-induced senescence in MIN6 cells. We also explored whether this protection was achieved via modulation of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase 4 (NOX4)/reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathway. METHODS: We used PA to establish a lipotoxicity model in MIN6 cells. We assessed cell viability by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and insulin secretion with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) assay. We used flow cytometry to measure calcium concentration, β-galactosidase activity, cell cycle distribution, ROS production and mitochondrial membrane potential. Western blot was used to analyze the expression of NOX4 and senescence markers p16 and p21. We also performed molecular docking to predict the binding mode between curcumin and NOX4. We knocked down NOX4 to confirm its role in curcumin's protective effects. RESULTS: PA significantly reduced MIN6 cell viability, insulin secretion and intracellular calcium concentration. PA induced cellular senescence, as evidenced by increased β-galactosidase activity, upregulated p16 and p21 expression and cell cycle arrest in the G0/G1 phase. PA activated the NOX4/ROS pathway, leading to ROS overproduction and a decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential. Curcumin treatment partially reversed these effects. Molecular docking showed curcumin binds strongly to NOX4 (binding energy: -8.4 kcal/mol). NOX4 knockdown enhanced curcumin's effects on oxidative stress and cell senescence. CONCLUSION: Curcumin mitigates PA-induced senescence in MIN6 cells and restores insulin secretion by inhibiting the overactivation of the NOX4/ROS pathway and reducing oxidative stress.

article.title: Differential reproductive effects of two insect growth regulators (20-hydroxyecdysone and methyl farnesoate) on non-target aquatic organism: A case study using Daphnia magna.
article.authors: Meng You; Yu Yang; Xinyu Chang; Yuting Zhang; Tao Wang; Hongyan Zhang; Runbing Xu
article.venue: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Toxicology & pharmacology : CBP
article.abstract: Two insect growth regulators (IGRs), 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) and methyl farnesoate (MF), are widely used in hormone-based pest control and may pose risks to aquatic ecosystems by disrupting the endocrine systems of non-target organisms. This study investigated the chronic (21-day) and acute (96-h) toxic effects of hazard characterization dose (50 μg/L) 20E and MF on reproduction, endocrine disruption, and underlying molecular mechanisms in Daphnia magna, a key model in ecotoxicology. Chronic exposure revealed that 20E significantly enhanced somatic growth (+5.4% body length at day 7) while inhibiting reproduction (-14.95% total offspring), whereas MF had no significant effects in surviving individuals, but suppressed overall reproduction through a mortality-driven effect. Acute exposure demonstrated that 20E elevated vitellogenin (+45.33%) and ecdysone levels (+22.09%), while MF primarily increased juvenile hormone (JH) synthesis (+7.99%). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that both compounds downregulated sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways, with shared downregulation of MFE (Methyl farnesoate epoxidase) and EPPL (Ethanolamine-phosphate phospho-lyase) genes critical for JH and lipid homeostasis. Molecular docking predicted that 20E and MF could bind to the ecdysone receptor (EcR) and methoprene-tolerant (Met) proteins, with MF showing higher binding affinity to EcR (-6.95 kcal/mol vs. -6.05 kcal/mol for 20E). These endocrine disruptions are consistent with the suppression of reproduction via altered cholesterol mobilization and steroidogenesis pathways. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms of estrogenic disruption in D. magna, highlighting the ecological risks of IGRs in aquatic environments.

article.title: Durable Adhesion in Polyphenol Hydrogel Adhesives: From Interface Aging to Long-Term Stabilization.
article.authors: Tianyi Xia; Jiaojiao Yang; Xiujuan Yang; Jianshu Li; Boyu Tang; Jun Luo
article.abstract: Polyphenol hydrogel adhesives have found broad application in wound management, tissue repair, leak sealing, and biointegrated systems due to their robust wet adhesion, versatile interfacial reactivity, and broad substrate adaptability. However, they often suffer from progressive interfacial aging, leading to diminished interfacial retention, compromised sealing integrity, and reduced functional stability during service. Improving interfacial retention is therefore critical for extending their utility in biomedical environments. This review begins by examining the time-dependent evolution of polyphenol hydrogel adhesive interfaces, highlighting the major mechanisms underlying adhesion degradation and the corresponding stabilization principles. We further summarize emerging strategies for long-term interfacial stabilization and outline future directions in interface-specific material design and performance assessment. By providing a comprehensive framework for understanding durable polyphenol-mediated adhesion, this review aims to guide the rational development of next-generation bioadhesives for increasingly demanding biomedical applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Polyphenol hydrogels have emerged as versatile wet adhesives for tissue sealing, wound protection, drug delivery, and dental treatment. Recent studies increasingly focus on whether these materials can maintain adhesion under physiological conditions over time. This Review discusses the time-dependent evolution of polyphenol-mediated interfaces, major causes of adhesion loss, and current strategies for improving interfacial retension. Future work should place greater emphasis on long-term testing under realistic service conditions, comprehensive biosafety assessment, and clinical translation. By integrating these aspects, this Review aims to support more reliable evaluation and guide the development of durable polyphenol hydrogel adhesives for wet, dynamic, and demanding biological environments, with improved safety, reliability, and translational potential.

article.title: Mitochondrial acquisition after the Asgard revolution: Reconstructing eukaryogenesis with insights for mitochondrial transplantation.
article.authors: Yuan-Yuan Li; Kevin B Frazier; Franklin R Tay
article.abstract: Mitochondria arose from an alphaproteobacterial endosymbiont that became integrated within an archaeal host during eukaryogenesis. The discovery of Asgard archaea has clarified host ancestry and supports reconstructions in which aspects of cytoskeletal and membrane complexity preceded mitochondrial acquisition. Organellogenesis involved genome reduction, gene transfer, protein import, metabolic coupling, and vertical inheritance. These evolutionary principles complement current mitochondrial transplantation recommendations by generating testable predictions about recipient dependence and the duration of rescue. Transplanted mitochondria are mature organelles introduced into cells already equipped to maintain mitochondria; the requirement for transient or durable function must nevertheless be tested for each indication. Aging can modify organelle delivery, recipient quality control, and tissue responses, with particular implications for the neurovascular unit and neuronal function. Extracellular vesicle delivery requires verification of mitochondrial cargo, potency, and compatibility. Measurable criteria distinguish delivery, uptake, cytosolic access, network interaction, persistence, and functional benefit, while separating evidence from aging, acute ischemia, and inherited disease models.

article.title: Distinct Thermosensitive Activation of HSF1 and HSF2 in Immune Cells During Aging.
article.authors: Prachayaporn Prasertsuksri; Nathan A Velaris; Donald A Jurivich
article.abstract: Heat shock factors (HSF1 and HSF2) critically maintain proteostasis under stress, yet their activation across the continuum of rising temperatures is incompletely understood. Furthermore, how age impacts thermally driven rheostatic changes in stress responses is not fully elucidated. Here, we investigate how different temperature levels impact HSF1 and HSF2 in Jurkat T cells and splenocytes from young and aged mice. Using Western blotting, EMSA, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation, we examined heat shock response changes across a range of thermal conditions. Unlike most cell types that require 42°C for HSF1 activation, Jurkat cells maximally responded at 41°C and splenocytes at 40°C. Optimal HSF1 activation coincided with maximal nuclear translocation, Ser326 phosphorylation, SIRT1 protein levels, and HSP RNA levels. By contrast, HSF2 nuclear translocation required a higher temperature (42°C) than HSF1. Age reduced HSF1 protein levels and nuclear translocation during thermal stress, while HSF2 protein levels were significantly elevated. These findings reveal distinct temperature-sensitive patterns of HSF1 and HSF2 activation of immunocytes during heat stress and identify age-associated alterations in this response.

article.title: Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside alleviates neurological injury after traumatic brain injury: involvement of cGAS-STING signaling and mitochondrial dynamics.
article.authors: Ruiqing Zhang; Wei Li; Pengbo Zhou; Yatao Wang; Dangli Ren; Jingjing Wang; Hanjie Niu; Hongtao Sun
article.abstract: Secondary neurological injury is a major determinant of functional outcome after traumatic brain injury (TBI) and is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction and disrupted mitochondrial dynamics. Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside (CAG) has antioxidant and mitochondria-protective properties, but its therapeutic potential in TBI remains unclear. The present study demonstrated that CAG significantly improved neurological, behavioral, and cognitive outcomes in mice with controlled cortical impact (CCI)-induced TBI, while alleviating histopathological damage, neuronal apoptosis, glial activation, and mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. Consistently, in H2O2-treated HT22 cells, CAG reduced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Mechanistically, transcriptomic, protein, and confocal immunofluorescence analyses showed that CAG reduced aberrant cGAS-STING signaling and attenuated abnormal subcellular redistribution of activated STING. In parallel, CAG restored mitochondrial dynamics, with a reduced p-DRP1 (Ser616)/DRP1 ratio and increased MFN1, MFN2, and OPA1 expression. Notably, DMXAA partially reversed CAG-mediated restoration of mitochondrial dynamics and neuroprotection, suggesting the involvement of STING signaling. CAG promotes neurological recovery after TBI by restoring mitochondrial dynamics homeostasis and attenuating neuronal injury, with the findings supporting the involvement of reduced cGAS-STING signaling in these effects. This study provides experimental evidence supporting CAG as a potential pharmacological strategy for mitigating secondary injury after TBI.

article.title: Aging in cardio-oncology: Pathophysiology, clinical implications and future directions.
article.authors: Cristina Madaudo; Antonio Cannatà; Egle Corrado; Daniela Di Lisi; Ludovico Rossetto; Oreste Fabio Triolo; Giulia Cacciatore; Francesco Bovo; Francesco Fiore; Umberto Attanasio; Valentina Mercurio; Alfredo Ruggero Galassi; Carlo Gabriele Tocchetti; Guido Iaccarino; Giuseppina Novo; Alessandra Cuomo
article.abstract: Population aging is changing the needs of patients seen in cardio-oncology. Older adults with cancer often have cardiovascular disease, multimorbidity, and reduced physiological reserve, which can complicate treatment and recovery. Patients of the same chronological age may differ considerably in cardiovascular health, functional capacity, and treatment tolerance. Frailty and geriatric assessment can help characterize these differences and inform care. This review examines the biological mechanisms linking aging, cancer, and cardiovascular disease and discusses their implications for cardiovascular risk assessment, cancer treatment decisions, and long-term survivorship. Treatment decisions require consideration of the expected oncological benefit, cardiovascular risk, physiological reserve, life expectancy, and patient preferences. Identifying and addressing reversible vulnerabilities may help patients tolerate effective anticancer therapy while preserving function and quality of life. During survivorship, cardiovascular care should account for previous treatment exposure, changing health status, and adherence to preventive therapies. Closer collaboration between cardio-oncology and geriatric medicine may improve the assessment and management of older patients. Evidence specific to frail and very old adults remains limited. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether geriatric and biological aging measures improve cardiovascular risk prediction, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

article.title: Persistent Hepatocyte Plasticity and Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming After Hepatitis C Virus Cure.
article.authors: Jean Agnetti; Samy Cherief; Christophe Desterke; Vanessa Bou-Malham; Nassima Benzoubir; Tuan Zea Tan; Jean Paul Thiery; Didier Samuel; Ama Gassama-Diagne
article.venue: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
article.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection disrupts hepatocyte polarity and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), contributing to liver disease progression. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) eradicate HCV infection in most patients, the risk of fibrosis progression and hepatocellular carcinoma persists after viral clearance. Whether antiviral cure fully restores hepatocyte differentiation, polarity, and epithelial identity programs remains unclear. We investigated whether HCV-induced EMT and lipid metabolism alterations are fully reversible following DAA treatment. METHODS: Huh7 hepatoma cells and Huh7 cells stably expressing a full-length HCV replicon were cultured in three-dimensional Matrigel to assess morphogenesis, polarity-associated features, and EMT. Spheroid morphology, canalicular-like organization, EMT markers, and transcriptomic signatures were analyzed using microscopy, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, and microarray analysis. The effects of DAA treatment (sofosbuvir with or without velpatasvir) were evaluated in vitro. Publicly available transcriptomic data from liver biopsies collected before therapy and within five days after its completion, were analyzed. RESULTS: HCV replicon expression altered canalicular-like organization and induced actin-rich protrusions in 90% of Huh7-R spheroids. DAA treatment efficiently suppressed HCV replicon expression and partially restored epithelial morphology, reducing protrusions to 25%, without normalizing them to the control level (2.5%). EMT-associated changes, including reduced E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin expression, were only partially corrected by DAA treatment. Transcriptomic EMT scoring showed persistent mesenchymal features in DAA-treated cells and in patient biopsies collected at the end of treatment. In parallel, genes involved in lipid metabolism and hepatocyte differentiation remained dysregulated. CONCLUSIONS: These findings show incomplete restoration of epithelial organization after suppression of HCV replicon expression in vitro and incomplete normalization of selected transcriptional signatures at the end of DAA treatment in patient liver samples. They suggest that cellular plasticity and metabolic reprogramming may persist after treatment and contribute to long-term liver disease risk.

article.title: Fam172a deletion exacerbates hepatic steatosis and alters SRSF3-associated PPARγ isoform regulation.
article.authors: Meng-Han Li; Jun-Wei Wang; Man-Rong Xu; Ya-Wen Zhang; Ming-Yun Chen; Jiang-Feng Ke; Zhi-Hui Zhang; Yu-Jie Wang; Mei-Fang Li; Lian-Xi Li
