article.abstract: Family with sequence similarity 172 member A (FAM172A) has recently been implicated in metabolic diseases such as obesity and atherosclerosis; however, its hepatocyte-specific functions and downstream mechanisms in hepatic steatosis remain incompletely defined. In this study, we observed significant upregulation of FAM172A in the livers of mice with diet-induced hepatic steatosis. Liver-specific deletion of Fam172a exacerbated high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic steatosis and metabolic dysfunction, accompanied by increased expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) and genes involved in fatty acid uptake and lipogenesis. In vitro, Fam172a overexpression attenuated triglyceride accumulation and reduced PPARγ expression, while the PPARγ antagonist GW9662 attenuated lipid accumulation in Fam172a-deficient primary hepatocytes. Proteomic analysis and co-immunoprecipitation identified serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 3 (SRSF3) as an interacting protein of FAM172A. Fam172a deletion reduced hepatic SRSF3 expression and was associated with altered Pparg splicing in liver tissue. In primary hepatocytes, Fam172a deletion increased the PPARγ2/PPARγ1 ratio at both the mRNA and protein levels. SRSF3 restoration partially rescued lipid accumulation in Fam172a-deficient hepatocytes, while SRSF3 knockdown partially attenuated the protective effect of FAM172A overexpression. CLIP-seq provided evidence of an interaction between SRSF3 and Pparg RNA. Collectively, these findings support a protective role for hepatic FAM172A and implicate SRSF3-associated regulation of PPARγ isoform expression in its effects on lipid accumulation, highlighting FAM172A as a potential therapeutic target.

article.title: Immunotherapy targeting an endogenous retrovirus decreases islet senescence markers and preserves glucose control in a mouse model of type 2 diabetes.
article.authors: Daniel Bjørklund Andersen; Nanna Skeltved; Gabriel Mira González; Thomas Garde-Due; Iker Ausina; Clara Iacumin; Lasse Neukirch; Anne-Marie Andersson; Emeline Ragonnaud; Joachim Størling; Claus Desler; Frederik Otzen Bagger; Kaare Villum Grunddal; Peter Johannes Holst
article.abstract: Type-2-diabetes is characterized by progressive metabolic stress and accumulation of senescent cells in key metabolic tissues, such as the pancreas, adipose tissue, and liver. Cellular senescence - an irreversible growth-arrested, and pro-inflammatory cell state can lead to induction of endogenous retrovirus (ERV) expression, which can also trigger cellular senescence. This possibly implies that a self-reinforcing ERV-senescence axis contributes to the metabolic decline and T2D. Here we developed and tested a mouse endogenous retrovirus (muERV) based active immunotherapy targeted at the most intact muERV, IAPE (Intracisternal A-type Particles elements with an Envelope) to eliminate cells expressing muERVs and senescence associated proteins in a mouse model of accelerated diabetes combining a high-fat diet (HFD) with dexamethasone (DEX) and streptozotocin (STZ) (DS-HFD). Immunized DS-HFD mice (DS-HFD + IAPE-Tx) showed increased B and T cell responses towards IAPE. Antisera generated using our IAPE-targeted active immunotherapy was used to confirm activation of IAPE expression in the murine β-cell line MIN-6, following both inflammatory (cytokines) and chemical stress (STZ and DEX). In Vivo, DS-HFD + IAPE-Tx mice showed reduced weight gain, improved fasting insulin-glucose homeostasis and oral glucose tolerance. They furthermore showed reduction in histomorphometry features consistent with steatosis, hepatocyte binucleation, reduced adipocyte size, and pancreatic islet senescence markers p16INK4a and p21Cip1/waf1, with a slight decrease in islet IAPE. Finally, we show activation of a human orthologue to IAPE, HERV-K, in cytokine-exposed isolated human pancreatic islets and EndoC-βH5 β-cells. Together, our results suggest that ERV antigens are expressed in metabolic disease models and may be targeted by immunotherapy to improve metabolic parameters, through a potential senolytic or senostatic-related but so far undefined mechanism.

article.title: Involvement of PINK1-related Mitophagy and Necroptosis in TDI-Induced Experimental Asthma.
article.authors: Xiu He; Shuai Fu; Dengxiang Yao; Lijuan Zuo; Xiaoli Yuan; Yiyang Du; Zhiyao Qian; Jiaqi Ban; Qian He; Mingdan You
article.abstract: Toluene diisocyanate (TDI) is a prevalent cause of occupational asthma. Although mitophagy contributes to various pulmonary diseases, its role and downstream signaling in TDI-induced asthma remain unclear. In this study, we first utilized BALB/c mice to investigate the effects of TDI exposure on pulmonary injury, mitophagy, and associated regulatory mechanisms. Based on these findings, we constructed an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) network for TDI-induced asthma. Mechanistic connections predicted by the AOP were validated in vitro using PINK1-knockdown bronchial epithelial cells, assessing PINK1-related mitophagy, mitochondrial function, cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and necroptosis. Finally, we predicted potential natural product therapeutics through bioactivity screening and toxicity profiling, targeting key genes implicated in TDI-induced asthma. Integration of in vivo, in vitro, and AOP network analyses indicated that TDI exposure induced airway hyperresponsiveness and pulmonary histopathological changes, along with elevated Th2 cytokine production. This exposure selectively upregulated PINK1 and Parkin expression, without altering levels of BNIP3, NIX, or FUNDC1. PINK1 knockdown mitigated TDI-induced mitophagy-related alterations, restored mitochondrial function, reduced cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and reduced necroptosis. In silico screening predicted β-lapachone, genistein, and apigenin as promising candidate therapeutics for TDI-induced asthma. Overall, PINK1-related mitophagy may contribute to TDI-induced occupational asthma, and natural compounds identified via in silico screening are potential candidates that require further in vitro and in vivo validation of their safety and efficacy.

article.title: Interactions between Hexokinase 2 and host proteins and their involvement in tissue tropism upon Hepatospora eriocheir infection in Eriocheir sinensis.
article.authors: Zhengfeng Ding; Yang Wu; Qilu Wu; Yini Xu; Yixin Shen; Xinyu Zhang
article.abstract: Hepatospora eriocheir is the causative pathogen of hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (HPND) in Eriocheir sinensis, and this microsporidian parasite specifically colonizes crab hepatopancreatic tissue. The molecular mechanisms underlying such tissue-specific infection remain largely unclear. Microsporidian parasites generally undergo extensive genomic degeneration, accompanied by the loss of oxidative phosphorylation pathways and most glycolysis-related genes. Nevertheless, H. eriocheir retains two paralogous hexokinase genes. Among them, HeHK2 exhibits relatively high sequence conservation but lacks detectable catalytic activity, indicating that this protein exerts non-enzymatic functions during pathogen infection. Immunofluorescence assays verified that H. eriocheir mainly resides in hepatopancreatic epithelial cells of crabs. Immunoprecipitation-Mass Spectrometry (IP- LC-MS/MS) was adopted to screen potential host proteins interacting with HeHK2. Three candidate proteins, including mitochondrial amidoxime reducing component (mARC), alpha-amylase 2-like protein and C-type lectin, were selected for subsequent co-immunoprecipitation validation based on their biological functions associated with host energy metabolism and innate immune regulation. Histological and ultrastructural observation further revealed mitochondrial aggregation and abnormal morphological changes in infected hepatopancreatic tissues. These interactions suggest a working model in which HeHK2 may contribute to hepatopancreas-specific infection by modulating mitochondria-associated host metabolism and innate immunity; however, direct functional evidence for this model requires further investigation.

article.title: Inhibiting apolipoprotein C3 alleviates ferroptosis and cell damage induced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
article.authors: Yaoyang Liu; Xuejing Yang; Tianchun Ni; Jialu Zong; Chen Qian; Xudong Wang; Juan Yu
article.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore the induction effect of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) infection on ferroptosis and inflammatory response in human hepatoma cells (Hep3B) and the regulatory effect of apolipoprotein C3(APOC3) on ferroptosis sensitivity. METHODS: Hep3B hepatocytes (MOI=5, 10, 15) were infected with the wild standard strain of PA (PAO1) for 4 h, 8 h, and 12 h respectively, and the survival rate of cells under different infection concentrations and times was detected by CCK-8. The morphological changes of cells were observed under an inverted microscope to determine the infection conditions. After adding ferroptosis inhibitors or siRNA respectively to inhibit the expression of APOC3, lipid droplets were labeled using oil red O staining, and the formation of lipid droplets was observed under an inverted microscope. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) were detected using a fluorescent probe (DCFH-DA), and lipid peroxidation levels were detected using a microplate reader. The expression levels of Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor α (PPARα), APOC3 and related inflammatory factors were detected by RT-qPCR. The protein expression levels of APOC3 and the ferroptosis-related proteins SLC7A11 and ACSL4 were evaluated by Western blotting. The morphological changes of mitochondria in cells were observed by transmission electron microscopy. The content of Fe2+ in cells was detected using a divalent iron ion probe. RESULTS: With the increase of infection concentration and the extension of time, the survival rate of Hep3B cells significantly decreased after PAO1 infection, and the cell morphology gradually changed from spindle-shaped to round and accompanied by fragmentation. The number of red lipid droplets within the cells increased with the increase of the bacterial load. The fluorescence intensity of ROS was enhanced. The expression of PPARα mRNA was down-regulated and the expression of APOC3 mRNA was up-regulated. The volume of mitochondria decreased, the membrane density increased, and the cristae were reduced or even disappeared. Western blotting further confirmed the changes in APOC3 protein expression and ferroptosis-related proteins, including SLC7A11 and ACSL4, following PAO1 infection and APOC3 knockdown. The intracellular lipid peroxidation level was significantly increased. Compared with the control group, the levels of IL-6 and TNF-α significantly increased after PA infection. After inhibiting the expression of APOC3, the expression level of ROS decreased, lipid peroxidation reduced, the number of lipid droplets decreased, the content of Fe2+ decreased, mitochondrial damage decreased, and the expression of ferroptosis-related factors decreased. CONCLUSION: After the action of PA, cell activity significantly decreased, intracellular ROS generation increased, and intracellular lipid peroxidation was enhanced, leading to cell damage and death. Meanwhile, APOC3, as a key downstream target of PPARα, PA promotes the generation of APOC3 by inhibiting the expression of PPARα, and APOC3 reduces the hydrolysis of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (TRL), thereby promoting lipid droplet formation. It causes the accumulation of lipids within cells. However, the continuous inhibitionof APOC3 can reverse this effect. That is, after PA infects cells, it can promote the increase of APOC3 expression, leading to lipid metabolism disorders, and APOC3 plays a promoting role in the process of PA promoting ferroptosis in cells.

article.title: Polyaniline-modified red mud promotes chain elongation during anaerobic fermentation of waste activated sludge through a hydrated electroactive interface.
article.authors: Qiupeng Cai; Junguo He; Wei Qiu; Bin Wu; Yongyang Wang; Kang Fang; Xiang Zou; Jie Zhang
article.abstract: Medium-chain fatty acids (MCFAs) production from waste activated sludge is constrained by poor substrate release and inefficient utilization of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and reducing equivalents. Polyaniline-modified red mud (RM@PANI) was developed as a hydrated electroactive mineral interface to address these limitations. At 2 g/L, RM@PANI increased MCFAs production to 12.4 g COD/L, 2.27 times the control, and raised the caprylate fraction from 12.6 % to 36.7 %. At 1 g/L, it produced 19.5 % more MCFAs than bare RM. RM@PANI mobilized EPS, sustained hydrolysis and acidogenesis, and enriched taxa associated with hydrolysis and chain elongation (CE), particularly the CE genus Sporanaerobacter. PANI coating increased local acetate hydration and raised the simulated diffusion coefficient from 0.003 to 0.368 Å2/ps. Higher atoE abundance suggested greater genetic potential for SCFA transport. Community restructuring, cell clustering, and faster acetate transport were consistent with tighter coupling between acidogenesis and CE. Meanwhile, RM@PANI increased electron exchange capacity, lowered charge-transfer resistance, expanded the intracellular NAD(H) pool, and enhanced metabolic potential across reverse β-oxidation and fatty acid biosynthesis. Electron transfer efficiency increased from 69 % to 76 %, with more electron equivalents recovered in MCFAs. Several flavin-related genes were more abundant in the RM@PANI group, while DFT calculations showed stronger RF-surface charge transfer, supporting flavin-mediated electron transfer as a potential interfacial process. RM@PANI improved MCFAs production by coupling precursor supply, SCFAs transport, microbial organization, and electron utilization at a hydrated electroactive interface, providing a route for converting industrial residues into functional materials for sludge carbon recovery.

article.title: Ebola Virus VP40 C-terminal Lysine Residue Mediates Lipid Interactions and Dimer-Dimer Interactions.
article.authors: Hannah M Woods; Yogesh B Narkhede; Ukesh Karki; Michael J Norris; Prem P Chapagain; Olaf Wiest; Robert V Stahelin
article.abstract: The Ebola virus (EBOV) matrix protein VP40 is the main driver of viral assembly and budding, processes which depend on its ability to oligomerize at the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane (PM). VP40 forms dimers in the cytoplasm that traffic to the membrane and assemble into higher-order oligomers, but the specific molecular determinants governing the stability of these oligomeric interfaces are not fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of the C-terminal lysine residue, Lys326, in mediating VP40-lipid and VP40-VP40 interactions. Using a combination of molecular dynamics simulations and computational site-saturation mutagenesis, we predicted that while Lys326 has a minimal role in the stability of the isolated VP40 dimer, it is a critical determinant in stabilizing the interfaces of higher-order structures like tetramers and hexamers. Experimentally, mutation of this residue to alanine or aspartic acid (K326A or K326D) impaired VP40 PM localization, oligomerization, and in a charge-dependent manner, virus-like particle production. Our results indicate that a cationic residue is crucial not only for interactions with anionic phospholipids in the PM but, more importantly, for forming stabilizing networks across VP40 dimer-dimer interfaces. Together, these findings identify Lys326 as a keystone residue that couples membrane binding to the stabilization of essential higher-order oligomers, revealing a critical interface for EBOV assembly that could be exploited for future antiviral strategies.

article.title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
article.authors: Jin-An Zhou; Jun Tu; Jiang Yue; Qi-Er Zhang; Yalan Chen; Qiuju Fan; Jing Ma; Yong Zuo; Ning-Ning Liu; Jinke Cheng; Jianli He
article.abstract: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

article.title: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in Charcot-Marie-Tooth 1A and Charcot-Marie-Tooth 2A.
article.authors: Zhenyu Li; Yize Li; Ping Li; Zhiying Xie; Meng Yu; Jianwen Deng; He Lv; Wei Zhang; Zhaoxia Wang; Lingchao Meng; Yun Yuan
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) is released from cells during such processes as mitophagy and apoptosis and can act as an endogenous damage-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immune responses. We investigated levels of circulating cell-free DNA (ccf-DNA), including ccf-mtDNA and circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (ccf-nDNA), and serum interleukin-1β (IL-1β) in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease, specifically with CMT1A and CMT2A. METHODS: This study enrolled 51 patients with CMT disease (42 with CMT1A and 9 with CMT2A, 31 males and 20 females) and 13 healthy controls (6 males and 7 females). The numbers of copies of serum ccf-mtDNA and ccf-nDNA, were quantified using ND1 and ACTB, respectively, before being measured via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Serum IL-1β levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The number of ccf-DNA copies, ND1/ACTB ratio, and IL-1β levels were compared between the three groups. And the correlation analysis was performed. RESULTS: Serum ND1 levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls, so was the ND1/ACTB ratio in the CMT1A (p < 0.001) and CMT2A (p < 0.05) groups. Serum IL-1β levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls. The ND1/ACTB ratio was positively related to the number of onion bulbs in CMT2A. No significant differences in serum ACTB, ND1, ND1/ACTB, or IL-1β levels were observed between the CMT1A and CMT2A groups. CONCLUSION: Patients with CMT1A and CMT2A had higher levels of serum ccf-mtDNA and IL-1β than in healthy controls. These findings suggest association between increased circulating mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in CMT disease. However, no subtype-specific differences were identified between CMT1A and CMT2A.

article.title: HFPO‑TA induces developmental hepatotoxicity in hESC‑derived hepatocyte‑like cells by disrupting lipid homeostasis and mitochondrial function.
article.authors: Sujie Sun; Hao Chen; Yi Hu; Zhenying Lin; Haoran Ye; Qianqian Zhang; Jiuru Zhao; Xiaorui Liu; Zhiwei Liu
article.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA), an alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), can cross the placental barrier, raising concerns regarding fetal hepatic development; however, the mechanisms underlying its developmental hepatotoxicity remain poorly elucidated. Here, human embryonic stem cell-derived hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) were exposed to HFPO-TA at 3, 15, or 75μM for 28 days during hepatocytic differentiation. HFPO-TA accumulated intracellularly in a dose- and time-dependent manner and impaired hepatic function, evidenced by reduced albumin secretion and CYP activity and increased alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling revealed extensive disruption of lipid metabolism, including increased triglycerides, total cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein levels, and decreased high-density lipoprotein levels. HFPO-TA activated PPAR signaling and altered genes and proteins associated with lipid synthesis and oxidation, with significant perturbations even at the environmentally relevant concentration of 3 μM. Oil Red O staining and altered PLIN1 and PLIN2 expression confirmed lipid droplet accumulation. HFPO-TA also disrupted mitochondrial function, altered respiratory chain activity, reduced ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential, and up-regulated fission-fusion-related genes. Collectively, these findings indicate that HFPO-TA impairs hepatocyte differentiation through PPAR-mediated lipid remodeling and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting safety concerns for this PFOA alternative. Furthermore, HLCs are a valuable in vitro model for assessing the developmental toxicity of PFOA alternatives.

article.title: 2,4-Dichlorophenol induced sex hormone imbalance in zebrafish ovary via esr1-mediated cholesterol synthesis inhibition.
article.authors: Jiamin Shi; Rongjian Liu; Dongqiong Wei; Yang Zheng; Lei Yang; Samra; Cong Yuan; Yongmei Qi; Dejun Huang
article.abstract: 2,4-Dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP) is a persistent organic pollutant that disrupts endocrine homeostasis. Here, environmentally relevant concentrations of 2,4-DCP disrupted sex hormone balance in zebrafish, resulting in increased the ratios of estrogen (E2) to 11-ketotestosterone and E2 to testosterone, while inhibiting steroidogenesis pathway. However, the role of cholesterol as a precursor in this process remains unclear. Our results showed that 2,4-DCP significantly reduced the total cholesterol and free cholesterol in the ovary by downregulation of the genes srebp2 and hmgcr2 (for de novo synthesis of cholesterol), which decreased ovarian cholesterol availability. Consistently, inhibition of cholesterol synthesis using a specific inhibitor also significantly disrupted the sex hormone balance. Furthermore, 2,4-DCP exhibited anti-estrogenic effects in female zebrafish with high endogenous estrogen levels, as indicated by significantly suppressed the expression of esr1, esr2a and esr2b, as well as decreased vitellogenin levels. In the absence of estrogen, dual-luciferase reporter assays and point mutation studies confirmed that 2,4-DCP enhanced esr1/2b binding to the estrogen response element at the -452/-438 in the srebp2 promoter. These results indicated that 2,4-DCP inhibit cholesterol synthesis via competitive bindings to estrogen receptors. Then esr1 knockout zebrafish confirmed the key regulatory role of esr1 in cholesterol synthesis in vivo. Moreover, esr1 mRNA supplementation partially restored cholesterol synthesis and sex hormone level. These findings establish that 2,4-DCP impairs sex hormone balance by esr1-dependent transcriptional regulation of cholesterol synthesis, providing a theoretical basis for assessing the endocrine-disrupting effects of 2,4-DCP pollution in aquatic organisms.

article.title: Dairy farm system configurations and predictors of multidimensional climate-smart practice adoption in the U.S.
article.authors: Lauren Hunt; Rebecca C Mitchell; Meredith T Niles
article.abstract: Dairy systems face mounting climate pressures that require mitigation and adaptation. However, adoption of climate-smart dairy practices is typically evaluated one practice at a time, obscuring how producers combine practices into a whole-farm system. We surveyed U.S. dairy producers (n = 920) on adoption of 12 climate-smart practices and duration of use. Adaptation practices were widespread: 82-87% currently use indoor housing or cooling fans. Mitigation adoption was uneven; land-based strategies such as forage diversification were more common than capital-intensive manure and animal-based technologies. Discontinuation was rare for core infrastructure (5-8% of users for indoor housing and cooling fans) but reached about 30% for feed additives. Latent class analysis identified three farm-system configurations, distinguished primarily by grazing and land-based engagement and by longevity of current practice use: housing and cooling focused, diversified and moderate (shortest longevity), and grazing and land based (longest longevity). Grazing access and perceived practice efficacy were the strongest predictors of configuration membership; most perceived barriers, priorities, program participation, and climate beliefs were not significant. Configuration membership thus tracks a farm's existing structure more than most attitudes or institutional engagement. Mitigation opportunities differ by farm structure: housing- and cooling-focused farms have mitigation potential in manure management and forage diversification; feed additives and low-infrastructure manure practices such as composting may be most appropriate for grazing- and land-based farms; and diversified farms may benefit from multi-practice bundling. There is no single pathway to climate-smart practice implementation; outreach should be attentive to each farm's existing structure and operational history.

article.title: DHA-H and HPA restore impaired neurogenic phenotypes and BDNF-TrkB signaling in Ts65Dn neurospheres and hippocampus.
article.authors: Enrico Castroflorio; Joan Cabot; Margalida Suau-Fullana; Ain Justin Santillan; Guillermo Vicens Gomez; Paula Férnandez-García; Victoria Llado; Pablo V Escribá; Manuel Torres
article.abstract: Impaired neurogenesis is a hallmark of neurodevelopmental disorders, including Down syndrome, and contributes to long-lasting deficits in brain structure and function. Membrane lipid composition is emerging as a critical regulator of cell fate decisions in the developing and adult brain. Here we investigate the pro-neurogenic potential of the synthetic PUFA DHA-H (2-hydroxylated DHA) and its immediate metabolite HPA (Heneicosapentaenoic acid) in cellular and tissue models derived from the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome, using DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) as a reference pro-neurogenic ω-3 PUFA. In primary neurospheres, DHA-H and HPA increased the expression of neural stem and progenitor cell markers, including Sox2, Ki67, and Nestin, and stimulated proliferative activity, accompanied by a parallel upregulation of early neuronal differentiation markers such as Doublecortin and PSA-NCAM. Notably, both compounds promoted the recovery of these markers in Ts65Dn neurospheres, with HPA achieving restoration to wild-type levels for several markers, while DHA-H exerted beneficial effects that varied across the evaluated parameters. These improvements were associated with enhanced BDNF production and TrkB phosphorylation, highlighting the BDNF-TrkB signaling axis as a potential molecular mediator of their pro-neurogenic effects. In vivo, administration of DHA-H and HPA increased BDNF and phospho-TrkB protein levels, together with the number of proliferating cells and mature neurons in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus, suggesting enhanced activity of the adult neurogenic niche and potential neuroprotective effects. Together, our findings identify DHA-H and HPA as promising modulators of neural progenitor dynamics and neurogenesis in a trisomic context, revealing a lipid-dependent mechanism of neurodevelopmental plasticity and supporting their therapeutic potential for ameliorating impaired neurogenic programs in Down syndrome and related disorders.

article.title: Lipid-based nanoencapsulation prolongs the antinociceptive effect of cannabidiol in experimental neuropathic pain.
article.authors: Thalita da Cruz Monteiro Santana; Anna Beatriz de Oliveira Cruz; Lucas Gabriel da Silva Oliveira; Pedro Santana Sales Lauria; Daniele Brustolim; Eryvaldo Sócrates Tabosa do Egito; Max Denisson Maurício Viana; Cristiane Flora Villarreal
article.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is a debilitating chronic condition frequently refractory to available therapies, while the therapeutic potential of cannabidiol (CBD) is limited by its unfavorable physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties. This study investigated whether incorporation of CBD into a lipid-based microemulsion (LS-CBD) could improve its antinociceptive profile in a murine model of NP, and explored potential molecular mechanisms and safety. LS-CBD was prepared by a high-energy emulsification method and exhibited nanometric droplet size, narrow size distribution, high entrapment efficiency (96.8 ± 0.7%), and physicochemical stability over 60 days. Male C57BL/6 mice subjected to partial sciatic nerve ligation were evaluated for mechanical and thermal nociception following acute and repeated oral administration of CBD and LS-CBD (25, 50, and 75 mg/kg). Compared with free CBD, LS-CBD prolonged the duration of thermal antinociception (1-8 h vs. 2 h) and produced a significantly greater global antinociceptive effect. Peak antinociception did not differ between formulations (50.0 ± 14.9% vs. 53.2 ± 25.5%), indicating that nanoencapsulation prolonged the response rather than increasing its magnitude. Under repeated administration, LS-CBD produced significant mechanical antinociceptive activity on every day of the seven-day treatment period, while both formulations produced comparable and sustained thermal antinociception without evidence of tolerance development. At the molecular level, both CBD and LS-CBD increased Sod1 and Cat transcripts relative to naive animals, and reduced Nos2 and Gfap transcripts relative to neuropathic controls, in the dorsal root ganglia, suggesting attenuation of nitrosative stress and satellite glial cell activation. Neither treatment induced hematological, biochemical, or body weight alterations following repeated administration. These findings support lipid-based nanoencapsulation as a strategy to extend the duration of CBD antinociception after oral administration.

article.title: Apolipoproteins in nanoparticle-mediated brain drug delivery: promise, mechanisms, and misconceptions.
article.authors: Svetlana Gelperina; Matthias G Wacker
article.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Apolipoprotein E (apoE) plays a context-dependent role in nanomedicine for central nervous system drug delivery. It can facilitate cerebral endothelial recognition and increase brain exposure in nanoparticle systems while simultaneously promoting hepatic uptake, challenging its traditional interpretation as a brain-specific targeting ligand. AREAS COVERED: This review critically evaluates evidence from classical polysorbate-coated poly(butyl cyanoacrylate) (PBCA) and apoE-coupled albumin nanoparticles, apoE-derived peptide systems, solid lipid nanoparticles, and ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Attention is given to apoE presentation and isoform biology, protein-corona dynamics, LDL receptor family interactions, hepatic clearance, blood-brain barrier (BBB) status, route-dependent disposition, and blood-cell interactions. Advances in BBB models, LNP engineering, and translational strategies are also considered. EXPERT OPINION: ApoE should be regarded as a tunable regulator of nanoparticle biodistribution rather than a universal BBB shuttle. Development should focus on therapeutically active drug exposure in the relevant brain compartment rather than apoE binding, endothelial uptake, or total brain-associated signal. This requires assessment of whole-blood interactions, hepatic partitioning, receptor dependence, compartment-resolved brain disposition, payload release, pharmacodynamic activity, disease-specific BBB biology, and potentially apoE genotype. ApoE-based systems should be advanced only when they demonstrate a reproducible therapeutic advantage over comparable unmodified carriers and alternative brain-delivery strategies.

article.title: Real-World Health Monitoring Using Wrist-Worn Wearables in Community-Dwelling Older Adults in China: Mixed Methods Feasibility Study.
article.authors: Ying Bai; Yi Tang; Yiwei Zhao; Lixin Ma; Yanjun Ma; Zhibin Wang
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Real-world behavioral and physiological functioning, including heart rate, daily mobility, and sleep patterns, may provide information about aging and early neurodegenerative changes that is not captured by periodic clinical visits. Wrist-worn wearable devices offer a promising approach for continuous, passive monitoring of these domains. However, evidence regarding feasibility, usability, and acceptability in real-world observational settings among community-dwelling older adults in China remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study primarily aimed to evaluate the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of using wrist-worn wearable devices to monitor behavioral and physiological function in community-dwelling older adults under naturalistic conditions. As a secondary objective, the study descriptively characterized wearable-derived behavioral and physiological measures among participants with minimal consecutive valid monitoring. METHODS: We enrolled 486 community-dwelling older adults from the Beijing region of the China-Aging cohort, each of whom received a Huawei Band 8 commercial wrist-worn wearable device. A valid monitoring day was defined as 10 or more hours of wear time. Participants were classified into three monitoring-pattern categories based on predefined wear-time criteria: no valid monitoring day, nonconsecutive valid monitoring, and minimal consecutive valid monitoring (≥3 consecutive valid monitoring days). Demographic characteristics, health status, and cognitive and functional measures (Mini-Mental State Examination and Barthel Activities of Daily Living Index) were compared across groups. Usability, acceptability, and perceived barriers were assessed using a structured user experience survey. RESULTS: Of 486 participants, 224 (46.1%) achieved minimal consecutive valid monitoring, 156 (32.1%) had nonconsecutive valid monitoring, and 106 (21.8%) had no valid monitoring day. Self-rated health differed significantly across monitoring patterns (P=.005), whereas no significant differences were observed for the other measured baseline characteristics. Among participants with minimal consecutive valid monitoring, mean daily heart rate was 72.1 (SD 8.6) bpm, median daily step count was 6177 (IQR 4249-8872) steps/day, and sleep data were available for 211 out of 224 (94.2%), with a median sleep duration of 7.23 (IQR 6.48-8.04) hours. The user experience survey was completed by 106 out of 486 (21.8%) participants, with higher participation among those with more sustained monitoring. Respondents generally reported favorable usability and acceptability; common barriers included device discomfort, data synchronization issues, and battery life. CONCLUSIONS: Wrist-worn wearable monitoring was feasible under naturalistic conditions for a substantial proportion of community-dwelling older adults in China, with generally favorable usability and acceptability among survey respondents. However, monitoring patterns varied considerably across individuals, highlighting challenges for long-term use and large-scale implementation. These findings support the potential of wearable technologies for longitudinal monitoring outside clinic-based assessments. Further research is needed to establish the stability and clinical relevance of wearable-derived behavioral measures over longer monitoring periods.

article.title: Nanoplastics as Hepatic Toxicant Vectors: Interactions with Environmental Chemicals, Organelle Dysfunction, and Regulated Cell Death.
article.authors: Amr Ali Mohamed Abdelgawwad El-Sehrawy; Safa Al-Kayyat; Djaloliddin Mansurov; Dhara N Patel; Priya Priyadarshini Nayak; Neeraj Bainsal; Ahmed Hjazi; Divya Singhal; Aseel Smerat; Abbas Nuaithal Nema
article.abstract: The environmental accumulation of nanoplastics (NPs) raises concerns regarding their potential effects on hepatic function. Experimental studies suggest that NP exposure can be related with altered mitochondrial electron transport chain activity, reduced ATP availability, changes in Keap1/Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and impaired mitophagy. NPs have also been linked to cytoskeletal alterations, disrupted autophagic flux, and metabolic disturbances that can contribute to processes relevant to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This review critically evaluates regulated cell death pathways correlated with NP exposure, containing intrinsic apoptosis, RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL-mediated necroptosis, and NLRP3/cGAS-STING-associated pyroptosis. The available evidence implicates oxidative stress, mitochondrial and lysosomal dysfunction, altered autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, and regulated cell death in nanoplastic-associated hepatic effects. However, mechanistic evidence varies in strength, and observed responses depend on particle composition, surface characteristics, exposure conditions, and experimental models. Particular attention is given to distinguishing associative findings from experimentally supported causal mechanisms and to the limitations of extrapolating results from polystyrene nanoparticle models to other nanoplastics. By integrating evidence on mitochondrial quality control, microRNA-mediated metabolic regulation, and modulated cell death, this review identifies main knowledge gaps relevant to future mechanistic studies and toxicological risk assessment.

article.title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling.
article.authors: Sung Hoon Cho; Shawna K Brookens; Ariel L Raybuck; Kaylor Meyer; Yeeun Paik; Jennie Hamilton; Jingxin Li; Karel Kalecky; Chloe Park; Juyeon Lim; Sakeenah L Hicks; John Karijolich; Teodoro H Bottiglieri; Jeffrey C Rathmell; Denis Mogilenko; Christopher D Scharer; Mark R Boothby
article.abstract: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis - a major metabolic use of this amino acid - was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Gls, the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into mouse B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired. Otherwise, it was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, that is, the conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival, involved supporting progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

article.title: Integrative genomic SEM analysis of shared genetic architecture and candidate genes for insulin resistance-related metabolic traits.
article.authors: ShuYan Li; Yi Liang; Guangwen Zhu; Lijiao Wu; Hong Li; Yu Li; Qiu Chen
article.abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for the latent factor, followed by risk locus annotation, fine-mapping, transcriptome-wide association analysis, gene-level prioritization, enrichment analysis, and exploratory structural biology assessment of selected missense substitutions. The single-factor model showed acceptable but not optimal approximate fit and captured a biologically consistent genetic pattern, with positive loadings for fasting insulin, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio and a negative loading for insulin sensitivity index. The latent factor showed detectable SNP heritability and revealed 3,067 genome-wide significant candidate SNPs, with Q_SNP retained as a complementary SNP-level heterogeneity diagnostic.. Functional annotation identified 100 genomic risk loci and 1,530 FDR-significant genes in MAGMA. Fine-mapping prioritized multiple candidate regions, including loci near PPARG, RSPO3, SLC38A11, SLC39A8, BCL2, GDF5, and SPATA5. TWAS and FOCUS further highlighted candidate genes involved in adipocyte biology, glucose-lipid metabolism, insulin secretion, and expression regulation, including PPARG, MLXIPL, TCF7L2, FAM13A, CCDC92, and SLC22A3. Enrichment analyses suggested that genetic signals associated with the insulin resistance-related latent factor were mainly linked to fat distribution, cardiometabolic traits, adipose tissue, mesenchymal cell lineages, and active regulatory genomic regions. In a separate exploratory analysis, AlphaFold3 modeling, ThermoMPNN prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested structural perturbations for three ultra-rare missense substitutions in nominated candidate proteins: BCL2-W188G, GDF5-C400Y, and RSPO3-C129Y. These substitutions were selected using functional-impact annotations and modeling feasibility, were not GWAS lead or fine-mapped causal variants, and do not establish the mechanisms underlying the GWAS associations. These findings provide an integrated genetic and structural framework for understanding shared mechanisms underlying insulin resistance-related metabolic abnormalities, while emphasizing the need for further experimental validation.

article.title: Lethal and sublethal influence of triflumezopyrim on life history traits and enzyme activities in the bean bug, Riptortus pedestris (Hemiptera: Alydidae).
article.authors: Gefan Tian; Jianglong Guo; Jingjie An; He Yuan; Zhixu Hu; Yaofa Li; Zhanlin Gao
article.abstract: Riptortus pedestris (Fab.) is an important soybean pest in East Asia, where its piercing-sucking feeding behavior leads to soybean syndrome. Triflumezopyrim, a novel mesoionic insecticide, has been widely applied to control sap-sucking insects. However, its lethal and sublethal impacts on R. pedestris remain poorly understood. This study investigated the lethal and sublethal effects of triflumezopyrim on R. pedestris using bioassays, age-stage two-sex life table analyses, and enzyme activity measurements. Results demonstrated that triflumezopyrim exhibited strong toxicity (LC50 = 7.46 mg/L) and notable repellent activity against R. pedestris. Exposure of nymphs to sublethal concentrations (LC10 and LC30) significantly prolonged nymphal development and the adult preoviposition period, while reducing adult longevity, oviposition duration, and fecundity in the parental (F0) generation. In addition, LC30 exposure produced adverse transgenerational effects in the F1 generation, including extended adult preoviposition period, decreased male longevity, reduced oviposition duration, fecundity, net reproductive rate (R0), intrinsic rate of increase (r), and finite rate of increase (λ) of the population. Moreover, both LC10 and LC30 treatments led to substantial elevation in the activities of antioxidant (superoxide dismutase and peroxidase) and detoxification (multifunctional oxidase and glutathione S-transferase) enzymes. These findings indicate that triflumezopyrim exerts strong acute toxicity and pronounced sublethal inhibitory effects on R. pedestris, ultimately suppressing population growth potential. This study offers a scientific basis for the rational use of triflumezopyrim as well as the development of strategies for the management of this species.

article.title: Transcriptomic age acceleration is associated with plasmablast-related immune remodeling in IgG4-related disease.
article.authors: Motohisa Yamamoto; Ryuta Kamekura; Masaaki Uehara; Yuta Ichii; Kenichi Takano
article.abstract: Biological aging profoundly influences immune function, yet its role in shaping immune remodeling within chronically inflamed tissues remains unclear. We investigated whether transcriptomic age identifies a plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern in IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). To address this question, bulk RNA sequencing was performed on submandibular gland lesions from 49 patients with IgG4-RD and 3 controls. Transcriptomic age (tAge) was estimated using a transcriptome-based aging model, and age acceleration was calculated as the residual from chronological age. Associations between age acceleration, immune transcriptional modules, and clinical characteristics were evaluated using Spearman correlation analyses. Transcriptomic age correlated with chronological age (ρ = 0.473, P< 0.001), whereas age acceleration was associated with serum IgG4 concentrations (ρ = 0.446, P = 0.001). Among immune transcriptional modules, the plasmablast signature showed the strongest positive association with age acceleration (ρ = 0.312, nominal P = 0.029), although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons (FDR-adjusted P = 0.304). Germinal center B-cell and activated B-cell programs showed inverse trends. The plasmablast module also correlated with serum IgG4 levels. Together, these exploratory findings suggest a coordinated pattern linking transcriptomic age acceleration, plasmablast enrichment, and enhanced IgG4 responses. Rather than establishing a mechanistic pathway, these findings identify a candidate plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern that warrants validation in independent cohorts.

article.title: A stress-adapted fiber state promotes clonal expansion of deleted mitochondrial DNA.
article.authors: Diego Perez-Rodriguez; Ilaria Dalla Rosa; Anastasia Magoulopoulou; Sara Ricciardi; Samantha Davidson; Rebecca Lasalandra; Renata Kabiljo; Aine Moylett; Tamara Hill; Tengfei Wan; Aleck W E Jones; Chloe F Moss; Charlotte Zierz; Melissa L Salazar; Radha Desai; Shar-Yin N Huang; Yves Pommier; Monika Hofer; Robert D S Pitceathly; Martin A M Reijns; Joanna Poulton; Christos Proukakis; J Paul Simons; Mats Nilsson; Robert W Taylor; Ian J Holt; Antonella Spinazzola
article.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion and multiple deletions frequently coexist in mitochondrial disease, neurodegeneration, and aging, yet how the two relate and why deletions accumulate focally remain unresolved. Here, longitudinal bulk and in situ analyses of Mpv17-/- murine muscle reveal that a compensatory rise in mitochondrial transcripts per mtDNA initially offsets severe, uniform mtDNA depletion, preserving the respiratory chain. However, this response carries a delayed cost: by six months transcripts decline, mtDNA deletions emerge, and respiratory-deficient fibers appear. Paradoxically, fibers harboring deletions accumulate supra-physiological amounts of mtDNA, despite prior depletion. This expansion is invariably accompanied by elevated Hsp60, and the same holds in human mitochondrial myopathy. We propose that depletion reprograms mitochondrial DNA and RNA metabolism, inadvertently promoting deletion formation and creating an Hsp60-high fiber state permissive for clonal expansion. Therefore, depletion and multiple deletions can be sequential phases of a common degenerative process, relevant also to aging and neurodegeneration.

article.title: Dopamine turns mitochondrial stress into inflammation.
article.authors: Rodrigo Pacheco
article.abstract: Daniali et al. show that dopamine drives mitochondrial stress, mtDNA release, and cGAS-STING-dependent IL-6 production in human macrophages. These findings suggest a mechanism linking dopaminergic signaling to mtDNA damage signatures increasingly detected in blood from patients with Parkinson's disease.

article.title: Phytochemical analyses, antimicrobial, antioxidant and anticancer activities of endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa.
article.authors: Amr H Hashem; Nosiba S Basher; Abeer S Aloufi; Salem S Salem; Mahmoud M Fawzi; Mohamed M Abdelaziz; Ahmed S Abdelrahman; Mohamed S Khader; Abdallah E Emam; Mohamed A Goma; Ahmed R Salama; Nasir A Ibrahim; Sulaiman A Alsalamah; Fahd A Nasr; Amer M Abdelaziz
article.abstract: Fungal endophytes considered one of the major sources of promising bioactive compounds. This study aimed to isolate endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa for the first time, and to evaluate their biological activities. Results illustrated that, two fungal endophytes isolates were isolated, identified as Alternaria sp. and Alternaria alternata morphologically and genetically. Phytochemical analyses of these two fungal isolates metabolites showed significant amounts of phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, and alkaloids. GC-MS analyses of the crude extracts of these two fungal isolates showed that, major compounds in these extracts belong to the classes of fatty acid esters, fatty acids, and terpenoids. Results revealed that the MCF-7 cancer cells was susceptible to the anticancer effects of both fungal isolates crude extracts, with IC50 values of 96.3 and 117.4 µg/ml, respectively. Additionally, it showed promising antibacterial efficacy against pathogenic bacteria and fungi. Moreover, both crude extracts of fungal isolates exhibited antioxidant activity, with EC50 values of 234.8 µg/ml and 133.4 µg/ml respectively. Endophytic Alternaria species from leaves of R. pruinosa are a novel source for bioactive compounds that used in different medical fields.

article.title: Study on the association between the low-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein ratio and clinicopathological characteristics of breast cancer: A retrospective analysis incorporating subgroup evaluations by age, body mass index, and menopausal status.
article.authors: Lei Dong; Can Liu; Lixin Li; Xiaotong Zhang; Wei Xu; Gaosai Dai
article.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) represents the most prevalent malignant tumor among women globally, with its pronounced heterogeneity presenting significant challenges for precision diagnosis and treatment. Aberrant lipid metabolism, particularly the ratio of low-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein (LHR), has garnered considerable interest in relation to BC development and progression. Nevertheless, the association between LHR and clinicopathological characteristics remains inadequately explored. To address this gap, the present retrospective study analyzed 583 BC patients who underwent surgical treatment at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University. Preoperative blood lipid profiles and clinicopathological data were systematically collected to investigate the association between LHR and critical features, including molecular subtypes. The findings indicated that LHR levels were significantly elevated in patients aged 46 years or older, postmenopausal women, and individuals with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher. Subgroup analyses incorporating age, menopausal status, and BMI suggested potential interactions between these clinical factors and LHR. Although univariate analysis demonstrated an association between LHR and certain clinicopathological features, multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that menopausal status, rather than LHR, was the sole independent predictor of ER-positive and PR-positive status. Therefore, LHR should not be considered an independent predictive biomarker for receptor status. In conclusion, although the LHR demonstrates statistically significant associations with certain clinicopathological characteristics, its modest effect sizes and discriminative ability close to chance indicate limited clinical utility as an independent biomarker. These preliminary findings highlight the need for future research focused on identifying reliable metabolic signatures. Such studies should consider utilizing multi-marker panels instead of relying exclusively on individual lipid metrics for risk stratification in breast cancer.

article.title: Mesenchymal stem cells inhibit ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons of Parkinson's disease mice by phosphorylating STAT6.
article.authors: Xuesong Wang; Mengting Zhang; Wenjing Ding; Yue Wang; Lei Fang; Shannah Erasmus; Yan Xu; Yichi Zhang; Lin Zhou; Lincai Li; Zhengwei Zou; Junsong Ye
article.abstract: Ferroptosis is recognized as a critical driver of dopaminergic neuronal injury. Emerging evidence suggests that the neuroprotective effects of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells are partially mediated through signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) signaling. However, few studies have investigated whether bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells can modulate ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons, and the specific regulatory role of STAT6 in neuronal ferroptosis remains poorly understood. We established an in vitro model of Parkinson's disease using SH-SY5Y cells treated with 1-methyl-4-phenyl-pyridinium and an in vivo model of Parkinson's disease using mice exposed to 1-methyl-4-phenyl- 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells were administered via Transwell coculture in vitro and stereotactic brain injection in vivo. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy, and behavioral tests were used to evaluate neuronal protection and motor function recovery. We assessed phosphorylated STAT6 (p-STAT6), the active form of STAT6, as well as markers related to ferroptosis, iron metabolism, and oxidative stress. Interventions with interleukin-4, AS1517499, and Cas9-mediated STAT6 knockout were performed to verify the regulatory role of the STAT6/p-STAT6 signaling pathway. Laser confocal microscopy was used to analyze the subcellular distribution of p-STAT6 and further elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells-mediated neuroprotection in Parkinson's disease. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells increased tyrosine hydroxylase expression in dopaminergic neurons and alleviated motor dysfunction in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells promoted p-STAT6 phosphorylation at Tyr641. Nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation assays showed that bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells restored nuclear p-STAT6 levels, while confocal microscopy confirmed the nuclear translocation of p-STAT6. Activated p-STAT6 stimulated the SLC7A11-GPX4 antioxidant pathway and restored reduced glutathione levels. Meanwhile, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells downregulated DMT1 expression, thereby reducing intracellular iron accumulation, reactive oxygen species production, and lipid peroxidation. Interleukin-4 recapitulated the anti-ferroptotic effects of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, whereas AS1517499 abolished their neuroprotective effects. STAT6 knockout eliminated the ability of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells to inhibit neuronal ferroptosis. This study demonstrates that bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells induce p-STAT6 phosphorylation at Tyr641 and facilitate its nuclear translocation. Activated p-STAT6 alleviates iron overload and lipid peroxidation by regulating SLC7A11-GPX4 and DMT1. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells activate the STAT6 pathway to inhibit neuronal ferroptosis, increase tyrosine hydroxylase expression, and improve Parkinson's disease-related pathological changes and motor deficits.

article.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
article.authors: Qinfen Wu; Junhua Hu; Naibijiang Abuliezi; Yihan Sun; Yanyan Wu; Xiaoyi Dun
article.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

article.title: Olvanil Reduces Subcutaneous Fat Accumulation and Lipogenic Gene Expression, Without Alleviating Hepatic Oxidative Stress or Histopathological Alterations in Mice with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
article.authors: Elda Cristina Villaseñor-Tapia; David Alejandro Curiel-Pedraza; Edgar Rubén Mendieta-Condado; Jorge Alberto Rodríguez-González; Alejandro Arturo Canales-Aguirre; Edwin Estefan Reza-Zaldívar; Ana Laura Márquez-Aguirre
article.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by excess intrahepatic lipid accumulation due to lipid overflow and synthesis, as well as impaired lipid oxidation. Olvanil (OLV) is a nonpungent capsaicin analog that has previously been shown to have anti-obesity effects in diet-induced obesity models. Nevertheless, its effects on fatty liver remain unclear. In this study, we evaluated the potential of OLV to address lipid metabolic dysfunction and MASLD-related hepatic abnormalities. C57BL/6 mice were fed a high-fat/high-fructose diet for 24 weeks, with or without OLV (25 mg/kg/day) administered by oral gavage for the last 8 weeks. We primarily evaluated the effects of OLV on liver function markers and the hepatic expression of key genes involved in lipid metabolism to assess its potential in reducing MASLD progression. We confirmed that OLV promoted lipolysis in adipocytes and significantly reduced body weight gain and fat accumulation, particularly in subcutaneous adipose tissue. At the molecular level, we demonstrated that OLV reduced the expression of lipogenic genes (ACC, FASN, SREBP-1c, and PPAR-γ). However, we observed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels and increased interleukin-6 and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances levels in liver tissue. Moreover, histopathological alterations such as hepatic steatosis and lobular inflammation tended to be more pronounced in OLV-treated animals than in untreated MASLD animals. In conclusion, while OLV reduced subcutaneous adiposity and liver lipogenic gene expression, it did not improve hepatic oxidative stress or histopathological alterations in a murine MASLD model. Free fatty acid-mediated lipotoxicity may be present, exacerbating hepatic oxidative stress and inflammatory changes; therefore, further studies are needed to confirm the proposed metabolic pathway.

article.title: Breast Milk and Allergic Disease Development: Immunological Factors Associated with Eczema, Food Allergy and Wheezing/Asthma.
article.authors: Alessandra Catalogna; Carlo Agostoni; Simona Barni; Roberto Berni Canani; Laura Carucci; Letizia Ciliberti; Serena Coppola; Antonio Corsello; Gregorio Paolo Milani; Francesca Mori; Rita Nocerino; Bernardo Sousa Pinto; Giulia Carla Immacolata Spolidoro; Mattia Giovannini; Daniel Munblit
article.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Human milk (HM) contains a diverse array of immunological, microbial, and metabolic bioactive factors that may influence early immune maturation and allergic disease susceptibility. This narrative review examines current evidence linking major HM bioactives with eczema, food allergy, and wheezing/asthma, integrating mechanistic findings with human observational and clinical data. RECENT FINDINGS: Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), secretory IgA (sIgA), human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), cytokines, fatty acids, short-chain fatty acids, the HM microbiome, and extracellular vesicles have all been implicated in pathways relevant to epithelial integrity, microbial colonization, and immune tolerance. However, associations with allergic outcomes are heterogeneous and frequently context dependent. Findings vary according to lactation stage, maternal characteristics, infant susceptibility, microbial exposures, and outcome definition. Mechanistic evidence is often stronger than prospective clinical evidence, and no individual HM component or bioactive profile has yet emerged as a reproducible predictor of allergy protection. Current evidence supports viewing HM as a dynamic maternal-milk-infant biological network rather than as a source of isolated protective factors. Future studies should integrate repeated HM sampling, rigorous allergic phenotyping, and multi-omic approaches to distinguish causal mediators from biomarkers of maternal or infant biology.

article.title: Molecular mechanisms, functional diversity, and therapeutic implications of HSP90 isoforms in lung cancer.
article.authors: K P Janani; S K Lalithammbika; P K Praveen Kumar
article.abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) is a critical molecular chaperone that ensures the stability and maturation of oncogenic client proteins in lung cancer. This review examines the distinct roles of HSP90α, HSP90β, GRP94 and the mitochondrial paralog TRAP1 in driving disease progression. While HSP90α governs invasiveness and metastasis, HSP90β maintains homeostatic oncogenic signalling. TRAP1 serves as a metabolic lynchpin, facilitating metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial cytoprotection, and resistance to apoptosis. Together, these isoforms stabilize key drivers such as EGFR, ALK and KRAS, fostering therapeutic resistance. Utilizing systems biology, bioinformatics and comparative analysis of experimental studies, this review explores the high-throughput identification of HSP90 isoforms as central "hub genes" within the lung cancer interactome. The therapeutic potential of mitochondrial-targeted drug delivery systems and isoform-selective inhibitors designed to minimize systemic toxicity are explored in detail. Ultimately, understanding isoform-specific dynamics and multi-omics regulatory networks is essential for developing personalized, selective interventions to overcome drug resistance and improve lung cancer management.

article.title: Multi-cohort and single-nucleus transcriptomics identify a five-gene lactylation-related panel and a disease-dependent hepatocyte glycolysis-lactylation-related expression program in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
article.authors: Yang Mi; Ziang Liu; Xiaolong Li; Xuchen Zhao; Wei Xue; Zongyuan Che; Yulin Feng; Ruijun Ru; Rongjia Zhang; Yanzhang Tian
article.abstract: Lysine lactylation couples glycolytic flux to protein and chromatin regulation, but the expression landscape of lactylation-related genes (LRGs) in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) has not been mapped. We analysed 320 LRGs across eight bulk, single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic datasets. Sixty-six LRGs were differentially expressed in a merged training cohort (51 controls, 49 MASH). A severity-anchored funnel and four machine-learning algorithms then converged on a five-gene panel (SIRT1, CEBPZ, TKT, RPL14, CD2BP2). A neural network on the panel reached a nested cross-validated AUC of 0.89 and detected MASH against histologically normal liver in a classifier-external cohort (AUC 0.90-0.97). The panel did not separate MASH from simple steatosis (NAFL), a boundary shared by all four benchmarked signatures (AUC 0.50-0.70). In 265,271 nuclei from 48 livers, the LRG expression program localised to hepatocytes and rose most significantly in Hep3, a sterol- and lipid-biosynthetic state that expanded 7.2-fold in MASH. Hepatocyte transcriptomic LRG scores tracked glycolysis across MASH patients (rho = 0.93, n = 19) but not across controls (rho = 0.01, n = 23; P = 1.3 × 10⁻⁶ for the difference). This disease dependence exceeded that of 1,000 expression-matched random gene sets. Hep3 and glycolysis signals were oriented centrilobularly in Visium sections from four donors. The panel offers a transcriptomic MASH detection axis, and the Hep3-centred program a hypothesis for hepatic lactylation that lactylomic profiling can now test.

article.title: Oxeiptosis in gastrointestinal cancer: molecular mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and future perspectives.
article.authors: Islam Ahmed Abdelmawgood; Michael Ibrahim Boushra; Donia Mohamed Hussien; Esraa M Abdelhalim
article.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies represent a major global health burden characterized by high mortality rates, pronounced genomic heterogeneity, and resistance to conventional therapies. While cancer research has historically focused on apoptosis, non-canonical regulated cell death (RCD) pathways have recently emerged as critical regulators of oncogenesis and tumor suppression. Among these pathways, oxeiptosis is a recently identified, non-inflammatory, and caspase-independent cell death mechanism triggered by hyperphysiological levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This pathway is mechanistically governed by the mitochondrial Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)/phosphoglycerate mutase family member 5 (PGAM5)/ apoptosis-inducing factor mitochondria-associated 1 (AIFM1) signaling axis. Under conditions of toxic oxidative stress, elevated ROS levels activate Keap1, facilitating the PGAM5-mediated dephosphorylation of AIFM1. This review synthesizes the pathophysiological roles of oxidative stress and the regulatory landscape of oxeiptosis across major GI cancers, including esophageal, gastric, colorectal (CRC), pancreatic, and hepatocellular carcinomas (HCC) 1. Although clinical translation in esophageal and pancreatic cancers is currently constrained by a paucity of direct experimental data, recent multi-omics and bioinformatics analyses have identified oxeiptosis-related gene signatures as robust prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers in gastric cancer and HCC. Furthermore, preclinical evidence demonstrates that small molecules and natural products can successfully exploit the oxeiptotic cascade to bypass established apoptotic resistance. Specifically, the natural compounds sanguinarine and auriculasin trigger potent, PGAM5-dependent oxeiptosis in CRC models, while phenethyl isothiocyanate, dasatinib, and methyl-cantharidimide exhibit strong therapeutic synergy in HCC cell lines. Collectively, targeting oxeiptosis represents a highly promising preclinical strategy to overcome chemoresistance in GI malignancies; however, further in vitro, in vivo, and clinical investigations are essential to validate its therapeutic efficacy and determine whether modulating this pathway translates into improved patient survival and clinical outcomes.

article.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and experimental analyses identify macrophage-associated STAT3 signaling contributing to ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy.
article.authors: Shi Qiu; Rongqin Dai; Xiaopei Huang; Wenliang Zhu; Wenxiao Zhang; Lingxiao Feng; Jianxu Yang; Mengqi Huo; Huanzhang Shao
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) is a major complication of sepsis, but how inflammatory immune cells contribute to ferroptosis-related myocardial injury remains unclear. We investigated ferroptosis-associated transcriptional remodeling in SCM and the functional contribution of macrophage STAT3 signaling. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication analysis, and independent mouse and human transcriptomic cohorts were integrated to characterize ferroptosis-associated changes. Driver and suppressor signatures were analyzed separately. STAT3 was silenced in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by conditioned-medium transfer to H9C2 cardiomyocytes. Ferroptosis-related injury was evaluated using lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, molecular markers, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) intervention, and an SCM mouse model. RESULTS: Ferroptosis-associated transcriptional features showed marked cell-type heterogeneity. Inflammatory macrophages exhibited prominent STAT3-related inflammatory signaling and extensive predicted communication with cardiomyocytes. Independent cohorts revealed context-dependent changes in ferroptosis driver and suppressor programs. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated macrophages induced cardiomyocyte injury, lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, decreased GPX4, and increased ACSL4. Macrophage STAT3 knockdown partially attenuated these changes, reduced inflammatory responses, and altered Cp expression. Fer-1 further alleviated conditioned-medium-induced injury. Consistent ferroptosis-related molecular alterations were observed in SCM mice. CONCLUSION: Macrophage STAT3 signaling contributes to a paracrine inflammatory environment associated with ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury, linking inflammatory macrophages to myocardial injury in SCM.

article.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
article.authors: Andrea Witowski; Thilo Bracht; Lena Kröger; Katharina Rump; Hartmuth Nowak; Lars Bergmann; Matthias Unterberg; Tim Rahmel; Britta Westhus; Alexander Wolf; Patrick Thon; Dominik Ziehe; Christian Putensen; Stefan Ehrentraut; Alexander Zarbock; Frank Wappler; Jerome Defosse; Dietrich Henzler; Barbara Sitek; Andreas Schnitzbauer; Ulrik Stervbo; Kamil Rosiewicz; Christian Hugo; Sindy Neumann; Philipp Pagel; Andreas Pascher; Nina Babel; Michael Adamzik; Birte Dyck; Björn Koos
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID). RESULTS: SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles. CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

article.title: A synbiotic nanoemulsion modulates metabolic dysfunction and organ functioning in high-fat diet-induced obese mice.
article.authors: Noor Virk; Irfana Liaqat; Saima Masood; Iram Liaqat; Sheryar Afzal; Aimi Syamima Abdul Manap; Abdelrahman M A Elseory; Maujid Masood Malik
article.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity is associated with metabolic disturbance and structural changes in the intestine, liver, kidney, and adipose tissue. This study evaluated the effects of a co-formulated nanoemulsion containing silk fibroin (a proposed prebiotic) and Lactobacillus rhamnosus (a probiotic), referred to here as a synbiotic nanoemulsion, in HFD-induced obese mice. A synbiotic nanoemulsion was prepared using a high-energy method and characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy and FTIR analysis. Forty-eight male mice were randomly divided into eight groups (n = 6) and fed different diet for 16 weeks. Body weight was recorded weekly, following biochemical, histological, and histomorphometric analysis. Compared with the normal diet group (31.82 ± 1.18 g), HFD-fed mice showed a significant increase in body weight (48.7 ± 0.07 g) and severe dyslipidemia, evidenced by elevated total cholesterol (222-276.5 mg/dL), triglycerides (195-289.5 mg/dL), and low-density lipoprotein (104.8-140 mg/dL), with reduced high-density lipoprotein levels (9-23 mg/dL). Synbiotic supplementation significantly reduced blood urea nitrogen (8-10 mg/dL), serum creatinine (0.55-1.0 mg/dL), alanine aminotransferase (28-39 U/L), and aspartate aminotransferase (129-141 U/L). Furthermore, systemic inflammation was also reduced reflected by lowered TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, alongside increased IL-10 levels as compared to HFD group. Histological and histomorphometric analysis showed improved organ architecture in the synbiotic-treated group, with several measurements close to those of the normal diet group. In this HFD mouse model, the fibroin-L. rhamnosus nanoemulsion was associated with lower body weight, improved lipid profile, liver, kidney, and inflammatory markers, and improved tissue morphology. These findings support further study of the formulation. The design does not allow conclusions about synergy, nanoemulsion-specific delivery effects or mechanisms.

article.title: The development of a digital PCR approach for the detection of fecal contamination using Bacteroidales and vertebrate mtDNA probes.
article.authors: Sylvia Etim; Dipanwita Raha; Alyssa N Sanchez; Mirna Ghemrawi; George Duncan; Bruce McCord
article.abstract: Fecal contamination of food such as fruits and vegetables remains a major public health concern. The United States (US) Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people get sick from foodborne illness every year. The quality of farm produce is affected by pathogens from feces or environmental factors that might affect their growth, harvest, and distribution. Rapid and reliable detection methods are therefore essential for identifying contamination sources and improving food safety monitoring. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based methods provide a sensitive and specific approach for detecting bacterial DNA in food samples, including fecal-associated microbial markers such as Bacteroides or other host-associated targets. The goal of this study was to develop a method using digital PCR to detect fecal (Bacteroides) contamination on agricultural produce (strawberries) and to compare these results with standard real-time PCR-based methods. Fecal samples from cattle, rodents, poultry, and other animals were collected, and bacterial DNA (Bacteroides) from these samples was collected and analyzed, and the resultant procedures could detect femtogram levels of bacteria in a sample. To determine the origin of the fecal contamination, mtDNA primers and probes were next developed for multiple vertebrate species using either single or multiplex PCR. These assays were developed, optimized, and validated to detect concentrations as low as 10 copies/µL mtDNA of sample, making these procedures useful in determining the origin or source of fecal contamination of produce.

article.title: Gut microbiota as a key player in diabetes mellitus: mechanisms, dysbiosis, and emerging interventions.
article.authors: Saiyad Bastaminejad; Salar Bakhtiyari; Amin Heidari; Esmaeil Ebrahimi
article.abstract: The gut microbiome has emerged as a critical regulator of metabolic and immune homeostasis, with significant implications for diabetes mellitus. This narrative review synthesizes findings from selected landmark original investigations published from 2000 to 2026, examining the role of the gut microbiome in both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). As a narrative rather than a systematic review, this synthesis does not follow a registered protocol or an exhaustive, reproducible search strategy. Observational studies frequently report dysbiosis, characterized by reduced microbial diversity and altered taxa, as a feature of both prediabetes and diabetes, correlating with poor glycemic control and complications, although the specific taxa and dysbiotic signatures implicated vary across geographically and ethnically distinct populations, indicating that dysbiosis is not a uniform, population-invariant hallmark of disease.
