In the spleen, cell cycle, DNA replication, and DNA damage response programs were prominent, indicative of increased proliferative activity, and cell type deconvolution showed increased proportions of megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cells and decreased proportions of natural killer cells, while AOPs flagged a potential risk of sustained genomic and proliferative stress. Based on the existing AOP framework, we did not find any enriched Key Events in the kidney (reprogrammed vs. old). In the liver, AOP analysis identified pathways regulated in opposition to liver steatosis, indicated by activation of nuclear receptor signaling (Ppara, Pparg) and restoration of fatty-acid oxidation and metabolism. Our findings highlight tissue-specific responses to partial reprogramming and emphasize the need for larger, controlled studies to clarify physiological outcomes and safety.

article.title: Dietary Lipid Sources and Lysolecithin Modulate Growth, Lipid Metabolism, Hepatopancreatic Health, and Intestinal Microbiota in Macrobrachium rosenbergii.
article.authors: Zongsheng Qiu; Xinyi Wei; Jianle Yang; Yuqiang Wei; Shasha Liu; Jianhua Zhao; Qiyou Xu; Clement R de Cruz
article.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary lipid sources and lysolecithin (LL) supplementation on the growth performance, lipid metabolism, hepatopancreatic histology, and intestinal microbiota of Macrobrachium rosenbergii. A 56-day feeding trial was conducted using six isonitrogenous diets containing fish oil (FO), soybean oil (SO), or a 1:1 FO-SO blend (mixed oil [MO]), and each supplemented with or without 0.5% LL. Results indicated a significant interaction between dietary lipid sources and LL supplementation on growth performance (p < 0.05). The MO diet supplemented with LL yielded the highest growth rates, while LL supplementation significantly improved feed efficiency (p < 0.05). Regarding histological status, the dietary SO treatment induced a significant increase in hepatopancreatic lipid deposition (p < 0.0001) and histological alterations, while LL supplementation reduced lipid deposition and improved hepatopancreatic morphology. Dietary lipid source significantly affected muscle n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs; p < 0.01). However, a significant interaction between dietary lipid source and LL supplementation was observed specifically for hepatopancreatic total n-3 PUFA (p = 0.0053). Gene expression analysis confirmed that LL modulates lipid metabolism in a source-dependent manner, upregulating fatty acid oxidation pathways (Pparα and Cpt1) in FO groups while influencing synthesis pathways (FAS) in SO groups (p < 0.05). Furthermore, LL supplementation significantly altered the composition of intestinal microbiota, specifically enriching beneficial bacterial genera in dietary SO-treatment (p < 0.05). In conclusion, the dietary treatment combining MOs and LL showed beneficial effects on growth performance, lipid metabolism, and hepatopancreatic health in M. rosenbergii.

article.title: Ethnopharmacological evaluation of Irvingia gabonensis (Aubry-Lecomte ex O'Rorke) Baill. seed extract: integrated computational and in vitro assessment of antioxidant, antidiabetic, and anticancer activities with in vivo validation of antidiabetic activity.
article.authors: Ahamefula Anslem Ahuchaogu; Cletus Anes Ukwubile; Ifeoma Uzoamaka Nwabekee; James Onyedikachi Nwagba
article.abstract: UNLABELLED: Irvingia gabonensis has been extensively investigated for its phytochemical composition and diverse biological activities, including antioxidant and metabolic effects. However, integrated studies combining phytochemical characterization with computational assessment of multiple disease-relevant molecular targets and corresponding experimental biological endpoints remain comparatively limited. This study therefore evaluated the antioxidant, antidiabetic, and anticancer potential of the methanol seed extract of I. gabonensis using an integrated approach comprising phytochemical profiling, computational analyses, and in vitro biological assays, with in vivo validation specifically restricted to antidiabetic activity in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats. Preliminary phytochemical screening and LC-MS/MS profiling revealed phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, phytosterols, and triterpenoids, including quercetin, kaempferol, chlorogenic acid, rutin, β-sitosterol, oleanolic acid, and ursolic acid. The extract exhibited total phenolic and flavonoid contents of 185.6 ± 4.2 mg GAE/g and 96.4 ± 2.8 mg QE/g, respectively. Molecular docking indicated favorable docking scores and predicted interactions of selected phytochemicals with α-amylase, α-glucosidase, DPP-4, Keap1, BCL-2, EGFR, and VEGFR-2, with quercetin showing favorable predicted interactions across several targets. In vitro, the extract showed concentration-dependent antioxidant activity, with DPPH and ABTS IC₅₀ values of 82.6 ± 3.1 and 76.3 ± 2.7 μg/mL, respectively, and inhibited α-amylase (IC₅₀ = 112.4 ± 4.6 μg/mL) and α-glucosidase (IC₅₀ = 104.3 ± 4.1 μg/mL). Anticancer activity was evaluated exclusively in vitro. The extract exhibited differential cytotoxicity against PC-3, MCF-7, and HCT116 cancer cells compared with the non-malignant HEK293 comparator cell line, with lower cytotoxicity toward HEK293 cells under the tested conditions. Annexin V/PI analysis further demonstrated increased apoptotic cell populations in extract-treated cancer cells. In vivo evaluation was restricted to antidiabetic activity. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats, treatment with the extract (400 mg/kg) reduced fasting blood glucose and HbA1c, restored insulin levels, improved lipid profiles, enhanced endogenous antioxidant defenses, reduced lipid peroxidation, and ameliorated diabetes-associated histopathological alterations. Collectively, these findings provide computational, in vitro, and in vivo evidence supporting the antidiabetic potential of I. gabonensis seed extract. The observed anticancer effects remain limited to in vitro evidence, and the differential cytotoxicity observed relative to HEK293 cells should not be interpreted as evidence of tumour selectivity. Further studies employing tissue-matched non-malignant cells, appropriate animal tumour models, and mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and toxicological investigations are required to establish its anticancer potential. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00779-1.

article.title: Nutritional profiling and pharmacological investigation of Baccaurea motleyana peel and seed through experimental and computational approach.
article.authors: Md Rabiul Hossain; Md Hossain Sami; Md Shafayet Hossain; Tasnuva Faiz Tanisha; Yusha Fami; Jafrin Akter Eisha; Soumik Chowdhury; Rukyea Yasmine Mysha; Md Zia Uddin
article.abstract: UNLABELLED: Natural products that contain bioactive phytochemicals have been gaining a growing interest as a source of therapeutic agents in the treatment of oxidative stress-related metabolic disorders and cancer. The purpose of this study was to examine the nutritional composition, phytochemical profile and therapeutic potential of Baccaurea motleyana (Rambai) fruit peel and seed extracts using integrated in vitro, in vivo and in silico approaches. Qualitative and quantitative phytochemicals, proximate nutritional composition, antioxidant activity (DPPH and ABTS) and antidiabetic activity (α-amylase inhibition by starch-iodine and DNSA assays) were analysed for the ethanolic extracts while the anti-cancer activity was performed using MTT assay against HeLa cells. Tentative compounds identified from GC-MS analysis was screened for molecular docking against α-amylase and DPP4 protein, followed by ADMET analysis and MD simulations. The peel extract presented significantly higher amount of phenolics (67.63 ± 0.26 mg GAE/g), flavonoids (32.51 ± 0.30 mg QAE/g) and tannins (12.29 ± 0.08 mg TAE/g) than seed extract and exhibited better antioxidant, α-amylase inhibitory and moderate anticancer properties with cell death of 30-40% compared to > 95% cell survival of seed extract. The peel extract significantly decreased the fasting blood glucose in alloxan induced diabetic mice in a dose dependent manner for 14 days. A total of 86 bioactive compounds were identified using GC-MS analysis, of which fatty acid esters, sterols, and terpenoids are the major classes. Molecular docking studies showed that the three compounds, namely Spiro [4.5]decan-7-one, 1,8-dimethyl-4-(1-methylethyl)- and 2(1 H)-Benzocyclooctenone, decahydro-10a-methyl-, trans- had high binding affinities to both the α-amylase and DPP4 enzyme. The drug-likeness and low toxicity were confirmed by ADMET analysis while the molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA and PCA revealed the stability in protein-ligand interaction. Overall, these results suggest that B. motleyana peel could be a good source of bioactive compounds for therapeutic applications in metabolic disorders and cancer. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00784-4.

article.title: Electroacupuncture Alleviates Chemotherapy- Associated Cancer-Related Fatigue by Restoring Mitochondrial Homeostasis.
article.authors: Shiyin Lie; Xi Xiao; Miaomiao Xu; Jingchun Zeng; Liming Lu; Jietao Lin
article.abstract: ObjectiveCancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a persistent and debilitating symptom commonly associated with cancer cachexia and impaired physical function, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the anti-fatigue effects of electroacupuncture (EA) and to explore its underlying mechanisms.MethodsA CRF mouse model was established by 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) administration. EA was applied at ST36. Fatigue-related behaviors were assessed using rotarod, grip strength, swimming, and open-field tests. Skeletal muscle morphology was evaluated by histological staining, and mitochondrial ultrastructure was examined by transmission electron microscopy. Mitochondrial function and oxidative stress were assessed by measuring membrane potential (ΔΨm), mtDNA content, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity. The expression of mitochondrial dynamics-related genes was analyzed by RT-qPCR.ResultsEA significantly alleviated fatigue-like behaviors, improving muscle strength, endurance, and locomotor activity in CRF mice. EA preserved muscle fiber morphology and increased cross-sectional area. Mitochondrial structural damage induced by 5-FU was markedly attenuated by EA. Furthermore, EA restored mitochondrial membrane potential and mtDNA content, reduced ROS levels, and enhanced SOD activity. The dysregulated expression of mitochondrial dynamics-related genes was also normalized by EA.ConclusionsEA can alleviate CRF by regulating mitochondrial dynamics and reducing oxidative stress in skeletal muscle, highlighting its potential as a novel intervention for CRF treatment.

article.title: Lipid Mediators and Metabolic Inflammation: From Molecular Mechanisms to a New Therapeutic Paradigm
article.authors: Ivchuk V.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation is a common pathogenetic mechanism of metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, and neurodegenerative diseases. This essay critically analyzes the role of lipid mediators in the pathogenesis of chronic inflammation and substantiates the thesis that the key factor in the transition from acute to chronic inflammation is not the excessive production of pro-inflammatory mediators, but the insufficiency of pro-resolution pathways. The molecular mechanisms of metabolic reprogramming of immune cells are reviewed, in particular, the switching of macrophages between glycolytic (M1) and oxidative (M2) phenotypes, the role of CD36 and FATP2 in lipotoxicity, impaired β-oxidation of fatty acids, and the accumulation of toxic lipid intermediates (free cholesterol, ceramides, lactate, succinate). The dual nature of lipid mediators is analyzed – from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids (LTB4, PGE2) to specialized pro-resolution mediators (SPMs), including lipoxins, resolvins, protectins and maresins. Data on the imbalance between pro-inflammatory and pro-resolution mediators in atherosclerosis, metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, neurodegenerative and autoimmune diseases are presented. Special attention is paid to the concept of “unalamation”, which radically rethinks the etiology of chronic inflammation. A therapeutic paradigm based on the stimulation of endogenous pro-resolution pathways (SPMs and their synthetic analogues) is substantiated as an alternative to traditional anti-inflammatory therapy that inhibits pro-inflammatory mediators. The limitations of existing research, controversies, and prospects for further scientific exploration in this field are discussed.

article.title: Lipid Nanoparticle-Encapsulated mRNA Encoding CagW, a Conserved Component of the Helicobacter pylori Type IV Secretion System, Protects Mice Against H. pylori Challenge
article.authors: Zhao Y, Cheng H, Zhou S, He L, Xiu C, Huang B, Lu X.
article.venue: 预印本平台（数据库未注明）
article.abstract: Background: Roughly one person in two carries Helicobacter pylori, a pathogen classified by the World Health Organization as a group I carcinogen, and the steady loss of antibiotic efficacy has made prophylaxis an urgent rather than an optional goal. No mRNA vaccine against this organism has yet been tested in the clinic, and CagW, a conserved inner-membrane subunit of the H. pylori type IV secretion system (T4SS), has never been evaluated as an mRNA-encoded antigen. Methods: A codon-optimised construct carrying a signal peptide, the CagW coding sequence and a human IgG Fc tag was synthesised, transcribed into mRNA, encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and shown to direct antigen expression in HEK293T cells. C57BL/6 mice received three intramuscular doses of CagW-Fc mRNA-LNPs (5 µg mRNA each) at 14-day intervals; animals given alum alone, luciferase mRNA-LNPs or CagW protein adsorbed to alum served as comparators. Humoral readouts (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a, IgM, IgA and secretory IgA), lymphocyte proliferation, CD4+/CD8+ subsets, intracellular IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-17A and circulating cytokines were quantified before challenge, and protection was assessed after live challenge. Results: The formulation (93.2 nm; PDI 0.13; approximately 90% encapsulation) produced CagW-specific protein in vitro. Vaccination raised high-titre CagW-specific IgG (maximal on day 42), IgM and mucosal sIgA, and drove Th1/Th2-type cellular activation (IL-2, IL-4, IL-12, IFN-γ and IL-17A). After challenge, immunised animals carried markedly fewer gastric bacteria and showed lower urease activity than controls. Conclusions: CagW-Fc mRNA-LNPs are therefore a credible mRNA vaccine platform for H. pylori and warrant further preclinical development.
